title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The station funnel uses powered surfaces and an IR entry sensor. The separate Froggy mechanism acquires coral/algae from the floor and scores L1/processor; its source gives a 48:1 X60 pivot and 2:1 X60 roller drive. A linked shaft/chain keeps the side plates synchronized, while added angle reinforcement stiffens their weak direction.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes reinforcement after structural analysis and a software interlock that delays retracting Froggy until the chassis backs away from the reef. The main arm’s motor placement is also used for counterbalance.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Low-level work can justify a dedicated mechanism when it shortens cycles and releases the primary scorer for another role. That benefit is conditional on interference: two mechanisms must be able to store, acquire and move without colliding. A geometric safety interlock should therefore be part of the architecture reference. “Button released” is not sufficient evidence that an external mechanism can retract safely.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test concurrent main-arm/Froggy poses, compare complete L1/algae cycles, and verify retreat detection before retraction under localization error.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A wide four-bar collector feeds the lightweight coral/algae effector on a string-driven continuous elevator. The interview describes thicker carbon after a week-five collector member bent and cracked; the caption does not safely establish the thickness. Later cage guides and capture wheels replace a slower alignment approach.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links width to driver tolerance, elevator construction to speed/weight/CG, and the revised cage capture to reducing an approximately twenty-second climb process toward roughly ten seconds.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The motorized scoring cycle is only one part of match throughput. Wide acquisition can reduce driver correction, while a faster endgame can recover entire scoring cycles. Those gains can justify mass in guides or reinforcement even when they increase subsystem weight. The original and revised climb should not be averaged into one time, and the gain should not be applied to a team whose approach geometry differs.

text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure failed-pickup rate, full extension deflection and complete cage-approach-to-secured time. Repeat impact tests on the reinforced collector instead of assuming more carbon fixes every load direction.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The source describes an efficient floor collector, V-shaped powered centering path and a differential elevator/arm transmission. Equal coordinated belt motion translates the carriage; differential motion changes arm angle while the motors stay low. The retained technical record also describes a custom-sealed suction effector and piston/scotch-yoke vacuum source.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team’s explicit objective is short, fast coral cycles and resistance to defense without excessive sacrifice of algae capability. Keeping arm/elevator drive motors at the base serves low moving mass.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A differential does not eliminate shoulder or elevator effort; it redistributes that demand across shared actuators. Motion limits, current and saturation must be considered in joint space and motor space. The vacuum end effector can reduce exposed gripping hardware, but seal geometry and surface condition become critical. A short-cycle strategy also needs coordinated human-player supply and a path that avoids interference with partners.

title: Published / retained construction account

The robot retains an elevator-based station-fed scorer and later adds a compact curved-rack algae intake. The architecture should retain the dated add-on history rather than imply the final robot existed at the first event.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The team explicitly credits 4414’s 2023 continuous elevator. Its carriage combines a pivot, wrist and compliant coral/algae end effector; range sensors and a transverse wheel actively center coral. The software models tested safe poses and allows only transitions connected in a graph.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The wrist should not be justified only by branch reach. It also changes how coral can be presented to the trough, so its value can rise in a low-task alliance role. The price is a larger configuration space: correct endpoint poses do not prove that the path between them is safe. A tested edge graph is a concrete way to carry mechanical clearance assumptions into software.

title: Published / retained construction account

## Published / retained construction account

A narrow initial ground concept became a wide collector, feeding an internally belted elevator and arm that can score toward either side. This is a process reference as much as a hardware reference. The team tested a game constraint before committing to a cycle architecture, then used known mechanism families to reduce development risk. Wide acquisition helps only when the handoff can keep up and the arm can safely retract past both field and robot structure. A multi-subsystem state should retain possession information so a timing variation does not silently drop coral.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The collector uses one motor, a passive guide wall and wheel/roller contact to orient floor coral without a separate vertical-roller stage. A chain-driven lateral slide on Igus guides corrects scorer position. A cascade elevator and custom drivetrain complete the retained architecture.

A passive orienter exchanges actuator count for sensitivity to incoming pose, wall friction and driving direction. A lateral scorer can remove some last-meter chassis correction, but it must be stiff enough that the camera’s intended offset corresponds to the actual end-effector position. Ground-source supply and local correction should therefore be assessed as one cycle, including the human player’s delivery error.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

Before Worlds, passive polycarbonate funneling and one lower belt were replaced by molded powered flaps that contact awkward coral orientations. The retained ladder-style placement mechanism also received a cam after early L4 tipping/alignment difficulties. The interview separately describes a ratcheting climb that can retain partial progress after disable.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The serializer change is explicitly tied to coral settling into specific trapped orientations. Retaining a climb after power-off is described as an important requirement, not an incidental effect of gearing.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A funnel that succeeds in the common orientation can still create a stable mechanical equilibrium in an uncommon one. Powered flaps need to disturb that equilibrium without ejecting or crushing the piece. Likewise, an L4 scorer should be judged by placement stability and alignment delay, not only reaching the nominal height. These are distinct revisions and should not be attributed to one unchanging opening-week robot.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Deliberately place coral in every previously trapped pose, measure recovery time, and test L4 placement after abrupt chassis stops. Verify retention with the actual disabled climb configuration.

A post-Niagara ramp/retention change reduces coral bounce-out and permits longer-distance station delivery. A fast unloaded lift is valuable only if the queued piece remains controlled and the effector settles accurately. Keeping the next coral on the ramp while holding algae can remove travel from the next cycle, but requires distinct possession states and a deliberate handoff. The reported lift time should remain a mechanism claim rather than a full-cycle time.

## Published / retained construction account

The over-bumper collector uses four rollers after early prototyping. An indexer retains the note and serves amp delivery through a virtual linkage. Simplicity should be evaluated per task rather than imposed uniformly. Removing an unnecessary roller can improve collector dynamics, while adding climb reserve can preserve a match outcome after damage. Those are compatible engineering decisions. Single-side climbing also changes structural loads and roll, so redundancy is only real if the frame and scoring mechanisms tolerate the alternate load case.

title: Published / retained construction account

## Published / retained construction account

The build thread records replacing a slower, note-damaging conveyor with a more direct curved feed, carbon-roller shooter changes, replaceable intake assemblies and pivot stiffening. Later posts describe a friction damper, changing pivot belts, a ratio change from 125:1 to 100:1, and Worlds logs exposing belt skipping when the arm extended.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties the direct feed to speed/note preservation, the damper to waiting several seconds for the angle to settle, and the revised ratio to faster rotation. Log comparison between motor and external encoder exposed a mechanical slip rather than merely a software aiming error.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This history explains why commanded angle, measured motor angle and true launcher angle are different quantities. Increasing control gains cannot reliably fix a slipping transmission. The fastest pivot also is not the one with the shortest complete aim-to-shot time if it oscillates afterward. The early proposal to climb using the shooter must remain a proposal unless later installation evidence supports it.

title: Retained full-caption account
text:
## Retained full-caption account

The recap follows kickoff incentives, floor-supplied coral, 1323’s preplaced autonomous and L1 specialization, 2910’s backside auto and algae security, then Einstein. The author disclaims knowing who invented several techniques first. Its 2022 three-second-possession interpretation is disputed and must not become rule guidance.

title: 1. Kickoff: rank incentives differ from point value
text:
## 1. Kickoff: rank incentives differ from point value

[Navigation 150–395 s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1UsbJD-zRjU&t=150)

**Source account / attributed commentary:** The commentator compares match points with the ease of earning different ranking points. In his retrospective, leave-plus-one-coral and a deep climb plus park appear relatively accessible, making coral-level completion an important qualifier differentiator.

**Conditional interpretation — analyst reasoning:** This is a prediction framework tied to a field of teams, not an immutable task ranking. If a bonus becomes routine, its marginal ranking value falls even though its point value is unchanged. Evaluate the expected event population and rule revision before allocating mechanism effort.

source_locator.section: 1. Kickoff: rank incentives differ from point value

title: 2. Why algae looked unattractive early
text:
## 2. Why algae looked unattractive early

[Navigation 600–665 s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1UsbJD-zRjU&t=600)

**Source account / attributed commentary:** The recap explains why some teams initially discounted processor play: scoring could also deliver algae to the opponent, whose human player might convert it. It contrasts that with the apparent availability and speed of coral cycles.

**Conditional interpretation — analyst reasoning:** Expected net value depends on the receiving human player and the opponent’s recovery opportunity. Treating all processor actions as a fixed two-point gain, or all algae as poor value, erases those conditions. A kickoff judgment can be reasonable and still become obsolete as skills and congestion change.

title: 3. Rule-aware starting geometry
text:
## 3. Rule-aware starting geometry

title: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
# How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU

Published: 2026-05-04. Review: 2026-10-25. Automatic English captions; 1388 timestamped segments. Every exported caption was read. The final caption begins at 46:19; this is not a video-duration measurement. No raw transcript is redistributed. No visual audit was possible.

A complete available-caption study of the upper-bracket final and all three 2026 Einstein finals. The central account is the coupling of autonomous contact, transition position, neutral-zone supply, steal timing, shoot-on-the-move passing and 4065’s defensive geometry. Breakdowns and uncertain intent remain explicit confounders.

Compare whole alliance control loops, not drum rate against turret rate in isolation. A robot can make a smaller immediate score while changing who owns the next supply of fuel, who can arrive before a shift starts and which opponent must cross a defended bottleneck. The source’s counterfactual wins and point-denial estimates are hypotheses, not measured individual contributions.

source_locator.section: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis

title: 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest
text:
## 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=7s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The introduction treats the upper-bracket meeting plus three finals as one strategic series. Daly fields 4065, 4414 and 1323; Newton fields 868, 2046 and 2910. The creator credits both Daly’s scoring pair and 4065’s defense. Later passages explicitly describe interruptions to 1323, 868 and 2046. The account therefore contains several changing robot-availability states rather than four repetitions of the same six healthy machines.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

An architecture comparison should condition on operational state. A two-turret alliance beating two dumpers in the final result does not establish an unconditional turret advantage: starting positions, autonomous contact, defensive assignments, fuel distribution and failures all change between matches. Conversely, describing the series only as breakdowns discards the account of deliberate supply control. Preserve both explanations until footage and team logs can separate them. The six active robots are the match-specific roster; a reserve on the championship alliance must not be silently treated as an active participant in these four recordings.

title: 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route
text:
## 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=35s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 1323 beginning at an angle and cutting ahead of 2910 rather than first translating sideways. He says this leaves one corner of fuel but permits a larger sweep around the pile. He attributes 2910’s later misalignment and intake corner catching to the rotation caused by that encounter. On the other side, 4414 makes a central pass with a following 4065 route, collects near the hub wall and returns to score from the outpost side. He connects 4414’s net and hopper to retaining a large collection across the bump and clearing it before autonomous ends. His belief that the teams timed the opposing routes is explicitly an assumption.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

The useful design requirement is an autonomous system whose acquisition envelope, collision recovery and route compatibility are evaluated together. A route can abandon a small pocket yet improve total possession by reaching a more valuable arc first. A high collection rate can create an exit-path problem if the loaded robot cannot traverse the selected obstacle without shedding fuel. A net is therefore part of the mobility–storage interface, not an isolated capacity feature. None of this gives a dimension, actual retained count or certified causal diagnosis of 2910’s auto error. Reproduce the route interaction with synchronized overhead video and logs before concluding that the same cut always defeats the same opponent.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The account praises 4065 for ending near midfield and immediately reaching across to contest Newton’s transition fuel. It contrasts 868 ending deeper on its own side and arriving after 1323 and 4414 have already collected and moved ahead of it. The commentator argues that a defender arriving late misses a short opportunity to reduce the autonomous winner’s transition scoring. He describes Daly converting its uncontested collection into sustained transition output.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Treat autonomous terminal pose as the initial condition of teleop, including the defender. Maximizing a small autonomous contribution may be a poor trade if it places that robot too far from the next high-value interception. The source describes a timing window, not a universal instruction to send a defender immediately across the field. The outcome depends on the actual active-hub schedule, legal routes, expected collector arrival and whether intercepting one scorer leaves a partner free. Official fuel confirms a 65–30 transition advantage for Daly in this match, but that alliance total cannot measure the individual value of 4065’s terminal pose or prove the stated cause.

## 5:14–9:00 · Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=314s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 1323 and 4414 splitting the neutral zone, circling through fuel and passing it back while their hub is inactive. They also occupy enough of 2046’s path to make acquisition awkward. He contrasts this with a dumper stopping to pass a batch. In his account, 2046 finds little fuel in the neutral zone, returns toward its own corner reserves and later has difficulty obtaining another hopper. He mentions 868 holding fuel and a 4065 blocker delaying part of 2910’s final discharge.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

This is a coupled acquisition, passing and interference role. Passing while moving can let an off-shift robot keep collecting instead of serializing collect, stop, orient and release; the same motion can close an opponent’s useful approach. That does not make every turret a good moving passer. Intake throughput, feed continuity, aiming under motion, range, loaded acceleration and the ability to keep fuel on the intended side all matter. Fuel temporarily held in a third robot is another supply state, even if that robot scores little. The source supplies neither a complete fuel ledger nor timing measurements, so avoid turning this account into a quantified claim that turrets always clean the field faster than drums.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The analysis follows 2046 from an unproductive neutral-zone visit into a corner collection, then into a later cross-field steal. It says the later departure gives 1323 roughly three additional seconds before the steal arrives. In the other direction, 4414 can leave earlier to remove Newton’s stashed fuel. Later, 1323 screens 868 so 4414 can cross back, while 2046 again arrives late. The creator frames these actions as compounding consequences of the earlier neutral-zone cleanup, not independent isolated tricks.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Track location and inventory at every shift boundary. A robot with the same amount of fuel but a different terminal position can have a very different next assignment. Supply denial may first force a detour, then postpone a steal, then expose a partner’s prepared pile; simply counting immediate defended scoring seconds misses those downstream opportunities. The reported three-second gain remains an estimate from edited commentary. Alternative explanations include traffic, operator choice and recovery from previous contact. An auditable event log should separate observed departure, observed arrival, unknown fuel count and inferred causal link, rather than give one long causal sentence the status of a directly observed fact.

title: 13:47–16:07 · Upper bracket finish: attacking a prepared corner can matter more than another neutral-zone lap
text:
## 13:47–16:07 · Upper bracket finish: attacking a prepared corner can matter more than another neutral-zone lap

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=827s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

Near the end of the first match analysis, the creator praises 4414 for taking fuel from a Newton corner. He argues that this forces 2046 into another neutral-zone trip instead of short local cycles. He also describes 2910 passing to replenish its own side. His explanation is that the dual turrets can continue hunting scattered fuel while moving, whereas the dumper pair loses efficiency when it can no longer fill efficiently before returning to a firing position.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

A hopper-full shooter rate is not the marginal match rate when the remaining fuel is dispersed. Distinguish release-limited, collection-limited and route-limited phases. A high-rate drum can still be strategically excellent if partners prepare dense piles or clear crossings; a moving turret can still be slow if each remaining pickup is difficult. title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The commentary describes 1678 attempting a steal while its hopper is extended, making it bump-only at that instant. 6324 notices and interrupts the return rather than continuing to fill itself. The creator estimates 6324 has a much smaller load and 1678 a larger one; he says the delay consumes roughly the remaining useful scoring interval. He also acknowledges that 1678 still removes fuel from Johnson and could pass or score it later, so the steal is not automatically valueless.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Value the inventories on a schedule. Removing fifty hypothetical fuel from an opponent is not the same as adding fifty score now, and a delayed load can become exposed to a reciprocal steal. Likewise, a small hopper on a support robot is not automatically a reason to defend: the partner needs a current scoring window worth protecting, and the delay must survive the opponent’s available escape. The exact hopper counts and twelve-second estimate are not independently measured. A visual event log should mark the route block, changed configuration, attempted escapes, release and actual first scoring time, with unknown counts left null.

title: 28:40–30:18 · A pick, a reciprocal steal and the fact that large loaded hoppers remove fuel from the field

## 28:40–30:18 · A pick, a reciprocal steal and the fact that large loaded hoppers remove fuel from the field

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1720s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 28:40–30:18 · A pick, a reciprocal steal and the fact that large loaded hoppers remove fuel from the field

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 6324 screening to let 4946 leave while 1678 and 2481 collide or congest the middle. He then notes 6324 taking back fuel from Milstein’s side during part of its own scoring time. His explanation is that the neutral zone has become sparse partly because so much fuel is already held in 1678 and 2481. The initial Milstein steal has value, but the delayed use of that inventory allows Johnson to recover some of the supposed advantage.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

An alliance can be rich in fuel but poor in immediately accessible scoring opportunities. Large loaded hoppers reduce shared field supply for everybody, including the owner’s partners; an opponent with another reachable reserve may temporarily have the better play. This is a dynamic inventory and timing problem, not simply hopper capacity times shooter rate. The collision and screening intent still require footage. A useful agent should be able to explain why the same 6324 can screen, steal and score at different moments without collapsing those actions into a generic “support” paragraph or assuming every action was a preplanned call.

title: 30:18–32:09 · A three-point final, a thirteen-point clean difference and the limits of the losing-auto thesis
text:
## 30:18–32:09 · A three-point final, a thirteen-point clean difference and the limits of the losing-auto thesis

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1818s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 30:18–32:09 · A three-point final, a thirteen-point clean difference and the limits of the losing-auto thesis

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The source closes by following Johnson’s prepared corner fuel and loaded robots, Milstein’s late effort to find reserves and both Milstein scorers returning for final cycles. He interprets the remaining supply and shift order as the reason Johnson can win despite losing auto narrowly. He also gives a no-penalty comparison of 678–691. The final recorded match is 688–691 because Milstein receives ten penalty points. The commentary’s claim that the auto loser has the better teleop conditions is an interpretation of this match state.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Preserve both margins: three in the official final, thirteen in fuel or clean output, with the penalty difference identified. This close result is sensitive to many events besides active-shift order. Compare it to the upper-bracket Daly example: there, winning auto accompanies strong transition position and cleanup that deny the opponent an easy supply setup. Here, the source argues the auto winner does not maintain that control and also faces crossing and screening problems. The transferable principle is to model the next supply state and routes under either autonomous outcome. It is not that auto has negative value, and the source does not establish a universal optimal margin.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Do not use an outro claim to certify channel completeness. The database’s discovered-video list and canonical-match list need their own inventories, including alternate recordings and any replayed attempts. This study covers the two described canonical matches and the author’s defense theory, through the last available caption. It contains no new direct visual observations and cannot be used to clear a pending visual-audit flag.

title: Questions for verification
text:
## Questions for verification

- Why is an expanded 1678 hopper also a route constraint, and how does that change who should attempt a steal?
- How can 254 deliberately stop scoring briefly yet improve its alliance’s output later? What makes the claimed causal effect unverified?
- Why does 6324’s choice to delay a loaded 1678 differ from a generic instruction that every scorer should always defend?
- Explain the creator’s rounded-bumper hypothesis for 4946 and identify at least three reasons that a circle alone cannot guarantee escape.
- What is meant by a defender having to play offense against a partner’s pick, and what would you observe to distinguish an intentional pick from ordinary congestion?
- Compare this video’s “lose auto narrowly” thesis with the earlier Daly account of compounding an auto win. Under what different supply and route assumptions can both be reasonable?
- What are the official final and clean scores of match 6? Why must the three-point final margin not be substituted for the thirteen-point clean margin?

title: Remaining uncertainties
text:
## Remaining uncertainties

- This is an August retrospective of May matches, with knowledge of outcomes. It is not evidence that these lessons were already consensus during kickoff or early season.
- The complete available captions were read; the underlying footage did not render. No described collision, perimeter, shot, pin or route is independently visually verified in this pass.
- The captions corrupt Curie, team names and several numbers. 6800 is Valor, 8613 is Barker, 2481 is Roboteers, 4946 is Alpha Dogs; exact identifiers are normalized only where rosters and context establish them.
- The creator estimates hoppers, potential points and delay durations, and openly guesses autonomous prescouting intent. None is an independently counted robot contribution.
- The commentary’s effective 55-second endgame groups a preceding active shift with the shared final period for one alliance. It must not replace the official final-30-second score component or the rule definition.
- The author is unsure whether an apparent hold on 2481 is a pin and cannot see the hub-side contact. Do not turn this into a legal ruling.
- Rounded-perimeter escape is a hypothesis from this interaction, not proof of immunity to defense. Traction, friction, contact normal, module torque, field obstacles and loaded mass still require examination.
- A close match after an autonomous loss cannot demonstrate that intentionally losing auto is globally optimal. The hypothesis requires comparable alliances, margin, supply-control ability and opponent response.

title: Einstein visual-audit protocol and current checkpoint
text: # Einstein visual-audit protocol and current checkpoint

source_locator.section: Einstein visual-audit protocol and current checkpoint

title: What this edition actually establishes
text:
## What this edition actually establishes

The corpus contains 80 canonical Einstein match records across 2022–2026: 18, 15, 15, 16 and 16 respectively. All 80 have a candidate recording link after recovery of the official 2022 match-2 page. A canonical TBA match row is not a verified inventory of every played/replayed attempt or every camera angle. That additional completeness check remains open.

Zero visual match audits are complete. Six recording pages were opened for access/identity checks; the rest were not individually tested in this pass. Representative recordings from all five seasons supplied metadata but no decoded match frame, remaining black and buffering. Normal reload, playback controls, a lower quality on the 2022 player, seeking on the 2026 player and documented media export did not produce footage. The failure is specific to these tested sessions; it does not prove all videos are unavailable or identify a network cause. It was not a visible bot challenge in this session.

The user authorized solving the prior CAPTCHA. On opening the normal watch page there was no CAPTCHA to solve. The transcript interface worked. All eleven previously pending exports were recovered. Two new available-caption reads cover six canonical 2026 matches, with detailed attributed accounts and conditional analysis. Nine recovered exports still await full content review. The prior 33 caption studies retain their inherited review scope. Nothing in this checkpoint is represented as permanent internal model memory or as visual watching.

title: Identity before tactics
text:
## Identity before tactics

Compare the title, year, teams, alliance colors, bracket position and final score. A similar title or a mirror association is insufficient. The rejected 2022 match-2 link previously pointed to match 15. The replacement is the official FIRST recording titled “Einstein 2 - 2022 FIRST Championship”; its visible description exactly matches red 1619/6672/254 scoring 164 and blue 3534/5940/6328 scoring 122. This establishes page identity, not independent visual identity. Keep that distinction if the video is mislabeled or contains a replay later in the file.

For each recording, preserve its exact URL, creator, available duration and any alternate-angle relation. Record whether a replay is the final scored attempt or an abandoned/no-score attempt. Do not silently overwrite the original evidence when substituting a better angle. In 2022 the semifinal stage is round-robin-style Einstein play; later double-elimination set/match keys use different conventions. Do not infer bracket order by sorting all seasons with the same filename heuristic.

title: A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes
text:
## A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes

View the full match from prestart through the final action at a speed that preserves the interactions being asserted. Establish where autonomous starts, teleop starts and the match ends in the source video. Link every event to both source time and the visible match clock when available. For edited analysis with pauses, rewinds or slow motion, use a piecewise mapping rather than assuming source seconds equal elapsed match seconds. A caption timestamp is a navigation pointer until aligned visually.

Then follow each of the six robots through the full sequence. Record acquisition source, held inventory only when countable, scoring location and configuration, crossing choice, passing destination, screen/defense target and changes of job. For 2026, identify the actual hub state and the robot’s preparation for its next active window. For 2025, record concurrent L1, algae and branch work rather than imposing a serial “finish high branches, then do L1” story. For earlier seasons, preserve their own field geometry, scoring constraints and endgame incentives; do not import the 2026 supply model automatically.

A role is an interval, not a permanent label for a team or a robot. The same robot can score, pass, screen, steal, defend and recover in one match. A stopped robot can affect a route while providing no intended defensive action. A robot with a loaded hopper can influence supply without scoring. A defender may change targets to protect a crossing instead of following its original mark. Keep those possibilities distinguishable in the log.

source_locator.section: A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes

title: What an individual event needs
text:
## What an individual event needs

Store event ID, match key, recording ID, source start/end, match-clock start/end, actors, current configuration, field location, directly visible action, visible outcome, uncertainty and evidence links. Distinguish “robot contacts opponent,” “opponent changes route,” “shots fall short” and “robot stops moving.” Those observations do not by themselves mean “intentional pick,” “successful defense worth one hopper,” “battery sag” or “radio failure.” Put those interpretations in separate fields with their supporting or missing evidence.

For a screen or defensive handoff, observe all participants before and after the interaction. A five-second delay may save another defender’s travel, but it may also cost the screening scorer an equally valuable cycle. Track the alternative route actually available and the time remaining in the scoring window. Do not turn a rough hopper capacity into denied points. For a steal, distinguish fuel removed from an opponent’s reserve, fuel retained, fuel passed, fuel later scored and fuel lost back to the opponent. Avoid counting a transfer twice.

Leave unknown counts null. An empty event list means footage unreviewed, not that the match contained no relevant event. A camera cut creates a blind interval even if broadcast commentary continues. Multiple robots near a pile do not reveal their exact pickup share. Hub counts cannot generally assign individual scoring when streams overlap. Use the official score only at its actual alliance/phase resolution.

title: Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story
text:
## Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story

Record the deployed envelope as seen at the interaction: extension can change a trench-capable robot into a bump-only robot. When a defender constrains rotation, identify the bumper contact and nearby hub, trench bar, wall or bump separately. Do not infer exact clearance, mass, traction, moment of inertia or motor current from a camera image. A rounded perimeter changes the contact problem but cannot guarantee escape under every friction and obstacle condition.

For an operational interruption, mark the last unambiguous functioning action, the first abnormal action, any recovery, and which capabilities remain. “Collects but shoots short” differs from “entire robot dead.” A mechanism appearing damaged is not a diagnosis of root cause. Electrical logs, operator testimony or a technical publication may explain a symptom later; preserve the chronology and attribution of that new explanation. Do not label an unobserved problem a brownout because the score dropped.

source_locator.section: Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story

title: Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output
text:
## Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output

Keep final score, clean score, penalties received and each relevant official phase or component. Reconcile arithmetic and identify which alliance had each active shift. Own first/second active-shift totals in 2026 occur at different wall-clock times for opponents. The final-period fuel component is not climb output. The stored 2026 finals all record zero tower points for both alliances; fuel and access remain the useful questions in this series.

For 2026 match 3, official auto fuel is 188–118; post-auto fuel is 529–509; final is 717–632 because Milstein receives five penalty points. The commentator’s post-auto numbers are alliance quantities. For match 6, clean output is 678–691 and final is 688–691, with ten penalty points received by Milstein. A three-point final is not a three-point clean result. Preserve this distinction in quizzes and causal explanations.

In the upper-bracket final, Daly wins auto 186–83 and transition 65–30 but does not win every subsequent fuel component. In finals 2 it does lead every recorded fuel component, with the final period only 169–165. In finals 3 the own active-shift totals are 311–79, while final-period fuel is 154–161. Those patterns guide what footage to investigate; they cannot identify how many fuel a defender individually denied.

source_locator.section: Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output

title: Completion and verification
text:
## Completion and verification

Do not set complete=true until full interval coverage, all-six-robot follow checks, identity and clock alignment, camera blind spots, score reconciliation and explicit unresolved claims are present. It is acceptable for a completed viewing to leave a particular action unresolved because it is occluded. That uncertainty must remain visible; viewing completion is not omniscience. A user correction should identify the event/claim, the better source or timestamp, the revised interpretation and which downstream design conclusions need reconsideration.

The intended next step is playable match footage or an authorized usable video source. Until it exists, the six expanded 2026 narratives remain commentary evidence, and all eighty visual records remain pending. The JSONL ledger is the durable queue; it is not a certification of work that could not be performed.

Mechanical selection rationale is not established by the code.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The swerve and localization must be considered together. A configured maximum speed is not a demonstrated match speed. Wheel calibration affects both the path tracker and the launch-distance estimate, so a copied drive configuration can corrupt scoring even when teleop feels acceptable. Check hardware revision, encoder scales and actual loaded wheel circumference before borrowing constants.

The published interface treats recovery and reverse flow as designed operating modes. That is useful architectural evidence, but it does not establish roller material, width, compression or impact survival. A profiled pivot can reduce abrupt actuation; whether it does so under contact depends on the real mechanism and controller settings. Separately controlled transport can stage a second cargo while releasing the first, but introduces coordination between occupancy sensing, launcher readiness and reverse recovery. Code supports the existence of these interfaces, not an independent throughput result or proof of jam-free behavior. A two-cargo game rewards preserving a reliable staged sequence; extra transport complexity should be justified by actual scoring continuity.

Requiring recent samples within tolerance is different from checking one instantaneous RPM. It can reject a momentary speed crossing after spin-up or a previous shot. The trade is delayed release versus launch consistency. The existence of front/rear motors does not establish independent spin control in competition, wheel dimensions, a turret, or exact release angle. Those require geometry and event evidence.

title: 2023 published robot account · intake
text: ## 2023 published robot account · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A pasta-roller intake grips a cone flange and pinches a cube, constraining cones to tip-in or tip-out. A roller reorienter supplies the additional rotational degree of freedom needed for an upright handoff. Rollers are powered coaxially through the reorienter.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted ground pickup in arbitrary orientations; human-player throwing could shorten travel by an estimated 40% and reduce loading-zone traffic. Coaxial drive protects motors and reduces mass at the intake edge.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit strategy-to-mechanism chain: changing the pickup source reduces travel only if orientation and handoff remain reliable. The 40% is the team’s route estimate, not an independently measured cycle improvement. A broad capture envelope transfers complexity downstream unless the robot can reduce the resulting pose uncertainty. Compare full acquisition-to-scoring cycles, including difficult orientations, rather than pickup speed alone.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: 2023 published robot account · transfer
text: ## 2023 published robot account · transfer

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A linear intake slider brings the piece inward and permits frontal compliance. A separate horizontal scoring-arm slider reaches across the intake. A time-of-flight sensor first distinguishes orientation at a fixed location, then locates the piece laterally. The elevator lowers while the intake expels to hand off.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team needed handoff despite variable piece position across the intake width.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Do not collapse the two sliders into a single motion. The intake reduces some uncertainty, then sensing and the receiving mechanism handle what remains. This avoids requiring perfect passive centering, at the cost of coordinated motion, sensor interpretation and collision clearance. Sensor occlusion, flange shape, cone reflectivity and loaded mechanism deflection are plausible validation concerns, not failures established by this publication.

title: 2023 published robot account · scoring
text: ## 2023 published robot account · scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A non-parallel four-bar provides scoring reach. An Everybot-style lightweight gripper squeezes the cone tip and pinches a cube. The release describes scoring all levels.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team chose the linkage for low mass and long extension, and judged the high-versus-middle scoring difference sufficient to justify the added capability.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The linkage choice belongs with the piece acquisition and handoff design. Saving moving mass can reduce the drive and tipping burden, but linkage workspace, joint play and gripper compliance determine the usable placement envelope. A later team using a single-stage elevator should not be read as proof that this four-bar was a failed architecture; the game, interface and required motion differ.

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

title: 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake
text: ## 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Polycarbonate rollers flex under impact; short dead-axle sections avoid a full-width shaft permanently bending. The team reports rollers deflecting more than half their diameter in bad hits. Deployment ties the two sides through chain and a cross shaft inside the frame.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compliance, weight and packaging drove the split-axle construction. The team explicitly reports axle-mount bolts shearing and deployment chain snapping, unresolved during the season.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A compliant roller is not the same as a robust entire intake. Moving deformation away from a long shaft can concentrate load in axle bolts or a mechanically coupled deployment system. This matters directly to 1833’s request for something beefy: copy the load path and its known limitations, not merely the visible material. The 2026 independently driven arms are a later response to the chain failure, not a configuration that existed throughout 2024.

text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

Likewise, suppressed electronics do not imply an unplanned electrical layout. Follow the team’s replies when interpreting the release. The existing interview synopsis documents the asymmetric launcher and trap system; this addition focuses on the explicitly published manufacturing and intake corrections.

title: The Flush in-season release · drivetrain
text: ## The Flush in-season release · drivetrain

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

29-inch square chassis with WCP X2i modules and a 5.9:1 drive ratio; the team optimized for roughly 18-foot average sprint distance. Protective panels isolate electronics from falling coral.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Stability at high reach and the expected travel distance drive the stated choices.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Optimize acceleration and usable travel under the expected route distribution, rather than unloaded top speed alone. A larger support polygon can help a reaching superstructure while increasing congestion exposure. The published dimensions and ratio are a configuration snapshot; they do not prove the same ratio is best for 1833 or a different game.

title: The Flush elevator and arm · scoring
text: ## The Flush elevator and arm · scoring

source_locator.section: The Flush elevator and arm · scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Single-stage elevator uses 2x2 uprights, cross bracing and chain drive on both sides. The release gives two Kraken X60s, 3:1 and 28 inches of motion; stator limits increased from 40A to 80A. The arm is rigidly tied side-to-side and its gearbox shimmed; the team describes detuning and reducing the drive to one motor at 100A to avoid tipping.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Rigidity, low backlash and precise automated control are explicit priorities.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Motor count and theoretical joint acceleration cannot be separated from robot stability. Dual-sided chain drive addresses carriage twist, while a rigid camera mount helps relate vision measurements to mechanism geometry. Preserve the stated revisions and the release’s mixed original/final motor annotations; do not silently combine every number into one certified event configuration.

title: The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake
text: ## The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake

source_locator.section: The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A full-width 4mm corrugated-plastic funnel loads from three sides through separately powered rollers. The gripper has independently powered left/right rollers, four coral rollers and two algae rollers, plus an open top.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted tolerant loading, horizontal L1 packing and precise placement. The open top avoids reef entanglement and permits a shallower coral release angle.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A funnel can absorb human-player variability while the gripper controls the final release. Independent sides support a different L1 placement policy rather than merely increasing raw roller power. This is an architectural option for a station-fed role, not evidence that floor coral pickup was unnecessary for every alliance. Corrugated plastic stiffness, folding and clearances must be evaluated in the installed package.

title: Validation still required
text:

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

text: ## The Flush climb/funnel interface · endgame

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The release describes a roughly 3.5-pound climber including motor and gearbox, stowed below the funnel, surgical-tubing extension and a 15:1 winch with a 2:1 pulley. A rear funnel ramp unfolds to clear the cage and climb.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compact packaging preserves the loading system while providing cage engagement tolerance.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The climb is coupled to the funnel’s motion and the loaded robot CG. A compact mechanism is not necessarily easy to approach under traffic; validate capture, retraction and failures with the actual funnel and piece state. These are team-reported design quantities, not measured masses or an exhaustive installed-version history.

text: ## The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls

source_locator.section: The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The Flush uses predictive target selection, smooth handover from driver motion, reef-clearance sequencing and separate local/global localization. The team reports 547/549 L2-L4 coral placements over its last two events. Quixshot is a distinct offseason coral launcher with manually tuned launch velocity differentials and a one-time intake deploy latch.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team reports that packaging a ground pickup with the in-season climber became difficult, so the compatible pickup was instead installed on the offseason launcher.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Do not attach Quixshot’s launcher to the in-season elevator robot. The 99.6% is a bounded team-reported placement statistic, not full-match reliability or 99.6% for every task. The published offseason answer says it did not deep-climb or handle algae at that point. The strongest transferable lesson is a deliberate interface and packaging trade, not the assertion that launching always beats placing.

Quixshot is a separate robot. The team’s July reply explains that a ground intake intended for the in-season machine conflicted with climber packaging and was installed on the launcher instead. title: 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader
text:
# 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

title: Toploader DPC serializer · transfer
text: ## Toploader DPC serializer · transfer

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A rotating capture mechanism scoops fuel from a circular plywood bucket. Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side rollers use omni wheels. Successive fuel pushes through a corrugated-plastic tube shaped by printed ends. The bucket separates into two sections for service.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team identified serialization as the limiting process and designed the robot around it. Independent drives allow software adjustment of rotation versus up-feed.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The capture point moves to available fuel rather than relying solely on gravity bringing fuel to a stationary throat. Independent feed authority can help tune pile interaction and column delivery separately, but the release does not establish a universal motor-ratio setting. Bucket geometry, turret support and electronics access are part of the same flow system. Prototype rates of about 15 BPS single-stream and 23 BPS full-width are comparison claims, not sustained match scoring rates.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader chassis · drivetrain
text: ## Toploader chassis · drivetrain

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A 27-inch square frame preserves circular bucket area without custom swerves or chamfered corners. Internal bars protect battery and module compartments; rear bumper mounts integrate armor for serializer protection.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Maximize the serializer’s available area with manufacturable hardware and protect internal mechanisms.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit packaging choice. It sacrifices some geometric freedom to keep the central circular feed volume useful with standard drive components. Frame perimeter, usable interior area and turret swept volume must be compared together. The team separately describes bump-only autonomous constraints; no unreviewed trench state or chassis specification should be inferred.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader inset turret · scoring
text: ## Toploader inset turret · scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The turret is supported from above and packaged to reduce swept volume. Its sliding bearing stacks polycarbonate and aluminum plates; printed PETG spacers set clearance empirically and grease reduces friction.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Moving scoring and feeding were judged worth a lower single-stream ceiling; small swept volume preserves hopper capacity and flow.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A turret changes more than aiming. Its supports and swept envelope can obstruct fuel entering the serializer, so a nominal capacity comparison that ignores the moving assembly is incomplete. This release supports a manufacturable impact-tolerant bearing concept, not exact dimensions, a universal bearing preload or independently verified shot accuracy. The team’s rate trade is tied to its intended moving role.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader independently deployed arms · intake
text: ## Toploader independently deployed arms · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Each intake arm uses an X44 deploy motor. Protected motors belt-drive compliant dead-axle polycarbonate rollers with silicone tubing and TPU pulley plugs. TPU belt supports retain the belts during deflection. A one-time kicker deploy uses surgical tubing and flexible plugs/string.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team explicitly connects independent deployment to eliminating the mechanically linked 2024 chain failure. Polycarbonate was preferred over SRPP to avoid permanent deformation changing belt centers.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Compliance must preserve transmission function, not just prevent fracture. A flexible arm changes belt geometry under load; supporting the belt during that motion is an integral part of the architecture. The team reports that TPU replaced brittle PETG roller plugs, with 100% infill and four-wall printing, and that wear still requires replacement every one or two events. Repairable consumables are not maintenance-free hardware.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake
text: ## Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Intake deployment extends a sliding hopper; surgical tubing retracts it. Two laminated layers of corrugated plastic provide stiffness. Slots are reinforced with 0.090-inch polycarbonate sandwiched between sheets; panels use tape and adhesive for replacement.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The publication emphasizes low mass, robust sliding and easy manufacture/repair with limited router access.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is a specific example of an intake–storage interface, useful to 1833’s morph chart. Linking deployment reduces independent actuation but also links faults and operating states. Slot reinforcement addresses local bearing and deformation loads that a generic corrugated-plastic wall description misses. Capacity, deflection and passage access should be measured in each loaded state; no unverified hopper capacity is assigned here.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader readiness and localization · controls
text: ## Toploader readiness and localization · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Scoring requires launch velocity, launch angle and turret yaw within tolerance plus a recent image with at least two tags. The serializer pauses when readiness fails. PhotonVision MultiTag selects camera poses using hub/total tag visibility and rejects old or ambiguous poses.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Single-driver operation reduces communication overhead; automated gating is intended to release fuel only from useful launch states.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Feed interruption is an intentional interface between aiming and serialization, not automatically a jam. A high mechanical BPS ceiling is useful only while readiness remains true. Logging the reason for each gating interruption would distinguish vision starvation, aim error and actual feed trouble. The release does not demonstrate those duty fractions or an electrical diagnosis of every stop.

text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

text: ## Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The team describes timestamping partner paths, targeting leftover fuel after the trench race, using reusable path partials and adjustable pauses without redeployment. A Pac-Man routine is identified at NorCal DCMP playoff match 1.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

A bump-only robot was expected to reach midfield later; route selection was built around shorter partners rather than competing for the same initial race.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Architectural limitations can become planning inputs instead of being hidden by an ideal autonomous animation. Preserve the team’s distinction between pre-Champs crossing rules and later rules, and between experiments and actually used routines. A clever path is not proof every prototype routine competed. The release does not establish a tower mechanism; absence from the selected technical sections remains unknown, not certified absence.

title: 1833’s supplied 2026 design workflow
text:
# 1833’s supplied 2026 design workflow

The original workbook and PDF are preserved under team1833/. Their statements are historical team planning, not validated game rules or independent mechanism measurements. Cell-level and PDF-page text exports permit exact retrieval. No source workbook or PDF was edited.

The workbook contains parallel group task lists, numeric priority/difficulty judgments, formulas multiplying those ordinal values, and a cleaned must/might/won’t list. Some sheets have inconsistent priority scales. The cleaned list’s repeated “No” final-decision cells must not be interpreted as rejecting every must-do task. Group 4 even distinguishes autonomous climb priority in qualifications versus eliminations. Keep group opinions and later decisions separate instead of silently averaging them into a consensus.

The PDF maps requirements into intake, storage, shooter, climb, electrical and chassis concepts. It records historical mechanism references, pros/cons and open prototype questions about compression and roller materials. It explicitly asks for service access, wire protection and mechanical/electrical compatibility. The shooter page contains proposed distances, angles and velocities; these are unverified calculations, with launch-height, drag and other assumptions needing reconstruction before reuse. References such as 2020 spindexer slot capacity must not become universal capacity limits for 2026 bulk serializers.

For the agent: reproduce the task-to-requirement-to-concept chain, preserve alternatives and open tests, and distinguish kickoff judgments from later evidence. The early climb priorities are historical inputs; the user’s later correction and tower-only data establish a fuel-first default for the studied 2026 competitive context. Do not overwrite the original documents to make hindsight look like the initial decision. A future task sheet should carry rule revision, phase, partner assumptions, expected contribution, ordinal priority meaning, development cost, evidence and decision rationale. A mechanism comparison should identify which requirement it serves and what observation would change the choice.

title: Required 1833 task sheet
text:
## Required 1833 task sheet

For each new game/manual analysis, material rules revision or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of [the one-sheet template](../../team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx). Follow `docs/TASK_LIST_PROTOCOL.md` and `team1833/task_template_schema.json`, with all paths resolved from the corpus root. The template includes task outcome, phase, points/enabling value, priority, difficulty, recommendation, rationale, alliance dependencies, acceptance target, exact rule/source, uncertainty/test and separate human decision. No group tabs; no inherited season-specific decisions. Four previously blocked 604 image originals are now recovered and embedded (2023 robot; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper).

title: 1833 elite architecture and decision-quality edition
text:
## 1833 elite architecture and decision-quality edition

The owner requires an Einstein-level primary contributor, never a support-only design, and no turret. Relatively simple mechanisms should be optimized for elite output. Historical research remains available, including turret robots and complementary match assignments; those are not permission to violate this design brief. Read `docs/1833_DESIGN_DOCTRINE.md`, `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/1833_OPTIMIZATION_REFERENCES.md` and `docs/evaluations/DUNKTANK_REVIEW_2026-10-26.md`. Use `team1833/design_profile.json`, `team1833/design_review_schema.json`, `agent/design_rubric.json` and `examples/design_review_skeleton.json`. Structural validators audit the one-sheet workbook and review package; they do not establish engineering correctness or improved model performance. All paths in this paragraph are relative to the corpus root.

title: 1833 required task-list protocol
text: # 1833 required task-list protocol

title: Required deliverable and trigger
text:
## Required deliverable and trigger

For every new-season manual analysis, material rules revision, or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of `team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx` before presenting the final architecture recommendation. The required output is a populated workbook with exactly one worksheet, `Task List`. Do not create group tabs. The blank canonical template must remain blank. Save the populated copy under a dated season-and-brief filename; preserve previous analyses so changed priorities can be explained. For a small revision, revise a copy of the previous sheet and identify the changed assumption or rule and its consequences in the rationale. The template is a work product requirement, not a guarantee that a model will obey without being given this protocol.

title: Establish the decision context
text:
## Establish the decision context

Fill the six metadata inputs C2:H7: season/game; exact manual revision and governing source URL; target event, week and competition stage; expected alliance roles and opponent assumptions; 1833's time, people, fabrication, budget, robot packaging, practice and maintenance constraints; and agent/date/human review status. Unknown inputs must be explicitly marked unknown with the assumption used provisionally. Historical EPA, alliance scores and Worlds examples do not substitute for the current manual or team constraints. If these are not available, produce a provisional sheet and identify the missing inputs rather than inventing them.

title: Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms
text:
## Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms

Use one actionable task or required outcome per row, beginning at row 13. Cover every legal task and enabling capability that could matter: mobility and traversal, acquisition, storage and transfer, resource control, scoring, autonomous, endgame, alignment/sensing, defense/support, and other legal actions. These are starter categories, not mandatory robot subsystems. Add or rename categories when the game requires it. Record an excluded or inapplicable task with the reason instead of silently omitting it. Split the same task into separate rows when autonomous/teleop, event stage, alliance role, field location or game state changes its value materially. Keep a functional task such as collecting floor pieces separate from an architecture proposal such as a slapdown intake; mechanisms are evaluated after the functional priorities are stated.

Columns A–N are defined in `team1833/task_template_schema.json` and in the worksheet header. For each occupied task row, complete A–F and H–M; G is calculated. Use N/A plus a reason where a field truly does not apply, and unknown plus a smallest decision-changing test where evidence is missing. Column N is reserved for an actual human decision/rationale: leave blank or label pending human review until 1833 supplies a decision. Never fabricate human approval. Preserve the user's explicit corrections as attributed context alongside their date and scope.

title: Give priorities a defensible meaning
text:
## Give priorities a defensible meaning

Priority 1 means essential to the rule-derived elite primary-contributor objective, before architecture selection; 2 means valuable; 3 means optional. Difficulty uses the team's relative Fibonacci scale: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Explain the basis of both judgments in Why / tradeoff. Do not treat the product P×D as an objective ranking, a points-per-effort model or a decision rule. The supplied original workbook used priority times difficulty; this template retains that discussion aid without claiming it captures strategic value. A difficult must-do can remain a must-do. A high-point action can be unnecessary for this robot when an alliance partner covers it. Enabling tasks and denial can be valuable without directly scoring points.

Use the Agent recommendation dropdown: Must do, Might do, Won’t do, or Needs discussion. State the opportunity cost, partner dependency, game-state conditions and reliability assumptions that could change it. Column D should distinguish rule points from inferred enabling value; include timing, capacity, accuracy or probability conditions when quantified. Do not invent numeric precision when the data supports only a qualitative judgment.

title: Make each recommendation testable and traceable
text:
## Make each recommendation testable and traceable

Acceptance target / units must describe a measurable functional outcome under specified conditions, or explicitly say the target is not yet established. Examples include loaded collection success, release accuracy at a stated location, usable capacity with the mechanism swept envelope, sustained throughput including acquisition and readiness interruptions, or recovery time after a jam. These examples are not requirements or performed tests. Record the rule number/section/page and revision, and the exact source or corpus locator behind each factual claim. Clearly distinguish official rules, team-reported performance, attributed commentary, 1833's judgment and agent inference. Unknowns / smallest test should identify what observation or prototype result could change the priority or architecture.

After filling the sheet, compare at least two coherent architectures against the same prioritized tasks and constraints. Cite historical inspiration by year/team/version and inspect the whole acquisition-to-output interface. Feed architecture findings back into the sheet when they change difficulty, dependencies or acceptance criteria. Preserve both the initial reason and the reason for the revision. Do not jump from famous team names to compatibility claims.

text: # 1833 design mandate — owner instruction, 2026-10-26

title: Binding design brief
text:
## Binding design brief

Design to be the best robot on the field: an Einstein-level primary contributor, alliance-captain or elite first-round caliber. Never propose a support-role robot as 1833's architecture. Never propose a turret. Favor relatively simple mechanisms that achieve elite effectiveness through execution, acquisition, sustained throughput, autonomous, driving, controls, reliability, serviceability and extensive optimization. These are explicit user constraints, not conclusions inferred from EPA or a generic small-team stereotype. Only a later explicit user instruction can change them. Do not repeatedly ask to relax them.

Primary contribution is an objective to substantiate, not a guarantee of a future result or an instruction to do every available task. Rank functions by contribution to winning and eliminate low-value complexity. A dominant scorer can play defense or a complementary assignment in a particular match; that does not turn its architecture into a deliberately limited third robot. Preserve historical specialist examples, including 2025 parallel L1/algae assignments, as knowledge about alliance optimization. They are not authorization to cap 1833's own architecture at a support role.

For this profile, turret means a dedicated azimuth/yaw aiming assembly for the scoring mechanism. A chassis-aimed launcher can still have an adjustable hood, elevation pivot or other game-required motion if justified. Explain the cost of chassis aiming, angular acceleration, shot readiness, defender interaction and positioning. Do not disguise a turret under a different name, or delete useful historical turret research: its intake, feed, sensors and failure histories may still be transferable.

The 2027 game is unknown in this analysis. Do not prescribe a 2026 drum, a 2024 low chassis or any historical geometry before reading its rules and strategic constraints. Transfer the optimization approach, not an unexamined shape. A game requiring vertical reach may justify an elevator even though a short chassis worked in another game.

The owner reports that 1833 peaked at eighth worldwide EPA in 2026, was around 35th at this instruction, and was top 75 worldwide during 2025.
