title: Alliance selection and design ceiling
text:
## Alliance selection and design ceiling

The owner's warning is that an excellent narrow specialist may survive the first selection round and become the first available second-round pick of alliance 8, instead of joining a leading alliance. The 2026 official manual section 10.6.1 confirms first-round order 1→8 and second-round order 8→1; section 13.2 adds Worlds' third round 1→8 and four-team rosters with three starters. This is an incentive to build an independently valuable leading robot, not a deterministic theorem about draft outcomes. Captains, first picks, scouting judgments, availability, declines, autonomous compatibility and game-specific marginal value affect actual choices; a first-round pick list is not necessarily EPA order. Check the next season's rules rather than assuming the format persists.

Do not optimize 1833 merely to be the best remaining specialist. Analyze qualification ranking power, individual offensive production, autonomous ownership of contested resources, contribution with ordinary partners, and ceiling alongside elite partners. Report why the design would plausibly be attractive as a captain or first-round partner. Do not invent a numerical probability of an Einstein appearance or draft position.

title: Simplicity means removing costs while retaining output
text:
## Simplicity means removing costs while retaining output

Compare mechanisms by actuators, coupled states, interfaces, tolerance sensitivity, manufacturing burden, software commissioning, driver demands, service operations and development time—not silhouette or motor count alone. A simple-looking elevator can hide elaborate alignment, handoff, vacuum or trajectory control. Reduced moving inertia, reliable acquisition and short dead time can produce elite output without decorative complexity. Conversely, a necessary capability must not be omitted merely to make the robot look simple.

The specific exemplars and their limits are researched in `docs/1833_OPTIMIZATION_REFERENCES.md`. 7769's jam remedy is evidence that stronger feed is not automatically better; its rack failures prohibit treating its entire mechanism as perfected. Orbit's compact 2024 robot combined low packaging with substantial controls and refinement. OP 2025 used familiar high-level functions but considerable integration. Orbit 2025 used a differential transmission and vacuum system with real maintenance and control costs. The owner's comparison of 1261 with Orbit is an attributed diagnostic lead, not a verified causal account of another team's failures.

title: Architecture decision review and task quality protocol
text:
# Architecture decision review and task quality protocol

This protocol addresses the DunkTank output reviewed on 2026-10-26. The historical artifact earned 68/100 under the recorded rubric; that is a reviewer assessment, not a model benchmark. The new 1833 constraints also make its support-only baseline unacceptable as a current recommendation. Do not change its original score retroactively or present an untested replacement design as a demonstrated improvement.

source_locator.section: Architecture decision review and task quality protocol

title: 1. Establish functional priorities before choosing a role or mechanism
text:
## 1. Establish functional priorities before choosing a role or mechanism

Start with rule-derived actions and constraints, including autonomous, primary scoring, enabling resource flow, endgame and denial. Record phase and game-state effects before specializing an architecture. Identify what would make 1833 the strongest primary contributor. Map the objective into measurable useful outcomes; do not fill the task sheet with priorities that merely restate a preselected specialist role. Keep outcome tasks, implementation concepts, compliance constraints and alliance-wide results distinct. Extra rows are not evidence of comprehensive understanding. Retain one sheet; use labeled rows or a hierarchy inside that sheet rather than group tabs.

Record initial neutral functional priorities and the reasons for any changes after architecture comparison. A team's assignment alongside exceptional partners is a scenario, not proof that the robot should depend on those partners for fundamental scoring. Follow the binding no-support and no-turret constraints in `docs/1833_DESIGN_DOCTRINE.md`.

source_locator.section: 1. Establish functional priorities before choosing a role or mechanism

title: 2. Model the game as state and flow
text:
## 2. Model the game as state and flow

Identify inventories, locations, capacity/weight thresholds, scoring eligibility, occupied goals, possession, reload/discharge behavior, deadlines and final evaluation conditions. Model autonomous, transition and endgame separately where the rules differ. Opening a return chute can change feasible sustained flow, but does not establish that returned pieces are accessible or instantly reusable. Include return delay, collection success, route interference and control latency. Check rule-specific settling/scoring cutoffs rather than applying an invented universal end timestamp.

For each candidate, construct a timed match/resource model under at least three named scenarios: ordinary or weak partners; strong partners; and elite defended play. The same partner capabilities, field rules, opponent assumptions and external supply must apply to every candidate within a scenario. Show acquisition, travel, alignment, release, recovery and waiting separately, and document which operations overlap. Use measured or sourced values when available; otherwise use explicitly labeled plausible ranges and sensitivity analysis. Unknown inputs cannot silently become optimistic constants. Do not add overlapping time costs twice or count the same enabled alliance points as multiple robots' individual output.

Calculate whole-alliance output and compare the counterfactual replacement: same partners, different 1833 architecture. Report direct contribution, enabled contribution, denied contribution and opportunity cost separately, with interactions explained. A shared multiplier can help the opponent. A hostile reset may enable them to score again. Evaluate per-goal final-state recovery instead of a binary full-refill test. A maximum possible score or denial is not an expected match result.

source_locator.section: 2. Model the game as state and flow

title: 3. Compare capacity and deployment choices explicitly
text:
## 3. Compare capacity and deployment choices explicitly

A field threshold is not automatically an onboard capacity requirement. Compare at least three plausible capacities or storage arrangements spanning the proposed choice. For a 100-piece cumulative threshold, 50/75/100/150 are illustrative candidates, not prescribed targets. Consider existing target inventory, multiple deliveries, collection delay, cross-field distance, throughput, spill, usable packing and loaded maneuverability. Compare fixed versus expanding storage before adding expansion. Record what packing fraction means and reserve volume for conveyors, structure, supports, electronics, moving swept volume and trapped pieces.

Use deliverable capacity under stated motion and wear conditions. If delivery efficiency is eta, capacity C and residual r, account for losses without double-counting them; a simplified effective delivery estimate C*eta-r must state its assumptions. A 100-count load with 98% retention cannot guarantee 100 delivered. If the field threshold is measured by weight, piece counts are a proxy requiring tolerance and calibration rather than a certified exact trigger. Inventory sensing and target-state sensing are distinct problems.

source_locator.section: 3. Compare capacity and deployment choices explicitly

title: 4. Select between credible complete candidates
text:
## 4. Select between credible complete candidates

Compare at least two viable non-turret primary-contributor architectures. Do not use an intentionally weak alternative to justify a preferred concept. Compare mission output, controllability, defended performance, autonomous, loaded dynamics, resources, complexity and development time using common assumptions. A high-level sketch or bounded layout is sufficient at this stage; exact fabrication drawings and invented motor ratios are not required.

Establish the physical envelope: legal start/deployed dimensions, ground transition, storage volume, lift to outlet, entry aperture, collision/swept volumes, electrical access and loaded CG. Label dimensions measured from governing CAD separately from provisional allocations. Resolve cheap geometry questions before a large prototype. Identify which values could reverse the choice, show those sensitivities, and define fallback milestones.

An original mechanism is allowed without a famous reference. Its essential interfaces still need a causal explanation and a test. For borrowed mechanisms verify year/team/version, game-piece diameter/material/deformability and competition hardware legality. The 2022 Rapid React cargo diameter is 9.5 inches, not 7 inches. Never transfer compression, traction or roller speed merely because both objects are called balls. Keep representative source images and locators available to the next reviewer; claim visual review only when actually performed.

title: 5. Make the task workbook substantive
text:
## 5. Make the task workbook substantive

Every occupied row must carry a task-specific dependency and rationale. Identify actual predecessor tasks or external conditions, relevant mechanism interfaces, and effects of failure. Repeated generic statements about coordination or unverified CAD do not satisfy this requirement. Explain difficulty using a consistent basis such as interfaces, maturity, tolerance, manufacturing and commissioning. Do not pretend the Fibonacci scale is a calibrated numeric effort estimate. Distinguish no relevant task (N/A) from a real task excluded from the robot.

Column K contains an authoritative acceptance requirement or a clearly unresolved target. Column M identifies the unknown, the test that resolves it, and the decision it changes; merely copying K after an introductory sentence is insufficient. Distinguish screening targets from release criteria explicitly. Preserve row/requirement IDs in the design record so cross-row conflicts can be reconciled. If one row allows two residual balls and another requires a guaranteed 100-ball delivery from a 100-ball load, label the former as intermediate screening and prevent release until the system target is met.

Keep agent recommendations and human decisions separate. Check summary formulas, caches, validations and occupied-row coverage. Run `python scripts/audit_task_workbook.py PATH.xlsx`; its duplicate-field warnings require human review, not automatic deletion of legitimately shared dependencies. It cannot validate physics or infer the semantic consistency of every target.

title: 6. Test only where the value justifies the iteration cost
text:
## 6. Test only where the value justifies the iteration cost

First verify rules and field apertures, then use inexpensive envelope and analytical checks. Only where consequential uncertainty remains, test the cheapest capacity/transition or one-lane geometry that can change the choice. Then prototype representative loaded flow, sensing and reversal; integrate at full capacity when the smaller tests support it. Complete defended/dynamic trials and practice validation before calling the system competition-ready. State hypothesis, conditions, sample size, measured quantities, screening/release target, and decision consequence for each test. A proposed 20/20 result is an acceptance target, not measured evidence or a statistical reliability guarantee.

title: 7. Deliver and preserve the decision
text:
## 7. Deliver and preserve the decision

Deliver the populated single-sheet workbook; one selected architecture and the complete alternatives comparison; quantitative scenario/capacity results with input provenance; physical envelope; exact reference locators/images; and prioritized open tests. Maintain assumptions, decisions, rejected alternatives, user corrections and test results in a dated design record. Fill `examples/design_review_skeleton.json` as a machine-readable summary and run `python scripts/validate_design_review.py FILE.json`. Apply `agent/design_rubric.json` with evidence for each score. The no-support and no-turret gates take precedence over a high numeric score. Validation is structural; a human must judge whether inputs and conclusions are credible.

## Solo ranking capability and proportional evidence

For a new architecture, explicitly map each ranking objective to independent capability or external prerequisites and quantify the individually achievable route with margin. Include a passive-partner stress case in addition to ordinary/elite alliance comparisons. Complete the solo RP record and validation economics; the latter must identify decision consequences, expected costs, cheapest evidence and stopping rules. A bounded improvement can use a short comparison and update only affected task rows, rather than repeating full CAD or model development. title: 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history
text:
## 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history

Primary facts: the release describes a two-chamber shooter revised to a 2.75-width configuration, almost 70 nominal capacity and typically 50–60 in play. Team replies describe a static hood avoiding an exposed hood belt, and a feed jam corrected by stopping the lower indexing rollers. They also report rack-tooth breakage that persisted despite current-limit mitigation, with spares and repairs needed. Their linked technical slides currently display that the file was deleted. Those slides were not read. The retained mirror snapshot ranks 7769 fourth worldwide at EPA 309.29; it is a dated snapshot, not live verification. Official event results support an elite competitive season.

1833 transfer analysis: the useful principle is that usable match throughput is a system property. More capacity can add loaded inertia, acquisition dwell and feed pressure. More powered contact can make a congested path worse. Begin with a clear hypothesis about the limiting stage, instrument occupancy and delay at each transition, and change one stage before attributing a scoring gain. Test the near-empty, partly full and fully packed states separately. Under a defended shot, distinguish lost aim time, inaccessible geometry, supply starvation and a genuine mechanical jam. A simple hood can reduce interfaces and service work, but its advantages depend on the scoring aperture and collision environment of the new game.

The rack failure is an equally important lesson. Do not label every CHUNK component an optimized design merely because the robot performed exceptionally. Borrow the output discipline and diagnose its failure modes; do not recreate a known weak load path without a correction hypothesis and impact test. Preserve version labels so an early divided shooter and later wider arrangement are not combined into an imaginary single fielded version. The owner's desire to emulate 7769 means elite execution of a coherent primary scorer, not a requirement for a particular hopper size, rack intake or lane count in 2027.

title: 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development
text:
## 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development

Primary facts: the reveal gives an approximately 11-inch highest stowed point. Official results identify Orbit as a 2024 world champion. The mechanism is chassis-yaw aimed; its elevation/pivot motion is not a turret. In the CAD release, a team member warns that low packaging did not make every individual mechanism superior and that substantial work was needed. The team's controls explanation describes physically limited motion commands, skid/collision handling, driver assistance and automated shot readiness. Treat this as a team account rather than an independent performance decomposition.

1833 transfer analysis: low CG can increase usable acceleration and reduce settling, but free speed or stowed height alone cannot predict cycles. Compare time to accelerate, brake, reacquire heading, capture a piece and release a valid shot under contact. The cost of chassis aiming must be included in a non-turret architecture's state model. It may be small when acquisition exits with a useful heading and the driver can approach efficiently; it may be large when position and heading are constrained together. Geometry and software must be co-designed so that the driver requests remain physically feasible.

This example validates ambition with a compact architecture. It does not justify eliminating a necessary game function, assuming development is easy, or concluding that the lowest robot always wins. A low package that creates rare disabling piece poses may lose more match contribution than it gains in an ideal cycle. Preserve the existing note-deflector study as a reliability problem alongside the positive architecture example. The future design should carry an explicit optimization budget: time for loaded tuning, autonomous coordination, repeated defended acquisition, operator feedback and service drills. Hardware simplicity buys development capacity only if the saved effort is actually invested in those areas.

title: 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces
text:
## 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces

Primary facts: OP describes choosing architecture early and selecting the simplest concept it thought could meet competitive goals, while noting that the robot was more demanding than desired and lacked a hanger at its first event. Its 33-page binder documents a ground intake, separate coral straightening/handoff stages, elevator, gripper and climb, with explicit sensing, service and stiffness details. Software and fabrication are documented as part of the robot, not omitted from the complexity account. The existing corpus already contains five technical notes from this binder. In this pass all 33 pages' extracted text was read; that does not certify every drawing visually. The source publication requests that its original documents not be rehosted; this edition links them and retains authored research notes rather than adding the source PDF.

1833 transfer analysis: a concept can be stated as an intake, elevator and wrist without being an easy robot to commission. The high-level simplicity resides in a short functional chain with clear ownership of each transformation, not in pretending that orientation, capture or controls are trivial. Decompose a coral cycle into acquisition, orientation, handoff, clearance, elevation, approach, release and retreat. Observe which stages can overlap without compromising retained state. An indexed piece that arrives consistently can save both actuator travel and repeated driver correction.

The relevant design comparison is not vacuum versus rollers in isolation. It is whether the complete capture-to-release system tolerates the expected piece poses and contacts while achieving repeatable short cycles. Evaluate a simpler effector's potential benefit against the additional upstream alignment it demands. A more constrained handoff may reduce end-effector burden but increase throat-jam sensitivity. Deliberately choose where the tolerance belongs and measure success across that interface. Similarly, service access and wiring restraint are output-preserving design functions; a nominally faster mechanism that repeatedly loses sensors or requires lengthy disassembly can have lower event contribution.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550?page=2 (post 29 and controls discussion); https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf (physical pp 5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25,28); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550 (post 28). Exact construction remains in the five existing technical notes and primary publication.

title: 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution
text:
## 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution

Primary facts: Orbit credits a closed-belt differential elevator reference and describes floor pickup as a cycle-time choice. Team posts identify pressure feedback and maintenance of an adhesive belt connection. Its championship recap discusses alliance interference and switching a partner to predictable loading-station lanes. A later intake-assist post explains driver-intent conditions and velocity correction. These accounts establish that optimization includes control and traffic management, not only a short mechanism list. They do not show that a differential or vacuum is universally simpler for another team.

1833 transfer analysis: separating moving hardware from actuator location can reduce inertia while creating motor-space coupling and calibration work. A differential should be assessed over simultaneous lift/pivot demands, saturation and failure recovery rather than judged by the number of motors saved. A vacuum can make a gripper visually small while moving complexity into sealing, pressure generation, state sensing and maintenance. Those are valid choices if they improve the whole cycle under the team's resources; they are not free complexity elimination.

For match modeling, faster individual floor pickup does not necessarily produce faster alliance throughput if robots fight over the same accessible pieces or routes. Compare shared supply and traffic policies explicitly. A robot designed to dominate can adopt a lane or temporary complementary assignment without having been designed as a weak support machine. The historical alliance discussion is therefore useful to 1833's elite ceiling even though support-only architecture is prohibited. Reserve time to test driver assistance at speed with realistic errors; a theoretically optimal command that surprises the driver may degrade acquisition. Observe driver workload and repeatability as well as mechanism motion time.

title: Apply the lessons without assuming the 2027 game
text:
## Apply the lessons without assuming the 2027 game

Begin with the strongest primary-contributor objectives permitted by the new game. Compare a small number of coherent no-turret architectures. Prefer deleting a mechanism or powered interface when the same useful function can be achieved with fewer failure modes, but preserve a necessary capability even when it requires engineering. Invest saved complexity in sustained output, autonomous, acquisition quality, driver assistance, service readiness and iteration. Set measurable optimization experiments and retain the failures as prominently as the successes. Neither a simple concept nor a famous reference establishes performance until its interfaces and operating conditions have been evaluated.

title: DunkTank agent output review and regression case
text:
# DunkTank agent output review and regression case

The corrected assignment is 2024 WCP CADathon DunkTank. The earlier Hero Heist prompt attribution was corrected by the user, so it incurs no deduction. Reviewed artifacts: the user's supplied one-sheet task workbook and detailed design recommendation. Preserve their original state; this review is not a revised design or evidence of an implemented prototype.

The recorded review score is 68/100: assignment/context 9/10; rules/math 10/12; strategic model 8/14; task decomposition 7/10; workbook substance 7/10; reference quality 7/10; architecture 8/12; alternatives 2/8; tests 4/6; usefulness 6/8. This is an evidence-anchored reviewer judgment with ordinal partial credit, not a calibrated accuracy measurement. The subsequently supplied 1833 doctrine rejects a support-only architecture independently of that historical score.

Verified strengths: 58 tasks on one sheet; 43 Must do, 7 Might do, 8 Won't do; summary caches and priority-times-difficulty calculations match; no cached Excel error cells; final human decisions pending. Core stack math gives 48 ordinary basketball points, 60 possible final stack bonuses, a 31-point successful preload-plus-exit routine and 33 1/3 points for 100 successful endgame electrolyte scores. The packing calculation gives about 6.31 cubic feet at an assumed 60% fraction before mechanism intrusion. Those batch ceilings are not a match model. The output recognizes useful versus harmful clears, shared bonuses, ball return delay and intake-to-outlet integration.

Failure 1 — specialist selected before marginal comparison: two capable basketball partners are assumed, but no same-partner timed comparison establishes whether an electrolyte-only robot beats a mixed or basketball-capable candidate. Repair: model direct, enabled and denied output and a counterfactual replacement, including weak/ordinary and elite defended scenarios. For 1833, a support-only candidate is disallowed by the new owner instruction.

Failure 2 — threshold converted into capacity: row 25 makes 100 delivered onboard balls essential because the tank clears at a cumulative 100. Multiple smaller deliveries and existing tank inventory are not compared. Repair: evaluate capacities and fixed/expanding storage with travel, collection, mass/volume, losses and actual useful resets. Do not assert that a smaller design is necessarily better either.

Failure 3 — full refill used as denial proxy: final bonuses are evaluated per stack. An opponent that cannot refill all three can still restore one or two. Repair: model per-stack recovery, prerequisite dependencies, time left, and the attacker's lost scoring. Maximum 60 denied points is a conditional upper bound, not expected contribution.

Failure 4 — boilerplate dependencies: 50 of 58 J cells repeat the same coordination/route/timing sentence; the other eight repeat an exclusion sentence. Difficulty explanations similarly repeat that a number is provisional. Repair: require task-specific predecessor/interface/failure conditions and difficulty drivers. Task count and nonblank cells alone earn no substantive-quality credit.

Failure 5 — contradictory acceptance targets: row 25 requires at least 100 delivered; row 28 initially permits two residuals; row 56 requires 98% retention. Row 13 specifies 20/20 combined auto exits/discharges whereas rows 21/39 specify 18/20. Repair: define authoritative system release targets, screening stages, loss margins and test conditions, with traceable requirement IDs. Do not quietly label inconsistent targets equivalent.

Failure 6 — historical piece-size error: the recommendation describes 254's 2022 reference as 7-inch cargo. The official 2022 manual section 5.7 specifies 9.5-inch fuzzy inflated cargo. Repair: verify year-specific diameter, material and compliance before importing intake compression or contact speeds. The primary/secondary roller arrangement is supported by 254's binder; preserve the valid principle while correcting the dimensional statement.

Failure 7 — deferred physical feasibility and optimization: routes, field opening, packaging and resources are acknowledged unknown, but the output still selects capacity and expansion. Endgame/auto open-chute flow deserves investigation without assuming a physically accessible instant recycling loop. Repair: cheap aperture and envelope checks, state/flow model, capacity trade study, then integrated loaded tests. No complete new DunkTank recommendation is certified by adding this protocol.

Evidence locators: original workbook rows 13,21,25,28,32,39,56 and column J; detailed recommendation sections on hopper, compared alternative and first tests. Original uploaded attachments remain with the user and are not silently rewritten. Scoring criteria are in `agent/design_rubric.json`.

title: 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history
text:
## 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history

Primary facts: the release describes a two-chamber shooter revised to a 2.75-width configuration, almost 70 nominal capacity and typically 50–60 in play. Team replies describe a static hood avoiding an exposed hood belt, and a feed jam corrected by stopping the lower indexing rollers. They also report rack-tooth breakage that persisted despite current-limit mitigation, with spares and repairs needed. Their linked technical slides currently display that the file was deleted. Those slides were not read. The retained mirror snapshot ranks 7769 fourth worldwide at EPA 309.29; it is a dated snapshot, not live verification. Official event results support an elite competitive season.

1833 transfer analysis: the useful principle is that usable match throughput is a system property. More capacity can add loaded inertia, acquisition dwell and feed pressure. More powered contact can make a congested path worse. Begin with a clear hypothesis about the limiting stage, instrument occupancy and delay at each transition, and change one stage before attributing a scoring gain. Test the near-empty, partly full and fully packed states separately. Under a defended shot, distinguish lost aim time, inaccessible geometry, supply starvation and a genuine mechanical jam. A simple hood can reduce interfaces and service work, but its advantages depend on the scoring aperture and collision environment of the new game.

The rack failure is an equally important lesson. Do not label every CHUNK component an optimized design merely because the robot performed exceptionally. Borrow the output discipline and diagnose its failure modes; do not recreate a known weak load path without a correction hypothesis and impact test. Preserve version labels so an early divided shooter and later wider arrangement are not combined into an imaginary single fielded version. The owner's desire to emulate 7769 means elite execution of a coherent primary scorer, not a requirement for a particular hopper size, rack intake or lane count in 2027.

text:
## 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development

Primary facts: the reveal gives an approximately 11-inch highest stowed point. Official results identify Orbit as a 2024 world champion. The mechanism is chassis-yaw aimed; its elevation/pivot motion is not a turret. In the CAD release, a team member warns that low packaging did not make every individual mechanism superior and that substantial work was needed. The team's controls explanation describes physically limited motion commands, skid/collision handling, driver assistance and automated shot readiness. Treat this as a team account rather than an independent performance decomposition.

1833 transfer analysis: low CG can increase usable acceleration and reduce settling, but free speed or stowed height alone cannot predict cycles. Compare time to accelerate, brake, reacquire heading, capture a piece and release a valid shot under contact. The cost of chassis aiming must be included in a non-turret architecture's state model. It may be small when acquisition exits with a useful heading and the driver can approach efficiently; it may be large when position and heading are constrained together. Geometry and software must be co-designed so that the driver requests remain physically feasible.

This example validates ambition with a compact architecture. It does not justify eliminating a necessary game function, assuming development is easy, or concluding that the lowest robot always wins. A low package that creates rare disabling piece poses may lose more match contribution than it gains in an ideal cycle. Preserve the existing note-deflector study as a reliability problem alongside the positive architecture example. The future design should carry an explicit optimization budget: time for loaded tuning, autonomous coordination, repeated defended acquisition, operator feedback and service drills. Hardware simplicity buys development capacity only if the saved effort is actually invested in those areas.

title: 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces
text:
## 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces

Primary facts: OP describes choosing architecture early and selecting the simplest concept it thought could meet competitive goals, while noting that the robot was more demanding than desired and lacked a hanger at its first event. Its 33-page binder documents a ground intake, separate coral straightening/handoff stages, elevator, gripper and climb, with explicit sensing, service and stiffness details. Software and fabrication are documented as part of the robot, not omitted from the complexity account. The existing corpus already contains five technical notes from this binder. In this pass all 33 pages' extracted text was read; that does not certify every drawing visually. The source publication requests that its original documents not be rehosted; this edition links them and retains authored research notes rather than adding the source PDF.

1833 transfer analysis: a concept can be stated as an intake, elevator and wrist without being an easy robot to commission. The high-level simplicity resides in a short functional chain with clear ownership of each transformation, not in pretending that orientation, capture or controls are trivial. Decompose a coral cycle into acquisition, orientation, handoff, clearance, elevation, approach, release and retreat. Observe which stages can overlap without compromising retained state. An indexed piece that arrives consistently can save both actuator travel and repeated driver correction.

The relevant design comparison is not vacuum versus rollers in isolation. It is whether the complete capture-to-release system tolerates the expected piece poses and contacts while achieving repeatable short cycles. Evaluate a simpler effector's potential benefit against the additional upstream alignment it demands. A more constrained handoff may reduce end-effector burden but increase throat-jam sensitivity. Deliberately choose where the tolerance belongs and measure success across that interface. Similarly, service access and wiring restraint are output-preserving design functions; a nominally faster mechanism that repeatedly loses sensors or requires lengthy disassembly can have lower event contribution.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550?page=2 (post 29 and controls discussion); https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf (physical pp 5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25,28); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550 (post 28). title: 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution
text:
## 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution

Primary facts: Orbit credits a closed-belt differential elevator reference and describes floor pickup as a cycle-time choice. Team posts identify pressure feedback and maintenance of an adhesive belt connection. Its championship recap discusses alliance interference and switching a partner to predictable loading-station lanes. A later intake-assist post explains driver-intent conditions and velocity correction. These accounts establish that optimization includes control and traffic management, not only a short mechanism list. They do not show that a differential or vacuum is universally simpler for another team.

1833 transfer analysis: separating moving hardware from actuator location can reduce inertia while creating motor-space coupling and calibration work. A differential should be assessed over simultaneous lift/pivot demands, saturation and failure recovery rather than judged by the number of motors saved. A vacuum can make a gripper visually small while moving complexity into sealing, pressure generation, state sensing and maintenance. Those are valid choices if they improve the whole cycle under the team's resources; they are not free complexity elimination.

For match modeling, faster individual floor pickup does not necessarily produce faster alliance throughput if robots fight over the same accessible pieces or routes. Compare shared supply and traffic policies explicitly. A robot designed to dominate can adopt a lane or temporary complementary assignment without having been designed as a weak support machine. The historical alliance discussion is therefore useful to 1833's elite ceiling even though support-only architecture is prohibited. Reserve time to test driver assistance at speed with realistic errors; a theoretically optimal command that surprises the driver may degrade acquisition. Observe driver workload and repeatability as well as mechanism motion time.

title: Owner's four-lane example: preserve the actual chronology
text:
## Owner's four-lane example: preserve the actual chronology

The owner reports that 1833 did not finish fully CADding its two-lane shooter before changing to four. The team recognized that four lanes fit on the frame and adopted that opportunity. The stated decision chain was more lanes → more BPS → more throughput → more fuel scored → more ranking points → less dependence on partners → stronger seeding → more control over playoff alliance formation. This is an owner-reported packaging-led architecture decision, not a completed two-lane robot followed by a measured two-to-four-lane prototype campaign. No before/after test data, exact BPS multiplier or dimensions were supplied. Do not invent them or imply that the team wasted a finished build.

The transferable reasoning is to find inexpensive ways to raise the ceiling of the core scoring task early. If available space and a shared architecture allow more parallel scoring lanes at acceptable added cost, assess the clear gain promptly and make the decision before spending effort detailing the inferior package. An agent should recognize that opportunity, not require the team to fabricate both designs or finish both CAD assemblies to justify it.

Check the few interfaces that can invalidate the gain: available feed across the width, launch energy and electrical headroom, acquisition and inventory, shot validity/accuracy, physical clearance and added mass. This is targeted engineering reasoning, not an excuse to stall an evident improvement with a sprawling research program. Four lanes need not mean exactly twice sustained match output: the owner's qualitative decision chain is preserved while unmeasured multipliers remain unknown. Translate the available parallel capacity into the RP-relevant outcome under explicitly stated assumptions.

title: First priority: ranking objectives 1833 can achieve independently
text:
## First priority: ranking objectives 1833 can achieve independently

Design essential scoring and prerequisite capability so 1833 can pursue the most valuable independently achievable ranking bonuses without another robot completing required actions. Never make 'two capable partners will handle it' the justification for omitting a core prerequisite. Evaluate the robot's individual acquisition, autonomous and sustained scoring ceiling before relying on ideal alliance synergy. This reinforces the no-support-only architecture rule; it does not require every available mechanism or allow a turret.

For every ranking objective in the actual manual, record the exact conditions and classify it as: independently achievable; own contribution only with an explicit external prerequisite; or inherently dependent on another team/opponent. State which actions the robot owns, which are external, and whether the remaining dependency is controllable. A cooperation condition requiring an opposing alliance action cannot honestly be called solo-achievable. Win/tie RP also depends on relative alliance/opponent output; distinguish independently satisfiable bonus conditions from a claim of guaranteed match victory.

Map each solo-achievable objective into required auto contribution, teleop contribution, sustained valid throughput, time/supply assumptions and reliability margin. State attainable limits and shortfall explicitly. Use the actual rule thresholds and phase multipliers; do not copy 2026 thresholds into 2027 or invent unavailable game information. When thresholds permit different routes, compare the simplest route that preserves elite primary contribution. Once a threshold is secure, assess additional output for wins, tiebreakers and playoff ceiling rather than accumulating irrelevant features.

Compare candidates with two passive or weak partners for their independent bonus capability and direct output. Also analyze ordinary and elite partners for ranking/win potential and playoff interactions. The passive-partner stress case is an engineering diagnostic, not a literal claim that every alliance partner will contribute nothing. Do not double count partner output as 1833's ability. Report both threshold capability and confidence/range under defended, disrupted and late-match conditions.

The objective is strong ranking performance that gives the team more control over alliance selection, alongside an elite playoff robot. Seeding first and choosing preferred partners remain goals, not guarantees: opponent strength, RP rules, tiebreakers, scheduling, failures and draft availability also matter. Do not use those uncertainties to lower the stated ambition or recommend dependence on a specialist partner.

title: Spend validation effort where it can change the choice
text:
## Spend validation effort where it can change the choice

Use the cheapest adequate evidence in this order where applicable: governing rules and existing source data; rough frame/envelope layout and interference checks; simple rate, energy, cycle and volume bounds; existing mechanisms or representative interface tests; a narrowly scoped prototype; then integrated loaded validation when required before operation. This is a menu scaled to the uncertainty, not a command to perform every stage or endlessly iterate. Prototype evidence can be essential when friction, piece deformation or stochastic flow cannot be bounded adequately. Do not label a calculation a performed experiment, or ship an untested reliability claim.

For each proposed test, identify: the uncertainty, the competing decisions it can separate, the result that would change the choice, estimated money/CAD/fabrication/person-hours and schedule cost, cheapest available substitute, and a stopping rule. If all plausible outcomes lead to the same choice, explain why the test is not worth doing for architecture selection. Commissioning or required safety/legality checks may still be necessary for operating hardware; distinguish that purpose from open-ended design exploration. Unknown costs must be labeled rather than invented.

For a major architecture choice, retain the comparison and game model required by the design-review protocol. For a bounded improvement such as recognizing additional lane space, a short decision note with the old/new package, marginal cost, decisive interface checks and RP/throughput consequence can suffice. Do not demand full competing CAD models, fabricated designs or a large simulation to re-prove unchanged parts of the robot. Update affected task rows and targets instead of rebuilding the entire analysis by rote. Report when more evidence is truly necessary and why.

Simplicity means the least implementation burden that meets the ambitious objective, not the least hardware regardless of performance. A modest addition that substantially increases core throughput or secures an independently achievable RP may be an excellent simplification of the overall competitive problem. Conversely, adding mechanisms that do not improve ranking independence, expected wins or elite playoff output needs a strong opportunity-cost justification.

title: 1833 actuation and historical research scope
text:
# 1833 actuation and historical research scope

Owner instruction, 2026-10-26. Never recommend pneumatics for an 1833 robot. Treat this as a binding team choice rather than asserting that pneumatic technology is universally obsolete. Prefer an electrically actuated mechanism or a justified passive alternative. Historical references may contain compressors, reservoirs, valves and air cylinders; retain source accuracy and extract useful geometry, then explicitly explain how the proposed non-pneumatic actuation changes loads, holding, packaging, release, recovery and controls. Do not silently copy a pneumatic actuator, assume electric replacement is mechanically identical, or rename a pressure-powered mechanism to bypass the constraint. An electrically powered vacuum mechanism is a separate historical pressure-system example, not automatic permission to introduce pneumatic actuation; flag the actuation interpretation explicitly and use a non-pneumatic baseline.

Current historical coverage, 2026-10-27: the authorized 2018/2019 expansion is now represented by two game chapters and thirteen curated primary-source robot-year studies. Read HISTORICAL_2018_2019_TRANSFER.md and data/historical_2018_2019_audit.json from corpus root. This is a substantial selected-source expansion, not a top-25-per-year ranking cohort or exhaustive version certification. Consider 2015 mechanisms selectively when they offer useful transfer beyond existing records. Exclude 2016 as a source of proposed mechanism inspiration, and do not recommend mechanism references older than 2015. The owner's negative appraisal of the 2016 game is a design-research preference, not a factual claim that the event did not exist.

Deprioritize bulk 2017 intake/storage/shooter research where its transfer lessons substantially overlap with the 2026 corpus. Preserve the owner's view that many designs are scaled or repackaged equivalents as an attributed transfer hypothesis, not a universal proven statement about every robot. Study 2017 only when there is a distinctive useful lesson; do not import capacities, ball properties or rates between years without checking them.

title: Low-profile sprint chassis and gearbox
text:
## Low-profile sprint chassis and gearbox

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [10, 11].

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The binder specifies a six-wheel West Coast layout with center drop, two nitrile traction wheels and four omnis. A flat three-MiniCIM gearbox arrangement lowers the package beneath the intake. The middle pinion receives an additional bearing plate rather than remaining unsupported against the other motors. Two drive ratios are published, along with wheel sizes and nominal speeds.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

The team lists short-sprint acceleration, maneuverability, platform clearance and resisting defense as design goals, while a wide wheelbase accommodates a raised load and a partner.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The valuable feature is integration: lowering the gearbox also lowers the intake rest position, which changes acquisition geometry. Moving the pickup upward to clear motors would impose a new lifting/rolling transition on every cube. Omnis can reduce scrub while traction placement still matters for pushing and ramp contact. A new chassis must evaluate the actual support polygon and loaded CG, not copy the wheel count as a performance recipe. Reported high-gear free speed does not establish defended acceleration or stopping distance.

text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

First check intake rest height and field-obstacle breakover in a section view. Then calculate traction/current-limited acceleration and the raised-load tipping boundary; test only the uncertain transition if it can change the layout.

title: Compliant jaws and reversible wrist scoring
text:
## Compliant jaws and reversible wrist scoring

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [14].

source_locator.section: Compliant jaws and reversible wrist scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Opposed wheel groups sit on polycarbonate jaw plates. The binder reports two 775pro intake motors with 5:1 reduction and four sets of 2-inch compliant wheels per side. The wrist has a separate motor, chain reduction, adjustable tensioner, angle encoder and zeroing switch. The stated roller surface speed is approximately 32 ft/s.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Acquire either the 13-inch or 11-inch cube presentation quickly, center it with little driver precision, clamp securely during wrist motion, and score from either side.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The pickup combines tolerance at the contact with control of the retained pose. Wheel compliance accommodates the covered crate while the wrist removes a drivebase reversal. A new piece can have a different friction/elasticity regime: 32 ft/s is not a universal optimum. More surface speed can add bounce or surface damage without reducing approach time. Separate capture authority from holding authority and from the wrist trajectory. The retained piece, jaw opening and lift pass-through must clear at the same time.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Compare a swept volume of the largest allowed piece in skewed poses against the uprights and bumper. If contact uncertainty remains, use one adjustable jaw fixture and measure capture, retained pose and release rather than build competing complete robots.

text:
### Limits

title: Continuous lift rigging and partner-load structure
text:
## Continuous lift rigging and partner-load structure

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [12, 13].

source_locator.section: Continuous lift rigging and partner-load structure

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Pull-up and pull-down Dyneema cable runs act on both sides of the elevator. Spring tensioning addresses changing fleet angle. The binder specifies a 15-inch separation between pull-up runs for cube passage. The elevator gearbox has four 775pros and two ratios; the low ratio serves climbing and the high ratio serves scoring. Bearings react on different tube faces and edges to support moments.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Allow cube passage, rapid full-height travel, and the torsional loads associated with lifting two robots, while keeping the intake low when stowed.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Continuous rigging, stage mass and counterforce determine which mass the motor lifts at each segment. The two-sided arrangement can reduce racking only if stiffness, alignment and tension remain adequate. A spring tensioner is not a generic cure for incorrect spool tracking, excessive stretch or sharp cable edges. The published travel and climb timings are design goals/source claims, not measurements reproduced here. For an electric-only adaptation, fixed gearing or electric shifting must still deliver a credible scoring/climbing torque-speed envelope.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Derive lift kinematics and force through every travel segment. Check overlap, tube-face contact stress, shaft moments, cable bending radius and tension access; evaluate score and climb loads separately before selecting gearing.

text:
## Hook, forklift and aligned two-robot lift

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [15, 16].

source_locator.section: Hook, forklift and aligned two-robot lift

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A hook pivots from a retained spring-loaded state to a hard stop. Deployable forks support a partner while the elevator/hanger arrangement raises the pair. The binder discusses keeping the combined CG under the bar and allowing a cube through the fork spacing. Cylinders retain or deploy historical components; they are not permitted actuation for a new 1833 recommendation.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Lift a broad range of partners quickly, preserve ordinary scoring passage, and react partner loads without rotating the pair away from the support.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The partner interface is a structural mechanism, not just two pieces of carbon tube. The load travels from partner underside/bumpers through forks, their pivots and tensile reactions into the elevator/chassis. Docking clearance and partner drive geometry determine whether the “universal” aspiration holds. A no-air redesign needs a positive retained state during violent driving and a repeatable deployed stop. Merely replacing a cylinder with a motor leaves latch release, power loss, backdrive and accidental triggering unresolved.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Draw the complete force diagram and docked support geometry using a worst-case partner envelope. Separate partner approach reliability from winch capacity and test a proof load only after the structural path and safety factors are justified.

text:
### Limits

## Coordinated transitions, scale sensing and qualification independence

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [6, 7, 18, 19, 20].

source_locator.section: Coordinated transitions, scale sensing and qualification independence

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The software section describes spline trajectory generation. The binder names pure pursuit, while pinned public code defaults to nonlinear feedback. Event deployment remains unresolved, modeled feedforward and a motion planner for intake/wrist/elevator transitions. Gravity and acceleration terms support superstructure control. A driver-station webcam estimates scale angle from the colored arm. The team’s championship report describes selecting combined switch/scale auto when switch scoring by partners was uncertain.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Score early, reduce collision risk inside the superstructure, and position at the necessary scale height rather than always lifting blindly to a fixed maximum.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A game-state objective maps into several engineering requirements: reliable capture preserves the next path; scale attitude changes required height; an early autonomous lead changes the opponent’s teleop catch-up burden. The camera location and contemporary rules matter. The transferable principle is state-informed motion, not permission to reuse an old off-board sensing arrangement under a new manual. All three line crossings remain partner-dependent even when the robot owns switch scoring.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Define legal transition states and rejection/recovery behavior before coding auto sequences. Use logged target age and mechanism readiness; validate uncertain transitions rather than assume a perfect path simulation proves acquisition.

text:

title: 2018-148 — Robowranglers: Uppercut
text:
# 2018-148 — Robowranglers: Uppercut

An intentionally undersized, short robot uses a single-speed drive, lightweight cascading elevator and cube-normalizing polycarbonate intake. The elevator collapses below the scale transit height. A separate winch/hook and partner-capture roller/forks support climbing. Major assemblies are removable modules.

title: Strategic interpretation
text:
## Strategic interpretation

Uppercut’s strategic advantage is a coupled acquisition, orientation and transit package. Collapsed clearance preserves route options while a normalized cube pose helps packing. The publication’s fast lift and climb claims need their original load conditions. Its extensive prototyping resources are historical context, not a cheap-iteration prescription for 1833.

title: Undersized frame, scale transit and removable modules
text:
## Undersized frame, scale transit and removable modules

Version: Uppercut judges pamphlet snapshot. Source: https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [1, 2].

source_locator.section: Undersized frame, scale transit and removable modules

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The pamphlet describes a small frame several inches inside the permitted limits, a single-speed drive with stated 18 ft/s top speed, and enough collapsed clearance to travel under the scale regardless of tilt. Subsystems remove as modules. Electronics occupy a compact two-sided panel kept low.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Improve agility and cube cycle speed, preserve field routes and permit replacement/upgrade of assemblies through the season.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Small external dimensions can reduce swept turning area and open routes; small internal dimensions can also make service and wiring harder. The module concept succeeds only when connectors, fasteners and structural interfaces are actually accessible. The under-scale benefit is a game-specific clearance condition and should not be generalized to any new field. A single speed removes shifting hardware but must cover defended drive and transit loads with the chosen motor/wheel system.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Check actual bumper envelope, all stowed protrusions and service removal directions. Compare route time with the robot in its real low state, including the time to lower before entering the route.

title: Boot-mediated cube orientation and lightweight capture
text:
## Boot-mediated cube orientation and lightweight capture

Version: Uppercut judges pamphlet snapshot. Source: https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [6, 8].

source_locator.section: Boot-mediated cube orientation and lightweight capture

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The intake flips a captured cube over a boot into a preferred tall/narrow orientation. The team describes Lexan construction and a passive preload retainer nicknamed the drinking bird. It reports six intake revisions before bagging and explicitly connects orientation control to packing cubes on the scale/switch.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Capture cubes in varied orientations while delivering a consistent final pose and keeping the elevator payload light.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

An intake can do useful sorting and reorientation before the scoring mechanism ever moves. The important transformation is entry pose to stable exit pose. Boot geometry, piece inertia, roller contact and the backstop determine whether the cube rolls as intended or wedges. A different box with soft walls or different aspect ratio may not rotate predictably. The historical number of revisions describes what 148 did; for 1833, first reason through geometry and use a bounded contact experiment only if the pose transformation remains uncertain.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Create an entry-pose map including open fabric face, diagonal approach and partial capture. Check whether each pose converges to the desired orientation and whether a reversal can recover a jam without hand intervention.

text:

title: Cascading lift with lightweight stages
text:
## Cascading lift with lightweight stages

Version: Uppercut judges pamphlet snapshot. Source: https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [3].

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The team describes a cascading elevator with two 775pros, a chain-driven bottom stage and Dyneema-coupled upper stages. Thin-wall tubes, printed rollers and constant-force springs reduce the active lifting burden. The pamphlet reports approximately 90-inch maximum height and below-42-inch collapsed height, along with a sub-half-second lift claim.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Move a cube rapidly to scoring height while retaining low travel clearance and minimizing carried structural mass.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The collapsed-to-extended ratio, stage overlap and moving mass are interdependent. A mechanism that looks like a generic elevator may owe its performance to a light intake, careful bearing arrangement, counterbalance and restrained side loads. Cascading kinematics should be derived explicitly; do not copy a published timing into a design target without knowing travel, load and timing endpoints. Rope strength advertising is not an installed safety factor after knots, terminations, wear and small pulleys.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Derive each stage’s speed and cable force, compare deflection at full reach and check the retained cube clearance through every intermediate position. Inspect counterbalance behavior near both travel limits.

## Independent winch and active partner capture

Version: Uppercut judges pamphlet snapshot. Source: https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [4, 5].

source_locator.section: Independent winch and active partner capture

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The hook is carried up by the elevator, detaches from its retained mount at the bar, and remains while a three-775pro winch raises the robot. An A-frame manages the pair’s balance. A one-way roller draws in a partner-deployed strap and positions the partner on supporting forks; the source reports lifting itself plus a full-weight partner in under three seconds.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Keep a partner secure and aligned during a fast shared climb rather than rely on the partner simply remaining balanced on a support.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Partner capture is not the same as partner lift force. The strap/roller controls relative motion while forks support vertical load. Strap availability, deployment, approach and partner compatibility remain dependencies. A separate winch changes the scoring elevator’s load duty but adds motor/gearbox mass and service interfaces. For a new game, compare that whole-system cost with the actual bonus value. Electric-only latching must preserve a safe retained state and a controlled release; no load rating is inferred from the pamphlet photograph.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Specify the partner interface and load cases before detailed winch selection. Evaluate docking error, strap failure, anti-backdrive and the combined CG during the full lift, not just at the final pose.

title: 2018-1678 — Citrus Circuits: Lemon Zest
text:
# 2018-1678 — Citrus Circuits: Lemon Zest

A six-wheel drive with front omnis carries a two-stage cascading elevator, rotating wrist and cube intake for front/back scoring. A detachable hook, ramp and cable winch create a buddy climb. The published CAD discussion explicitly separates an earlier horizontal roller intake from a later 1323-derived side-to-side design omitted from the public assembly.

title: Strategic interpretation
text:
## Strategic interpretation

This is a reference for front/back workspace and for distinguishing published CAD from the installed mechanism. Do not infer missing intake dimensions from its CAD absence. The historical pneumatic jaws, hook and ramp require non-pneumatic adaptation for 1833; front/back motion is still a permitted alternative to a yaw turret.

title: Earlier horizontal roller versus shared side-to-side intake
text:
## Earlier horizontal roller versus shared side-to-side intake

Version: Lemon Zest earlier/later intake distinction. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1678-citrus-circuits-2018-cad-release/166149. Physical PDF pages: not applicable; see source locators.

text:

The intake’s provenance is useful context, but is not permission to reconstruct private details or label an earlier roller as the championship intake. For transfer, identify which visible/published contact arrangement is actually supported, and explicitly leave unavailable dimensions unknown.

title: 2018-1610 — Blackwater Robotics: Cotton J
text:
# 2018-1610 — Blackwater Robotics: Cotton J

A six-wheel West Coast drive, compact flipped gearboxes, compliant wheel cube intake and narrow two-stage elevator combine scale reach with a reused elevator climb. The binder records an intake/elevator interference-driven redesign and a weight-constrained choice of climbing mechanism.

title: Strategic interpretation
text:
## Strategic interpretation

The most useful lesson is interface propagation: a wider intake changed the chassis, then the wrist sweep conflicted with elevator uprights, then the lift needed custom bearing blocks. This is exactly the sort of spatial coupling to expose before 1833 commits expensive CAD/manufacturing time. The team’s historical partner-dependent climb priority is context, not 1833 doctrine.

title: Flipped gearboxes reclaim internal frame space
text:
## Flipped gearboxes reclaim internal frame space

Version: Cotton J Rev 2 binder. Source: https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [8, 9].

source_locator.section: Flipped gearboxes reclaim internal frame space

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The chassis uses chain inside drive rails and a dropped-center six-wheel arrangement. The binder describes custom flipped gearboxes developed with 2363, positioning MiniCIM motors over the wheels to recover about eight inches of internal room. It also describes exhaust-air motor cooling on the historical pneumatic system.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Save interior volume for mechanisms while using a familiar drive architecture.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The dimension reclaimed at one interface is only useful if motor service, chain access and bumper protection remain viable. The source itself warns that chain-in-tube maintenance requires precision. Do not copy an exhaust-air cooling feature into an electric-only robot, or assume its thermal benefit exists without the original air duty cycle. Compare useful free space, not just frame dimensions, when evaluating how many scoring lanes or a lift can fit.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Draw section views for motor removal and chain tension/service. Account for wiring and guards in the claimed free volume before allocating it to another mechanism.

title: Wheel contact, active clamping and internal belt packaging
text:
## Wheel contact, active clamping and internal belt packaging

Version: Cotton J Rev 2 binder. Source: https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [10, 11].

source_locator.section: Wheel contact, active clamping and internal belt packaging

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The team compared claw and wheel concepts, chose green compliant wheels, and adjusted geometry for wide/narrow cube presentations. The fabric over the open face caused difficulty, so pneumatic arms maintained contact pressure. Belts/pulleys moved inside tubes for a thinner intake; later plastic tubes removed nearly a pound.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Maintain grip across different cube faces and orientations while reducing the intake’s size and lifted mass.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Friction, normal force and entry geometry work together. The trouble with the fabric face shows why a nominal cube dimension is insufficient contact data. An electric jaw would need controlled compliance or a passive spring characteristic instead of assuming cylinder force is reproduced by a rigid motor position. Internal belts protect the drive but can make replacement slower. Added lightness at the end of a wrist reduces joint torque more strongly than the same reduction near the chassis.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Check contact-force and tolerance ranges for actual piece faces; compare a passive compliant jaw and electric adjustment only where the required behavior differs. Preserve belt replacement access.

text:
### Limits

title: Interference-driven narrow elevator redesign
text:
## Interference-driven narrow elevator redesign

Version: Cotton J Rev 2 binder. Source: https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [12].

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The initial elevator was too wide for the intake’s required flip: the intake motors hit the uprights. The team narrowed the elevator to 13 inches and designed R4-bearing mounts because available linear kits did not fit the revised space.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Allow the intake’s vertical rotation while retaining the necessary scoring reach.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A statically fitting intake is not a fitting rotating intake. The critical envelope includes motors, pulleys, retained piece and compliance under load. Narrowing a lift can cure an interference while increasing torsional loading or reducing room for cables. This case should trigger an early swept-volume study; it does not justify waiting for a polished complete CAD model before noticing the conflict.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Create a coarse lift/intake/piece swept envelope first. Check bearing spacing, off-axis moment and service access after narrowing; only detail the accepted architecture.

title: Limits
text:
### Limits

## Elevator reuse and positive anti-backdrive lock

Version: Cotton J Rev 2 binder. Source: https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [13, 14].

source_locator.section: Elevator reuse and positive anti-backdrive lock

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

With little weight margin, the team compared an elevator lift, a carried hook with separate winch and a tape-measure deployment. It selected elevator lifting, added a motor/gearbox and placed hooks under the vertical intake. A pneumatic pin locks the elevator to avoid backdrive. Lift zeroing and encoder limits support normal operation.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Reuse existing reach and reduce additional climb hardware under a tight mass budget.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Reuse can be simple at the architecture level but changes structural loads by orders of magnitude relative to a cube. The intake hooks, carriage, lift bearings, gearing and lock now participate in supporting robot weight. An electric-only adaptation needs a positive holding arrangement appropriate for power loss and release under load; motor stall is not automatically an equivalent lock. The source’s low climb priority cannot be transplanted to another bonus structure.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Recalculate the complete climbing load path and latch reaction, then compare added hardware with marginal match/RP value. Validate release and recovery behavior before approving the shared mechanism.

title: 2018-2898 — Flying Hedgehogs: V1 scale robot / V2 switch rebuild
text:
# 2018-2898 — Flying Hedgehogs: V1 scale robot / V2 switch rebuild

The binder separates an initial elevator/tilting-bucket scale robot from a later switch/exchange arm robot. V2 retained the original drivebase and intake while changing reach and controls. Published sections document mechanical faults, manufacturing constraints, sensor assistance and a mapped-arm operator control.

source_locator.section: 2018-2898 — Flying Hedgehogs: V1 scale robot / V2 switch rebuild

title: Strategic interpretation
text:
## Strategic interpretation

This is an explicit failure/recovery case, not an elite-primary architecture to copy wholesale. V1’s conceptual coverage failed to become reliable reach; V2 improved the achievable role under severe time constraints. 1833 should borrow evidence about tolerances, interface validation and recoverability while maintaining its primary-contributor objective.

title: Offset-pivot capture retained through the rebuild
text:
## Offset-pivot capture retained through the rebuild

Version: 2898 V1 intake retained on V2. Source: https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [7, 15].

source_locator.section: Offset-pivot capture retained through the rebuild

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The binder describes an offset-pivot compliant-wheel intake, approximately half-inch compression and a 775pro in a flipped 10:1 gearbox. V2 reused the intake with a different wheel durometer to ease alignment.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Capture varied 13-inch and diagonal cube poses; retain existing useful hardware during the reconstruction.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

An intake can remain worth using even when the surrounding architecture fails. The pivot offset changes the way the cube opens and closes the contact geometry; wheel stiffness changes both grip and centering. The published surface speed is a historical setting, not evidence that the replacement durometer alone improved match cycles. Treat retained hardware as a candidate with known interfaces, not a reason to force an otherwise poor layout.

text:
### Proposed validation — not performed

Check capture and retained-pose consistency on the real piece surfaces. Confirm whether any changed roller stiffness affects compression, motor current and release.

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

V1 combined a continuous first stage with a cascading second stage, two 775pros, custom slides and constant-force springs. Its light tilting bucket had a separate pivot. The results page lists elevator problems, inadequate height from the cascading design, manipulator/intake misalignment and sensor failure.

title: Team rationale or evidence boundary
text:
### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Initial intent was scale capability without losing switch/exchange usefulness; the combination lift was intended to provide fast motion and potential future climbing.

title: Engineering interpretation

### Engineering interpretation

The desired capability set was broader than the delivered mechanism. This is negative evidence against accepting nominal height and an ideal timing calculation without rigging/overlap and tolerance review. The binder lists several coexisting faults, so no single failure should be declared the exclusive cause. A new agent should carry these failure modes into its uncertainty register, not tell a story that every elevator is inherently unreliable.

That emergency strategic compromise is not authorization for 1833 to start with a support ceiling.
