- **inherited_source_bounded_study**: The rebuild uses a single front slapdown collector, an expanding storage enclosure over an inclined roller floor, and a full-width raised shooter at the opposite end. Corner swerve modules sit below this path; the launcher side structure carries the drum and hood and attaches down toward the drive rails. Source dimensions give a 27.5 by 27-inch frame. The hopper panels and their joints surround the ball path, so screw heads on the hood can rub a sliding wall. A source reply specifically explains using flathead screws there. Some electronics moved above the brainpan, but under-pan equipment still needs underside access. Preserve that service split. Do not infer battery removal without its source view. Locator: data/physical_studies.jsonl#physical-2026-2910-rebuild

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

Original: two collectors → constrained serpentine transport → fixed launcher. Rebuild: slapdown acquisition → bulk hopper/roller-floor path → launcher. Read both full physical studies; the original inlet merge and several rebuilt interfaces remain unknown.

title: Physical arrangement and swept space
text:
## Physical arrangement and swept space

The original places deployment links beside a constrained transport path. The rebuild allocates inventory volume and an active floor beneath it. Mouth deployment, stored inventory, launcher support and electronics access must be evaluated as one package; a compact intake alone says little about sustained feed.

title: Independent motions and powered functions
text:
## Independent motions and powered functions

Count collector deployment coordinates separately from roller motors, floor drive and hood motion. Two collectors do not automatically double throughput, and a single slapdown does not make the hopper feed problem disappear.

title: Burdens avoided
text:
## Burdens avoided

A less constrained bulk path can avoid repeated direction changes and dedicated conveyor transitions, if pieces can still reach the feeder consistently. Fewer deployment linkages may simplify impact recovery and replacement.

title: Burdens retained
text:
## Burdens retained

Bulk inventory introduces bridging, starvation, compression and center-of-mass effects. An active floor adds contact and power demands. Rebuild development time is itself a cost; no numerical time saving or causal season improvement is established by the reviewed construction.

title: Engineering hypothesis
text:
## Engineering hypothesis

Evaluate pickup rate, usable stored capacity and sustained release together. A simple mechanism that starves the launcher cannot meet an elite throughput target. Conversely, a more elaborate collector that feeds no faster may spend space and iteration budget without useful benefit.

title: Rival explanation
text:
## Rival explanation

The apparent improvement may depend on launcher changes, code, field strategy or testing maturity, rather than collector topology alone. Treat the before/after history as a source of hypotheses, not a controlled experiment.

title: When the preference reverses
text:
## When the preference reverses

A constrained path may win when orientation/order matters or bulk feed is unreliable. A bulk path may win when high inventory and simultaneous feed dominate. Select using the new game piece and geometry, not the historical team name.

title: Unknowns
text:
## Unknowns

Common-condition rates, exact interface geometry, actual jam frequency and isolated effects of each redesign. Do not infer hidden plumbing or installed pairings from different binder snapshots.

title: Proposed check; not performed
text:
## Proposed check; not performed

Before replacing an architecture, calculate capacity, clearances and bottleneck rates. Test the single most uncertain transfer or hopper-floor section only if its outcome can change the decision.

title: Outcome evidence
text:
## Outcome evidence

No controlled architecture comparison or individual cycle-time measurement performed.

title: Research complete architectures with minimal owner explanation
text:
# Research complete architectures with minimal owner explanation

The owner should supply priorities and correct consequential mistakes. The research agent owns discovery, source extraction, reconstruction and engineering explanation. Do not require Jack to narrate every robot before research becomes possible. The five initial architecture cases show the expected depth and the attribution boundaries; they are examples, not proof that a particular topology wins every game.

source_locator.section: Research complete architectures with minimal owner explanation

title: Objective and architecture selection
text:
## Objective and architecture selection

Design an elite primary contributor capable of independently achieving important ranking-point requirements and owning essential scoring prerequisites. Preserve the no-turret, no-pneumatics and no-support-only constraints. Simple and effective is the objective: fewer unnecessary independent motions, possession transfers and integration dependencies while retaining the capability that wins the game. A low motor count is not a performance target by itself. This doctrine does not lower the goal to a cheap or limited robot.

First identify the useful task set, route and throughput requirement from the actual game. Compare complete viable architectures under the same tasks, resources, rules and event assumptions. Only then optimize individual mechanisms. A brilliantly executed subsystem cannot rescue an architecture that spends its effort on the wrong job. Do not treat this statement as proof that any particular historical turret caused a poor season.

title: Work the agent must perform
text:
## Work the agent must perform

1. Discover candidates using the retained elite-performance cohort, official results and primary construction sources. Start with top performers but also include documented rebuilds, contrasting topologies and mechanically relevant out-of-cohort examples. A rank threshold is a discovery filter, not a causal design label. Do not expand a database by adding thin summaries when the missing information is possession, packaging or version history.
2. Search team build threads, interview captions, CAD releases, code and technical documents. Read the relevant source, not just a search snippet. Use selected code to test a control-sequence claim and exact source figures for visible geometry. Record commit, page, post or timestamp. A caption transcription is not a visual audit; a CAD link is not inspected CAD. Automatic captions require caution with numbers and names.
3. Reconstruct each complete path in plain language: where the piece starts, which surface first contacts it, what retains it, every possession transfer, the transit pose, scoring release and recovery. Separate distinct cone/cube paths or preload paths. Do not invent a transfer to make a diagram complete.
4. Write the engineering explanation yourself. It need not appear verbatim in a team publication. Anchor the premises, label the causal argument as inference, explain the physical mechanism and state when it would fail. Distinguish published intent, owner testimony, published outcome, analytical deduction and an unperformed test. Unknown intent is not a reason to omit sound engineering analysis.
5. Challenge the preferred architecture. State its strongest rival, useful capability that the rival buys, hidden costs in the simpler option and the conditions that reverse the choice. Preserve counterevidence such as complex robots with good service records. Avoid a popularity contest or a complexity morality tale.
6. Update canonical records, regenerate all derived views and run preservation, retrieval and attribution checks. A source being searchable does not prove the mechanical conclusion. Keep dated configuration boundaries; an IRI feature is not automatically a Worlds feature.

title: Compare a vector of costs
text:
## Compare a vector of costs

Record independently controlled positioning coordinates, powered transport functions, binary actuations, possession handoffs, acquisition alignment burden, collision/control states, fabrication precision, service access, electrical demand and loaded dynamics separately. Stage count is not independent DOF count. Passive or mechanically coupled links may have one coordinate; roller motors still add power and control demands. Drive yaw and driver positioning can carry complexity removed from the mechanism. Do not sum these categories into an invented universal simplicity score.

For every additional motion or separate intake, answer: which essential task becomes possible or faster, how much complete-cycle improvement is plausible, what new transfer/clearance/control/service cost appears, and can passive geometry or chassis positioning achieve the same useful result? An added release mechanism may be worthwhile; a nominally simpler narrow intake may lose badly if approach time dominates.

title: Worked analytical deduction: inclined fixed lift
text:
## Worked analytical deduction: inclined fixed lift

Conditional on the owner's approximately 30–45 degree angle being measured above horizontal, a carriage moving distance s along the mast follows x = x0 + s cos(theta), z = z0 + s sin(theta). Therefore horizontal advance per vertical rise is cot(theta), about 1 to 1.73 over that angle range. This is an original geometric deduction from an attributed assumption, not a measurement of 1746. It immediately asks whether floor pickup, required scoring reach, legal extension and transit poses fit the same line. Add the hand/wrist reach and swept volume before claiming feasibility. If the angle convention differs, revise the model.

A fixed mast removes a shoulder coordinate but couples height and reach. Gravity along the rail is m g sin(theta); rail-normal gravity loading is m g cos(theta), before dynamics and other forces. These terms explain why return and bearing loading deserve attention, but do not size the actual elevator. A long stroke may require additional stages, reducing overlap or stiffness. Use real masses, stroke, rigging and friction before sizing motors or declaring an inertia advantage. Neither the owner account nor these equations establishes a measured cycle time.

source_locator.section: Worked analytical deduction: inclined fixed lift

title: Complete-cycle and outcome evidence
text:
## Complete-cycle and outcome evidence

Use Tcycle = Tacquire + Ttravel + Ttransfer + Tscore + Trecovery with overlapping operations handled explicitly. For approximately repeatable independent attempts, expected acquisition effort can scale like Tattempt / psuccess; this is a conditional model, not a season statistic. Do not invent p, ignore recovery travel or add simultaneous intervals twice. Compare distributions and failure modes, not just the cleanest clip. Include loaded driving and alignment in the scenario.

An Einstein appearance establishes competitive relevance. An alliance victory does not establish that one robot's architecture beat another architecture, and a season EPA estimate is not measured individual output. Keep the owner's claim that vision could improve 1746 as a hypothesis; estimate a gain only after measuring alignment/auto losses and demonstrating the proposed control change.

title: Ask the owner only when the answer changes the work
text:
## Ask the owner only when the answer changes the work

Before escalating, inspect the available primary sources and separate configurations. If a missing dimension prevents exact CAD but not architecture comparison, preserve it as unknown and continue. Ask a narrow question when two plausible interpretations change the recommendation or when only the owner can resolve a consequential installation detail. Explain the decision affected; do not ask for an essay or for the owner to do candidate discovery. Stop dependent work while a genuinely necessary question is pending, and continue unrelated authorized research.

Current bounded questions: exact 1746 stage convention and angle, DCMP/Worlds/IRI feature chronology, and individual acquisition/alignment losses. None prevents the present source-bounded architecture studies. The 359/1833 comparison remains an attributed lead until mechanism, game-demand and performance evidence is gathered. No new claim about 359's construction or causal inferiority is established here.

source_locator.section: Ask the owner only when the answer changes the work

title: Acceptance before calling a case useful
text:
## Acceptance before calling a case useful

A case needs a source/version boundary, typed premises, full supported piece path, package/swept-space explanation, independent motion inventory, avoided and retained costs, causal hypothesis, rival explanation, reversal condition, unresolved gaps and a decision-changing check. An image must be useful for its claimed scope; a thumbnail cannot certify hidden rigging. Missing imagery stays an explicit gap. No exact dimensions, performance rates or fabrication approval can be inferred from fame, captions or schematic drawings.

Machine checks enforce record completeness, parity, links and preservation. They do not validate the hypothesis or predict a future agent's design quality. Use the architecture evaluation cases to audit generated reasoning; human mechanical review and targeted physical evidence still decide whether an actual design is sound.

title: 2026-2910: BLITZ original
text:
# 2026-2910: BLITZ original

Generated from `data/physical_studies.jsonl`; edit that authoritative record.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

Two collectors approach the chassis from opposite sides. They feed a constrained serpentine path and a fixed-yaw launcher rather than a deep open bulk hopper. The launcher structure occupies one end of the base, while the four-bar links occupy side deployment space. The binder base image shows four corner drive modules and a lightened pan. Electronics under the pan require turning the robot over and removing its protective belly sheet according to the team release; do not draw those electronics as accessible through the ball path. Battery removal direction is not established. A fixed launcher can aim with the chassis while the side collectors sweep laterally, but that is a control and route advantage, not unrestricted acquisition in every heading.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

Fuel meets either powered collector, crosses its bumper-side transition, enters the constrained conveyor, follows successive direction changes and reaches the feeder/variable-hood launcher. The exact merge of the two intake streams into the serpentine is not reconstructed by the isolated binder renders. Treat that merge as a critical unknown, not a straight connection invented in CAD.

title: Annotated views
text:
## Annotated views

Editorial reconstruction. Not to scale; only explicit dimension labels are source dimensions. No CAD-derived measurements. Dashed envelopes are schematic and not clearance certification.

![physical-2026-2910-original-side](../../images/physical/physical-2026-2910-original-side.png)

![physical-2026-2910-original-transition](../../images/physical/physical-2026-2910-original-transition.png)

title: Mirrored four-bar collectors
text: ## Mirrored four-bar collectors

title: Published construction
text:
### Published construction

Separate roller motors turn the exposed collecting surfaces. Deployment motors move multi-link arms; the linkage carries the roller across the frame boundary. The original binder reports X44 deployment at 79.37:1 and X60 roller drives.

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary
text:
### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

Deployment sets the mouth outside the bumper; rollers catch fuel from either side and move it inward. The piece must remain supported as it leaves the collector. A collector reaching its angle target is not proof a ball entered the conveyor.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A four-bar can change roller height and fore-aft position together. Impact accommodation requires the whole linkage, transmission and hard stops to permit the intended motion. A flexible plate alone does not establish a reliable collapse mode. Two mouths also require a merge that does not oppose incoming streams.

title: Transfer and compatibility limits
text:
### Transfer and compatibility limits

Transfer lateral acquisition only with the merge, support contact and deploy load path. Two-sided collection is not authorization for a partner-dependent passing architecture.

title: Unknowns
text:
### Unknowns

Exact impact hard-stop geometry, capture sensor, merge gap and roller surface speed remain unknown. Later team replies report original intake fractures and chain faults.

title: Proposed validation, not performed
text:
### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

title: Constrained inventory, feeder and fixed launcher
text: ## Constrained inventory, feeder and fixed launcher

source_locator.section: Constrained inventory, feeder and fixed launcher

title: Published construction
text:
### Published construction

The binder depicts multiple successive powered contacts below the elevated launcher and a variable hood; two X60 feeder motors and three X60 launch motors are reported.

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary
text:
### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

The conveyor carries fuel through successive bends; feeder delivery must stop when the launcher is not ready. Release leaves the chassis at the hood-defined angle, while chassis yaw provides aim.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Each bend changes which surface supports the ball. Long controlled paths can preserve ownership but consume inventory volume and create opportunities for drag. A quoted 25-fuel/s feed capability does not demonstrate the complete route can sustain that rate while acquiring and scoring.

title: Transfer and compatibility limits

# 2026-2910: RE-BLITZ rebuild

Generated from `data/physical_studies.jsonl`; edit that authoritative record.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

The rebuild uses a single front slapdown collector, an expanding storage enclosure over an inclined roller floor, and a full-width raised shooter at the opposite end. Corner swerve modules sit below this path; the launcher side structure carries the drum and hood and attaches down toward the drive rails. Source dimensions give a 27.5 by 27-inch frame. The hopper panels and their joints surround the ball path, so screw heads on the hood can rub a sliding wall. A source reply specifically explains using flathead screws there. Some electronics moved above the brainpan, but under-pan equipment still needs underside access. Preserve that service split. Do not infer battery removal without its source view.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

The front collector lifts fuel across the bumper into the expanded hopper. Ten inclined rollers keep a broad stream moving toward the feeder. The backing panel returns piled fuel toward the shooter entry instead of allowing it to remain above the active floor. Feeder contacts lift and accelerate the stream; drum and powered hood contacts launch it. The full path must preserve width, not merely have a wide drum at the end. The same intake motion deploys storage, so acquisition and containment are mechanically coupled.

title: Published construction

### Published construction

A single-pivot arm uses thick plates, #35 deployment chain and powered lower contact. The source reports 2-inch and 1.25-inch rollers and a 40:1 later deployment ratio.

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

Lowering the arm opens the mouth and deploys storage. The leading roller pulls fuel toward the lower powered contact; that contact carries it beyond the bumper into the floor. The team release says the deployed collector rests on bumper fabric.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Impact loads run through arm, pivot attachment and the deployed stop. Using the bumper as a stop makes fabric thickness and bumper installation part of the collector geometry. A stronger chain cannot correct a mouth held too high by the bumper.

The powered lower contact and simple arm are independently useful. Retain a deliberate load-bearing stop and check new bumper geometry; copying plate thickness alone does not validate impact survival.

title: Broad roller floor and return backing
text: ## Broad roller floor and return backing

source_locator.section: Broad roller floor and return backing

title: Published construction
text:
### Published construction

Ten inclined rollers drive fuel toward a four-motor feeder. A low-friction backing panel redirects loose inventory toward the entry. The team later combined feeder and floor powertrains.

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary
text:
### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

A ball can arrive anywhere across the floor; successive rollers push it to the rising feeder. Balls hitting the front backing slide back toward the pickup region. During a pause the system must avoid packing fuel harder into an unavailable launcher.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The panel changes where gravity returns balls. A rate gain attributed to its addition is evidence of a whole-path bottleneck, not proof that every hopper benefits from the same slope. The rear launcher and front enclosure form one flow volume.

title: Transfer and compatibility limits
text:
### Transfer and compatibility limits

Preserve width from storage to feeder and inspect low-fill starvation. Different roller floors cannot be joined by matching nominal ball diameter alone.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

A front collector and horizontally sliding wall feed a broad floor inside a square drivebase. The launcher stands across the rear; the floor hinges upward from its rear attachment to expose the electrical bay beneath. Intake-end floor supports rest on module-mounted hard stops and a retaining pin prevents unintended lifting. The hopper grows horizontally with the intake and vertically with a climber-linked upper enclosure. The whole render establishes the front-to-rear arrangement but does not establish every swept clearance. The battery and electronics are low, below the transport floor; the inspected electrical render shows component placement with the floor removed, not a complete battery-change sequence.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

Fuel enters the front rollers, passes over the collector pivot and onto a floor with tube rollers and flex-wheel rollers. The floor feeds a curved tunnel, which turns travel upward toward the drum. Feeder, accelerating backing contacts, drum and hood share responsibility for the final entry state. The earlier interview calls the later path J-shaped and reports abandoning an S path; the new page is a separate publication snapshot. It names a different drum material from the retained interview, so do not fuse both descriptions into one certified build.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

Four corner drive modules surround a very low transport and launcher assembly. The inspected CAD screenshot shows wide transverse rollers and launcher motors packed into the central space between modules. The launcher changes elevation instead of yawing independently of the chassis. Its feed transmission is organized around the elevation pivot so a ring can pass into the launcher across its angle range. A raised climb/trap pose shown in another source image is not the everyday driving envelope. Battery location and removal path cannot be established from these images, and are deliberately omitted from the layout.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

A floor note reaches the pickup mouth and is pulled inward while lying approximately flat. Rollers move it through the low transport path to the pivot-related feed region. Launcher contacts then accelerate and release it at the selected elevation. A later deflector keeps a note from entering the space under the shooter. That deflector prevents an unwanted alternative route; it is not another powered feed stage. Climb/trap operation reuses moving hardware but introduces a separate lifted geometry and dynamic timing problem.

Concentric power routing can keep belt-center relationships stable while a launcher pivots. It does not alone prove the note remains constrained. That requires actual overlap of driving and supporting contacts through the worst angle.

title: Published construction

### Published construction

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

The launcher is brought to the intended elevation before feeding. The contacts accelerate the note; chassis heading supplies azimuth. A feed pause while aiming is normal operation, not automatically a jam.

title: Engineering interpretation

source_locator.section: 2025-1323: AURELIA binder plus team sensor replies

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

The ground pickup spans the front of the base. Coral and algae mechanisms share an axis but have distinct contacts and drives. A central shoulder turns a four-stage elevator supported by an A-frame tied into the base; the carriage carries a compact differential wrist and two-piece end effector. The elevator changes both height and fore-aft position because its whole mast pivots. High scoring therefore sweeps a volume above and across the base, while ground intake deployment occupies the front. The base uses different module clearances fore and aft. Published stage and shoulder renders establish subassembly construction, but battery location, complete wire routing and removal operations remain incomplete.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

For coral, floor rollers catch and center the tube, then lift it into a direct handoff. The receiving end effector must be positioned before the donor releases its constraint. The elevator/shoulder move the retained tube to height; the differential reorients it while separate rollers manage placement and release. Algae follows its own intake contacts into the shared end effector, or is acquired from the reef. Climbing changes the force path: cage capture and support contacts allow the shoulder to lift the chassis rather than just a piece.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

A circular bucket fills much of the square chassis between standard corner modules. A rotating capture assembly sits inside it and pushes fuel up a central tube to an inset turret. The turret hangs from structure above, keeping supports out of the approaching fuel stream; its yaw envelope consumes space that would otherwise store or guide fuel. The bucket splits into two pieces, and a removable rear panel provides battery access. Separate intake arms at the front deploy a sliding hopper. Internal bars protect the battery/module compartments, and rear bumper hardware carries serializer armor. The inspected ghosted source view shows bucket, column and upper support relationships, but does not dimension the complete electrical compartment.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

Front rollers bring loose fuel into storage and the circular bucket. The capture assembly rotates through the available pile rather than waiting for balls to find one stationary throat. Independent up-feed rollers push captured fuel into the corrugated tube. Successive balls push the column upward into the turret; release is enabled only when launch and localization readiness are valid. The physical queue can remain occupied when the software pauses feeding.

title: Whole robot and packaging
text:
## Whole robot and packaging

The retained interview describes an intake, roller floor and replacement drum shooter constrained by the existing chassis. The newly inspected publisher thumbnail establishes the exterior hopper walls, top mesh and exposed upper roller area on the numbered robot. It cannot establish the internal feed geometry. The side reconstruction below therefore shows only a functional contact order from the interview, with all distances, bumper crossing and module/electronics locations marked unknown. This is an honest partial reconstruction rather than a measured robot layout.

title: Piece flow
text:
## Piece flow

The intake sends fuel to a roller floor. Upstream contacts accelerate it toward a 3-inch steel drum with powered hood rollers. The upper restraint became passive after its powered form drove balls downward into jams. Reported compression differs between drum and final roller; those values describe the retrofit contact regions, not universal spacing recommendations.

Acquire into the hopper, then use floor transport to supply the replacement shooter. Intake deployment and automatic shooting agitation compete in a command priority hierarchy.

title: Engineering interpretation

### Engineering interpretation

A control system must decide which command owns deploy motion. Simultaneous desired actions cannot be assumed to occur independently just because they appear in different subsystem lists.

title: Passive restraint and stepped-compression retrofit
text: ## Passive restraint and stepped-compression retrofit

title: Published construction
text:
### Published construction

The interview reports a passive carbon upper restraint, a four-X60 3-inch steel drum, powered hood rollers, 3/8-inch drum-region compression and 1/2-inch final compression.

title: Team rationale / attribution boundary
text:
### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

title: Editorial operating reconstruction
text:
### Editorial operating reconstruction

Preaccelerated fuel reaches the drum while the passive upper contact supports/restraints it without actively pushing it downward. Final roller contact increases the reported compression before exit.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The relevant transfer is a sequence that avoids driving fuel into an occupied region. Changing an active contact to passive alters both velocity and reaction force. A different incoming speed or path length can reverse the benefit of the same nominal compression.

title: Transfer and compatibility limits
text:
### Transfer and compatibility limits

Use passive versus powered restraint as a design question. Do not fabricate the original cross-section or transplant compression without defining free diameter, compressed gap and support direction.

title: Unknowns
text:
### Unknowns

No inspected internal detail or video frame supports the contact locations. Compression definition, fuel condition, measured rate and electrical headroom remain unresolved.

title: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
A complete available-caption study of the upper-bracket final and all three 2026 Einstein finals. The central account is the coupling of autonomous contact, transition position, neutral-zone supply, steal timing, shoot-on-the-move passing and 4065’s defensive geometry. Breakdowns and uncertain intent remain explicit confounders.

Compare whole alliance control loops, not drum rate against turret rate in isolation. A robot can make a smaller immediate score while changing who owns the next supply of fuel, who can arrive before a shift starts and which opponent must cross a defended bottleneck. The source’s counterfactual wins and point-denial estimates are hypotheses, not measured individual contributions.

title: Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route
text: The useful design requirement is an autonomous system whose acquisition envelope, collision recovery and route compatibility are evaluated together. A route can abandon a small pocket yet improve total possession by reaching a more valuable arc first. A high collection rate can create an exit-path problem if the loaded robot cannot traverse the selected obstacle without shedding fuel. A net is therefore part of the mobility–storage interface, not an isolated capacity feature. None of this gives a dimension, actual retained count or certified causal diagnosis of 2910’s auto error. Reproduce the route interaction with synchronized overhead video and logs before concluding that the same cut always defeats the same opponent.

title: Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay
text: This is a coupled acquisition, passing and interference role. Passing while moving can let an off-shift robot keep collecting instead of serializing collect, stop, orient and release; the same motion can close an opponent’s useful approach. That does not make every turret a good moving passer. Intake throughput, feed continuity, aiming under motion, range, loaded acceleration and the ability to keep fuel on the intended side all matter. Fuel temporarily held in a third robot is another supply state, even if that robot scores little. The source supplies neither a complete fuel ledger nor timing measurements, so avoid turning this account into a quantified claim that turrets always clean the field faster than drums.

An auditable event log should separate observed departure, observed arrival, unknown fuel count and inferred causal link, rather than give one long causal sentence the status of a directly observed fact.

title: Finals 1: a successful Newton auto, 1323’s reported beaching and 4414’s deliberately deferred scoring
text: This is evidence against a policy that always maximizes every currently scoreable second. Giving up immediate fuel can buy the next load and remove the opponent’s future load. The official record makes the trade concrete: Daly has zero transition fuel while Newton has 57; it is not evidence that the collection produced transition points. Daly later has 83 and 117 in its own active shifts and 140 in the final period, but loses 456–518. That result neither proves the delayed-scoring choice bad nor validates the creator’s healthy-robot counterfactual. title: How 254 beat their California counterparts at the World Championship! | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
A complete available-caption study of 2026 Einstein match 3 (Curie–Milstein) and match 6 (Milstein–Johnson). The retrospective connects tall-dumper throughput to crossing risk, neutral-zone control, coordinated steals, 4946’s rounded perimeter and 6324’s flexible screening role. Its “lose auto by one” thesis is a conditional hypothesis, not a settled rule.

Architecture determines the set of routes available at a particular loaded configuration. Extended storage can turn a trench-capable robot into a bump-only robot during the exact interval when a steal requires escape. A partner that clears a crossing can be worth more than another marginal load, but the value depends on current inventory, shift timing and the defender’s recovery. Test these interactions as an alliance system.

The creator then introduces his thesis that losing autonomous by a very small margin may be advantageous because of the sequence of active shifts and who can control the next returned fuel.",

      "text": "The nine-fuel difference is a measured alliance result, while “lose by one” is a strategic hypothesis. The hypothesis depends on the cost of the lost auto margin, expected transition production, who controls the middle when fuel returns, the ability to store supply and whether the opponent can interrupt the setup.       "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },
    {
      "kind": "broadcast_report",
      "text": "The account describes Johnson sending 6324 to score an already loaded hopper, using 2337 for some scoring and later support, and keeping 4946 in a cleanup/passing role. The creator likes having at least one capable neutral-zone cleanup robot, while wondering whether 2337 could have spent more of the transition denying 2481. He later praises 2337 for switching among defense, a screen and small scoring contributions, rather than staying in one fixed task all match.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1140s",
      "source_video_seconds": [
        1140,
        1266
      ],
      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },

      "kind": "analyst_inference",
      "text": "The opportunity cost of transition collection depends on starting inventory. A loaded robot gains less from another collection pass and can cash in the brief scoring window; a suitable partner can still secure supply. The source therefore offers a hybrid alternative to both “everyone score now” and “everyone collect now.” It does not prove every alliance needs exactly one dedicated passer. A third robot can contribute by changing another robot’s accessible path or timing, and that effect should be evaluated alongside its own points. Visual auditing should record the order of those job changes rather than infer it from a season-average statistic.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1140s",
      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },
    {
      "kind": "broadcast_report",
      "text": "The creator pauses the match to discuss 4946’s rounded or semicircular bumper area. He argues it can rotate and roll around contact that would hold a flat-sided square, and distinguishes a continuous curve from a hexagon or octagon with flat faces. He also explains that a defender obstructed by 6324’s pick temporarily faces an offensive problem: it must escape the screening robot before reaching its original target. His square-on-square defense model emphasizes keeping contact faces aligned, using rotation and not overcommitting to a translational feint.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1266s",
      "source_video_seconds": [
        1266,
        1606
      ],
      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },

      "kind": "analyst_inference",
      "text": "This is an interesting mechanical hypothesis because the perimeter changes contact geometry and the moment generated by a push. It is not a proof that a rounded robot always has leverage or that polygons are always trapped. Real contact includes compliant bumpers, friction, traction limits, module directions, loaded inertia and nearby walls. A curved perimeter can also change packaging, bumper construction and available acquisition width. The transfer test should compare the complete loaded drivetrains and controlled contact angles. The pick reversal is a driver-training insight: a good defender needs escape practice as well as pursuit practice. Team intent and the exact curvature remain unverified without primary geometry and footage.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1266s",
      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },

      "kind": "broadcast_report",
      "text": "The commentary describes 1678 attempting a steal while its hopper is extended, making it bump-only at that instant. 6324 notices and interrupts the return rather than continuing to fill itself. The creator estimates 6324 has a much smaller load and 1678 a larger one; he says the delay consumes roughly the remaining useful scoring interval. He also acknowledges that 1678 still removes fuel from Johnson and could pass or score it later, so the steal is not automatically valueless.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1606s",

        1720

      "kind": "analyst_inference",
      "text": "Value the inventories on a schedule. Removing fifty hypothetical fuel from an opponent is not the same as adding fifty score now, and a delayed load can become exposed to a reciprocal steal. Likewise, a small hopper on a support robot is not automatically a reason to defend: the partner needs a current scoring window worth protecting, and the delay must survive the opponent’s available escape. The exact hopper counts and twelve-second estimate are not independently measured. A visual event log should mark the route block, changed configuration, attempted escapes, release and actual first scoring time, with unknown counts left null.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1606s",
      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },

      "kind": "broadcast_report",
      "text": "The creator describes 6324 screening to let 4946 leave while 1678 and 2481 collide or congest the middle. He then notes 6324 taking back fuel from Milstein’s side during part of its own scoring time. His explanation is that the neutral zone has become sparse partly because so much fuel is already held in 1678 and 2481. The initial Milstein steal has value, but the delayed use of that inventory allows Johnson to recover some of the supposed advantage.",
      "source_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oo5nP00wVBM&t=1720s",
      "source_video_seconds": [
        1720,
        1818

      "text": "An alliance can be rich in fuel but poor in immediately accessible scoring opportunities. This is a dynamic inventory and timing problem, not simply hopper capacity times shooter rate. The collision and screening intent still require footage. A useful agent should be able to explain why the same 6324 can screen, steal and score at different moments without collapsing those actions into a generic “support” paragraph or assuming every action was a preplanned call.",

      "research_pass": "recovered-caption-pass"
    },
