A smaller cup helps stabilize the hatch through the pass-through motion.","The carriage and wrist move the retained piece to the required height and side of the robot. A spring-loaded telescoping section assists seal contact on pickup; wrist valves expedite unseating at release. Exact pressure thresholds and release timing remain unverified."],"packaging_and_motion":"The 25 × 19-inch unbumpered frame uses a dropped center. The offset mast leaves room for the wrist and piece to sweep past it. Cup compliance makes loading forgiving in the approach direction, but introduces motion that must remain inside the opposite-side transfer corridor. Slide and binder lift mass figures are 14 and seven pounds respectively, with no confirmed common assembly boundary.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis and approach sensing","construction":"Six-wheel single-speed West Coast drive, four 4-inch outer Colsons, two center tread wheels, and two CIMs per side. Five JeVois cameras support localization with infrared illumination; the workshop identifies another driver camera.","operation":"Encoder-based drivetrain motion and a vision extended Kalman filter support field approach. The cameras estimate target distance, heading and skew.","team_rationale":"The team chose a compact robot to evade defense and shorten cycles.","engineering_analysis":"Track width, moving mass and stilt placement constrain lateral stability. Camera utility depends on usable views across wrist and lift motion.","interfaces":"Camera extrinsics and illumination need repeatable mounts. Encoder scale and image timestamps affect pose agreement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect mounts and wheels after impacts, and test recovery when the lift or cargo obscures a camera.","unknowns":"Pose accuracy and high-lift stability under defense.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/971-spartan-robotics-2019/350389"]},{"name":"Elevator and pass-through wrist","construction":"Carbon-fiber two-stage continuous lift, Dyneema and printed pulleys, one 775pro at reported 10.25:1. Onyx carriage with Delrin bearings, BAG wrist at reported 175:1 and spring-loaded telescoping aluminum.","operation":"A potentiometer and absolute encoder support lift positioning. The dead-axle wrist swings the tool past the offset elevator.","team_rationale":"Team sought low center of gravity and wrist motion fast enough to keep up with the lift.","engineering_analysis":"Fast extension is useful only if cable routing, carried mass and swing settle within the placement tolerance.","interfaces":"Offset mast and carriage travel must clear the loaded wrist through the entire cross-chassis path.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect printed pulleys, rope, carbon joints, bearing wear and hose snag during telescoping.","unknowns":"Mass boundary, joint construction and loaded timing.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]},{"name":"Floor intake and vacuum tooling","construction":"Polycarbonate four-bar, BAG VersaPlanetary pivot, current-limited 775pro roller drive with two-inch omnis, commercial pump driven by a 775pro and compliant cups.","operation":"Omnis provide a centering surface for the ball. Bellows improve station contact and a smaller cup stabilizes a hatch. Valves help unseat the tool.","team_rationale":"The collector addressed weak direct depot pickup. Bellows improve compliance at the station.","engineering_analysis":"Vacuum area alone cannot predict resistance to peeling. Preserve seal under acceleration, surface defects and partial contact.","interfaces":"Roller centerline, wrist extension and pump/valve timing must present the ball to the cup before carrying it away.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check seals, hoses, pump and contamination. Test roller stalls and early lift after imperfect contact.","unknowns":"Leak margin, force conditions and acquisition interlocks.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]},{"name":"HAB3 stilts","construction":"One 775pro at reported 31:1, over-center spring ankles and feet with one-way bearing wheels.","operation":"Feet hold their geometry through lift, then pivot to move the robot onto the platform. Stilts retract and the drivetrain completes entry.","team_rationale":"The design targets a short late-match climb with room for another robot on HAB3.","engineering_analysis":"A passive transition depends on the center of mass crossing the intended boundary and one-way wheels resisting backslip.","interfaces":"Stilt foot, step edge, bumper and wheel contacts determine each support change.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect spring and bearing behavior under asymmetric loads, including incomplete ankle transition.","unknowns":"Qualification loads and partner envelope.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]}],"revisions":["The team added the four-bar after direct depot suction proved ineffective. Workshop images show several candidate cups but give no chronology for the individual candidates."],"transferable_principles":["Design for the full round trip when choosing a mechanism workspace. Add acquisition assistance at the point where the piece is hard to present to the retention tool."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Pass-through is weak if travel requires turning anyway, or if the loaded sweep blocks localization or adds too much settling time. Suction fails as a shared tool if one piece cannot maintain a seal under the expected disturbance."],"remaining_gaps":["No reconciled lift weight, force/reliability measurements, or event-specific stilt and cup chronology."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2019-971_p12.jpg","reason":"Four-bar floor roller."},{"path":"images/history_2019-971_p14.jpg","reason":"Nested cup face."},{"path":"images/history_2019-971_p18.jpg","reason":"Stilt and ankle detail."},{"path":"images/history_2019-971_p19.jpg","reason":"Camera and illumination package."}]}

title: 2026-1768 RoboChiefs 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-1768","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","title":"Nashoba Robotics Nightshift reveal","locator":"Posts 1 and 7","review_basis":"Read April release and the Nightshade follow-up.","facts":"Nightshift used four X60 drum motors and an independently driven shooter entry roller. The earlier twin indexer required local field tuning at URI.","limitations":"Reveal supplies an onseason anchor, with few dimensions and no event-by-event build list."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","title":"Team 1768 2026 release and retrospective","locator":"Posts 8–17, 21–25 and 27–30","review_basis":"Read team's schedule, failure reports, gearing changes and results in the public thread.","facts":"Only swerves and bellypan survived rebuild as original components. A motor-to-entry pinch affected the old machine. Offseason changes coupled floor, entry and shooter gearing.","limitations":"Reported BPS and accuracy are team estimates without a shared test protocol."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf","title":"Nashoba Robotics Tech Slides","locator":"PDF pp. 2–6","review_basis":"Downloaded team attachment and read the extracted mechanism specifications.","facts":"Slides give intake, linkage, hopper, floor and drum construction and ratios. They include changes the team separately dates to offseason.","limitations":"The slides and post 16 describe the moving hopper attachment differently. Verify the actual link and hardware version before transferring dimensions."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Nightshade used divided shooting and twin spindexer feed. Nightshift changed the central fuel path to a full-width roller floor, shooter entry and drum while retaining much of the intake concept. The team reports nine days to operational status within the eleven-day gap from URI to WPI. The bellypan and swerve modules were the physical carryovers. Later offseason changes shifted the limiting interface again, from floor supply to launch consistency and battery sag.","piece_flow":"Nightshade needed fuel to drop into space between the battery and omni wheel while avoiding the counterrotating-wheel region. Fuel caught between a Kraken and the entry roller could stop the system. Nightshift feeds from an expanding hopper over a broad roller floor, through the compliant entry and into the drum and powered hood rollers. The spaced entry wheels introduced before IRI were intended to organize lanes and reduce lateral interactions between launched fuel.","packaging_and_motion":"Four-bar stow couples bumper clearance, hopper movement and trench height. Week 0 did not fit stowed. Later geometry allowed a trench start aimed toward midfield and folded the kicker over the bumper. The slides describe a bumper-mounted stationary hopper and a moving section with SRPP sides, polycarbonate back, carbon tube and freely rotating sleeves to reduce trapped fuel.","subsystems":[{"name":"Four-bar intake and expandable hopper","construction":"Two two-inch polycarbonate rollers with silicone grip, static half-hex kicker bars, SRPP upper links, aluminum lower links and a MaxSpline jackshaft under the floor. Slides describe one X60 at 90:1 deploy reduction.","operation":"Cross-shaft and chains drive both sides. The lower links provide a repeatable hard stop and the hopper changes volume with deployment.","team_rationale":"Team optimized trench clearance while keeping the intake inside perimeter at start and leaving useful internal space.","engineering_analysis":"Flexible plates that survive impact may still move transmission centers enough to lose tooth engagement. A rigid load path across the transmission can be sized separately from the rest of the side plate.","interfaces":"Deploy shaft to links, kicker to bumper, moving wall to collector, roller motor to first roller.","service_and_failure_modes":"After Worlds a chain replaced a skipping motor belt. A thrown chain prompted polycarbonate flanges. Team suspected plate flex and poor wrap on a 12-tooth pulley. Roller-to-roller belt had no reported skipping.","unknowns":"Resolve upper-versus-lower hopper attachment wording by build version and measure belt-center displacement under torque.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]},{"name":"Floor and entry","construction":"WCP stubs and custom plugs, three through-shafts of squish wheels, thin aluminum tube rollers with silicone, and shortened belt center distances by 0.030 inch. April entry had its own X60.","operation":"Floor conveys fuel toward the entry. Offseason revisions combined floor and entry drives, then increased floor speed as launch consistency improved.","team_rationale":"The team shortened centers to reduce current and tried spaced entry wheels to separate fuel into lanes.","engineering_analysis":"Speed increases shift load downstream. Compare full-width trajectories before increasing floor command, and log chain motion as well as average current.","interfaces":"Hopper to floor, floor rollers to compliant entry, entry to drum compression zone.","service_and_failure_modes":"The combined chain could contact itself in long operation. Confirm chain clearance with warmed hardware and accumulated slack.","unknowns":"Loaded current by version and whether all lanes feed equally at low fill.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]},{"name":"Drum and hood","construction":"Four X60s drive a four-inch aluminum drum with CatTongue tape. Slides specify powered hood rollers, a roughly three-pound external steel flywheel, and a 20-DP printed hood rack flanked by aluminum plates.","operation":"The hood pivots under X44 power. A later ratio brought kicker surface speed closer to the drum. Team reports spinning up from zero for each shot.","team_rationale":"Flanking rack plates resist tooth shear. The team matched surfaces more closely to improve shot consistency and regarded continuous spin as poor value given inertia and kicker friction.","engineering_analysis":"Reducing surface speed mismatch can narrow launch variation, but fast feed and a lower-angle, higher-power shot can erode voltage headroom.","interfaces":"Entry release to drum, drum to hood contact, rack mesh to hood position, shared electrical supply to drivetrain.","service_and_failure_modes":"Offseason flywheel belt slack caused shredding and led to a sliding tensioner. Team reports late-match brownouts after faster tuning.","unknowns":"Onseason exit-speed distribution, power traces, hood angle map and initial versus final flywheel ratios.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Nightshade used improvised Lexan, cardboard and tape guides. Nightshift rebuilt after Week 3, with later DCMP intake work. Before IRI came spaced entry wheels, then combined floor and entry and revised shooter gearing. Team ultimately reported about 28 BPS at RiverRage."],"transferable_principles":["Treat a rebuild as an interface and schedule decision. Separate drop-in space, transport rate and shot quality in validation. Leave time for code changes when mechanisms become mechanically coupled."],"disconfirming_conditions":["More feed is counterproductive if trajectory spread or brownout reduces total makes. A similar four-bar loses value if local frame and bumper geometry cannot accommodate the required trench states."],"remaining_gaps":["Endgame installation, final swerve spec, tested current and precise event chronology for every intake detail remain open."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/525192/30","locator":"Early Nightshade load-in photo attachment","purpose":"Candidate for annotating motor and entry pinch, and required drop-in space."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf","locator":"Slides 3–6","purpose":"Candidate construction views for the pivot chain, floor stub axle and hood sector stack."}]}

title: 2026-1706 Mirage complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-1706","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1706-ratchet-rockers-2026-cad-release-mirage-champs-version/522276","title":"Ratchet Rockers Mirage championship release","locator":"Posts 1, 4–7, 9 and 11","review_basis":"Read the team release and written responses in the public thread.","facts":"Both turrets use two CANcoders, the cable carriers have a four-pound constant-force return, front and rear shooter rollers run at different speeds, and the A-bot shooters had a strict 12-inch envelope. The sloped intake plate addressed fuel trapped during retraction.","limitations":"The release comments give design intent and fixes. They do not specify the complete spindexer roller geometry or shooter control maps."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/522276/13","title":"Mirage offseason B-bot discussion","locator":"Posts 13, 15, 17–18, 21 and 25","review_basis":"Read the public thread’s October continuation and team comparisons.","facts":"Team reports 14-inch B-bot turret envelopes, roughly 84 fuel in the B-bot hopper, and roughly 12–13 versus 11–12 BPS for A and B respectively. It documents breaking in a tighter printed turret gear.","limitations":"Reported rates lack fill, battery and test protocols. Keep B-bot claims separate from the championship configuration."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Mirage packages two independently rotating shooters over twin indexing paths. The team protected the space for indexing with Thrifty Narrow swerve modules and treated each 12-inch A-bot shooter cylinder as a firm boundary. The resulting integration problem spans power transmission, cable travel and repeatable absolute angle sensing on both shooters. The published comparison with the B bot provides an example of what changed when the package was relaxed.","piece_flow":"Fuel crosses the bumper at the front intake and reaches the twin spindexer region through a sloped transition. The indexing assembly supplies the two shooter paths. At each launch module the front wheel and rear accelerator wheels have different commanded mechanical speed relationships through their transmission. The release establishes that topology, with insufficient detail to assign a final cone construction, compression, or loaded delivery rate to each branch.","packaging_and_motion":"The narrower modules redistribute drivetrain bulk away from the spindexer. The team allowed slight contact between the intake plates and bumper foam to preserve edge distance at holes. A remnant telescoping tube served as a stiffener for the Limelight mount in the released configuration. Its presence alone provides no basis for assigning a climb level to that version.","subsystems":[{"name":"Intake and stow transition","construction":"Sloped plate between front intake and indexing region. Bumpers use formed 1/8-inch 5052-H32 backing stock with holes on a one-inch pattern, PE foam and a sewn cover.","operation":"The transition guides fuel out of the pinch region while the intake pulls in. Local foam displacement permits the mechanism to travel past the bumper edge.","team_rationale":"Fuel formerly lodged below the transition, dented the spindexer wall and prevented retraction. Iterating the plate substantially improved the behavior.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate stow with fuel deliberately left at the interface, including dented walls and aged foam. Clearance measured with an empty robot can miss this failure.","interfaces":"Intake plate to foam, mounting holes to edge, slope to spindexer wall.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect for a fresh witness mark or dent and check that repair foam has comparable compliance. The team’s alternative XPE was still under evaluation.","unknowns":"Plate angle, roller transmission and allowable interference.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1706-ratchet-rockers-2026-cad-release-mirage-champs-version/522276"]},{"name":"Twin launch modules and turret services","construction":"Two turret assemblies, dual CANcoders on each, and spring-retracted cable chains running through blue pulleys. Shooter drivetrain preserves distinct speeds and rotation directions for front and rear rollers.","operation":"The team describes residue-based angle reconstruction using the Chinese remainder method. The spring takes up returning cable carrier during rotation.","team_rationale":"Fit the complete path in a 12-inch A-bot cylinder while preserving the fuel path and speed relationships.","engineering_analysis":"The two angle signals extend the uniquely measurable range if their ratios and offsets are suitable. Offset consistency after service and cable reaction torque under motion matter to repeatability.","interfaces":"Fuel entrance to accelerator rollers, encoder gearing to azimuth estimate, and fixed wiring to moving carrier.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect cable tracking over full permitted travel and compare both raw absolute angles after a repair. Belt and shaft alignment were cited as possible contributors to B-bot behavior.","unknowns":"Encoder tooth counts, sensor reconciliation, cable travel limits and actual hood calibration.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1706-ratchet-rockers-2026-cad-release-mirage-champs-version/522276","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/522276/13"]}],"revisions":["For Champs the team iterated the sloped intake plate. The offseason B bot had larger turrets and a tight printed 8-DP spur gear. It was broken in at reduced speed until reported current dropped to roughly 10–15 A maximum, then greased. The team estimated a three- to fourfold reduction in backlash versus A bot."],"transferable_principles":["Budget motor, belt, wiring and sensor envelopes inside every duplicated turret. Compare shooter accuracy and feed balance together, since doubling the launch modules doubles potential paths without establishing equal supply."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The twin layout loses its advantage if one stream frequently starves, cable travel constrains the useful aim range, or a single launcher clears match loads faster after accounting for alignment and outages."],"remaining_gaps":["Final intake and spindexer assembly details, including the exact split between shared circulation and independent uptake, branch rates, climb installation by event and the deployed shot solver remain open. The public interview caption request returned HTTP 429 and supplied no evidence."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/522276/2","locator":"Questions on cable routing, tube and shooter transmission","purpose":"Candidate figures to annotate against the team answers in posts 4 and 7."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/522276/8","locator":"Sloped transition discussion","purpose":"Candidate for a marked-up fuel pinch and intake stow view."}]}

title: 2024-2075 Masquerade complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-2075","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972","title":"Team 2075 Enigma Robotics Presents Masquerade","locator":"Posts 1, 5, 7 and 8, March 2–April 11","review_basis":"Read team reveal and event updates.","facts":["Reveal identifies a start-of-match intake release. Kentwood update reports intake robustness changes, LL3G, LED feedback, shuttling and automatic note pickup, and a climb redesign adding Trap. Team reported 9/12 successful qualification traps and 4/4 in eliminations at the Michigan state championship."],"limitations":"Team event report, not an independent match audit or a drawing set."},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90","title":"Behind the Bumpers — 2075 Enigma Robotics","locator":"1:18–2:10 intake views; 2:37–3:20 deck and panel; 3:50–5:10 head, side drives and Stage","review_basis":"Visually inspected public storyboard frames at approximately five-second intervals.","facts":["Shows distinct low and raised pickup views, underside intake sections, a clear deck and tall hinged assembly, opposing launch rollers, a side chain drive, and a suspended robot in match footage."],"limitations":"Caption requests returned HTTP 429. Sampling does not establish motor count, materials, or the speaker’s rationale for the pivot design."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Masquerade uses compact floor collection hardware at the bumper and a tall scoring assembly on a pivot. The photographs and interview frames distinguish a low acquisition arrangement from a raised roller position. Above a clear deck, the launch assembly presents two wheel rows at the end of a supported structure that can rotate relative to the base. The later event reports make endgame a meaningful part of the architecture. The team retained note pickup and Speaker/shuttle functionality while replacing the climb system and adding Trap between district events.","piece_flow":"With the front of the robot tilted toward the camera, separated underside roller groups are visible beside the bumper. Other views show the green and gray roller spanning the front higher up. The clear deck sits below the entrance to the central upright mechanism, with a wide horizontal roller visible at the foot of its panel. That geometry is consistent with an inward handoff then elevation toward the launcher. The frames identify the contact regions, while the source does not establish the drive timing, exact note storage position, or how the note is routed for Trap. The team separately reports automatic note detection for pickup, which establishes a perception feature without identifying internal possession sensors.","packaging_and_motion":"The upper assembly is held between paired sides, with a prominent lateral chain and sprocket visible at one end. Keeping the launcher above the floor intake leaves room for a steep path while placing a substantial moving structure close to the front collector. The bumper and clear deck constrain where the note can enter. The match segment shows the endgame configuration changing the chassis attitude, so a pit pose alone cannot define the outlet location at the Stage.","subsystems":[{"name":"Floor pickup and higher roller assembly","construction":"Visible green and gray wheel groups on a transverse shaft; underside inspection frames expose multiple roller and support groups below the blue bumper.","operation":"Pickup hardware can be presented low or in a raised position. The team reveal identifies a separate start-of-match release action.","team_rationale":"The Kentwood update explicitly targeted reliability and robustness. Spring rate and wall pickup rationale were not verified in the primary material reviewed.","engineering_analysis":"Compliance would allow a narrow entry to accept differently worn rings, but if roller sections deflect unevenly the downstream handoff can arrive skewed.","interfaces":"Bumper opening, first nip and clear deck must overlap at entry. The raised roller assembly also needs clearance from the central scoring frame.","service_and_failure_modes":"After front impact, test both sides and the center with a loaded note. Inspect release hardware and roller alignment as distinct checks.","unknowns":"Exact segmentation and spring arrangement, wall pickup envelope and as-built change details.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]},{"name":"Transfer and scoring pivot","construction":"A tall panel with a transverse roller at its foot is visible below opposing large launcher wheels. Close-ups show lateral sprocket and chain hardware.","operation":"The upper assembly changes pitch relative to the chassis. The team reported a dedicated shuttling mode and automatic pickup.","team_rationale":"Team update records the functions. The reason for two-sided drive and any protected feedback transmission still needs primary confirmation.","engineering_analysis":"A two-sided support can resist twist only if the frame remains square and transmission loads stay balanced. A narrow beam condition can confirm occupancy while missing a skewed rim.","interfaces":"Lower pickup must hand off across the base of the panel. Pivot position governs the launch direction and alters adjacent clearances.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for side-to-side lash and clear-deck interference at loaded angle limits. Recheck sensing after chain tension changes.","unknowns":"Feeder timing, shot settings and exact pivot motor and encoder topology.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]},{"name":"Climb, Trap and controls","construction":"Visible upright structure and a field segment with the chassis suspended. Team reported a complete climb redesign plus LED and LL3G changes.","operation":"Michigan state results demonstrate repeated Trap use as reported by the team. The team tuned pickup and localization before that event.","team_rationale":"The update gives timing and capability changes but does not specify why each climb part was replaced.","engineering_analysis":"A stable chain-supported pose is required for a repeatable Trap delivery. Success counts do not isolate hook engagement from note delivery failures.","interfaces":"The suspended base, scoring structure and Trap opening must line up under load. Vision and feedback changes affect acquisition and approach independently.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check hook capture and Trap placement separately. A Kentwood roboRIO failure required replacement; the post does not establish its cause.","unknowns":"Actuator, hook linkage, shared pivot load path and measured Trap repeatability by failure category.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/5","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/7","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/8","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]}],"revisions":["March reveal establishes the intake deployment baseline. By Kentwood the team reported intake work, vision and feedback changes, shuttling, pickup detection and a new climb with Trap. Before state it tuned localization and pickup."],"transferable_principles":["Document both entrance geometries with a note present and confirm they converge on a common staged pose.","Track chain engagement, stable hang and successful deposit as separate stages."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A raised roller might primarily aid a distinct acquisition pose, so visual similarity cannot establish shared drive.","If the climb loads enter a separate frame, shooter-to-climber coupling inferred from nearby hardware would be overstated."],"remaining_gaps":["No primary verbal transcript, pivot wiring or spring specifications were recovered."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90&t=108","subject":"Underside intake groups"},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90&t=244","subject":"Shooter wheel rows and side transmission"},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/5","subject":"Team’s Kentwood configuration photo"}]}

title: 2018-148 Uppercut complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-148","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf","title":"Robowranglers Uppercut judges pamphlet","locator":"Physical pp. 1–8","review_basis":"Re-read the primary team PDF text from the downloaded copy and web extraction.","facts":"Team documents a compact single-speed chassis, hybrid chain/rope cascading elevator, cube righting over a boot, and a deployable hook with a separate partner capture and support system.","limitations":"Speed and climb capacity are team-reported. Pamphlet provides no force traces, detailed geometry or event history."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Uppercut integrates a direct scoring intake and a fast cascading elevator within a compact chassis. The floor module prepares a narrow, tall cube orientation for efficient plate packing and travels with it to the target. The elevator doubles as the deployment device for the climb hook, but a separate winch lifts the robot. Partner acquisition is yet another operation: a ratcheting roller retrieves a partner-provided rope, then forks support the partner from below. The architecture couples scoring and endgame through hook presentation while keeping their primary drives separate.","piece_flow":["The passive preload retainer secures the cube before the intake unfolds. A floor pickup comes over a shaped boot that tips it into the preferred tall, narrow orientation. The lift carries the oriented cube to a scoring preset. The described Auto-Score action places it and backs the chassis away.","For endgame the robot parks parallel to the bar, raises the elevator to place its temporarily attached hook, then lowers the elevator, leaving the hook behind. The winch tensions the line. In the partner sequence the other robot deploys a prepared rope, the one-way roller reels it in, and the partner comes onto the support forks."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team designed below maximum overall dimensions to maneuver and pass beneath either tilt of the scale with the elevator collapsed under 42 inches. Thin-wall tubing, printed rollers and the polycarbonate intake reduce raised weight. A two-sided low-mounted electrical panel leaves more room for mechanisms and maintains low mass placement. The hook mount must retain its orientation during driving and ascent yet release cleanly once supported by the bar.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and control package","construction":"Configurable single-speed drivetrain, two-sided electronics panel and Talon SRX encoder breakout.","operation":"The team reports an 18 ft/s top speed and describes trajectory correction and lift scoring presets.","team_rationale":"Compact footprint and light drive package support rapid cube cycling and passage under the scale.","engineering_analysis":"High straight-line speed only helps when acceleration, braking and lift clearance allow it. Constrain transit speed by raised center of mass and position confidence.","interfaces":"Mast stow envelope, chassis approach and preset release positions interact in an automatic placement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep encoder and electronics access compatible with module changes. Verify the eject/back-away sequence after reassembly.","unknowns":"Wheel and gearing configuration at specific events, acceleration and control abort behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]},{"name":"Boot and cube intake","construction":"Lexan intake, orientation boot and passive drinking-bird preload retention.","operation":"Acquisition moves the cube across the boot to convert different starting orientations into a narrow, tall output. The carried assembly then places it.","team_rationale":"The team chose orientation control early because it wanted more cubes to fit on the target. It reports six pre-bag intake revisions.","engineering_analysis":"The important interface is the distribution of final cube poses after fast floor pickups, including diagonal contact and fabric deformation. A righting feature can become a jam point if entry force stalls below its tipping threshold.","interfaces":"Rollers and boot govern the pose presented to the target. Fold/stow geometry also affects the preload retainer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect boot wear, fastener holes and reliable release of the passive retainer. Verify that a failed flip can be reversed.","unknowns":"Actuator and roller specs, boot profile and documented revision differences.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]},{"name":"Cascading elevator","construction":"Two 775pros, chain on the bottom stage, tensioned Dyneema on the top two stages, constant-force springs and printed rollers.","operation":"The pamphlet reports a floor-to-90-inch cube lift under half a second and collapsed height under 42 inches.","team_rationale":"The team used lightweight guide and tube construction and spring assist to reduce active lift load.","engineering_analysis":"A spring reduces some gravity burden, while acceleration and stopping still load every stage. Compare full loaded travel and settling rather than treating reported lift time as cycle time.","interfaces":"The carriage takes the intake and the top of the elevator temporarily carries the climb hook.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect chain and rope tension, spring attachments and high-stage guide wear. Confirm hook separation before lowering.","unknowns":"Drum or reeving dimensions, spring force, feedback geometry and repeatability.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]},{"name":"Hook winch and Robot Wrangler","construction":"Three 775pros and a four-stage winch reduction, central A-frame, deployable one-way roller and underbody forks.","operation":"The hook is carried up on a hook-and-loop mount and the separate winch lifts after bar engagement. A partner rope positions the partner onto the forks.","team_rationale":"Team designed to keep both robots balanced and reports lifting itself and a full-weight partner in under three seconds.","engineering_analysis":"Treat rope capture and structural support as distinct load cases. An off-center partner adds overturning torque and lateral loads even after successful capture.","interfaces":"Bar, hook, line, winch and A-frame form the main load path. Rope location and fork engagement determine partner alignment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hook retention versus release, verify fork seating, and assess failure to stop backdrive after interruption.","unknowns":"Fork geometry, winch holding mechanism, measured loads and partner compatibility list.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]}],"revisions":["The team reports six intake revisions before bag and emphasized module replacement for continued iteration. The pamphlet does not enumerate the six mechanisms or identify later event hardware."],"transferable_principles":["Define output piece orientation as part of the intake contract. Separate deploying a hook, hoisting the robot and constraining a partner into individually verifiable interfaces."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The boot adds cost without benefit if target capacity does not depend on orientation. A partner system loses value if alignment and partner preparation dominate available endgame time."],"remaining_gaps":["No underlying CAD, event chronology, independent cycle measurements or confirmed revision-by-revision geometry."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2018-148_p3.jpg","reason":"Cascading elevator layout."},{"path":"images/history_2018-148_p5.jpg","reason":"Rope capture and fork support."},{"path":"images/history_2018-148_p6.jpg","reason":"Cube orientation and passive retention assembly."}]}

title: 2022-4499 Highlanders 2022 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-4499","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf","title":"The Highlanders 2022 Technical Binder","locator":"pp. 3–13, especially feeder iterations p. 7 and climb p. 9","review_basis":"Re-read indexed binder text, specifications and figure descriptions through web retrieval.","facts":["MK4 L2 swerve, two-roller intake, two-station beam-break sensing, a printed double-sided feeder ramp, powered shooter hood and chain-driven climber are documented.","The binder separates an unstable first feeder with a flexing ramp from the revised flat deck and speed bump. The arm and elevator have separate motors and reductions.","The team describes camera-aided hub positioning, swerve path interpolation and combining several position estimates."],"limitations":["The binder reports subsystem specs and objectives. Its one-second loaded extension claim is for the elevator stroke. Full climb time and event-by-event hardware were not verified.","Binder identifies an OAK-D in the shooting system. Camera substitutions or other configurations require separate evidence."]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Maverick collects from one side with a pair of full-width rollers, funnels cargo into a low two-ball feeder and shoots with a powered adjustable hood. Heading comes from the chassis, which can translate independently of yaw. Endgame is a separate elevator-and-arm system tied structurally into both the feeder superstructure and chassis. The low cargo deck and centered climb address different mass and load cases.","piece_flow":"Floor cargo first meets the compliant pickup rollers, rides up and over the bumper, and is centered by rear mecanum elements and feeder flaps. Front feeder wheels move it across the flat deck toward the central bump, which brings the ball up into the indexing wheels. Inlet and outlet beam breaks observe flow and staging. The index wheels hold or advance cargo into the flywheels. The moving hood defines exit geometry and the mechanically driven rear roller acts on spin. The binder establishes capacity of two and an indexed release, with exact two-ball positions and spacing logic unresolved.","packaging_and_motion":"The nonparallel four-bar changes the roller pose between pickup and retraction. Feeder compression is concentrated at the bump, letting most of the transport remain low. The elevator carriage translates while the separate arm rotates, and chassis yaw steers shot azimuth. Check the arm sweep against the hood envelope and trace whether structural distortion during a hang could shift the indexing gap.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis and aiming","construction":"Square tube chassis, standardized mounting holes, inner electronics routing, MK4 L2 modules with four-inch nitrile-tread wheels.","operation":"Swerve accepts planar and angular velocities. Hub vision contributes position information alongside gyro heading and odometry.","team_rationale":"The team valued agile movement around the hub, straightforward integration and early time for other subsystems.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed-azimuth launcher makes chassis yaw accuracy a shot variable. Swerve can set yaw while translating, although intake approach still constrains where the chassis points.","interfaces":"Drive mounting, common feeder and climb references, hub camera and gyro.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tread and verify yaw references after contact. Camera bias or wheel slip can shift both path following and the shot setup.","unknowns":"Full aiming gate and camera calibration parameters.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]},{"name":"Intake","construction":"Two belt-driven aluminum rollers on a pneumatic nonparallel four-bar with quarter-inch polycarbonate plates. One Falcon drives the rollers.","operation":"Compliant wheels collect and rear mecanum ends steer cargo inward before the handoff.","team_rationale":"Survive impacts, collect at speed and retract around defenders.","engineering_analysis":"Soft wheel contact and yielding links address different disturbances. The rear lateral component only helps if the second roller still has traction as the ball clears the bumper.","interfaces":"Bumper clearance, feeder inlet and paired cylinder linkage.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect both sides for skew and the shared belt for damage after corner impacts.","unknowns":"Deployed gaps and any cylinder synchronization procedure.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]},{"name":"Feeder","construction":"Flat deck, printed double-sided bump, flaps, two-inch entrance wheels, three-inch compliant index wheels and two beam breaks.","operation":"The bump lifts cargo into the indexing nip just upstream of the launcher.","team_rationale":"Preserve a low two-ball package and stable grip while allowing a possible second collector.","engineering_analysis":"A localized rigid rise makes indexing compression less sensitive to long-deck flex. Too much squeeze can turn two-ball acquisition into a stall.","interfaces":"Intake exit, two sensor stations, launcher throat and feeder frame supporting the climber.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check ramp fasteners, sensor alignment and wheel wear before changing control timing.","unknowns":"Compression tolerance for worn cargo and exact occupancy state machine.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]},{"name":"Shooter","construction":"Two six-inch nitrile-tread flywheels, two Falcon motors, a geared hood and a two-inch backspin roller driven from the flywheel.","operation":"Changes RPM and elevation for range, with the chassis positioning for the shot.","team_rationale":"Repeatable fast shots from multiple ranges.","engineering_analysis":"Coupling rear contact speed to the main wheel reduces independent tuning variables. Wear can still change the effective ratio at the ball.","interfaces":"Indexer entry, camera-derived pose and hood position.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tread, belt and hood play when a range-map correction fails to repeat.","unknowns":"Measured exit spin, per-range settings and accuracy under contact.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]},{"name":"Climber","construction":"Two-stage elevator on tube rails, #25H chain drive, two Falcons, one-way carriage hooks and separately geared NEO 550 rotating arm.","operation":"Carriage and arm reach and transfer rung contact. Ratcheting hooks retain the robot after the match.","team_rationale":"Compact packaging and centering near the center of mass to reduce lateral swing.","engineering_analysis":"Rail alignment and chain tension matter under off-axis loading. The feeder structure is part of the climb load path.","interfaces":"Rung to hooks, rails and feeder/chassis tubes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bearing preload, chain slack, hook closure and hard-stop damage after an asymmetric catch.","unknowns":"Full rung transfer state sequence, swing feedback implementation and loaded approach statistics.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}],"revisions":["First feeder used a belt and flexible sheet ramp. Its successor used a flat plane and a raised indexing bump. Dual-side provision remained a packaging option in the binder."],"transferable_principles":["Measure compression at a repeatable index point, and include feeder supports in any loaded climb fixture that represents this frame."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A central bump loses its advantage if cargo stacks at the convergence or if climb loads move the roller reference. A fixed-azimuth shot loses cycle time if chassis yaw is repeatedly blocked."],"remaining_gaps":["Event camera chronology, complete climb sequence, achieved approach-to-hang timing and indexed-feed performance on worn cargo."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf","locator":"pp. 5–8","purpose":"Published intake, feeder path and shooter diagrams for the over-bumper handoff and indexed release."}]}

title: 2026-2046 Bearricade Mk.II complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-2046","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","title":"Bearricade Mk.II Technical Binder","locator":"PDF pp. 16–18, 20, 22–32 and 36–38","review_basis":"Downloaded the binder linked by the team and read the extracted mechanism and programming pages.","facts":"Documents prototype bottlenecks, final collector, hopper, staged roller floor, powered S-curve, passive adjustable hood, and the decision against allocating weight to a climber.","limitations":"Binder roller count and speed figures should be checked against drawings and hardware before replication. Capacity and control settings are team figures."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823","title":"Bear Metal CAD and technical binder release","locator":"Posts 3, 6, 9, 11, 13 and 19","review_basis":"Read release replies on deploy, test history, autonomous selection and post-district indexer change.","facts":"Two X44 deploy motors drive a slapdown pivot. After DCMP two floor motors improved loaded efficiency. Team estimates 23–25 BPS and about 95 percent accuracy at Worlds.","limitations":"No common protocol, confidence interval or match-wide average accompanies the quoted performance."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Bearricade Mk.II is a fixed-heading drum shooter over a broad, actively driven fuel path. The team’s high-fidelity beta used three shooter channels and was limited by indexing and current. Its Week 1 machine preceded a rebuild that mainly widened the superstructure, carrying forward concepts that were already working. The team also explored a turret briefly after beta and chose to continue its original architecture. The binder records the weight and storage trade that led away from a six-pound climber.","piece_flow":"Three collector rollers hand fuel across the bumper into the expanding hopper. Floor rollers with increasing speed move fuel toward a powered superstructure that draws it around a compact S-curve. A four-inch drum and passive adjustable hood launch fuel. The team removed floor agitation wheels after they delayed engagement with the superstructure roller. These are distinct zones of transport, pickup and launch, with separate opportunities for blockage and overdrive.","packaging_and_motion":"The binder specifies a 27-inch square chassis with SDS MK5n modules, L1 drive ratio, four-inch Spike wheels and underside HDPE skids. A brainpan and removable polycarbonate panel provide access below the mechanisms. Collector pivot drives a sliding polycarbonate hopper on ball-bearing guides. The team lists capacity around 60 for a trench route and 75–80 for a bump route. These are route-specific capacities.","subsystems":[{"name":"Slapdown collector and hopper","construction":"Two X44 deploy motors drive a sprocket and pivot arm on a stationary axle. Three dead-axle polycarbonate rollers use a one-side gearbox and belt train. Printed links couple the collector to the hopper extension.","operation":"Collector pivots down to pick up fuel and moves the hopper plate along slides. A net limits escape.","team_rationale":"The team picked a familiar simple deploy, iterated compression and added metal reinforcement at stub axles.","engineering_analysis":"A loaded hopper can increase deploy forces through the printed linkage and slider friction. Validate asymmetric hit recovery with a filled extension.","interfaces":"Pivot axle to arm, roller stubs to reinforced structure, linkage to slider, net to fuel envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt and stub retention after impacts, plus slider alignment and print cracking. Hopper detachment was a service objective.","unknowns":"Exact deployed and stowed margins, linkage force and net fatigue.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]},{"name":"Staged floor and powered S-path","construction":"Binder lists ten 1.25-inch horizontal tubes with silicone and CatTongue grip, 21:20 stages, two X44s, and two X60s on the compact S-curve superstructure.","operation":"Speed steps upward toward the exit. A backed transition actively draws fuel from the floor into the shooter.","team_rationale":"Rollers displaced a difficult belt bed. After DCMP the team added a floor motor to stay in a better efficiency band and increase usable speed.","engineering_analysis":"Motor count and bus draw can move in opposite directions when a loaded motor leaves its efficiency band. Evaluate energy across an entire burst.","interfaces":"Floor-to-S-curve roller traction and clearance, molded backing to drum entry, drivetrain and scoring shared battery.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early belt tension loaded axles and fuel could spin in place. Inspect roller grip, backing and timed accumulation at the intake to the S-curve.","unknowns":"Binder gives 1410 to 2297 RPM. Confirm the actual number of speed stages, including transition rollers, before recreating the ratio stack.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]},{"name":"Drum, hood and aim","construction":"Four-inch aluminum drum with grip tape. Passive printed hood backing and commanded angle from −10 to 60 degrees. The binder lists 3000 RPM.","operation":"Normal shots depend on chassis heading and hood selection. Negative angle enables the special reverse shot while pressed against the hub. Lookup-table trim is available to the operator.","team_rationale":"The team credits smooth backing with reducing unpredictable bounce and identifies idle speed oscillation as an early tuning issue without supplemental flywheel inertia.","engineering_analysis":"Measure loaded and idle response separately. The reverse shot is useful only where alignment and release conditions stay repeatable under contact.","interfaces":"Powered S-path to drum nip, hood setting to exit, localized pose to heading and lookup table.","service_and_failure_modes":"Monitor drum velocity recovery during a full burst and inspect backing wear for lane-dependent changes.","unknowns":"True field shot distribution, power traces, and controlled reverse-shot results.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]}],"revisions":["Wood alpha exposed indexer space and belt issues. Triple-channel beta highlighted power and feed limits. The Week 1 machine gave way to the wide drum rebuild. Subsequent changes included floor motor count, with later world-event rate estimates."],"transferable_principles":["Size the powertrain at loaded operating points and tune floor, transition and launcher separately before increasing overall speed. Reserve physical clearance for maintenance before freezing the hopper."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A passive hood is a weaker choice if exit-speed variability or wear under the intended fuel supply exceeds the acceptable trajectory spread. The wide drum’s cycle value falls when defense consistently denies chassis alignment."],"remaining_gaps":["Independent validation of Worlds rate and accuracy, event-level assembly changes, and matched floor/transition/launch power traces are open."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view#page=27","locator":"Binder pp. 27, 29 and 31","purpose":"Candidate figures for staged floor, S-path and hood interface."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/523823/11","locator":"Team deploy reply and attachments","purpose":"Candidate pivot-arm and sprocket service views."}]}

title: 2018-2910 Kayla complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-2910","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","title":"2910 CAD Release 2018","locator":"Posts 1, 6, 8, 13, 14 and 16–19; published render in post 1","review_basis":"Read original release replies and visually inspected the corpus copy of the team render.","facts":"The team documents internal belt routing and a build-season belt failure, shift and lock cylinders, passive platform wheels, thin-section X-contact steering bearings, and effectively one-to-one absolute azimuth sensing.","limitations":"The render is a single view of the released design. No assembly file, footage or competition software was inspected."},{"url":"https://www.frc-handbook.com/ref/28","title":"FRC Design Handbook reference 28","locator":"Robot Design Concept","review_basis":"Read the independent description of the cube handoff and static lift hooks; compared visible layout with team render.","facts":"Identifies a through-bumper orientation intake and separate carriage roller claw on a two-stage continuous lift, with hooks used for climb.","limitations":"Secondary description. Its speculative wheel-change rationale and spooled-lift label are excluded in favor of the team's belt account."},{"url":"https://frcteam2910.org/competition-history/","title":"Team 2910 Competition History","locator":"2018 Power Up section","review_basis":"Read the team's season account.","facts":"Identifies the robot as Kayla, describes maneuverability as the drive objective and lists the 2018 championship division and finalist outcome.","limitations":"Season retrospective gives no individual cycle metrics."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Kayla combines a low through-bumper cube path, a separate elevator-mounted scoring tool and a swerve chassis. The lift drive sits out of the piece path by routing the belt through the tubes. The same mast provides endgame lift capacity by switching gearbox range and locking after climb. Its distinctive integration problem is to fit the intake opening, side-clearance rollers, steering modules and mast base in the same chassis without making the internal lift drive impractical to repair.","piece_flow":["A floor cube enters the central bumper opening. Lower rollers draw and orient it into the receiving space of the roller claw, which travels independently on the carriage. This sequence is described in the handbook and the two roller heights are visible in the team render. Exact roller commands and handoff confirmation are undocumented.","The carriage takes the cube to plate height, and the claw's driven contact provides the release interface. The low pickup pose needs enough overlap for both assemblies to control an imperfectly centered cube without trapping it as the carriage leaves."],"packaging_and_motion":"The chassis can translate sideways without rotating its intake away from a target. The team added two unpowered rollers at the mast base for sideways crossing of the platform. The belt's protected route leaves usable volume around the mast and keeps loose objects away from the drive element, but replacement requires splitting the stages. The published render shows upper hooks near the mast crossmember and the lower intake inside the front bumper gap.","subsystems":[{"name":"Swerve and azimuth feedback","construction":"Custom modules with thin-section X-contact bearings and MA3 absolute sensors. The steering output and encoder branch have equivalent gearing.","operation":"The sensor reports module orientation across power cycles. The team confirmed that an effectively one-to-one encoder relationship avoids routine re-zeroing.","team_rationale":"The team wanted freedom to maneuver around field obstacles and considered the game suitable for swerve.","engineering_analysis":"Absolute angle preserves the datum only while the keyed or geared relationship holds. Offset changes or encoder gear slip can bias both steering and any inferred chassis motion.","interfaces":"The bearing carries steering-axis loads, while calibration ties encoder angle to the actual wheel direction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck the mechanical and software datum after module replacement. Check wheel clearance at full steering sweep near bumper brackets.","unknowns":"Drive motor feedback and quantitative accuracy under load.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://frcteam2910.org/competition-history/"]},{"name":"Cube collector and carriage claw","construction":"Through-bumper floor rollers and a separate belt-and-wheel roller claw visible at the lowered mast, described in the handbook.","operation":"The floor mechanism orients the incoming cube and the claw takes it vertically to the switch or scale.","team_rationale":"The handbook ties this arrangement to varied cube orientations. A firsthand team comparison for this choice was not located.","engineering_analysis":"A transfer can reduce raised collector mass but needs a stable orientation after asymmetric contact. A miscentered cube can wedge between stationary rollers and the moving receiver.","interfaces":"Bumper gap, roller contact height and carriage home position jointly define admission and handoff.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect roller compliance and repeat the transfer after collision or carriage service.","unknowns":"Wheel revision chronology, retention force, home sensing and recovery behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://www.frc-handbook.com/ref/28"]},{"name":"Belt lift and climb","construction":"Continuous two-stage lift with belt routed around bearing pulleys through tubes. Separate pneumatic cylinders shift range and lock the elevator. Upper hooks visible in the release render.","operation":"High range handles cube placement. Low range handles climbing, and the separate lock holds after climb.","team_rationale":"Team favored belt protection and avoiding spool-tracking concerns.","engineering_analysis":"The hard-stop event shows why clamp-edge radius and terminal impact matter independently of nominal belt strength. A climb changes loads at the carriage attachment, mast guides and lock.","interfaces":"The fixed end on the carriage, internal pulley path, gearbox and lock share responsibility for load transfer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports about 45 minutes to replace a belt, including removing guide bearings, separating stages and threading without twist.","unknowns":"Lock geometry, full belt specification, climb qualification and confirmed climb states.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://www.frc-handbook.com/ref/28"]},{"name":"Sideways platform clearance","construction":"Two waterjet-cut 6061-T6 free rollers at the base of the elevator.","operation":"They provide rolling contact at the platform rather than letting the chassis settle on a fixed low surface.","team_rationale":"Team reports fewer instances of bottoming out, with occasional sticking still possible.","engineering_analysis":"A passive roller only helps while driven wheels retain normal force and torque.","interfaces":"Wheel vector, platform edge and roller axis must align with the crossing direction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check roller bearings and mounts for strikes and inspect whether damage reduces floor clearance.","unknowns":"Tested crossing angles and loaded ground clearance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095"]}],"revisions":["A fiberglass tensile-cord belt failed after a hard-stop strike cut it at a sharp carriage fixture. Team removed the edge and switched to steel tensile cord, reporting no recurrence through the release discussion."],"transferable_principles":["Design access before hiding a transmission inside structural tubes. Budget a sacrificial or rolling contact surface where a known obstacle intersects the chassis envelope."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The belt package loses value if inspection requires excessive disassembly or a termination cannot tolerate the load case. Side rollers cannot recover a route that unloads the driven wheels."],"remaining_gaps":["No event-specific hardware map, complete climb load path, match configuration of roller wheels or pickup software."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2018-2910_source.jpg","reason":"Team render showing the central floor opening, carriage, upper hooks and passive rollers."}]}

title: 2023-1727 INCLINE complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-1727","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf","title":"REX 2023 FIRST Charged Up Technical Binder","locator":"Printed pp. 4–14, especially Arm p. 8, Elevator p. 9 and Intake p. 10","review_basis":"Read team binder text and labeled drawing text on p. 6 through the web tool.","facts":"The binder identifies the drivetrain, a rotating arm and two-stage lift, the direct compliant roller intake, low-mounted electronics and scoring poses.","limitations":"The double substation is a design objective. The capability discussion names floor and single-substation collection. Free drive speed is a published estimate. The binder does not assign hardware to individual matches."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Incline uses a rotating support arm and telescoping lift to position a single side-roller head for both collection and scoring. The team describes the controls as polar coordinates. The arm sets angle and the elevator sets reach, so those axes can move together without asking the driver to reposition the chassis for every change in height. REX's game analysis called for a robot that could create links and engage with limited help. Direct acquisition, a low chassis and preselected geometry address different parts of that goal.","piece_flow":"For floor or single-substation collection, the arm and elevator bring the roller head to the piece. Mixed-durometer wheels deform around cones and around cubes whose inflation varies. The same head retains the piece while the two positioning axes change angle and reach and presents it at the intended node for outtake. There is no separate transfer in the documented path. The binder reports less than 90 degrees of arm movement and over three feet of lift extension. It does not specify the complete release-direction or roller-current schedule.","packaging_and_motion":"The arm turns about a dead axle also used in powering the elevator, with a modular connection between assemblies. The sponsor panel doubles as lift protection and a cable-chain track. REX locates ballast inside three drive rails and the battery horizontally over the belly pan. Inference: on extended poses, stability depends on horizontal offset and chassis acceleration as much as on lift height. Check the swept polycarbonate head and cable chain between presets, especially when leaving ground pickup with a piece retained.","subsystems":[{"name":"Swerve and base","construction":"24 by 28 inch aluminum MaxTube chassis with REV MAXSwerve, four NEO 1.1 drive motors and four NEO 550 steering motors. Drive reduction is 5.08:1. A 1/8-inch aluminum belly pan and 15 lb of steel rail ballast sit low.","operation":"Independent steering permits translation around obstacles and a wheel-lock configuration for station use.","team_rationale":"REX sought strafe mobility and a low center of gravity. Toggle clamps are specified for rapid bumper swaps.","engineering_analysis":"Test downhill braking and direction reversals with a representative high extension, where wheel load transfer can undermine pose control.","interfaces":"Arm and ballast loads enter the frame. The belly pan protects and carries electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect clamps, wheel steering zero and rail retention after hard impacts.","unknowns":"Loaded speed and measured stability margin.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]},{"name":"Arm and telescope","construction":"Arm uses one NEO 1.1 with 100:1 MaxPlanetary and two 30 lb gas springs. A turnbuckle adjusts the fixed-center chain. The two-stage Thrifty Bot lift uses custom string and pulleys, a 9:1 planetary and a 2:1 external gear stage.","operation":"The two axes can travel simultaneously to a preset. The shared axle and removable lift attachment integrate the drives.","team_rationale":"REX cites shorter piece transit and straightforward removal of the arm from the elevator.","engineering_analysis":"Gas assist varies with geometry. Check shoulder tracking across extension because both gravity leverage and reflected inertia change.","interfaces":"Shared axle, lift mount, string path and protected cable chain all cross the pivot-to-extension boundary.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check string tracking and tension, chain slack and spring mounts before retuning. Confirm the lift can be removed without losing alignment.","unknowns":"String anchoring and event-specific tension settings.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]},{"name":"Roller head and controls","construction":"Six four-inch VEXpro flex wheels, four 30A and two 45A, in quarter-inch polycarbonate. One NEO drives the head. Lift and arm use PID position control.","operation":"Preset scoring poses coordinate both axes. PathPlanner event markers run subsystem commands during autonomous travel.","team_rationale":"The team prioritized positive capture despite variable piece compliance and reduced driver input.","engineering_analysis":"A failed grab ties up the scoring axes. Measure acquisition tolerance in yaw, height and piece deformation before extending the concept to crowded approaches.","interfaces":"Head rides the moving lift. Electrical leads must traverse the pivot and the extension track.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check polycarbonate hole elongation, wheel wear, wire strain and whether an interrupted preset can be recovered cleanly.","unknowns":"Exact head reduction convention and acquisition confirmation method.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]}],"revisions":["The team reports changing from difficult-to-service inverted electronics on an earlier robot to a topside belly-pan layout. The binder also reports upgrading battery leads from 6 to 4 AWG with right-angle fastening. No dated 2023 manipulator swaps were established."],"transferable_principles":["Design pickup and placement as a common pose map when one head can retain both pieces. Use the protective panel as a defined wiring surface if cable motion can be inspected."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The direct path loses its benefit if bumpers or field lips force repeated realignment, a held piece obstructs retraction, or combined axis motion consumes the available stability margin."],"remaining_gaps":["End-of-travel and recovery behavior in deployed code, double-substation coverage, measured cycle times, and exact as-competed configurations."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"Binder pp. 6, 8–10 and 12","subject":"Overview, pivot/lift interface, mixed-wheel head and electrical layout.
