title: 2025-3663 CPR 2025 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-3663","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U","title":"3663 CPR, Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Clackamas interview, 1:19–2:25 design and software, 2:33–4:38 arm, 4:46–6:17 climb","review_basis":"Read the on-page English transcript of team interview; no footage claims","facts":["Team chose a sideways elevator with carriage-mounted arm for access around the elevator, moved wrist and grabber belts inside 2 by 2 aluminum by iteration four, and used an elevated-pivot cage latch that retained through gearing."],"limitations":["Captions describe demonstrations but do not establish exact roller geometry, rigging, physical speed or how long the cage retained load under worst-case conditions."]},{"url":"https://www.cpr3663.com/cpr-blog","title":"CPR team blog","locator":"2025 robot outreach and REEFSCAPE demonstrations","review_basis":"Read team outreach descriptions","facts":["CPR reports demonstrating the 2025 machine with coral and algae, including scoring PVC coral on a reef at the Cedar Park Church Block Party."],"limitations":["Outreach copy gives capability context only and no hardware change log."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Sideways lift and arm structure","construction":"Elevator presented sideways with a pivoting arm mounted on its carriage. The interview identifies 2 by 2 aluminum on the arm.","operation":"The lift supplies height and the arm reaches past the lift to move between intake and scoring presentations.","team_rationale":"The team wanted pass-through-style access and judged passing through the elevator itself unsuitable. They also aimed for a low center of gravity.","engineering_analysis":"If the carried arm and piece load the carriage off center, check guide loading and wrist deflection at reach. The benefit depends on access around the upright throughout the motion, including with a loaded tool.","interfaces":"Carriage reacts arm loads, and lift height sets the clearance available for pivoting near the bellypan.","service_and_failure_modes":"After impact, compare the measured tip path to its taught path before commanding an aggressive low transition.","unknowns":"Stage count, carriage guides, reduction, motor placement and exact motion limits.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U"]},{"name":"Wrist, grabber and scoring controls","construction":"Internal belts drive the wrist and grabber. The same tip handles coral and algae.","operation":"Present the tool for collection, keep the piece through the arm swing, then place it at the chosen target using the level-specific software pose and speed.","team_rationale":"External belts in early design were exposed to snagging on the reef. Software work emphasized avoiding robot and field collisions and placing pieces precisely.","engineering_analysis":"Enclosing transmission reduces exposure to reef contact and can complicate belt inspection. A protective tube only helps if the service route permits restoring belt tension and wrist zero repeatably.","interfaces":"The 2 by 2 arm is both structure and transmission enclosure. Wrist orientation and chassis approach determine release geometry together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect belt tracking and exits after contact. Exercise collision limits with a real coral and algae, since each enlarges the moving envelope differently.","unknowns":"Internal reduction, grabber contact materials, sensing, calibration and release settings.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U","https://www.cpr3663.com/cpr-blog"]},{"name":"Deep cage latch","construction":"Elevated pivot and latch that flips the cage; the final described holding method is drivetrain gearing within the climber, with a planned ratchet omitted.","operation":"Latch into the cage, rotate to move the suspended chain toward the robot middle and lower the scoring arm clear.","team_rationale":"Deep climb mattered for ranking points. CPR wanted a small package and designed around battery and elevator balance. The team reported gearing held long enough in its use.","engineering_analysis":"Measure the suspension point relative to the loaded center of mass. Small offsets change hanging angle and the loads on the latch and structure.","interfaces":"Climb rotation shares space with the arm. Battery location and mast mass influence hang attitude.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check gear backdrive after disable, with wear and the least favorable loading. Inspect cage pin and latch engagement after repeated off-center capture.","unknowns":"Gear reduction, latch actuation details and timed retention under varied loads.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Cedar Park made a lift with an arm mounted on the carriage. The sideways elevator layout let the arm reach around the lift to give the access pattern the team wanted from a pass-through robot. A common arm-tip grabber does coral and algae work. The arm changes position relative to the carriage, while the wrist sets the tool presentation. This arrangement puts the scoring routes and endgame into one shared clearance problem: the arm has to stay clear of the bellypan during ordinary motion and lower out of the climber's sweep during endgame.","piece_flow":"The intake pose brings the carriage-mounted grabber to the piece. The common wrist and grabber take the piece through lift and arm motion, then the software selects the position and placement speed for the level. The team describes L1 through L4 coral and processor and net algae; in the interview they narrate a reef coral and a net algae demonstration. The exact floor versus station entry geometry, retention contacts and eject sequence remain unresolved.","packaging_and_motion":"Separate the carriage's vertical travel, arm sweep, wrist motion and powered grabber from the pivoting cage system. The sideways elevator preserves arm access beside the mast, but the arm envelope includes the reef and the bellypan. A replacement belt, wrist zero or carriage repair should therefore be checked in transition as well as at the endpoints. The battery also serves as a packaging and balance constraint in the climb layout.","revisions":["Team describes four arm and grabber design iterations, moving belts inward between the early and fourth designs. The ratchet remained a proposal in the described configuration."],"transferable_principles":["Translate the access objective into a tool path before selecting lift orientation. Protect belts where the tool enters field structure, and allocate a separate tested arm pose for the climber."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Mast-side reach loses value if carriage stiffness or arm clearance makes transitions slow. Gear-only cage holding needs reevaluation if load, lubrication or wear increases backdrive."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact acquisition method, lift rigging, swerve module specification, measured cycle and climb distributions, and later-event hardware chronology."],"recommended_images":["Interview arm chapter at 2:57–3:38 for a candidate side view of the carriage and internal-belt explanation.","Climb chapter at 5:27–5:53 for a candidate image of the cage pivot and arm clearance. Frame content still needs inspection."]}

title: 2019-2910 Jordan complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2019-2910","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","title":"2910 CAD Release 2019","locator":"Posts 5, 7, 9, 12, 18","review_basis":"Read team replies on motor protection, roller contact, HAB supports and cargo-arm gearing.","facts":"Motor guards followed approximately seven NEO clipping failures. The lower roller uses a narrow compliant wheel next to its pulley. A tensioner and keyed/bolted interface reduce output play. The kickstands address overhanging rear wheels and partner loading.","limitations":"Released geometry and practice footage were not inspected."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","title":"2910 CAD Release 2019, PatrickW reply","locator":"Post 28","review_basis":"Read the team response on ground hatches, reveal hardware and bumper mounting.","facts":"Second-generation hatch variants competed from the first event. Ground hatch pickup was used only occasionally because alignment often cost more time than a station trip.","limitations":"No inventory of individual hatch revisions."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2019/359697","title":"Team 2910 Code Release 2019","locator":"Posts 1, 10, 12","review_basis":"Read release and steering-versus-drive controller discussion.","facts":"The release describes vision-assisted hatch alignment. Steering Spark MAX units used PWM, drive controllers CAN for integrated encoder feedback.","limitations":"The team did not verify the proposed PWM latency advantage."},{"url":"https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe","title":"2019CompetitionRobot-Public","locator":"137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe, CargoGrabberDefaultCommand, HatchPlacerSubsystem, GrabHatchFromFloorPart1/2Command, ClimbCommand and ClimberSubsystem","review_basis":"Read Java from pinned public checkout.","facts":"Cargo commands distinguish intake, centering, hold and target-specific ejection. Floor pickup commands rotate and transfer to the placer. The climb macro combines pitch correction, drivetrain, solenoids and the bottom cargo roller.","limitations":"Static inspection only. Commands do not certify event configuration, physical geometry or successful execution."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Jordan separates cargo, hatch and HAB duties on a four-module swerve chassis. Cargo uses an angular arm and dual rollers. The station-facing hatch placer can also receive a hatch from a separate floor gatherer. The endgame uses a climb actuator and kickstands plus drivetrain and roller coordination. The architecture gives operators distinct paths for the two game pieces, with floor hatch pickup reserved for situations where the loading stations are occupied or a favorable pickup presents itself.","piece_flow":["Cargo is drawn between rollers, centered using beam-break feedback and carried by the arm. The pinned code requests 0.06 upper output with zero lower output when centered at the commanded pose, and different roller commands for rocket and front cargo ship ejection.","The station approach can use vision and the placer checks either of two limit switches. For a floor hatch, the first command retracts the placer and lowers the gatherer. The second raises the gatherer to a 90-degree target, extends and closes the placer, briefly reverses the gatherer, then stows and retracts."],"packaging_and_motion":"Guarding the swerve openings adds a collision reaction path near the NEOs. The lower roller drive pulley consumes axial room needed by a normal full-width wheel. During HAB parking, front contacts and a rear support replace the rear wheels as they overhang the platform, and partner load can act at the front bumpers.","subsystems":[{"name":"Swerve and bumper mounting","construction":"Four wheels, protected NEO locations at bumper cutouts, chassis standoffs and captured 1/4-20 bumper fasteners.","operation":"Drive encoder feedback returns over CAN for odometry. Steering commands use PWM and roboRIO control.","team_rationale":"Guards addressed recurring motor clipping. Captive fasteners support repeatable bumper changes.","engineering_analysis":"A guard needs a stiff load path and a deflection margin to the motor throughout the module sweep.","interfaces":"Bumper wood transfers load to its 1 × 1 frame, then to spacers and threaded chassis standoffs.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bent guards and trapped fasteners after contact; retain tool access past the guard.","unknowns":"Impact load cases and calibrated travel.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2019/359697"]},{"name":"Cargo arm and rollers","construction":"Arm gearbox with long chain run, inline tensioner and keyed/bolted sprocket-to-gear hub. Lower pulley shares roller width with a narrow compliant wheel.","operation":"Beam states and arm pose determine drive, centering and soft hold. The code changes roller bias at the rocket because cargo could ride up the target.","team_rationale":"The team prioritizes backlash near the output and limits current while stalled in hold.","engineering_analysis":"Output lost motion multiplied by arm reach shifts the contact point. Centring confidence should be distinguished from detection by one beam.","interfaces":"Roller contact width, target approach and arm angle set ejection behavior.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect chain tension, hub fasteners and optical alignment; a false beam condition can drive a stall.","unknowns":"Loaded endpoint error and retained force.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]},{"name":"Hatch system","construction":"Floor gatherer and placer with distinct extension, gripper and placement solenoid outputs, plus two limit switches.","operation":"The floor gatherer rotates the hatch into the extended placer's capture zone. Station pickup avoids the extra transfer.","team_rationale":"Team reports the floor system was alignment-sensitive; the competition design replaced the reveal's wheeled hatch tool.","engineering_analysis":"A timer after grab does not establish possession. Verify overlap through partial capture before reversing the gatherer.","interfaces":"Hatch presentation angle, gatherer axis and placer stroke define the transfer pose.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect switches, gatherer stow and hose paths. Partial seating can appear valid on one switch.","unknowns":"Finger geometry and version-specific clearances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2019/359697","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]},{"name":"HAB climb and supports","construction":"Code declares separate climber and kickstand solenoids. Team describes rear support plus two forward supports.","operation":"The climb macro requests extension, forward drive, bottom roller and pitch correction together. Supports hold bumpers above the platform with rear wheels off.","team_rationale":"Forward supports were added for sharing HAB3 with 1323 in practice.","engineering_analysis":"Analyze transitions and partner reactions at the support polygon, including partial deployment.","interfaces":"The bumper and chassis carry partner contact loads. Pitch control depends on attitude sensing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Confirm support deployment before adding partner load. Protect lines and valves from chassis contact.","unknowns":"Main actuator dimensions, qualified loads and deployment verification.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]}],"revisions":["Guard structure added after the first event. Reveal hatch design changed before competition. Front kickstand supports were added for shared-climb practice at championship."],"transferable_principles":["Design ejection for target entry geometry, and size output backlash from endpoint error. Treat floor pickup as a match-time choice that competes with driving to a station."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The rare floor recovery may not justify a separate gatherer if it takes more time than queueing. Overhang support fails the architecture if bumper loading or partner alignment puts the resultant outside the support polygon."],"remaining_gaps":["No event-specific binary verification, force testing, complete climb load path or dimensioned CAD review."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2019-2910_source.jpg","reason":"Team release render for whole-robot orientation."},{"path":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","reason":"Team bumper section image accompanying the captive-fastener explanation."}]}

title: 2026-2481 Roboteers 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-2481","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc","title":"Team 2481 Roboteers interview","locator":"0:43–1:38 launcher; 2:23–4:16 collector; 4:34–6:34 storage and floor; 6:48–9:13 driving and practice","review_basis":"Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.","facts":["Four-wide shooter uses staged acceleration.","The team added a collector motor after stalls and changed wall supports after catches and racking.","Bump-only travel and loaded gearing were part of the scoring strategy."],"limitations":"Reported 20 BPS and 115 fuel are team claims. The interview does not establish independent capacity or full-match throughput."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Roboteers built a large fuel carrier whose value depended on unloading a useful batch through a wide shooter. The robot traded the trench route for more volume and took the bump with that load. Its collector, hopper walls, feeder and wheel gearing therefore belong in the same design decision. An empty sprint or a bench burst would leave the difficult parts of the architecture untested.","piece_flow":["The wide roller gathers fuel while a relief plate reduces direct bulk pressure on the collector.","Fuel fills the deployable volume and settles onto interlocking floor rollers.","The floor and serial contact stages move fuel into four launch lanes. The top contact conditions fuel entry without requiring another driven roller in that position."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team describes a relatively narrow chassis dimension that makes the direction of bump crossing matter. The larger loaded footprint comes from extending walls. Heavy hardware sits low, but fuel raises the combined center of mass and can surge as the robot starts up the bump. The route must be wide enough to cross on a repeatable heading even when a defender approaches.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and pressure relief","construction":"Three-inch grip-covered intake roller with two motors in the reported later setup. A plate limits fuel weight pressing directly on the intake.","operation":"Keep the intake running while fuel accumulates just inside the mouth.","team_rationale":"The team added the second motor after stall problems.","engineering_analysis":"Separate lack of available torque from an unfavorable contact load. A pressure barrier can prevent bulk inventory from continuously loading a roller intended to accelerate one layer at a time.","interfaces":"The roller opening must stay useful across a wide mouth while walls retract and extend.","service_and_failure_modes":"A pressure-relief feature can become a pinch point if fuel wedges under it. Test new and worn balls while pushing against a full bin.","unknowns":"Precise gaps, currents and endurance data are unresolved.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]},{"name":"Expanding hopper and floor","construction":"Flexible side structure and a roller floor feed the four-wide launch section. The team revised wall support geometry.","operation":"Deploy the hopper for bulk collection. The floor presents lower fuel while the rest of the load settles.","team_rationale":"The team changed supports after racking and catches.","engineering_analysis":"More static volume gives diminishing returns if the added fuel bridges above the floor, spills during travel or takes longer than the active scoring window to clear.","interfaces":"The floor must coexist with electronics and route-clearance requirements. The stowed wall envelope sets bump clearance and access to the drivetrain.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure load retention over repeated crossings and examine where a bent wall first intrudes into the roller path.","unknowns":"The 115-fuel estimate is a source claim under unspecified packing conditions.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]},{"name":"Four-wide launcher","construction":"Multiple accelerator contacts feed a wide launch assembly. A passive upper contact and electric hood actuation are described.","operation":"Build fuel speed over successive contacts, then launch at the selected angle and flywheel speed.","team_rationale":"The extra upper contact improved the entrance without adding a powered roller in that location.","engineering_analysis":"If launch contact force varies by lane, equal speed commands do not imply equal release speed or trajectory. Measure misses by lane and shooter speed recovery during a full burst.","interfaces":"The floor and shooter need equal flow across the width. A single loaded lane can reduce consistency even if the motor has ample total power.","service_and_failure_modes":"Bracket repairs and actuator changes show the value of replacing a high-load mounting point without rebuilding the floor.","unknowns":"Reported BPS lacks a confirmed measurement window and scoring conversion rate.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]},{"name":"Loaded drivetrain and routes","construction":"The team describes custom adjustable-gearing swerve, large wheels and a chassis shaped to cross the bump.","operation":"Approach in the planned direction, climb the obstacle loaded and return to a scoring position.","team_rationale":"The team chose gearing for loaded current and the crossing rather than maximum possible speed.","engineering_analysis":"Compare the obstacle route with the alternative under realistic traffic. More fuel per trip can still lose if repeated turns, beaching or queueing consume the scoring window.","interfaces":"Drive tuning, fuel retention and the approach geometry are coupled. Electrical demand rises when the drivetrain and feeder operate together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test from a partially discharged battery and a poor entry angle. The team credited practice as well as mechanical changes.","unknowns":"No controlled timing across routes, configurations and driver practice levels.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]}],"revisions":["Collector changed from one motor to two after stalling.","Hopper support geometry revised after catches and racking.","Electric hood actuator replaced a pneumatic approach in the reported configuration."],"transferable_principles":["Test a loaded route before choosing gearing or capacity.","Keep intake roller force separate from hopper inventory where practical.","Compare scored fuel per complete cycle, including travel, stalled feeds and misses."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The trench route can reverse the capacity trade if it removes enough defense exposure or travel time.","A smaller hopper can match effective output when the active window or the feeder sets the limit."],"remaining_gaps":["No independent match-by-match cycle sample or controlled comparison of shooter configurations."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2022-2046 Amelia Bearhart complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-2046","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","title":"Behind the Bumpers 2046 Bear Metal | Rapid React","locator":"1:20–4:19 collector and staging, 4:35–5:55 shooter, 6:12–7:56 climb","review_basis":"Read timestamped English transcript of the team interview at Chezy Champs.","facts":["The team reports three pickup surface states, unequal-thickness sacrificial polycarbonate pieces and a complete spare collector.","Ultrasonic detection advances the superstructure a controlled distance and triggers driver vibration. Printed rollers center the poly belts.","Fixed angle reduces mass. Continuous belt telescopes and an inner/outer arm sequence use swing to reach traversal."],"limitations":["The climb speed is a postseason team claim, with no timing distribution or visual audit."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-robot-rapid-react/405155","title":"2046 Robot — Rapid React","locator":"March 9–10, Darren Collins posts 1, 5, 6, 12 and 13","review_basis":"Read team replies in indexed Chief Delphi thread.","facts":["The March intake used printed hubs and urethane belting strips. The fixed hood was set for upper-hub shots from beyond eight feet and could use the launchpad."],"limitations":["Early material details and the stated range boundary apply to the published Wilsonville-era configuration."]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Amelia Bearhart uses a swerve base to position a fixed-heading, fixed-angle upper-hub shooter. Cargo collection and staging are designed around quick recovery after contact and clear feedback about the two-piece load. Four belt-driven telescoping arms give endgame separate contact sets, so the shooter does not have to carry a rung hook.","piece_flow":"At Chezy, a griptape-covered tube and mecanum contacts gather floor cargo and converge it directly into the superstructure. The first cargo advances a controlled distance. On detection of another ball, the existing ball is moved farther up to make room. Controller vibration marks acquisition and the count caps at two. Printed rollers track poly belts through the lift, then feed wheels deliver the cargo into the main shot wheel and backspin contacts. The Limelight gives the drive team a hub reference. Rejection hardware was outside this review.","packaging_and_motion":"Concentrating shot geometry in a fixed package leaves space and mass for the telescopes, while chassis yaw and allowable range carry more of the targeting burden. The outer and inner arm pairs occupy separate engagement geometry. During transfer the hanging robot swings and changes the outer hook trajectory. The useful tolerance includes loaded deflection and dynamics at the release from mid, as well as static reach.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and service joint","construction":"Early printed hubs with belting flaps. At Chezy a smaller griptape tube, mecanum centering and polycarbonate breakaways with a thicker inner piece.","operation":"Drops to pick up and feeds directly to the superstructure. Crew swaps breakaways or the complete spare collector.","team_rationale":"Early flap and Velcro configuration pushed too many balls away. Inner breakaway was thickened because it broke more often.","engineering_analysis":"A deliberate weak joint can protect the downstream frame if the failure load stays above ordinary pickup loads and below the load that bends the frame.","interfaces":"Roller centering, mounting plates and repeatable handoff to lift.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reported swapping the full assembly if breakaway repair would take more than about three minutes. A hard hit can still bend metal plates.","unknowns":"Actual joint failure load and spare swap procedure.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-robot-rapid-react/405155"]},{"name":"Two-ball lift and feedback","construction":"Custom printed tracking rollers, poly belts, ultrasonic sensing and driver controller haptics.","operation":"A detected ball advances the lift a set distance. Detecting the next creates room and updates driver feedback.","team_rationale":"The team describes acquisition notification and limiting held cargo to two.","engineering_analysis":"Distance indexing depends on traction and repeatable sensor placement. Slip can create a mismatch between count and actual stage position.","interfaces":"Collector exit, first/second cargo spacing and shooter feed nip.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking and run a stopped/restarted feed with two worn balls.","unknowns":"Encoder basis, exact detection location and count recovery logic.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM"]},{"name":"Fixed launcher","construction":"Fixed hood and chassis-relative heading, shooter and feed wheels, backspin contacts and Limelight.","operation":"Shoots from a preferred ring around the hub and farther when needed. Chassis provides azimuth.","team_rationale":"Team cited weight and serviceability. Field-house testing provided coverage within the fixed geometry.","engineering_analysis":"Removing hood motion trades an alignment degree of freedom for a more limited shot corridor. Route availability is part of measured shooter throughput.","interfaces":"Lift feed, chassis pose and vision target.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check fixed mount reference and rear-contact wear before retuning distance settings.","unknowns":"Exact exit angle, range-to-speed map and accuracy distribution.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-robot-rapid-react/405155"]},{"name":"Belt telescopes","construction":"Four continuously belt-routed telescoping arms arranged as inner and outer pairs.","operation":"Starts from mid. The inner pair catches high and lifts off mid. Chassis swing brings the outer arms to traversal.","team_rationale":"The team favored belt travel for speed and fewer spring problems, and added two arms to speed the sequence.","engineering_analysis":"Belt timing and hanging dynamics are coupled. A slightly different initial pitch changes the outer hook’s path at the transfer.","interfaces":"Arm hooks, rung loading, belt travel and chassis swing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking, hook closure and left-right asymmetry. Record missed-transfer recovery as well as clean cycles.","unknowns":"Rigging, sensors and onseason vs. Chezy timing changes.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM"]}],"revisions":["Wilsonville-era flap configuration was followed by rubber, then the Chezy small-tube griptape configuration. The March thread already announced traversal. The later sub-three-second claim belongs to the Chezy discussion."],"transferable_principles":["Set the sacrificial joint and changeover procedure together. Evaluate fixed-shot geometry against routes, and compare climbs from approach through retained hang."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The fixed shot loses time when preferred firing lanes are contested. The four-arm speed advantage can reverse if pitch and hook timing require a narrow setup window."],"remaining_gaps":["Module details, two-ball control states, shot consistency under contact and measured climb distribution by version."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","locator":"1:20–4:19 and 6:43–7:56","purpose":"Seek stills of the Chezy breakaways, collector handoff and telescoping arm pairs."}]}

title: 2023-604 2023 published robot (name not independently confirmed) complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-604","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","title":"Quixilver 2023 Robot and Code Release","locator":"Post 1, Strategic Design, Intake, Handoff and Scoring Arm, Code Release","review_basis":"Read the team's written retrospective through the web tool.","facts":"Documents the orientation and translation stages, range-based transfer, scoring linkage and operator role change.","limitations":"Cycle-distance savings are the team's estimate. The post warns that CAD is mirrored from the physical robot."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023","title":"Quixilver FRC-2023 code","locator":"src/main/java/frc/robot/commands/AdjustSliderForMeasure.java, AdjustElevatorXForHandoff.java and HandoffPiece.java","review_basis":"Read the three command implementations in the released 2023 tree.","facts":"The measure pose depends on orientation. The transverse axis clamps and updates its target from filtered range. Handoff commands release, receive, lift and clearance movements.","limitations":"The release also contains a separate beta migration. Code review here uses FRC-2023 and does not establish which build ran at each event."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Quixilver designed its cycle around acquiring ground cones from arbitrary approaches, reducing the need to queue for the double substation. Its floor intake captures first and resolves orientation later. Two translation tasks are distinct: the intake slider pulls the captured piece toward the center of the chassis, and the scoring assembly moves across the roller width to meet its actual lateral location. The four-bar and elevator carry the received piece to the grid. Quixilver believed a single extra cycle could matter in a close match and reported an estimated 40 percent reduction in trip distance for the single-substation route they analyzed.","piece_flow":"Opposed intake rollers grab a cone flange or pinch a cube. Cone capture collapses many floor angles into two cases, tip in or tip out. The software uses a distance comparison at a prescribed geometry to choose the orientation case. The roller assembly rotates the piece upright for the exchange, and the intake slider brings the piece inward. Another filtered distance reading determines the cross-chassis handoff position. At the meeting point the elevator lowers the receiving gripper, the intake rollers expel and the gripper receives. The handoff command also lifts toward a post-transfer height, pulls the arm toward its minimum angle and commands the appropriate slider clearance. The same gripper pinches cubes or grips cones near the tip and rides the scoring assembly to the chosen level.","packaging_and_motion":"Roller drive crosses the reorienter pivot coaxially so the motors can be placed away from the vulnerable outside edge. Intake fore-aft slider motion creates a capture-to-transfer stroke and provides some compliance in head-on contact. Cross-chassis motion solves a separate offset along the rollers. The code clips its lateral target to the axis limits and revises it if filtered piece position moves enough during alignment. Inference: the achievable handoff region is the intersection of the two axes' travel, sensor view, intake release geometry and gripper compliance.","subsystems":[{"name":"Floor intake and reorienter","construction":"Pasta-style paired rollers, powered rotating roller assembly and linear intake slider. Roller power passes through the reorienter coaxially.","operation":"The rollers grip the piece and constrain cone direction to one of two states. The rotating assembly makes a pose suitable for transfer.","team_rationale":"Quixilver sought ground acquisition regardless of cone orientation, with the motor mass and exposure reduced at the intake's leading edge.","engineering_analysis":"The two-state assumption is valuable only if skewed cones settle into one of those states with predictable range readings.","interfaces":"Coaxial transmission crosses a moving pivot. Slider alignment fixes the receiver's fore-aft and height window.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect slider travel after frontal contact. Test roller grip and range separation with folded flanges, soft cubes and parts shifted by impact.","unknowns":"Roller materials, exact reductions and capture probability by approach angle.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]},{"name":"Sensing, cross-slide and transfer","construction":"Time-of-flight ranging, powered transverse scoring slide, vertical elevator and coordinated transfer commands.","operation":"Orientation selects the measurement pose. Filtered range plus an offset sets the lateral position. Roller release and receiving commands overlap as the system clears the exchange.","team_rationale":"The lateral slider was added because the piece can land anywhere across the roller span. The team wanted handoff across that span.","engineering_analysis":"A clamped axis target can still be unreachable for the jaw. Test the edges for transfer completion, not just encoder arrival.","interfaces":"Sensor line of sight couples piece geometry to axis position. The gripper, elevator, arm and intake are all command requirements during handoff.","service_and_failure_modes":"After replacing sensors or guides, verify tip-in/out readings and transverse offset. Try an interrupted exchange with a half-seated piece.","unknowns":"Drop detection and recovery rates, precise sensor mounting and calibration tolerances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]},{"name":"Scoring linkage and operator interface","construction":"Non-parallel four-bar with an Everybot-style roller gripper on the elevating assembly. The original driver-station keyboard selected scoring location.","operation":"The linkage extends to the mid and high rows. The driver later aligned manually while the operator selected piece type and row.","team_rationale":"The team chose the linkage for reach and lower weight. It reports the driver eventually outperformed the automatic location-scoring sequence.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate both manual and automatic release against total time and repeatability once the drive team has practiced. Tip grip makes cone attitude sensitive to contact slip.","interfaces":"Four-bar, elevator and transverse slide stack loads between the claw and chassis.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check joint play at extended poses and verify that a slipped cone still clears the node during retract.","unknowns":"Arm transmission, grid clearance under load and measured manual-versus-automatic performance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]}],"revisions":["The team chose the pasta roller after testing other roller intakes. The driver-operator split shifted from target selection plus automatic scoring to manual alignment with operator piece and level selection."],"transferable_principles":["Reduce many initial piece orientations to a few stable sensed states. Use independent axes for independent handoff errors when the cycle savings justify the control work."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The strategy weakens if single-substation feed is inconsistent, range estimates overlap for malformed pieces or alignment and retries consume the saved travel time."],"remaining_gaps":["Matched cycle-time trials, deployment chronology, full transmission specifications and end-to-end acquisition and recovery measurements."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"Intake and Handoff and Scoring Arm sections","subject":"Candidate team views of coaxial drive, deployed slider and lateral alignment. Explicitly label mirrored CAD."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2018-971 Curiosity complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-971","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","title":"971’s 2018 Robot Overview, Sabina Davis and Annie Wang","locator":"Physical slides 3–24","review_basis":"Re-read extracted slide text and inspected rendered workshop pages.","facts":"Slides specify separate proximal chain and distal cable drives, spring-deflection feedback for the intake, and separate hanger and partner-lift assemblies.","limitations":"Slides show two lift versions without a dated installation sequence. No narration or CAD reviewed."},{"url":"https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf","title":"Spartan Robotics FRC 971 Technical Documentation 2018","locator":"Robot Overview, Function Objectives, Intake, Claw, Arm and Lift Prototyping","review_basis":"Read team-authored binder on public mirror.","facts":"The team wanted front/rear scoring. Intake geometry presents a cube at 45 degrees. The claw was shortened after snagging the cube zipper flap. The team moved from aluminum prototype links to carbon fiber.","limitations":"Overview abbreviates drive and arm details. Its low-gear speed differs from the workshop, and the lift prototype image load is not a full-system rating."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Curiosity uses two independently controlled arm joints and a compact claw for front or rear placement, with the chassis-mounted intake taking responsibility for floor alignment. This decouples a tough floor contact from a light scoring endpoint, while making the intake-to-claw transfer critical. A separate hanger and partner-support fork share packaging with the scoring arm. The approach targets rapid, accurate stacking with the robot facing either direction, which requires joint control through a wide workspace.","piece_flow":["Opposed webbed wheels draw in the cube and present it at a nominal 45-degree orientation. A rear/center beam break reports a suitable location, while two additional intake beam breaks address stuck scenarios.","The double-jointed arm presents its claw to the aligned cube. The claw closes with remote pneumatic actuation and has its own beam break. Once the claw has possession, joint motion carries the cube to a placement pose. The reviewed documents do not specify exact overlap timing or release interlocks."],"packaging_and_motion":"The clamshell chassis carries the arm and hanger gearbox close to the base. The chain-driven proximal link and cable-driven distal link extend in a common working plane. Pneumatic cylinders are tucked into the distal link and two air tanks into the proximal link. Low distal inertia helps acceleration, but internal packaging makes line routing, attachment inspection and field replacement consequential.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drivetrain","construction":"Six 5-inch Colsons, belt-driven clamshell layout with dead axles and a two-speed ball shifter.","operation":"Workshop lists 9.1 and 16.7 ft/s for low and high and identifies encoder, gyro, IMU and potentiometer signals in a state-space drive controller.","team_rationale":"The binder emphasizes maneuverability to avoid defense.","engineering_analysis":"Grip, shift timing and raised arm mass all affect path following. The binder gives different rounded speed figures, with low gear listed at 11 ft/s.","interfaces":"Belt tensioners, wheel pulleys and modular gearboxes share access with chassis electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect bonded pulley interfaces and tension before blaming steering error on estimation.","unknowns":"Cause of speed discrepancy and loaded shift behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]},{"name":"Series-elastic floor intake","construction":"Four-inch webbed Fairlane wheels, pivot gearboxes with series elasticity, magnetic spring encoder, absolute encoder, potentiometer, beam breaks and LIDAR.","operation":"The pivot loop incorporates measured spring deflection. Roller geometry and sensing align the cube for the claw.","team_rationale":"Prototype oscillations and a desire for active intake angle led the team to put an actuator in series with the spring.","engineering_analysis":"Deflection is meaningful only with known spring behavior and calibrated limits. Control must distinguish intentional contact from blocked motion.","interfaces":"The arm can acquire consistently only across the residual yaw and position spread at the floor intake.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check encoder zero, spring travel limits and a stalled cube with a blocked beam.","unknowns":"Spring stiffness, force limits and automatic recovery logic.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]},{"name":"Two-link arm and claw","construction":"Carbon fiber tubes and CNC joints, proximal chain, distal cable, dedicated motors in a shared gearbox and disk brake. Printed claw body uses pulley-and-string actuation from hidden pistons.","operation":"Arm profiles independently drive joints, while the claw converts cylinder motion into linear grasp. A claw beam monitors the piece.","team_rationale":"Early aluminum links were structurally inadequate. Pulley actuation reduced claw package and inertia, and shorter fingers reduced zipper jams at the cost of some control.","engineering_analysis":"Joint angle error and compliance translate into endpoint error according to configuration. With crossed workspace and a retained cube, verify the sweep around mast, intake and bumpers.","interfaces":"Claw shape must accept the oriented cube. Capstan anchoring and guide stiffness govern distal position repeatability.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope preload, bonded inserts and air lines; test zipper snag and beam false positives.","unknowns":"Joint gains, load limits and exact arm motor designation given the overview's different shorthand.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]},{"name":"Hanger and partner lift","construction":"Separate hook, two 775pros for the hanger in the combined gearbox, proximal-tube winch-line exit, spring-deployed partner fork with expansion stage.","operation":"The hanger loads the robot through the winch system. Fork deployment enlarges the partner's boarding area, and its low-friction underside permits exchange traffic.","team_rationale":"The team wanted a balanced quick hang with an alliance robot.","engineering_analysis":"Changing partner position changes fork bending and the moment around the hoist line. The historical prototype load label cannot qualify the competed system.","interfaces":"Hook, winch, chassis and partner support require independent attachment and retention checks.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify latching, unintended movement and release under asymmetric load.","unknowns":"Load rating, version differences and event use.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Intake prototypes evolved through wheel compliance and spring-actuated pivot changes. Arm moved from aluminum to carbon fiber. The wider claw was shortened following fabric snags. Slides identify V1 and V2 partner lifts without dates."],"transferable_principles":["Separate piece orientation from placement reach. Use a specific failure such as a fabric snag to decide finger length, and verify the remaining retention margin afterward."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The separate intake loses value if the claw cannot accept the pickup pose distribution. A two-link arm loses its packaging advantage if stiffness and collision margins require heavy reinforcement."],"remaining_gaps":["No complete rigging and fork load qualification, event chronology or narrated workshop review."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2018-971_p11.jpg","reason":"Carbon fiber links and transmission split."},{"path":"images/history_2018-971_p22.jpg","reason":"Intake pivot series elasticity."},{"path":"images/history_2018-971_p24.jpg","reason":"Different partner-lift views."}]}

title: 2018-1610 Cotton J complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-1610","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf","title":"Blackwater Robotics 2018 Cotton J Technical Binder, rev. 2","locator":"Physical pp. 5, 7–13","review_basis":"Team PDF text re-read from the downloaded original, cross-checked against web extraction.","facts":"The prototype program converged on a compliant-wheel intake with pneumatic pressure control. Motor sweep forced the elevator to narrow to 13 inches and required custom R4 bearing mounts. The finished climb reused the elevator, added a second motor and gearbox, and used a pneumatic locking pin. The gearbox arrangement reclaimed approximately eight inches of interior space.","limitations":"Binder describes the built design and selected changes. It provides no event-by-event build record or independent test results."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Cotton J uses a single cube-handling assembly on a two-stage elevator. That assembly must reach the floor, retain the cube during lift and release, rotate upright to stow, and present a climb hook. The team's priorities put pickup and drive first and climb last, partly because Levitate could supply a climb credit. Reuse kept a late climb within a tight weight budget but brought the intake's structure into the robot-weight load path.","piece_flow":["The floor pickup uses compliant wheels to pull in a cube presented on either its wide or narrow side. Pneumatic pressure keeps contact when one wheel encounters the fabric-covered open face.","Once captured, the cube stays with the lift-mounted intake as the carriage moves from pickup to the selected scoring height. The same wheel interface is available for release. Binder descriptions establish the shared pickup and placement assembly, while release commands and possession sensing are unspecified."],"packaging_and_motion":"The 28-inch-long by 32-inch-wide frame grew wider to fit the intake, even as the mast was narrowed to clear the intake motors through the vertical flip. External wheels, chain runs inside the frame tubes, and flipped motors recover central width for the working envelope. The geometry must be checked at intermediate flip angles and across elevator positions, particularly near wiring and any intake pressure lines.","subsystems":[{"name":"Six-wheel West Coast drivetrain","construction":"2 × 1.5-inch rails enclose chains from the driven center axle to front and rear axles. A custom gearbox developed with 2363 puts Mini-CIMs over the wheels. Flipping the Versa Block orientation creates a small center drop.","operation":"One Talon SRX leads two Victor SPX followers per side. Quadrature feedback goes to the master, and voltage compensation caps full command at 10.5 V.","team_rationale":"The team wanted useful turning and platform clearance while maximizing room for mechanisms. Mini-CIMs let the folded gearbox stay inside the perimeter.","engineering_analysis":"Enclosed chain routing trades central volume for visibility and tool access. Exhaust routed through 5/32-inch inlets and vented motor bolts may cool motors intermittently, depending on cylinder activity.","interfaces":"Rail bore alignment sets chain tracking. Wheel clearance, gearbox body and bumper brackets share the side envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Plan for chain replacement and motor access with the intake installed. The binder itself flags difficult chain maintenance.","unknowns":"Chain tension limits, temperature benefit and measured speed under load.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]},{"name":"Pivoting cube intake","construction":"Green compliant wheels on powered arms, with belts and pulleys internal to the tubing. Pneumatic cylinders apply pressure to the cube. The arms were changed to plastic tubing.","operation":"Wheels draw the cube between the arms. Arm pressure maintains contact while the cube faces present different dimensions and stiffness. The assembly flips upright for hook presentation.","team_rationale":"Wheel testing and a wood prototype helped tune the intake for both cube orientations and the loose fabric on the open face. Inboard belt routing reduced package thickness.","engineering_analysis":"Grip should tolerate uneven compression without rotating the cube out of the intake. Internal pulleys and lighter arms improve envelope and mass but concentrate bearing, wear and repair requirements in the arm.","interfaces":"Elevator carriage takes the intake mount and vertical pivot; wheel motors sweep next to the uprights. Hook loads enter the underside during climb.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pulley alignment, buried belts, arm joints and hook attachment. A soft fabric panel can increase compression without proportionally increasing retention.","unknowns":"Pivot actuator details, working pressure, roller speeds, grip forces and release sensing.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]},{"name":"Elevator and integrated climb","construction":"Two-stage mast in 2 × 1-inch aluminum with custom R4 linear bearing mounts. Two 2 × 1 tubing hooks are beneath the intake. A pneumatic pin locks the elevator.","operation":"The intake rotates upright and the elevator raises the hooks above the bar. The reused lift drive takes robot weight with the added motor and gearbox. The pin is the documented backdrive countermeasure.","team_rationale":"With about ten pounds remaining, the team rejected the separate winch gearbox and a more complicated tape-measure hook deployment.","engineering_analysis":"Treat bar capture, load transfer and locking as distinct events. The carriage, pivot, hook joint and mast guides see climb loads with a different magnitude and direction from scoring.","interfaces":"Bar to hooks to intake structure to elevator and chassis. The pin must line up under the actual loaded deflection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check pin engagement and support before releasing motor torque. Inspect guide binding and hook load symmetry.","unknowns":"Rigging topology, pin engagement sensing and validated climb capacity.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Wooden intake prototype preceded metal packaging and then lighter plastic tubing. The frame grew wider for the intake while the mast narrowed for its flip. The second elevator motor and locking pin were additions for climb."],"transferable_principles":["Budget the swept envelope jointly across modules before freezing either chassis width or mast section. Reuse an actuator for climb only after accounting for the full structural and holding path."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Reject this arrangement if cube compression requires more width than remains between the rails, or if a loaded mast cannot repeatedly align and positively engage the lock."],"remaining_gaps":["No verified event installation dates, climb test trace, detailed carriage rigging drawing or intake controls."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2018-1610_p9.jpg","reason":"Cube intake prototype and contact concept."},{"path":"images/history_2018-1610_p11.jpg","reason":"Narrowed mast and custom bearing guides."},{"path":"images/history_2018-1610_p12.jpg","reason":"Intake hook and elevator lock arrangement."}]}

title: 2026-1114 Simbot Tim complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-1114","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY","title":"Team 1114 Simbotics interview","locator":"0:35–1:19 collector; 1:58–2:27 retracting kicker; 3:06–4:24 floor and feeder; 4:34–6:08 route and controls","review_basis":"Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.","facts":["Collector and kicker feed an extending hopper.","Side agitators, floor rollers and a rising feeder form separate transitions.","A kicker originally stayed out and was linked to hopper retraction."],"limitations":"The interview reports roughly 80 fuel and a bump-oriented strategy. It does not provide measured inventory or full competition CAD."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Simbotics used a tall hopper and a drum shooter to carry and discharge a large batch. The route choice was tied to the physical system. The robot used the bump, which meant the collector, kicker and extension had to retract predictably before travel. The important engineering work is in the transitions between the intake, floor and rising feed. Each change either removed a dead spot or reduced the chance that the robot would be stuck in a geometry the driver could not use.","piece_flow":["The collector and lower kicker deliver fuel into the expanding hopper.","Side agitators loosen packed fuel and guide it toward the powered floor. Passive rollers occupy some spaces where fuel had stalled.","A compliant feeder forces fuel into the rising roller section. That section supplies the drum shooter at the height and approach it needs."],"packaging_and_motion":"The hopper, kicker and collector share the front envelope. Retraction folds the kicker as the hopper returns. This mechanical dependency can simplify operator commands, but the deployed geometry must still remain robust under a partially filled or deformed bin. A tall loaded hopper changes visibility, impact loading and the response of the chassis on the bump.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and folding kicker","construction":"The main roller and kicker send fuel up into the hopper. The kicker retracts with linked hopper motion.","operation":"Deploy for acquisition. Retract the hopper to fold the kicker before crossing.","team_rationale":"The earlier kicker could drop and stay extended. The linked version addresses that route problem.","engineering_analysis":"A mechanical dependency avoids requiring a separately timed command. The design still needs hard stops and enough freedom to retract with debris or misalignment.","interfaces":"The folded kicker must clear the frame and loaded hopper. The collector can also become a contact point during recovery from an obstacle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check partial stow after a hit and a stalled extension actuator. Look for a positive indication that the route envelope has been restored.","unknowns":"No exact linkage dimensions or clearance tolerance in the interview.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]},{"name":"Hopper and powered floor","construction":"Extending storage supplies a rolling floor with side agitators and passive contact elements.","operation":"Use agitation to move fuel out of side and rear dead spots and into the floor’s direction of travel.","team_rationale":"The team added passive rollers and high-grip surfaces after finding collection dead spots.","engineering_analysis":"The floor cannot pull fuel that is supported by its neighbors above the active contacts. Side agitation can destabilize a bridge while avoiding a steep drop or additional transfer.","interfaces":"Wall and floor positions must maintain a usable exit at all fill levels. A twisted belt drive couples motions and imposes belt routing constraints.","service_and_failure_modes":"Use a transparent mockup to locate stationary fuel during sustained output. Check belt tracking after impact and compare full with nearly empty behavior.","unknowns":"No measured live inventory or jam rate.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]},{"name":"Up-feed and drum","construction":"A compliant-wheel feeder drives fuel into a belt-coupled rising roller path and drum launcher.","operation":"Capture the floor output, raise the stream and place fuel into the launch contact.","team_rationale":"Added grip helped drive fuel down into the feed entrance.","engineering_analysis":"The most consequential gap may be a transition before the shooter, even when the shooter has ample acceleration. The rise should control the piece rather than counting on the next roller to recover a bouncing feed.","interfaces":"The floor angle, feeder nip and rising path need matched speeds and overlapping control.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch for a stalled feed wheel under bulk pressure and whether reversing can clear the same path without backing the hopper up.","unknowns":"Exact shooter angle, reductions and current limits unresolved.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]},{"name":"Driving and operator controls","construction":"The team describes multi-camera localization and intake states that change agitation behavior.","operation":"Stage the robot for scoring, signal readiness and use the known bump route with the hopper stowed as needed.","team_rationale":"The team selected the bump and a drum design for its expected traffic and preferred play.","engineering_analysis":"More inventory shifts the choice toward fewer trips. Driving around defense and aligning from a useful heading can still dominate the cycle.","interfaces":"Localization, vehicle heading and feed-ready logic determine whether a full mechanism produces a timely scoring burst.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a bad localization update, blocked route and beach recovery with a loaded bin.","unknowns":"No independent telemetry for shot pose, ready-state accuracy or route times.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]}],"revisions":["Kicker retraction was linked to the hopper.","Passive contacts and additional grip addressed fuel dead spots."],"transferable_principles":["Link motions when they always need to occur together and the combined mechanism still has a reliable fallback.","Treat floor-to-shooter transitions as distinct from theoretical launch capacity."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Independent actuation is useful when one mechanism must stay deployed while the other retracts.","A low-volume trench design can win the route trade where a loaded bump approach repeatedly loses time."],"remaining_gaps":["As-built layout, loaded crossing margins, distributions of sustained scoring rate and jam recovery."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2024-9483 Snapfire complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-9483","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.frc9483.com/robots","title":"Team 9483 Robots","locator":"2024 Snapfire section","review_basis":"Team publication read; separately inspected full-resolution portrait.","facts":["Identifies Snapfire and records the Bosphorus and Marmara regional wins and Milstein division win."],"limitations":"Season summary gives results; the portrait supplies geometry at one pose."},{"url":"https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","title":"Snapfire team portrait","locator":"Central roller stack and side plates above numbered bumpers","review_basis":"Direct visual review of team photograph.","facts":["Two thick, spaced roller contact regions per shaft across two prominent levels; multiple narrower transverse rollers behind and above; side pulley/belt and chain elements visible."],"limitations":"Exterior only. Dark areas, overlapping hardware and one parked pose prevent a complete part or transmission count."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg","title":"FIRST Updates Now 9483 interview announcement photographs","locator":"Post 153 image, especially lower-left view","review_basis":"Direct visual review of two published photos, cross-checked against team portrait.","facts":["Orange note visible among the roller structures, above clear panels; lower front module hardware and two inclined bars visible."],"limitations":"Still photos have no sequence or electrical identification. The linked interview captions returned HTTP 429 and interview content was unavailable."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Snapfire packages several levels of note-contact hardware into a tall assembly over a low drivebase. The team portrait establishes the separation between a wide upper roller assembly and larger paired contact surfaces facing out from a lower level. The pit photograph shows that an actual note can occupy the intervening volume. The architecture is best read as linked acquisition, controlled transport and launch problems: each interface must keep the note supported until the next contact takes over. The visible stack and protected deck are stronger evidence than any specific automatic scoring sequence.","piece_flow":"The reviewed stills establish a note position inside the upper/central mechanism and show the clear deck beneath it. They cannot establish which shafts run during that state or whether the note is staged there for Amp or Speaker. The corpus associates the upper assembly with articulated pickup and a bent transfer, then sensor-based staging and selection between Amp and shooter. Those are prior leads for verification. Mechanically, a bent path must control the rim at the entrance and at the last driven nip so that incoming orientation does not dictate exit orientation.","packaging_and_motion":"The portrait puts the main moving assemblies above the bumper line, with metal drive hardware still visible low at the corners. Long inclined members bracket the roller area from the frame up to the vertical structure. Their fixed geometry in both stills constrains the space available to a swinging arm or roller group. The clear panels shown from above lie close to the deck; they also keep loose objects and notes away from parts of the lower bay if the edges remain covered. Hinge axes, travel and electronics locations require different views.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and transfer","construction":"Several transverse rollers are visible in the upper assembly; the pit image exposes clear side material and a white transverse roller near the note.","operation":"Visible contacts give the ring successive surfaces along its width. Its direction through them and which are driven are unresolved in the stills.","team_rationale":"No collector design rationale in the reviewed team season text.","engineering_analysis":"Spanning the note width gives room for an off-center capture, but a flexible ring can cock if one rim reaches the next nip first. Compression should be measured with the arm loaded.","interfaces":"Outer roller to inner roller, then the clear guide and the launcher throat; guide edge height controls whether the leading rim dives below the next contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide edges and roller traction after impacts. Witness marks on one guide wall can reveal a biased feed before it becomes a jam.","unknowns":"Roller count, material, deployment geometry and drive routing from the old synopsis remain unconfirmed.","source_urls":["https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg"]},{"name":"Launcher and angular positioning","construction":"Two conspicuous upper/lower shafts carry paired, thick, textured contact bands. The side transmission is visible, but exact rotation direction and assignment of each drive element remain unknown.","team_rationale":"The reviewed primary photo supplies geometry only.","engineering_analysis":"A split left/right contact surface can feed a flexible ring asymmetrically if it is off center; check exit yaw and speed at multiple lateral offsets before adjusting a range map.","interfaces":"The upstream note position defines first contact; the frame-side transmission and its supports define how repeatably the exit direction can be held.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare physical release direction with commanded angle after side transmission service, especially at opposite ends of travel.","unknowns":"Pivot range, feedback, wheel speeds, and ready-to-fire logic require primary verification.","source_urls":["https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg"]},{"name":"Base and endgame packaging","construction":"The portrait shows front corner drive hardware below the roller frame, inclined supports and two upright side structures.","operation":"Drive hardware carries the moving upper assembly. title: 2024-359 Poi Pounder XXV complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-359","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2024-robot-reveal/455664","title":"FRC Team 359 2024 Robot Reveal","locator":"February 22, team post 1","review_basis":"Read primary team reveal post and identified its embedded video.","facts":["Team thanks 2910 for design inspiration. Reveal identifies the robot as Poi Pounder XXV."],"limitations":"The post does not assign individual design features to the inspiration."},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","title":"Poi Pounder XXV — Team 359 2024 Robot Reveal","locator":"0:06, 0:13–0:20, 0:27–0:29, 0:56–1:11","review_basis":"Visually reviewed the team video’s public storyboard at roughly one-second intervals.","facts":["Shows low approach to a ground note, loaded low and raised poses, a head reaching toward a practice wall opening, and a suspended chassis by the practice Stage."],"limitations":"Edited practice montage and sampled frames. No cycle timing or event reliability implied."},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4","title":"Behind the Bumpers — 359 Hawaiian Kids","locator":"1:24–2:13, 2:38–3:23, 4:12–5:20, 8:52–9:57","review_basis":"Visually inspected sampled pit interview and demonstration frames, about five seconds apart.","facts":["Wide tubular rollers and a clear guide hold an orange note below the paired wheel rows. Separate close-ups show chain and sprockets near the shoulder, nested perforated arm members, and a raised end assembly."],"limitations":"Caption request returned HTTP 429. Spoken explanations, exact reduction and sensors were not verified."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Poi Pounder XXV puts a roller-guided pickup and opposing-wheel launcher on an elevated moving assembly. That arrangement carries the ring away from the floor and up toward an elevated scoring opening without requiring a long deck-level conveyor. The reveal shows the mechanism in low pickup, angled launch and extended poses and includes a suspended Stage setup. The system must preserve control of the note while the drivebase and the arm are both changing attitude. The published interview images explain that mechanical problem well even without exact joint control settings.","piece_flow":"In the reveal, the robot approaches a floor ring with the outer rollers low. The pit demonstration shows a ring held across two tubular rollers, in front of a clear guide leading toward the paired launch wheel rows. A later demonstration shows the ring closer to those wheels. This supports a short transfer within the moving assembly, with the caveat that the stills do not establish the command sequence or powered contacts. Practice frames show the same head presenting a note at a wall opening and toward the Stage. A shooter shot depends on leaving the opposed wheel nip at speed, whereas a close placement depends more on head position and retention until the outlet reaches the opening.","packaging_and_motion":"An A-frame-like support rises out of a low chassis and the arm moves above a densely packaged deck. Close-ups show a wide shoulder region with chain drive elements and a perforated member moving within the arm structure. The arm-end package has its own visible side plates and pulley hardware. The Stage pose occupies a much larger envelope than normal driving. A critical interference check is the sweep of the loaded head and cable loops through the upright supports, chain and adjacent field structure.","subsystems":[{"name":"Arm-end collector and note guide","construction":"Two prominent full-width tubular rollers, clear guide surfaces and side plates; the orange ring is visible across the roller opening.","operation":"Low arm poses bring the roller opening to the carpet. The guide and rollers support the ring until the opposing wheel rows can take it.","team_rationale":"The team reveal demonstrates several uses of the head. The specific reason for avoiding a separate Amp handoff remains a prior interview lead.","engineering_analysis":"Retention depends on contact continuity as the arm accelerates. A guide wide enough for acquisition must still prevent the ring from migrating into one-sided launch contact.","interfaces":"Collector rollers and guide lead into the flywheel opening on the moving head. Their relative alignment must survive head motion and impacts.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide mounting and roller-to-roller gap after floor contact, then test note retention with the head sweeping through its normal pitch range.","unknowns":"Driven versus passive roller assignments, compression and detection sensors.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]},{"name":"Launcher and moving arm","construction":"The top/bottom wheel rows have visibly unequal lateral wheel coverage. Nested members and shoulder sprockets are visible in the interview images.","operation":"Shoulder motion changes presentation angle. The arm also reaches farther in the practice scoring poses than in the floor pose.","team_rationale":"Team credits 2910 broadly. The claimed choice to eliminate an extension stage awaits a readable primary account.","engineering_analysis":"A longer reach increases leverage on the shoulder and magnifies angular play at the outlet. Unequal wheel coverage may affect spin and lateral sensitivity, but the intended effect was not established here.","interfaces":"Shoulder transmission, sliding members and end assembly all contribute to exit position. Route the head harness for the combined angular and extension limits.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check shoulder play under load, cable strain near the nested members and contact symmetry on a centered note.","unknowns":"Actuators, reeving, travel, launch settings and whether or how wheel spin was tuned.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2024-robot-reveal/455664","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]},{"name":"Drivebase and Stage interface","construction":"Low rectangular base with corner module hardware, upright structure and protruding endgame hardware visible in practice.","operation":"Reveal frames around the Stage show a raised head and the base lifted off the floor during the same montage.","team_rationale":"No chain-load rationale established by the reviewed text.","engineering_analysis":"A repeatable suspended pose matters because the Trap opening fixes the outlet location independently of robot coordinate zero.","interfaces":"Chain engagement and chassis reaction determine reach to the opening. A note can remain in the head while this geometry changes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the suspension contact and arm position after a skewed engagement before judging placement consistency.","unknowns":"Module variant, chain attachment load path and field alignment logic.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]}],"revisions":["February reveal and later pit frames show low and raised states of the same general layout. No dated hardware change was verified."],"transferable_principles":["Evaluate retention in the moving head under acceleration, not just in a stationary handoff test.","Measure outlet pose under the real chain-supported load case."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If guide compliance allows the note to skew during fast articulation, the short transfer can still misfeed.","If Stage swing moves the outlet beyond the opening tolerance, static extension reach is insufficient."],"remaining_gaps":["Primary speech or code is still needed for extension-stage rationale, camera functions, control parameters and competition climb changes."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4&t=163","subject":"Loaded collector and launcher wheel spacing"},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4&t=119","subject":"Shoulder transmission and deck clearance"},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968&t=66","subject":"Practice Stage pose and extension"}]}
