text: {"robot_id":"2018-254","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.thebluealliance.com/team/254/2018","title":"Team 254 official and offseason match records","locator":"2018 season and event tables","review_basis":"Read results and reconcile the four official event subtotals","facts":"53–0–0 in official play. Arizona North 15–0, Silicon Valley 15–0, Hopper 16–0 and Einstein 7–0. Overall 94–6–0 includes offseason.","limitations":"Alliance results do not isolate an individual robot or mechanism."},{"url":"https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/","title":"Team 254 season page","locator":"Specifications and event results","review_basis":"Team publication","facts":"The six-wheel drive, pass-through lift, wristed acquisition and partner forks are central to the published design.","limitations":"Exact deployment and changes require an event-specific source."},{"url":"https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","title":"Lockdown technical binder","locator":"PDF pp. 10–16, 18–20","review_basis":"Binder construction, controls and existing source figures","facts":"Lift, drive, cube tool, hook and partner forks are illustrated separately.","limitations":"Page figures do not establish complete CAD, collision envelopes or physical verification."},{"url":"https://blog.team254.com/2018cmp/","title":"Team 254 championship account","locator":"Qualification matches and Einstein","review_basis":"Contemporaneous team account","facts":"The team describes three-to-four scale-cube autonomous routines and a switch-plus-scale alternative. On Einstein, 254 focused on the scale, 148 on the opposing switch and 2976 on defense around the portals.","limitations":"Team narrative describes allocation and reported performance."},{"url":"https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2018-Public/blob/2c06c1ea5c81b6ed970fa8bc2611f69467a08075/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2018/planners/DriveMotionPlanner.java#L28-L36","title":"Pinned public DriveMotionPlanner source","locator":"FollowerType declaration and initializer","review_basis":"Static read of pinned Java source","facts":"NONLINEAR_FEEDBACK is initialized by default. PURE_PURSUIT is also implemented as a selectable follower.","limitations":"The public release is distinct from a verified Houston deployment."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-frc-2018-code/166514","title":"Team 254 code release discussion","locator":"Announcement and team reply on cube release","review_basis":"Primary team explanation","facts":"The release describes nonlinear following and spline trajectories. The team describes a low-power withdrawal option for crowded cube placement.","limitations":"The published explanation does not provide a measured placement-rate comparison."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Lockdown went 53–0–0 across official 2018 competition. The machine made a large part of POWER UP a repeatable cube cycle: acquire directly into a wristed intake, retain the cube while raising it, then place it on either side of the lift. A two-speed six-wheel chassis gave the driver a separate tool for short approaches and longer traversals. A partner lift shared the vertical structure but created a different load case from ordinary scoring. At Houston the team varied autonomous tasks with alliance capability and used coordinated scale, switch and defensive roles. That combination of packaging, controls and alliance execution is essential to understanding the record.","piece_flow":["The opposed rollers take possession directly at the front. The jaws constrain the cube as it is lifted, so the robot does not release it into an intermediate conveyor.","The carriage and wrist move to a feasible scoring pose. Clear space in the elevator lets the retained cube pass through and exit toward the rear when that route saves a chassis turn. The controls coordinate those motions to protect the cube and structure.","Near a crowded stack, the robot can release more gently and withdraw rather than opening the jaws wide into adjacent pieces. Then the wrist and lift return to a low acquisition pose."],"packaging_and_motion":"The six-wheel base packages drive gearboxes and electrical hardware low. Two open lift uprights guide the carriage without filling the central passage used by the cube. At layout scale, that passage must fit the cube’s diagonal, tool contacts, wrist sweep and deflected cable runs together. Carrying the cube high changes wheel loading and makes abrupt lateral corrections more consequential. The late-match hook and partner forks route forces back into the lift and chassis, so their supporting structure and stow envelope are part of the original concept.","subsystems":[{"name":"Two-speed drivetrain","construction":"Six-wheel differential chassis with compact gearboxes and low-mounted hardware.","operation":"Select the useful ratio for the route and preserve a predictable approach while the elevator moves.","team_rationale":"Short-cycle acceleration and driving across the field impose different demands.","engineering_analysis":"A repeatable stopping pose makes the wrist and lift more useful. A faster top speed matters only where the route gives room to accelerate and decelerate.","interfaces":"Lift reactions and partner loads pass through the chassis. Driver approach heading interacts with the choice of front or rear release.","service_and_failure_modes":"A frame hit can change approach accuracy without obvious failure in the scoring hardware. Inspect gearbox and wheel retention after contact.","unknowns":"Source-reported speed is not loaded measured cycle performance.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]},{"name":"Roller intake and wrist","construction":"Opposed powered roller groups on a wristed cube manipulator with movable jaws.","operation":"Acquire from the floor, retain the cube while the wrist rotates, then drop or eject at the target.","team_rationale":"Front and rear releases widen the useful scoring poses.","engineering_analysis":"Maintaining possession across transit removes a transfer boundary. The mouth still needs to tolerate off-center cubes and the hold geometry must survive reversal and acceleration.","interfaces":"The cube envelope, wrist linkage and jaw opening compete for the same pass-through opening.","service_and_failure_modes":"A loaded cube can move under reversal or crowding. Gentle release is a separate operating condition from maximum ejection.","unknowns":"No complete tested capture envelope or independently measured hold reliability is available.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-frc-2018-code/166514"]},{"name":"Pass-through elevator","construction":"Two-stage lift with rigging and a clear center between the lift rails.","operation":"Raise the same cube tool to the target, then lower it and restore the floor pickup pose.","team_rationale":"One structure serves multiple scoring heights and works with the reversible tool.","engineering_analysis":"A short mechanical path still requires careful motion planning. Rail spacing, cable pretension and torsion become more important if the tool is extended and the piece sits off center.","interfaces":"The clear passage also needs room for cable motion and harness bend radius, while the elevator is the structural support for endgame loads.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check carriage binding, rigging wear and access to replace a cable without stripping unrelated mechanisms.","unknowns":"Source figures establish arrangement and selected dimensions, with dynamic deflection and friction unresolved.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]},{"name":"Hook and partner forks","construction":"Upper hook and deployable fork assembly integrated with the scoring lift.","operation":"Enter the climbing configuration, engage the bar and support an alliance partner when the setup allows.","team_rationale":"The endgame function made use of the same major lifting structure.","engineering_analysis":"Shared hardware saves a separate lift volume, but it raises design loads and demands a distinct mode. Partner geometry and alignment can dominate endgame reliability.","interfaces":"Bar, hook, carriage, forks and frame make one coupled load path. Folded hardware cannot obstruct normal cube cycles.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check fork alignment, unequal partner loading and whether the driver can abandon a slow setup.","unknowns":"No universal partner fit or verified safety factor follows from published renderings.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]},{"name":"Controls and autonomous","construction":"Spline trajectory following, coordinated lift and wrist commands, and a scale-attitude sensing account.","operation":"Schedule acquisition and lift states around the route, then release once possession and pose allow. Choose autonomous tasks with partner capability in mind.","team_rationale":"A useful start required early cube scoring and enough flexibility to cover uncertain switch capability.","engineering_analysis":"The closest transfer is making possession, target pose and return path explicit. Copying a controller does little if the robot cannot repeat the physical transition it is commanding.","interfaces":"A path can pass only if the tool and cube clear the route at the actual lift and wrist states.","service_and_failure_modes":"A missed acquisition or stale target estimate needs an explicit fallback. End-stop and transition checks need validation with the actual mechanism.","unknowns":"The binder names pure pursuit. The pinned release defaults to nonlinear feedback. The Houston binary remains unauthenticated.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2018-Public/blob/2c06c1ea5c81b6ed970fa8bc2611f69467a08075/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2018/planners/DriveMotionPlanner.java#L28-L36","https://blog.team254.com/2018cmp/"]}],"revisions":["Official competition and offseason records are separate.","Binder and public code preserve different software evidence. Avoid assigning the public release default to every event."],"transferable_principles":["Keep the cube in one tool when that tool can reach pickup and scoring poses with acceptable approach tolerance.","Trade robot yaw against tool motion using measured complete cycles, including recovery from poor pickups and crowded targets.","Give qualification autonomous routines enough independent scoring capability to remain useful with unfamiliar partners."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A dedicated wide collector may win if approach error dominates cycle time and a reliable transfer is available.","Front and rear release lose value when routes or field access force a consistent chassis heading.","A shared endgame lift loses value if its structural and access costs reduce the primary scoring rate."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact event-by-event hardware and code configurations, measured cycle-time distribution, loaded deflection, partner compatibility and field-aligned failure rates."],"recommended_images":[]}

text: {"robot_id":"2025-190","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","title":"190 CAD Release","locator":"June 19, posts 1, 3, 4 and 6","review_basis":"Read team release and replies","facts":["StackUp and Redundancy are separate competing robots. Belts guide coral, funnel closure secures it and clears climb, and star wheels assist V2 L4. Both builds used four lift motors rather than the considered six."],"limitations":["The two CAD links were discovery only. The 20 ms estimate was team-reported, without test conditions."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/8","title":"190 CAD Release, climber explanation","locator":"Post 8, Grant","review_basis":"Read written deployment, rope and hook walkthrough in public thread JSON","facts":["An undamped pulling gas spring deploys the arm, a spring-driven lock blocks refolding, and line tension releases the over-center grapple from its stow blocks."],"limitations":["Description includes hardware missing from release CAD. It does not supply proof loads or full event chronology."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/10","title":"190 CAD Release, V2 changes","locator":"Posts 10 and 12, strongalex and CamW","review_basis":"Read team replies in public thread JSON","facts":["V2 mass recovery funded algae tools. Team describes a rack-and-pinion floor algae intake that doubles as a coral stop, successive claw revisions and impact damage to intake plates."],"limitations":["Retrospective component accounts; estimates of iteration counts and weight do not establish a detailed event configuration list."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Station funnel and coral release","construction":"Belts in the closing funnel, an Allen-Bradley photoelectric sensor identified in discussion, and star wheels at the V2 outtake.","operation":"Guide the coral, close for transport or temporary storage, and transfer to the scoring tool. The star wheel lifts the pipe lip on exit.","team_rationale":"The same funnel motion was already needed for climb clearance. The star wheels helped when the release tool was slightly too low.","engineering_analysis":"A hard reference upstream can stabilize release. A soft capture envelope is still needed if a misaligned pipe reaches a closing funnel.","interfaces":"Funnel-to-tool feed, retracted intake as hard stop, and reef branch contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check asymmetric closure, sensor visibility and star wheel wear after repeated mis-height releases.","unknowns":"Belt ratios, sensor thresholds and full control sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/10"]},{"name":"Elevator and algae mechanisms","construction":"Four lift motors. Floor algae intake uses a synchronized rack and pinion with a belted 3:1 reduction from an X44. The revised claw uses a deeper C, X60 roller power and an extra grip-taped tube.","operation":"The intake extends for algae and retracts as a stop. The extension motor current can indicate that a coral has reached the stop. Claw pressure and driven rollers retain and move algae.","team_rationale":"Six lift motors offered an estimated 20 ms benefit. The linear intake met stop, camera and weight constraints. The claw needed greater holding torque.","engineering_analysis":"The intake's two jobs make its retracted position a scoring datum. Treat current rise as an indirect measurement, which a bind or crash may mimic.","interfaces":"Shared intake stop and coral tool, cross-shaft and two racks, camera clearance, and claw belt engagement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports plate fractures from collisions and rapid stops, and printed idlers to address belt skipping. Inspect synchronized travel and replace damaged plates before recalibrating the stop.","unknowns":"Control thresholds, claw reductions, field release poses and stage rigging.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/10"]},{"name":"Rope grapple climber","construction":"40 lb rated pulling gas spring, spool-gear release bearing, deployed-arm lock, redirect pulley and five-bar over-center grapple coupling.","operation":"Reel to release the arm, let the lock seat, then take up slack until line tension frees the grapple from the stow blocks. Guides route load into the surrounding plates.","team_rationale":"Magnets failed to hold through the deployment shock. The redirect controls fleet angle and helps the grapple rise within the cage under tension.","engineering_analysis":"Deployment and hoisting have distinct load paths. Repeatable slack stow is needed to avoid triggering grapple release before arm deployment.","interfaces":"Funnel clearance, reel, guides, release coupling and frame attachment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope stacking and abrasion, release timing, and guide or lock wear. The team used button heads and guide blocks to reduce snagging and gear ingestion.","unknowns":"Winch reduction and ultimate and repeated load capacity.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/8"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Gompei and the HERD built StackUp for the first event and planned Redundancy for stronger later competition. Time constraints made V2 an evolution of V1. The coral package consists of a belted closing station funnel, a four-motor elevator and a release tool that gained star wheels for L4. V2 added the ability to keep a coral in the closed funnel while the algae mechanism was occupied. The rebuild distributed mass reductions across the chassis, elevator, funnel and tool to make room for that added function.","piece_flow":"Station coral enters the belted funnel and can be secured by closure while the chassis moves away. The team says Redundancy could hold it there passively while handling algae. At handoff the coral enters the scoring tool against a physical stop, then rises on the elevator. V2 star wheels catch the coral lip to encourage an upward flip onto L4. An extending intake handles floor algae and a deeper C-shaped claw handles algae with driven contact. Exact acquisition-to-release sequencing for all algae destinations remains open.","packaging_and_motion":"The funnel closes both to constrain coral and to clear the climbing envelope. V2's translating floor algae intake retracts into the coral-stop location, clears the existing camera views and places its synchronization hardware behind the lift. That pairs the coral hard-stop datum with a movable, impact-exposed assembly. Structural lightening was also consequential: the team observed a slight bend in the climber-side drive rail at BattleCry after partial-depth pocketing of the side rails.","revisions":["StackUp early build, Redundancy upgrade, magnet-to-linkage grapple development, and rapid algae-claw iteration around WPI. Exact event installs are unresolved."],"transferable_principles":["Use an already-required clearance motion to constrain the piece. A measured hard stop can be a stronger transfer reference than a timing-only intake."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A translating intake loses its packaging advantage if the cameras can move cheaply or the hard stop shifts under impact. A rope deployment gains little if slack management makes setup or recovery unreliable."],"remaining_gaps":["Drive module, elevator rigging, validated complete-cycle timing, and exact scoring and climb changes by event."],"recommended_images":["Post 8 rope-path and grapple-release diagrams, with the team explanation of the missing CAD bearing.","Post 10 lightened rail and claw tensioner. Inspect originals before reuse."]}

Team reports four L4 autos at district championship."],"limitations":["Reported executions do not provide a success denominator or quantify mechanism timing."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Ground intake and handoff","construction":"Two sets of compliant wheels, independent intake and funnel drive, folding polycarbonate and printed guides, and a pivot. Binder specifies three screws at the main plate-to-axis attachment.","operation":"Gearbox sets contact direction and speed. Sensors distinguish early contact, centered possession and gripper receipt. Loading retries briefly with different commands after the intake beam clears.","team_rationale":"Team sought rapid orientation, protected low motor placement and modular access.","engineering_analysis":"Measure centering time across initial angles and test obstruction with a second tube. A downstream beam going clear can mean travel or loss, so confirm with the receiving sensor.","interfaces":"Ground contacts to funnel, intake pivot to wrist, and wrist readiness to transfer at elevator rest.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check guide edges, wheel wear, pivot zero and recurring retries after impact.","unknowns":"Exact contact widths, material stiffness and jam rate.","source_urls":["https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vQDmuOuYko6tsqzaVRxMaeidCp3j22V8D6hehm5MjMr2mTX2qjtZM0GDTF_Q82WCff1eS-U3_bndLev/pub","https://github.com/Programming-TRIGON/RobotCode2025/tree/c4582360ce8200a7d76610bd5a825d532fa4b58d","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/trigon-5990-2025-robot-reveal-tridog/493284"]},{"name":"Lift, wrist and algae add-on","construction":"Two-stage rope lift with two motor channels, custom guide blocks, ratchet tension adjustment, and quick-swap printed overload pulley. Tight gear spacing and direct pulley at wrist. Algae add-on uses a custom rack and pinion.","operation":"Set lift and wrist for transfer, reef release, or algae removal and scoring. Code opens wrist for reef clearance during certain elevation moves.","team_rationale":"Team wanted low lash and straightforward rope service, and designed the sacrificial pulley to protect the lift.","engineering_analysis":"Rope stretch or tension imbalance can shift the handoff and scoring references. Validate where the sacrificial link fails and what restrains the carriage afterward.","interfaces":"Guide block tolerances, rope tension, wrist pitch and chassis pose all contribute to release accuracy.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope tracking, pulley damage, wrist lash and printed guides. Reverify rest pose after servicing the lift.","unknowns":"Load capacity, rope specification, proof testing and exact algae force.","source_urls":["https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vQDmuOuYko6tsqzaVRxMaeidCp3j22V8D6hehm5MjMr2mTX2qjtZM0GDTF_Q82WCff1eS-U3_bndLev/pub","https://github.com/Programming-TRIGON/RobotCode2025/tree/c4582360ce8200a7d76610bd5a825d532fa4b58d","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/trigon-5990-cad-release-2025-tridog/500664"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"TRIDOG uses a broad pivoting floor collector to center coral and move it to a wrist on a continuous two-stage elevator. The collector doubles as an L1 scoring outlet and temporary coral holder while the wrist handles algae. A range sensor provides an early collection event, a beam break confirms centered coral, and the final feed waits on alignment between the intake, elevator and wrist. Two reef-facing tag cameras and a separate object camera support placement and acquisition respectively.","piece_flow":"Floor coral meets the compliant wheels and shaped funnel. The code pulses centering until presence is established, moves the intake and wrist to transfer, and runs the feed with the lift at rest until the gripper reports a piece. The feeder can supply the collector or gripper depending on robot heading and tool state. L1 can eject directly from the intake, including after reversing a coral from the wrist. Reef or lollipop algae uses the wrist plus its add-on mechanism. After net or processor release, the code can reload a stored coral once the elevator is at rest.","packaging_and_motion":"The collector pivot, lift and end-effector axis all change the handoff geometry. A separate algae attachment changes clearance and can block immediate coral loading. The collector places motors low and protects them from contact. The published assembly mass makes its effect on packaging substantial. Check loaded drive response and tipping margins with the elevator raised before borrowing the whole package.","revisions":["Team describes adding the algae system between competitions and trimming intake weight. The public release does not assign all mechanical changes to events."],"transferable_principles":["Separate early detection, centered presence and receiver possession. If a collector can score L1, use a deliberate reverse path to recover coral from the upper tool."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The storage and reverse-transfer option loses value if it jams frequently or the loaded floor mechanism consumes the mass budget needed for stiff, reliable elevated release."],"remaining_gaps":["Deep-cage hardware and competition use were not established by the reviewed materials. Full intake acceptance map and event-by-event versions also remain open."],"recommended_images":["Published binder Ground Intake and Elevator slides for drive, tensioner and sacrificial pulley annotation. Inspect the slide images before reuse.","Team release post 1 assembly drawing as an overview candidate only."]}

title: 2024-368 Team Kika Mana 2024 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-368","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","title":"Team Kika Mana 368 2024 spec sheet","locator":"Single page, labeled whole robot and four mechanism renderings","review_basis":"Extracted text and visually inspected rendered page.","facts":["31.5 by 26 inch, 115 pound Falcon SDS L4 platform. 1.5 inch collector roller, double-stage feeder elevator, 10 DP shooter rack, two Falcon-driven rope climbers. The shooter pivot actuates the climber ratchet."],"limitations":"Team specification and illustrative renderings. Exact geometry, revision tags, code and live motion were not independently inspected."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883","title":"Team Kika Mana 368 — 2024 Robot","locator":"Posts 1, 3, 6 and 11","review_basis":"Read the reveal, Los Angeles recap, wheel rationale and bumper fabrication reply.","facts":["Added shooter motor and wheel speed for wing-line accuracy after Los Angeles; strengthened front and replaced bumpers after stage contact. Predeployment and climb speed increase targeted a quicker Trap. The 3–1 wheel split intentionally adds spin."],"limitations":"Sub-three-second Trap was a target in the post. It is not a timed result."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Kika Mana keeps floor collection below the bumper and concentrates scoring in a taller assembly between independent climb uprights. A rack-driven variable-angle shooter delivers Speaker shots. A three-roller feeder on a double-stage extrusion elevator handles Amp and Trap and also conditions the ring before it reaches the shooter. The climb has its own motors but shares a mechanical dependency with the shooter pivot: the pivot actuates a ratchet. That interface means a complete design review must cover shot poses, chain engagement, and how the suspended frame reacts at the scoring opening.","piece_flow":"The front roller combines silicone-covered contact and modified flex wheels. Passive rollers center the ring as it feeds inward. In the tower, side rollers precompress the note for the shooter, which has specified vertical and side compression. For Amp and Trap the feeder itself is the scoring assembly, using its three traction-covered rollers and changing height on the elevator. The sheet establishes those branches and contacts; it does not show the exact staging sensors, feed motor direction, or the sequence that decides when the ring has passed the branch.","packaging_and_motion":"The rectangular drivebase supports the low collector, central shooter and feeder structure, and two tall hook channels. The sheet shows diagonals taking the tall assembly back toward the base. That suggests stiffness is critical for both scoring alignment and climb load transfer. The bumper jog accommodates the front intake opening. The team describes stretching a single loop of fabric around the perimeter, using pleats and relief cuts where the height changes. A clearance check should include bumper deflection under contact and the envelope of the moving reaction bar.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis, bumpers and acquisition","construction":"31.5 by 26 inch frame with Falcon SDS L4 and black neoprene. One 1.5-inch collector roller uses silicone tubing and modified flex wheels. Passive rollers center the note.","operation":"Floor pickup threads the note under the bumper, then passive guidance brings it into the feeder corridor.","team_rationale":"Team selected the protected layout to limit driving damage and passive centering for quick feeding. It strengthened the front after stage contact.","engineering_analysis":"The bumper protects the roller from direct horizontal contact only where its deflection and the obstacle geometry leave clearance. Test a low oblique impact as well as head-on driving.","interfaces":"Floor and bumper gap determine ring entry, while collector support stiffness maintains alignment to the passive guide and feeder.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the front-end support and bumper fit after a stage hit. Test pickup with an off-center ring before returning it to play.","unknowns":"Actual entry opening and front-end material changes between events.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/11"]},{"name":"Feeder and Amp/Trap elevator","construction":"Three 1.25-inch rollers wrapped with self-fusing electrical tape, side precompression rollers and a double-stage extrusion elevator.","operation":"The feeder guides a note toward Speaker launch and can present and eject it for Amp or Trap.","team_rationale":"Team attributes the side rollers to precompressing the note for the shooter. The spec sheet identifies the feeder as the Amp and Trap scorer.","engineering_analysis":"The note changes support and width at the shooter mouth. Variable precompression may shift the first wheel engagement to one side, changing spin or yaw.","interfaces":"Feeder exit must overlap the shooter inlet at the transfer pose, and the elevated outlet must clear the respective scoring lip.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tape wear and extrusion alignment, then test the handoff at both loaded and unloaded extension positions.","unknowns":"Elevator drive, extension, sensor layout and note routing timing.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1"]},{"name":"Pivoting Speaker shooter","construction":"3-inch Colsons in a 3–1 lateral split, dual Falcons with 1.67× speed increase, 10 DP rack. Team lists 0.5 inch compression and 2 inches of side compression.","operation":"Automatic ranging selects a shot using the pivot and launcher. The documented range extends from bumper to wing line.","team_rationale":"The asymmetric wheel contact intentionally imparts spin for shot stability. The second motor and higher speed targeted a better wing-line shot, especially in auto.","engineering_analysis":"A spin-inducing offset is only repeatable if the feeder stages the note laterally. Motor count and speed alone cannot establish dispersion.","interfaces":"Rack stiffness and support affect release elevation; pivot movement also acts on the climber ratchet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rack play and tooth contact after endgame loading. Compare left/right rim wear after an extended shot test.","unknowns":"Shot map, sensor feedback and rack mesh adjustment procedure.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/6"]},{"name":"Independent climbers and reaction bar","construction":"Falcon on each side with 18.75:1 reduction, UHMWPE rope on a 1.5-inch-diameter pulley, ratchet actuated by shooter pivot and delayed reaction-bar deployment.","operation":"Team describes automatic alignment and Trap sequencing, with hook predeployment and later reaction bar timing.","team_rationale":"Delay and higher speed were pursued to shorten climb and Trap cycle time.","engineering_analysis":"Hook load asymmetry can roll the suspended robot and shift the feeder away from its target despite correct extension.","interfaces":"Chain, hook, rope pulley, ratchet and reaction bar define the suspended pose while the feeder presents the note.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope winding and ratchet engagement individually, including off-center chain contact.","unknowns":"Ratchet phase, reaction bar timing and event-level Trap timings.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3"]}],"revisions":["After Los Angeles, the team reported hook predeployment, 20% faster climb-related actuation, dual-motor shooter changes, front reinforcement and new autonomous modes."],"transferable_principles":["Size the feeder and launcher as a pair using the loaded ring shape.","Test shared pivot/ratchet functions through every relevant transition."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If off-axis chain engagement causes substantial roll, nominal elevator reach overstates scoring clearance.","If stage contact shifts the front structure, bumper-protected intake still needs impact reinforcement."],"remaining_gaps":["No primary code, full CAD, time study or measurements of scoring dispersion were reviewed."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","subject":"Labeled shooter rack, feeder tower, intake and climber renderings"},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/11","subject":"Bumper jog and fabric relief cuts"}]}

title: 2025-1771 Driftwood complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-1771","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U","title":"1771 North Gwinnett Robotics, Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Worlds interview, 1:23–3:29 lift and centering, 3:48–6:49 wrist, pivot and transitions, 7:06–8:59 reef-state controls","review_basis":"Read on-page English transcript of the team interview","facts":["Team describes a 4414-inspired continuous two-stage lift, separate carriage pivot and wrist, surgical-tube closure, two range sensors with a centering wheel, safe-state graph and a reef dashboard."],"limitations":["Auto-caption terms were interpreted in context. No video geometry, climb construction, or event-wide cycle statistics were established."]},{"url":"https://www.northgwinnettrobotics.com/","title":"North Gwinnett Robotics team site","locator":"Homepage carousel caption for 2025","review_basis":"Read the team’s named robot caption","facts":["The team identifies the 2025 robot as Driftwood and describes it placing coral on the reef."],"limitations":["Caption confirms identity and task; no mechanical specification."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Continuous elevator and dual-axis carriage","construction":"Two-stage continuous elevator inspired by 4414's 2023 lift, carrying a pivot and separate wrist.","operation":"The pivot alternates between floor handoff and station angles, including station approaches from either side. Wrist sets the L1 shelf angle.","team_rationale":"The team targeted quick L1 and all coral levels, floor and station supply, and shorter or less predictable approaches under defense.","engineering_analysis":"An additional axis can recover release geometry lost to short lift stroke. It also raises the number of intermediate poses that need clearance and overshoot testing.","interfaces":"Lift height controls cross-brace clearance. Pivot and wrist determine both the receiving pose at handoff and placement pitch at L1.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck homing, mechanical stops and clearance on every allowed transition after a carriage impact or motor replacement.","unknowns":"Lift reeving, motors, reductions, mass and path coordinates.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]},{"name":"Shared roller claw and centering","construction":"Passive opening against surgical tubing, upper pull-in rollers, a transverse positioning wheel and two CANrange sensors.","operation":"Pull coral into the claw. Jog the tube toward dual detection, or deliberately shift it back for the L4 route. The claw can open around algae and retain it under elastic preload.","team_rationale":"The team wanted repeatable tube placement at release and explained that L4 needed an approach around the corner with its available lift height.","engineering_analysis":"Two binary observations can define an acceptance window without estimating continuous tube position. Their overlap must survive range thresholds, tube skew and changing grip force.","interfaces":"Upper rollers accept both station feeds and floor handoff. The piece position couples directly to the collision margin at L4.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for stretched tubing, seized positioning rollers, and a sensor stuck on or off. Test a timeout or manual recovery if dual detection never occurs.","unknowns":"Roller diameters, tubing preload, sensor thresholds and exact L4 offset.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]},{"name":"Transition and reef-state controls","construction":"Allowed-state graph for the mechanism and a reef occupancy dashboard with operator entry and automatic tracking of robot actions.","operation":"The graph routes tested moves. The dashboard can mark coral placement and removed algae and use a selected goal to choose the next target.","team_rationale":"The team wanted to reduce target-selection time on short cycles and switch between ranking-point and playoff priorities.","engineering_analysis":"Mechanical pose safety and scoring intent are separate state problems. A failed score or partner action can invalidate the dashboard even when the motion graph remains correct.","interfaces":"The target policy requests a pose and alignment, while the mechanism graph governs how the robot reaches it.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check behavior after an interrupted transition and after a failed score gets credited to occupancy. The interview included a dashboard restart, with no root cause given.","unknowns":"Fallback logic, position tolerances, homing recovery, and how driver overrides were implemented.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Driftwood packages a rotating pivot and wrist on the carriage of a continuous two-stage elevator. One spring-compliant roller claw receives from the floor collector or the human player station and handles algae as well as coral. The pivot provides station access from either side and swings the tool to the ground intake handoff. The wrist supplies a separate angle for a direct L1 shot. The team used horizontal movement of the tube within the claw as an extra clearance adjustment for L4, compensating for limited lift height.","piece_flow":"Coral from either supply reaches the upper pull-in rollers on the claw. Two CANrange units are treated as binary presence detectors. When only one sees the tube, the centering wheel shifts it until both register. For L4 the team deliberately moves the tube back from its normal centered location to get around the branch geometry. For L1, the wrist aims to eject onto the trough shelf. Algae is held by the same compliant tool, and the team describes using the centering wheel for algae release as well. The transcript leaves the precise algae scoring pose and floor collector internals open.","packaging_and_motion":"Vertical carriage travel, carriage pivot and wrist rotation all change tool clearance. A pivot swing at the wrong height can put the tool or its arm into the elevator cross brace. The software uses a graph of tested states and permitted transitions. The two-sided station approach can eliminate a chassis turn if the robot reaches the station with the other end forward, but both paths have to end in the same usable piece registration.","revisions":["Worlds interview documents the installed architecture as described there. No complete mechanism installation timeline was established."],"transferable_principles":["Design piece position as part of the tool pose. Build a graph from tested moves, and let the score policy select goals through that graph."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The benefit of a short lift and extra tool motions falls if repeatability at L4 degrades, dual detection is unreliable, or station access rarely rewards either-end approach."],"remaining_gaps":["Ground-intake construction and handoff tolerances, endgame hardware, drivetrain details and event-by-event chronology remain open."],"recommended_images":["Interview around 2:04–3:29 for candidate views of upper rollers, range sensors and shifted L4 piece position.","Interview around 7:54–8:44 for a candidate reef-state dashboard capture. Frame content requires separate inspection."]}

title: 2026-6329 Roman I → Roman II complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-6329","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342","title":"The Bucks’ Wrath Roman reveal and CAD release discussion","locator":"Posts 1, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 13","review_basis":"Read the original reveal, construction answers and the team's description of the two released configurations.","facts":"Roman I had a 20.75-inch outer drum, roughly six-inch center, separate electronics access panels and an upkicker with wheels on either side of a static bar. The team describes Roman II's floor pivot and internally protected shooter transmission.","limitations":"Written descriptions support the interfaces. Onshape assemblies and their linked binders were not inspected."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/19","title":"Roman II design and fabrication Q&A","locator":"Posts 15, 17, 19, 23 and 28","review_basis":"Read the team responses on ball path, impacts, fabrication and motor sizing in the public post stream.","facts":"Wide uninterrupted path, geared floor, low-compression UHMW transition, impact-folding intake, and field-replaceable traction tape. Team reports one floor motor was adequate at its chosen ratios.","limitations":"No current traces or controlled scoring-rate distribution in these posts. The post 23 author relays several details from teammates."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Roman I uses a central spindexer and turret. Roman II retains the four-bar collection concept and replaces the serial feed with a wide roller floor and drum. This changes the bottleneck from reliably isolating each fuel item at one uptake to maintaining broad, even delivery without disturbing the launch trajectory. The team explicitly credits observations and advice at Pine Tree with setting the rebuild in motion.","piece_flow":"Roman I’s moving floor and center drum direct fuel outward without designed compression in the bulk region. A fixed bar about one inch above the floor and wheels on either side drive fuel upward into the turret. In Roman II, the full-width floor supplies a double roller that presses fuel down and feeds it around a UHMW lower guide into the scorer at low compression. The team increased feed speed until it observed degradation of shot trajectory.","packaging_and_motion":"Long four-bar arms can collapse under frontal impact and flex in a side hit. The team says stowed height prevented trench use and accepted that autonomous disadvantage given their manufacturing resources and experience. In Roman II the intake SplineXL doubles as the dead shaft and pivot for the floor, allowing that assembly to swing up for electronics access. The hood sector gear is the exception to the otherwise protected external shooter drive envelope.","subsystems":[{"name":"Four-bar acquisition","construction":"Four-bar with SRPP and polycarbonate at pivots, 3/8-inch spacers, SplineXL drive, and a 95A TPU connector at the polycarbonate kicker arm. Custom compliant wheels were cast from VytaFlex 30.","operation":"Front impact can fold the linkage, while long arms can flex laterally. The collector delivers into either the circular or wide storage architecture.","team_rationale":"The team expected frequent midfield impacts, knew this linkage family and could make it with available equipment.","engineering_analysis":"Design the load path and recovery motion together. Side bending can still shift shaft alignment or change the stowed envelope.","interfaces":"Four-bar pivot stack, collector-to-hopper opening, kicker tube to TPU connector.","service_and_failure_modes":"Older two-inch wheels walked along dead axle tubes. Team reports the cast wheels lasted about one event plus practice and would consider commercial wheels for longevity.","unknowns":"Exact contact loads, wheel retention dimensions, return behavior and clearance in impact deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/19"]},{"name":"Roman I indexing and turret","construction":"20.75-inch outer drum, roughly six-inch center, polycarbonate and printed center construction, integrated spur gearbox and cantilevered uptake wheels. Printed turret pulley and bearing stack around 3/16-inch aluminum base.","operation":"Floor and center move fuel outward. The upkicker engages the fuel at the raised fixed bar and transfers it into the turret.","team_rationale":"Small center preserves space for fuel to drop into the spindexer. The team highlights service panels and low turret part count.","engineering_analysis":"Bulk agitation, bar height and uptake traction jointly determine whether an arriving item rises or stalls.","interfaces":"Rotating floor to bar and wheels, uptake to rotating turret, removable floor to electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check cantilever shaft deflection and bar clearance when replacing wheels. Team reports the turret bearing stack gave no issues.","unknowns":"Floor speed, wheel compression at the throat, turret launch settings and as-played current.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342"]},{"name":"Roman II wide feed and drum","construction":"Roller floor with flex wheels and grip tape, 47-tooth belts and one motor, with about 3:1 at the front roller and 2:1 elsewhere. Bolted, bent UHMW feed sheet and aluminum tube drum with drilled radial holes.","operation":"Double feed rollers guide fuel into the drum. A hood sector gear adjusts the launch geometry.","team_rationale":"Team chose rollers over concern a belt floor would sag under full load. Drill guides allowed drum work without a large lathe. Tape was repairable and available.","engineering_analysis":"The reductions can keep the single motor within a usable efficiency band. Verify this at full fill and when the front and downstream rollers load simultaneously.","interfaces":"Intake dead shaft to pivoting floor, feed pair to UHMW guide, guide to drum and adjustable hood.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tape cuts, belt tracking and guide retention. The floor pivot gives underfloor access without dismantling the feed train.","unknowns":"Matched loaded current, feed compression and widthwise shot variation.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/19"]}],"revisions":["Roman I underwent spindexer revisions before the released form. Roman II reused the collection linkage principle and changed the storage-to-launch path, transmission packaging and electronics access."],"transferable_principles":["Preserve an impact-tolerant module through a rebuild when its downstream handoff can adapt. Find the upper feed rate by measuring where shot quality falls, then size gearing and motors around the actual loaded point."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A different linkage can be preferable if trench routes dominate value. A wider feed loses its advantage if edge lanes starve or the drum cannot hold exit conditions during burst feeding."],"remaining_gaps":["Final drive and climb details, capacity by version, measured firing rates and camera calibration remain unverified. The PDF cross-linked in corpus notes identifies Team 6800's Downpour and was excluded."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/4","locator":"Team upkicker figure","purpose":"Candidate for marking the floor, static bar and cantilever wheel handoff."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/13","locator":"Roman I and II release links","purpose":"Candidate source for paired configuration views after separately opening and verifying the model states."}]}

text: {"robot_id":"2025-111","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716/139","title":"WildStang 2025 build blog","locator":"Posts 139 and 157, January design decisions","review_basis":"Read team accounts of prototype and robot release","facts":["Team abandoned pass-through and changed from three to two lift stages. Asymmetric compliant flaps, bottom roller and a sprung floating leader tackle three different entry problems."],"limitations":["Prototype and design text describe variants, with Midwest update needed to trace material and retention fixes."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","title":"WildStang pre-Midwest upgrades","locator":"Posts 372–373","review_basis":"Read team update and load explanation","facts":["Algae tool compression, reduction and sensing changed. A lighter climb and intake allowed both functions within the budget, but climber composite buckled beyond 90 degrees."],"limitations":["Some corrective designs are team reports and some remained planned."]},{"url":"https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195","title":"WildStang 2025 robot software","locator":"GroundIntake, CoralPath and SuperstructureSubsystem","review_basis":"Read control states, sensor checks and pose selectors","facts":["Floor feed is gated by superstructure readiness and coral detection. Code includes separate L1 staging and ejection and front/back station poses."],"limitations":["Public snapshot is not dated to individual matches."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Direct-handoff floor intake","construction":"Asymmetric compliant polycarbonate flaps, bottom roller, and spring-loaded floating leading roller pivoting about the middle shaft. Separate drive groups support L1.","operation":"Bottom contact lifts awkward orientations and the floating roller opens the throat. Flaps guide the piece into the existing gripper. Rear feed waits on receiver readiness.","team_rationale":"Small station funnel and skilled human-player loading made rerouting under defense hard. Team selected an intake that preserved the arm.","engineering_analysis":"Break bilateral symmetry to move a crosswise pipe away from a stable jam. Validate the acceptance map with skew and edge entry.","interfaces":"Leading roller clearance, gripper readiness, and shared climb sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team added bearing hats and wheel spacers after bearings escaped and wheels migrated. Check flank compliance and shaft fit after contact.","unknowns":"Final roller preload and stage-specific collection rates.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716/331","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]},{"name":"Elevator arm and two tools","construction":"Two-stage lift with separate coral roller gripper and algae claw. V5 coral tool uses aluminum gears and recessed wheels; later algae sensing uses LaserCAN.","operation":"Select arm and lift poses for source, reef and algae. The 6.5-inch tool center spacing was chosen to combine algae removal and branch placement from one drive pose.","team_rationale":"Team abandoned pass-through complexity. Later it adjusted algae compression and reduction after high holding current and unreliable seating.","engineering_analysis":"The hybrid cycle depends on bumper standoff, tool registration and algae compression at the same pose.","interfaces":"Funnel and ground feed converge on one coral tool. The algae load acts off the coral centerline.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch stripped pulleys, off-center algae pickup and gear impacts from the coral. Recheck claw compression after wheel swaps.","unknowns":"Full elevator rigging and final algae-contact stack across events.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716/139","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=13","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]},{"name":"Lightweight cage climb","construction":"Redesigned climb uses Spectra bracing tied to frame rails, a 1 by 1 structural member and a single-bar grabber. Team reinforced or replaced composite pieces with aluminum.","operation":"Capture cage and pivot to lift. Intake moves to its climb position once the superstructure reaches its prerequisite pose.","team_rationale":"Old climb and added intake exceeded mass allowance together. Single-bar grabber reduced mass and eased alignment.","engineering_analysis":"Beyond 90 degrees the load reverses in affected pieces. A part sized for tension can buckle in compression.","interfaces":"Brace to frame rails, cage to grabber and intake stow to climb sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect brace anchors, compressed parts and capture alignment after overload.","unknowns":"Final reduction and power-off retention details.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"WildStang placed separate coral and algae contacts on an arm carried by a two-stage elevator. The early robot collected coral from the station. After Northern Lights, the team added an over-the-bumper floor intake with a direct feed to the same arm-mounted coral gripper and a separate L1 route. The retrofit also forced a lighter climber, so floor supply changed both the robot's approach options and its structural mass budget.","piece_flow":"Station coral enters the funnel and feeds into the gripping wheels. In the retrofit, the lower roller kicks floor coral into a compliant entrance, asymmetric flaps turn it toward the center, and rear rollers feed it directly into the gripper when the arm is ready. The intake can hold a piece for direct L1 release. The coral tool uses sensed possession and the lift and pivot supply branch pose. A separate algae contact removes and carries the ball. The team targeted coral placement after algae removal from the same chassis pose using the tool center offset.","packaging_and_motion":"The 1778-inspired retrofit concept required a new arm and conflicted with the climber. The chosen 2046/118-inspired layout preserves the receiver. Rotation of the intake has to clear the arm in station and climb states. Retrofitting the intake therefore required control interlocks and a lighter cage load path as well as a mechanical mount.","revisions":["January pass-through and lift changes, early station-fed configuration, post-Northern Lights floor retrofit, and pre-Midwest algae and climb revisions."],"transferable_principles":["Preserve a verified receiving datum when adding floor supply. Check load direction over a mechanism's complete rotation before lightening it."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Direct handoff loses value if edge-entry jams or receiver waiting dominate. Hybrid scoring loses value if chassis motion is still needed after algae removal."],"remaining_gaps":["Measured cycle distributions, event-specific parts list and final climb holding detail."],"recommended_images":["Post 331 intake roller and flap drawings, and post 372 climb illustration. Treat them as published design figures pending geometry inspection."]}

title: 2023-1756 Argos 2023 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-1756","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","title":"Argos 2023 Judge Handout","locator":"PDF p. 2, drivetrain, intake/placer, arm, controls and bash guards","review_basis":"Read text of the team's handout via its season archive.","facts":"Describes the ball-screw shoulder actuator, perforated tube rack, integrated flipping head, paired guards and homing strategy.","limitations":"The handout describes intended functions and does not date configuration changes."},{"url":"https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb","title":"Argos 2023 robot code","locator":"src/main/cpp/commands/set_arm_pose_command.cpp and subsystems/intake_subsystem.cpp, bash_guard_subsystem.cpp","review_basis":"Read command and subsystem implementation in public checkout.","facts":"Profiles combine shoulder, extension and guard motion. Wrist flips are gated by extension. Piece detection uses distance and stator current, and guard homing has a failure path.","limitations":"Competition and practice settings coexist. The snapshot does not identify which build ran in a particular match."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Argos carried one intake/placer on a swerve-mounted telescoping arm. Shoulder angle, telescoping reach and wrist orientation position the piece. Two sliding guards protect the head in exposed poses when enabled, adding a separate axis to the clearance problem. The team paired presets on a dedicated operator panel with kinematic motion generation, so a scoring request represents a coordinated mechanism move.","piece_flow":"The dual roller rows engage the cone at its flange. Cubes are controlled between the lower compliant wheels and the aluminum tube, which also stiffens the head. The piece stays in the intake as the arm travels. The wrist can rotate beyond 180 degrees for cone presentation. The software has separate cone and cube intake and eject routines. Its detection logic combines a piece-specific time-of-flight result with absolute stator current above 7 A. Cone distances also feed a filtered position estimate.","packaging_and_motion":"The pivoting member houses a tube-in-tube extension, and the wrist needs swing clearance near the chassis. In the command implementation, selected poses include a bash-guard target. An arm waypoint path is profiled with a keep-out polygon, and its profiles are combined with a separately generated guard profile. During travel the wrist can start moving when extension and other command conditions permit. Inference: the programmed clearance has to cover the deflected, loaded mechanism and the game piece, especially following an impact or a homing offset.","subsystems":[{"name":"Shoulder and extension","construction":"Ball-screw linear actuator with custom gearbox raises the arm. Sprocket teeth engage a CNC-routed hole pattern in a nested tube as a modified rack and pinion.","operation":"The shoulder moves the inner tube's line of action, while extension sets radial reach. Position requests are converted to coordinated shoulder and extension motion.","team_rationale":"Argos documents configurable conversion from sensor readings to physical units and preset movement through a kinematic model.","engineering_analysis":"Actuator leverage changes through the pivot arc. A perforated rack also concentrates load at the hole edges. Test both for play and tracking in loaded reversals.","interfaces":"The shoulder pivot transmits reach and piece loads to the chassis. The extending tube carries wrist, rollers and their harness.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect actuator pivots, hole wear and tube guides. Verify virtual retract reference after changing guide fit or disassembling the transmission.","unknowns":"Actuator force curve, sprocket geometry and tube-guide stack.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]},{"name":"Wrist and roller head","construction":"Dual axles with compliant wheels, rigid aluminum tube and a powered flipping wrist.","operation":"The intake controls the piece while it changes orientation. The pose command distinguishes roller-up and roller-down targets and restricts early flips to a defined arm envelope.","team_rationale":"The integrated head serves both acquisition and placement. LEDs communicate intent and intake status.","engineering_analysis":"Cone flange engagement and cube compression impose different contact requirements. A current spike can also come from an obstruction, so evaluate it together with distance and retention.","interfaces":"Wrist and intake wiring follow the extending arm. The pose command reads piece orientation when selecting an end attitude.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check time-of-flight range with dirty sensors and crushed or skewed pieces. Validate reverse and interrupted wrist transitions with an actual piece.","unknowns":"Roller durometers, speed, field-side release accuracy and sensor false-positive rates.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]},{"name":"Bash guards and chassis","construction":"Paired guard tubes driven by a sprocket and hex shaft. Guards tilt downward and the drivetrain is swerve.","operation":"Guard deployment is operator-selectable. The subsystem has soft limits after homing, and pose command initialization can exclude guard motion when guard home has failed.","team_rationale":"The team wanted extra intake protection and specified a downward deployment angle to keep the guards in the bumper zone.","engineering_analysis":"Guard contact can redirect load into the chassis and a bent tube may consume clearance even when encoder position reads correctly.","interfaces":"Guard targets are included in the arm motion command. Chassis pose determines clearance to the grid and field structures.","service_and_failure_modes":"After side contact, check both tubes for unequal travel and rehome. Exercise the homing-failure branch before relying on degraded operation.","unknowns":"Guard material, impact ratings, exact event fit and measured scoring-wall clearance.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]}],"revisions":["The archived code contains competition and practice hardware definitions. No dated sequence of mechanical guard or arm revisions was established."],"transferable_principles":["Treat protection hardware as a moving subsystem with explicit targets, homing and collision checks. Use both geometric and load signals when the same roller contact must identify two different pieces."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If guard travel consumes grid clearance or repeated side impacts prevent retraction, deployment trades collector damage for cycle failures. If flange orientation varies beyond wrist and jaw tolerance, integrated pickup requires more driver alignment."],"remaining_gaps":["Quantified arm and guard clearances, exact stage and wiring service procedures, event revision chronology and timed pickup-to-placement distributions."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"PDF p. 2","subject":"Team handout overview with callouts for guard tubes, ball screw and flipping head."},{"source_index":1,"locator":"set_arm_pose_command.cpp","subject":"Derived diagram of independent wrist timing and the composed shoulder, extension and guard profiles."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2026-9496 Matterhorn complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-9496","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","title":"LYNK 9496 2026 build log","locator":"Posts 31, 34, 37, 64, 66, 69, 71, 78, 81, 91, 99, 117 and 123","review_basis":"Read early build posts and team answers via the public post stream.","facts":"Documents over-hopper shot orientation, shared four-motor shaft, floor geometry, center divider removal and fixed hood with range-dependent RPM.","limitations":"Early build figures are snapshots. The initial flywheel weights and ratios are not a final event specification."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144","title":"Matterhorn controls and final release Q&A","locator":"Posts 142, 144, 148, 152, 154, 160, 165–166 and 176–177","review_basis":"Read the team descriptions of readiness, localization, passive deployment and in-season service issues.","facts":"Fuel can obscure the front camera, so a side camera helps. Team combines pose-based aiming, calibrated RPM and readiness checks. It selected passive intake due to complexity, mass and space.","limitations":"The older code link in post 144 did not return the raw file. The written sequence supplies the evidence for control behavior."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Matterhorn is a fixed-hood, chassis-aimed drum with passive intake deploy and a sliding hopper. LYNK credits 254's Misfire as the archetype. Its over-hopper shot direction was chosen to fit a fast neutral-zone cycle with minimal rotation on the trench route. The architecture moves complexity into path planning, heading control, and reliable transitions from collection to launch. The team explicitly considered an active intake too costly in mass, space and tuning time.","piece_flow":"Two intake rollers powered by two X44s move fuel into storage. A shallow inclined roller floor advances the pile to a separately driven indexer and into the fixed-hood drum. LYNK removed the floor divider and the corresponding shooter middle plate, creating an uninterrupted two-wide path. The driver-facing shooting action pulses the intake rollers to agitate fuel, then enables floor and indexer when heading and drum speed are ready.","packaging_and_motion":"The trench is tight enough that the team traversed along its long axis and turned after leaving the run. A swerve module protrudes into the fuel path, with protected CANcoder wiring. A hopper full of fuel can block the front camera, making camera placement an interface with storage rather than a standalone controls choice. The passive collector can stay exposed when a powered retract would help.","subsystems":[{"name":"Passive intake and hopper","construction":"Two powered intake rollers, passively deployed collector, sliding hopper and retention net. The team reports using roller pulses while shooting.","operation":"Intake collects fuel and its roller direction can alternate for agitation. Hopper retention and exposure depend on deployed geometry.","team_rationale":"LYNK prioritized fewer active degrees of freedom while operating near its mass limit.","engineering_analysis":"Verify deployment from low traction and varying battery state. Measure whether pulsing recovers low-fill feed or interrupts entry pickup.","interfaces":"Rollers to hopper opening, deployment travel to stowed geometry, and collector extent to path and contact exposure.","service_and_failure_modes":"The team noted poor agitation and situations where it wanted to fold the intake. Check end stops, net tears and slide contamination.","unknowns":"Exact passive deployment sequence and slide construction, reset method and mass budget.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]},{"name":"Roller floor and uptake","construction":"Early build specified 7/8-inch tubes with 1/16-inch silicone, roughly 2.125-inch centers and ten-degree inclination. Two motors were tried on the floor after single-motor issues. Printed side guides narrow the path 0.85 inch per side.","operation":"Floor and indexer move fuel into the drum. The guides keep fuel away from pulleys. Team reported faster feed improved range spread.","team_rationale":"Removing the divider increased observed BPS. Team judged the wider path acceptable for accuracy in its tests.","engineering_analysis":"Electrical limits, loaded ratio and traction can masquerade as mechanical jams. Compare time to deliver at low and full fill using current and speed traces.","interfaces":"Floor to indexer compression, indexer to drum and side guides to pulleys.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early testing exposed low-voltage and current-limit sensitivity. Team used tape to enlarge a slightly loose idler and reported cracking at the CANcoder cover.","unknowns":"Final installed ratio, loaded current, definitive idler arrangement and late-season lane distribution.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]},{"name":"Fixed drum and shot control","construction":"Four motors on one shaft, supplemental brass and steel flywheel masses in the early build, fixed hood, and PhotonVision on Orange Pi 5 with Arducam OV2311. Side camera supplements the front.","operation":"Pose estimate selects field-relative heading. Distance lookup with interpolation sets RPM. The team describes continuous corrections and a readiness gate before feed.","team_rationale":"Simplicity left tuning time for drum PIDF, heading control and calibrated distance. The driver can still aim from pose when a fresh hub view is briefly unavailable.","engineering_analysis":"A one-variable range map works only across its tested launch envelope. Pose drift, RPM recovery, or lane interaction can produce systematic misses.","interfaces":"Drivetrain yaw to shot line, floor enable to readiness, and front camera field of view to hopper load.","service_and_failure_modes":"Log loaded RPM droop, alignment errors and vision loss before changing calibration. The bumper kit also needed an internal latch after impact dismounts.","unknowns":"Final hood angle, inertia, deployed code and shot envelope by distance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]}],"revisions":["Early tests added floor drive authority, removed the center dividers and adjusted side guides. The team later supplemented the obstructed front camera and reported the trade-offs of keeping the intake passive."],"transferable_principles":["Pair fixed shooter geometry with the most valuable routes. Validate the floor-to-drum handoff and readiness under full load before adding adjustability."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The case weakens when defense repeatedly denies the required heading, when passing needs precise bounce control, or when passive deployment fails in the available run-up."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact final inertia, deploy/reset geometry, drive module variant, endgame hardware and matched event measurements remain open."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/81","locator":"Divider removal attachment","purpose":"Candidate comparison of shared drum and earlier divided path."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/91","locator":"Team side-guide and belt discussion","purpose":"Candidate guide and pulley clearance view."}]}

title: 2024-2974 Shosty complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-2974","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466","title":"2974 Walton Robotics Build Blog 2024","locator":"Posts 2, 5, 9–15, 18, 20–21, 23, 26–28, 31–32, 35","review_basis":"Read dated primary build and programming posts from web rendering and public topic JSON.","facts":["Compared protected intake against two concepts; curved transfer replaced a longer prototype that was slow and damaged notes. Shooter design, sensor staging, intake repairs and belt diagnosis are dated separately."],"limitations":"Some posts describe proposals or practice configurations. The linked CAD, engineering summary, videos and code were not inspected for this entry."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/32","title":"Walton final programming update","locator":"May 7, section on logging","review_basis":"Read team account of the Worlds diagnostic and plotted signals as described in the post.","facts":["Amp aiming problem was traced to divergence between pivot motor and CANCoder position during extension. The team identified belt skipping and tightened the belt."],"limitations":"Narrative evidence gives the failure and intervention. It gives no load threshold or independent durability test."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Shosty is a compact ground-to-shooter machine on MK4i modules with Kraken drive and Falcon steering. A wide protected intake passes notes into a short curved transfer rather than carrying them through a long intermediate belt path. A variable-angle top/bottom shooter covers Speaker and Amp, making the pivot part of both delivery modes. A modular winch and Trap door opener were later priorities. The most instructive tradeoff is visible in the chronology: closing the gaps between mechanisms improved handling while also making the conveyor drive and lower pivot axle harder to reach.","piece_flow":"The wide floor collector hands the note into a curved guide and an active transfer roller. The team added an upstream optical sensor and a beam break at the shooter. The reported state machine brings the note to the shooter beam, then backs it off until the beam clears to avoid premature wheel contact. Ready states coordinate motor activity with sensor transitions. The team tested Speaker and Amp shots from the same launcher, reporting that waiting for spin-up made Amp delivery more consistent. Trap testing also used the shooter, with a separate mechanism proposed to open and hold the door.","packaging_and_motion":"Electronics were split around the central bellypan because the low-angle launcher passed over the available equipment height. Hard stops above the battery were added or planned to limit downward travel to 22.5 degrees. The camera bracket later replaced crossbars between the upper flywheel sets, turning camera mounting into a structural interface. The winch module encountered the protruding mini PC and later the main electrical panel during fit and service work.","subsystems":[{"name":"Protected intake and transfer","construction":"Carbon-fiber rollers with end adapters, 1/4-inch polycarbonate side plates and later replaceable guide pieces. Curved guide and dedicated NEO-powered upper conveyor roller.","operation":"The roller captures off-center notes and the driven curved transfer lifts the note into the shooter throat.","team_rationale":"Wide capture let drivers collect without slowing for precise alignment. The longer PVC/tubing conveyor was slower and marked notes in prototyping.","engineering_analysis":"A short handoff reduces residence time but amplifies interference between the roller drive, guide supports and launcher cross members.","interfaces":"An added shooter brace collided with the earlier power-transfer belt path, so the team installed a dedicated conveyor motor above the intake. The cover above the front assembly protected the path from notes and wheel contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"A crowned pulley free-spun as the polybelt overheated; timing drive and additional axle support replaced it. Keep a complete spare intake and inspect bent frame stock, side plates and bumper brackets after contact.","unknowns":"Final roller gap under impact and event-specific guide dimensions.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/15","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/18","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21"]},{"name":"Shooter, pivot and sensing","construction":"Carbon-roller top/bottom shooter with grip treatment and guides; pivot transmission with external CANCoder, hard stops and a friction damper added around the lower axle.","operation":"The sensors stage the note out of the accelerating nip; wheel spin-up and physical pivot settling precede feeding. Team later logged request-to-exit time.","team_rationale":"The first flywheel layout lacked desired velocity. A tread-loaded damper reduced the seconds spent waiting for the pivot to settle. The 125:1 to 100:1 ratio change targeted faster motion.","engineering_analysis":"A high-resolution motor trace is only an indirect angle estimate when compliant transmission stages can slip. Compare it with the output sensor while loaded.","interfaces":"The shooter base, bottom transfer roller, front swerve modules and pivot shaft occupy intersecting service paths. Access holes reduced the amount of hardware removed to extract the lower axle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tension at both sides, matching stop heights and encoder agreement. Noisy bearings were found during a District Championship ops check.","unknowns":"Final loaded-angle repeatability, full current draw, and exact World Championship shot calibration.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/15","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/27","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/32"]},{"name":"Winch and Trap development","construction":"Team built a winch module and reported changing hook guides and materials in development. A shooter-mounted two-pivot door opener with rotary servo release was reported in April testing.","operation":"The winch was tested on the defense base. Door-opening tests subsequently used a fully climbed, stabilized setup to obtain initial shot angles.","team_rationale":"Planar polycarbonate guides were selected to stabilize hook travel relative to rods; a second door pivot provided needed reach.","engineering_analysis":"Loaded suspension pose determines the door contact location and release angle. Bench-stabilized shots omit swing and chain compliance.","interfaces":"Mini PC and panel clearance affect installation of the winch; Trap requires door pressure, stable chassis pose and a viable shooter angle at once.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hook support material, module insertion clearance and release function as separate checks.","unknowns":"Exact event installation and competitive Trap outcomes remain open.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/27","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/28"]}],"revisions":["January concepts and February builds precede the March timing-belt transfer fix. Anderson damage motivated a spare intake and tougher guide. Post-Carrollton pivot work changed belt family and reduction; Worlds logs still caught a belt skip.
