GRITS later exposed a full intake side-plate crack."],"transferable_principles":["Record both motor-side and output-side angle while testing a loaded mechanism.","Measure request-to-exit latency when changing ratio, damping or staging."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If higher pivot speed produces longer settling, raw speed does not shorten the scoring cycle.","If the front structure moves under contact, nominal note clearance and spare-part interchangeability need retesting."],"remaining_gaps":["The separate match/audio link was excluded from construction evidence. Trap event configuration and success need primary confirmation."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/32","subject":"Motor-versus-CANCoder trace at the belt skip"},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21","subject":"Lower axle friction damper and intake guide changes"},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/27","subject":"Pivot disassembly and packaging around the winch"}]}

title: 2019-1610 Tuscarora complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2019-1610","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf","title":"Blackwater Robotics 2019 Tuscarora Technical Binder, rev. 2","locator":"Physical pp. 4–5 and 7–14","review_basis":"Team PDF design and controls sections re-read from downloaded original and web extraction.","facts":"The team rejected its suction prototype and developed a plunger-and-finger hatch tool. Cargo uses an over-bumper handoff and a separate carriage gripper. The binder reports nearly half the prior elevator mechanism weight. Wedges and the eight-wheel drive climb HAB2.","limitations":"No event-level hardware chronology, test distributions, or transfer timing."},{"url":"https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2019/team/1610","title":"FIRST FRC Event Web, team 1610","locator":"2019 team summary","review_basis":"Read the official 2019 identity field.","facts":"FIRST lists the 2019 robot as Cotton J, while the 2019 binder cover calls it Tuscarora.","limitations":"Registration label establishes a naming discrepancy only."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The team designed Tuscarora to service every rocket level for both pieces and allocated endgame effort to HAB2. The chassis carries the bulky first cargo contact near the floor. The moving elevator carriage carries a cargo gripper and an internal-expansion hatch tool. Pneumatic carriage extension supplies horizontal reach over the bumpers, while drivetrain traction and deployable wedges address the six-inch HAB step. The same front packaging therefore has to fit floor acquisition, scoring clearance and the climb transition.","piece_flow":["Cargo enters the over-bumper intake and is transferred to the carriage gripper with the elevator in receiving range. The gripper carries cargo to target height and the carriage actuators put the scoring hardware past the bumper. Exact roller commands and possession confirmation are undocumented.","The hatch tool enters the center hole. A pneumatic plunger rotates triangular fingers outward to grip the inside, and spring return retracts the fingers after actuation releases. The same carriage provides height and approach projection."],"packaging_and_motion":"External wheels and chain-in-tube rails preserve interior space. The added stationary cargo assembly increases overall mechanism mass while reducing the portion that moves vertically. The scoring slide requires an extended-state envelope at multiple lift heights. HAB wedges stow beside the intake and occupy its working region during deployment.","subsystems":[{"name":"Eight-wheel chassis and gearbox","construction":"West Coast rails are 2 × 1.5-inch tube with internal chain and sprockets. The two central axles have a small drop made by flipping Versa Blocks. Custom two-stage gearboxes use Mini-CIMs and vented mounting bolts.","operation":"Center drop assists turning; wheel traction becomes the HAB drive once the wedges establish a contact angle. Talon masters use quadrature encoders and a 10.5 V compensated command ceiling.","team_rationale":"Team retained the narrow internal chain packaging and compact 2363 collaboration gearbox from earlier seasons.","engineering_analysis":"More wheels can help bridge the step only if the needed driven contacts have sufficient normal force throughout the transition.","interfaces":"Wedge geometry determines first-wheel engagement; rail and gearbox tolerances determine chain tracking. Cylinder exhaust is routed through 5/32-inch gearbox inlets.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check chains through accessible inspection points and plan disassembly for replacements. Cooling depends on available exhaust flow.","unknowns":"Wheel loading through climb and measured cooling benefit.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]},{"name":"Cargo transfer and scoring lift","construction":"One over-bumper collector and one carriage gripper. Elevator uses 1/16-inch-wall aluminum and 1 × 1-inch tubing in its first stage; two carriage cylinders extend the scoring tools.","operation":"The collector and gripper overlap at the handoff pose. The elevator motor gearbox encoder sets an upper travel constraint, and a lower magnetic limit switch resets encoder position at the bottom.","team_rationale":"The team accepted added total hardware weight to cut vertically moving weight, and reports nearly 50 percent less elevator mechanism weight than the prior design.","engineering_analysis":"A low moving mass can improve acceleration and stability. The benefit depends on reliably transferring a soft sphere between independently mounted systems despite carriage error or intake deflection.","interfaces":"The collector exit, gripper throat and elevator home position define the transfer window. Carriage slide stroke also controls bumper and target clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"A failed bottom switch can undermine the datum. Check switch brackets, carriage play, hoses and interference during partial extension.","unknowns":"Rigging topology, measured handoff window, cargo release actuator sequence and jam recovery.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]},{"name":"Expanding hatch tool","construction":"A cylinder drives a plunger into pivoting triangular fingers with torsion-spring return. Team shows first and second printed versions.","operation":"The contracted tool fits the center opening, then deploys fingers internally. Removal depends on withdrawing the fingers cleanly after the target supports the hatch.","team_rationale":"Suction trials fell short. The team adapted an inside-gripping mechanism from 2363's 2015 recycling-can design.","engineering_analysis":"Internal engagement separates locating from clamping. Hole tolerance and angled approach determine whether the fingers catch the intended surface.","interfaces":"Carriage extension, center-hole registration and spring force set acquisition and release limits.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect printed pivot bores and spring return. A finger held open by a tilted panel can impede clean release.","unknowns":"Finger materials, deployed dimensions, grip force and partial-capture sensing.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]},{"name":"HAB2 wedge climb","construction":"Paired wedges stow beside the intake with pancake-cylinder pins.","operation":"Pins release the wedges; the intake lowers and the pins extend into the wedge centers. The robot drives up once the first wheel contacts the HAB.","team_rationale":"The team dropped direct cylinder-lift prototypes to avoid bending a cylinder and skipped HAB3 to prioritize rocket scoring.","engineering_analysis":"Use the ramp face and chassis reaction points to carry the step encounter, then verify how much side load reaches the retaining pins.","interfaces":"Both sides must reach the intended support geometry before the front of the frame or bumpers contact the platform.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pin seating and symmetry after impacts. An unlatched wedge can skew the robot or fail to lift a wheel.","unknowns":"Pin-load distribution, feedback and failed-deploy recovery.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Cargo evolved from several prototypes including a floating intake to a handoff system. Hatch development moved from suction to printed internal fingers. HAB2 moved from direct cylinder concepts to pinned wedges."],"transferable_principles":["Assign stationary and moving functions by cycle load. Make the home datum and handoff tolerance part of the same interface definition."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A direct-to-carriage intake may win if the transfer requires substantial driver alignment, or if the added front assembly compromises drive clearance."],"remaining_gaps":["No detailed software sequence or event-confirmed mechanism changes. The two primary sources disagree on the robot name."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2019-1610_p10.jpg","reason":"Cargo prototypes and two-stage piece flow."},{"path":"images/history_2019-1610_p11.jpg","reason":"Carriage extension and HAB wedge configurations."}]}

title: 2023-6328 Banana Split complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-6328","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java","title":"Cube handoff command","locator":"Constructor and command scheduling","review_basis":"Static read at commit 1759ecc7","facts":"Collector runs as a deadline while the arm moves to the cube handoff preset and gripper runs. The arm is sent home on command completion.","limitations":"Code establishes the intended command sequence. It does not measure successful transfer or establish every event binary."},{"url":"https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeFromFloorSweeper.java","title":"Direct floor sweep command","locator":"Height, front/back range and initialize/execute/end branches","review_basis":"Static read at pinned commit","facts":"The direct mode can follow an arm path toward a floor pickup, then vary the horizontal target along a low sweep while the gripper runs.","limitations":"Targets are software coordinates. They do not certify clearances or capture dimensions."},{"url":"https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/cubeintake/CubeIntake.java","title":"Separate cube collector subsystem","locator":"2023C defaults and periodic control","review_basis":"Static read at pinned commit","facts":"Software has separate deploy and roller behavior, initializes the relative angle from the absolute sensor, and profiles deployment.","limitations":"Values are tunable defaults, not proof of a particular deployment or installed calibration."},{"url":"https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/gripper/Gripper.java","title":"Gripper subsystem","locator":"Periodic protection and intake/eject factories","review_basis":"Static read at pinned commit","facts":"Intake uses a timed velocity-based sequence and returns to holding voltage. Different eject requests and high-temperature protection exist.","limitations":"A roller speed change does not independently confirm proper seating. No measured false-positive rate."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Mechanical Advantage’s released 2023 software exposes two distinct floor-acquisition paths. The arm can place its own gripper near a piece and sweep along the floor. It can also move into a preset that receives a cube from a separate collector. The extra collector can widen the useful driving approach while the arm provides greater pose freedom at the grid. The cost is an additional transfer, more states to coordinate and a moving arm envelope that matters during transit. That makes 6328 a substantive comparison with 1746: both can retain a piece in the final hand, while their main routes do not have the same approach and transfer costs.","piece_flow":["For a direct sweep, the arm follows a path to a low pickup pose. The operator can change horizontal reach while the gripper remains active.","For the separate cube route, the collector runs while the arm moves to the receiving preset and the gripper runs. The cube crosses from collector contact into the final gripper.","The final tool carries the piece through the arm path to the target. The gripper uses an eject profile appropriate to the selected objective."],"packaging_and_motion":"An articulated arm trades a compact constrained stroke for several ways to place the tool. Its path must clear the chassis and grid in intermediate poses, not just endpoints. The collector adds a folded volume near the floor and a receiving pose that must align collector discharge with the gripper. Where the hand reaches back across the chassis, cables and tool contents may establish a larger occupied volume than the bare arm links.","subsystems":[{"name":"Ground cube collector","construction":"Independent deployed collector and powered roller are represented in the released code. Deployment is profiled and zeroed using absolute and relative angle information.","operation":"Drive into a cube with the collector deployed and present it near the gripper.","team_rationale":"The release documents a dedicated route alongside direct pickup. It does not provide a controlled comparison of the two.","engineering_analysis":"A wider collector can improve approach tolerance, but a cube sent out skewed still needs to be recoverable at the receiver. The same alignment question moves from driver-to-mouth to collector-to-hand.","interfaces":"Collector pivot, roller outlet and receiving gripper pose must align while the chassis and arm may be moving.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for cube corners that stick at the exit and for false stow following impact.","unknowns":"Exact contact widths, loaded transfer speed and event-specific hardware not established by the code.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/cubeintake/CubeIntake.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]},{"name":"Arm reach and sweep","construction":"The released arm interfaces command preplanned poses and direct tool targets. The floor sweep varies horizontal reach while holding a low target height.","operation":"Approach the floor pose, sweep for acquisition and return home on command termination.","team_rationale":"The direct route offers another acquisition option without routing every piece through the cube collector.","engineering_analysis":"More reach and orientation freedom can save chassis repositioning. Evaluate the price in moving inertia and slower transition margins with the tool loaded.","interfaces":"The direct sweep needs space outside the frame and a path back from both front and rear.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether a pose is available near a wall after a bump or steering error. Test blocked path recovery with the piece retained.","unknowns":"Setpoint limits do not establish reachable physical contact under load.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeFromFloorSweeper.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/arm/Arm.java"]},{"name":"Handoff coordination","construction":"The collector is the deadline for concurrent arm and gripper commands. The arm targets the cube handoff preset and an indicator marks readiness.","operation":"Keep the receiver active during transfer, then command the arm to return toward home when the operation ends.","team_rationale":"The command comments specify an immediate cube handoff.","engineering_analysis":"The design benefits from overlapping motions, so handoff time is not automatically the sum of both actuator times. Still test early arrival, late arrival, interrupted input and asymmetric compression.","interfaces":"The collector-to-gripper gap, vertical approach and roller direction all affect whether the cube remains controlled through the interface.","service_and_failure_modes":"An interrupted command can leave a piece between contacts. Verify a recovery or clear-out route that does not force the arm through an occupied region.","unknowns":"The software does not establish transfer completion probability or all clearance assumptions.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]},{"name":"Gripper and scoring release","construction":"Motor-driven gripper with holding, intake and multiple eject requests. The code monitors roller speed and temperature.","operation":"Intake until the timed velocity sequence concludes, then hold. Choose an eject behavior based on the scoring objective.","team_rationale":"Separate release settings fit different scoring interactions.","engineering_analysis":"Speed-based detection is available even without an extra detector, but friction, an obstruction and true possession can all slow a roller. Verify which signals remain reliable after wear.","interfaces":"The gripper shares position targets with the articulated arm, and its own operating state determines whether the game piece will stay put during transit.","service_and_failure_modes":"The release includes high-temperature protection. Compare retention after a protective stop and after a stalled attempt.","unknowns":"No measured possession accuracy, scoring reliability or installed friction coefficients.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/gripper/Gripper.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]}],"revisions":["All code observations refer to one pinned release snapshot.","Separate collector and direct floor sweep are distinct operating paths in the same source."],"transferable_principles":["Compare the entire approach-to-score distribution when choosing a wide intake plus transfer versus direct capture.","Add explicit recovery states for a piece stopped between two mechanisms.","Count each controlled degree of freedom and each possession handoff separately."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A simpler one-tool path wins if its floor and scoring approach covers the actual field tasks with enough tolerance.","A separate pickup earns the transfer if it cuts approach time and poor pickups enough to pay for its mechanical and control burden."],"remaining_gaps":["As-built structural dimensions and competition configuration map, capture and transfer success distributions, measured moving inertia and loaded sweep clearances."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2023-118 Echo complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-118","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf","title":"2023 Echo Technical Binder","locator":"PDF pp. 6–14, printed sections 4–12","review_basis":"Read team binder mechanism and controls text via web tool.","facts":"Specifies chassis, telescoping arm, dustpan intake and end-effector drives, partner forks, preload catapult, vacuum pickups and avionics.","limitations":"Published specifications describe Echo without date-stamping each physical assembly. The team's catapult accuracy claim has no denominator in the binder."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-robonauts-118-2023-video/429565?page=3","title":"The Robonauts 118 – 2023 Video, team revision reply","locator":"Post 49, Ryan Stockton, March 30","review_basis":"Read team answer comparing red and blue robots and changes since reveal.","facts":"Both robots received intake, end-effector and base changes. Fork configuration and frame reinforcements differed on that date.","limitations":"A dated snapshot of two machines. The reveal footage and later match usage were not reviewed."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Echo divides normal piece cycling between a floor acquisition mechanism and a light telescoping scoring arm. A vector roller and dustpan collect and prepare pieces for the arm's roller head. Other mechanisms address separate match tasks. Blooper launches the preload cube, Swiper uses vacuum to acquire cubes, and forks help handle an alliance partner at the charge station. The binder and dated update describe different configurations, so the subsystem list should not be treated as a single as-built bill of materials for both robots.","piece_flow":"For the main floor route, the dustpan supports the acquired piece while the vector roller draws it in and the powered flappers center cones. The scoring head takes custody at an arm-accessible position and retains the piece on its own powered rollers through pivot, extension and release. That transfer is the functional reconstruction from the published mechanisms. The binder does not give the exact handoff trajectory. Blooper has a separate preload route with a servo-triggered launch. Swiper's vacuum route is documented as acquisition, with its downstream transfer or match use left unresolved.","packaging_and_motion":"A 26-inch square chassis carries the pivot and supports the intake sector gears and fork carriage. The team reverses the SDS Mk4 mounting to widen the support footprint and uses stainless ballast to lower center of gravity. At the opposite end of the mass budget, carbon telescope tubes, printed clamps and dead-axle carbon roller shells reduce moving mass. Inference: low stowed structures and the outward sweep of the intake and forks make the bumper plane, station edge and arm pickup envelope important interfaces.","subsystems":[{"name":"Floor intake and scoring arm","construction":"Bent-polycarbonate dustpan intake with waterjet grout-sponge wheels over a pool-noodle roller. Falcon reductions are 6.25:1 for the two-motor roller, 60:1 for pivot and 40:1 for flappers. Arm pivot and telescope are 118:1 and 15.58:1 respectively.","operation":"Waterjet sectors deploy the floor intake. A camera supports cone detection. A pivoting telescopic arm moves a double-roller head with silicone surfaces.","team_rationale":"The team specifies polycarbonate for impact resistance, shimmed hex interfaces to reduce backlash, and light arm/head materials to reduce moving mass.","engineering_analysis":"A soft roller may widen the capture window while changing centering under compression. Verify custody overlap and clearance before increasing axis speeds.","interfaces":"Dustpan delivery pose meets the arm head. Printed clamps attach the head to the carbon telescope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sponge adhesion, flapper clearance, shim wear and head clamp alignment after collision. Exercise transfer with skewed cones.","unknowns":"Handoff triggers, arm calibration, cube capture limits and cycle times.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-robonauts-118-2023-video/429565?page=3"]},{"name":"Partner forks and swerve","construction":"Backwards-mounted Mk4 L2 modules in a sheet-metal and billet chassis. Forks use 3/4-inch solid carbon rods, nonparallel four-bar, 230:1 lift, 28:1 deployment, over-center linkage and servo pawl release.","operation":"A driver camera aids alignment. Forks reach under the partner and lift and tilt it away from the floor.","team_rationale":"The team cites increased stability for its module placement and sufficient clearance under the partner for the slender rods.","engineering_analysis":"The support reaction depends on where the rods engage the partner. Test the full loaded system, including stance and station pitch.","interfaces":"Fork loads enter the carriage and chassis. Partner underbody geometry and pawl release affect recovery.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check ratchet engagement, fork damage and over-center geometry after load. Recheck frame squareness after contact.","unknowns":"Qualified partner envelope, fork load data and exact red/blue revision geometry.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-robonauts-118-2023-video/429565?page=3"]},{"name":"Blooper, Swiper and avionics","construction":"Blooper uses an extension spring, adjustable stop and servo pin puller. Swiper has two in-perimeter cups with independent 775 Redline-driven vacuum pumps. Custom avionics include a ten-channel CAN node and switchable low-current power.","operation":"Blooper fires once from the preload position. Swiper applies independent vacuum at its two contacts. Lua scripts coordinate selected autonomous and driver sequences, with gyro PID for station balance.","team_rationale":"The binder identifies a dedicated preload shot and a cube pickup developed in three days between Houston and Space City.","engineering_analysis":"Separate pumps can limit shared leakage effects, but seals still depend on cube surface. A separate preload shot saves arm sequencing only if launch consistency is maintained.","interfaces":"Spring preload and hard stop set release geometry. Vacuum and digital controls share chassis space and electrical supply with the main scorer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check latch reset, spring setting, seal integrity and device wiring after repairs.","unknowns":"Catapult trial count, vacuum retention and release sequence, and Swiper match use.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf"]}],"revisions":["By March 30 both robots had a lighter head, grout-sponge rollers, L2 in place of L1, reinforced belly pans and ballast. Both had lost the Ledge Walker. Red had the fork upgrade and different frame reinforcement after a bend during filming. The binder dates Swiper development between the Houston and Space City districts."],"transferable_principles":["Put mass low and make the long-reach head light. Separate a repeatable one-shot task from the cyclic manipulator when their geometry and duty cycles differ."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Dedicated mechanisms lose value if setup or service burden consumes scoring time. Fork utility depends on compatible partner geometry and repeatable alignment under match conditions."],"remaining_gaps":["Per-event robot configuration, actual Swiper usage, arm-transfer timing and verified loaded fork performance."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"PDF pp. 7–12","subject":"Candidate team figures for arm/collector interface, fork linkage, catapult latch and vacuum paths. Label red or blue hardware where identifiable."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2025-359 Hawaiian Kids 2025 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-359","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663","title":"FRC Team 359 2025 Robot Pic Reveal","locator":"Post 1, February 22","review_basis":"Read team reveal and opened robot photograph","facts":["Team credits 2910 Phantom arm lineage, lists a 26 by 33 in low-offset SDS L3+ swerve, 106 lb, floor and station coral, all four levels, both algae destinations and deep cage."],"limitations":["Reveal claims establish intended capability, not event reliability or hidden geometry."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4","title":"359 reveal discussion, mechanism revisions","locator":"Team posts 62, 63, 67, 71 and 79","review_basis":"Read team replies and opened extension and cage images","facts":["Wrist angle and broadside coral caused misses. Week 1 extension slipped under high drive. Chain replaced the outer extension belt, with an inner belt retained. Wider IGUS and a printed guide addressed routing near the added climber."],"limitations":["Team practice and event reports, with no load traces, build drawings or complete event serial history."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=3","title":"359 reveal discussion, early climb and auto","locator":"Team posts 48, 49 and 60","review_basis":"Read team replies","facts":["Team describes three L4 pieces from three sources and active cage hooks chosen to cope with cage movement."],"limitations":["Linked videos were not used as evidence."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Coral acquisition and wrist","construction":"Arm-mounted pickup and belt-driven wrist. Team reports additional tensioners for the wrist belts.","operation":"Present the tool to the floor or feeder, retain the piece through arm motion and release at the reef.","team_rationale":"The team reported that angled floor coral was easier to grab and that incorrect wrist angle made acquisition harder.","engineering_analysis":"Pickup tolerance should be plotted against both tube angle and lateral offset. Driver translation may turn a missed entry into capture while lengthening the cycle.","interfaces":"Wrist position affects roller-to-carpet and tube-to-tool contact. Telescope and shoulder set the gross scoring pose.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt preload and wrist reference after nose strikes. The reported broadside miss is a real acquisition boundary.","unknowns":"Wheel spacing, sensor logic and station receiving geometry.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4"]},{"name":"Arm extension and chassis","construction":"The 2910-derived mechanism retains an internal extension belt. 359 replaced the outer belt with chain using a WCP spline adapter for the pinion sprocket.","operation":"Shoulder and telescope carry the tool to branches, including L3 and L4. Team says it capped extension to roughly 50–60 percent power early to avoid slipping.","team_rationale":"Team attributes extension speed limits to longer reach and intake weight, and reports better operation after the chain retrofit.","engineering_analysis":"A slip that changes actual tool travel relative to feedback can appear as inconsistent placement. Positive drive can restore usable acceleration while introducing tension, lash and shock-load considerations.","interfaces":"Arm reaction feeds the base through the pivot. The wired tool moves with the telescope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Track chain tension, sprocket retention, stage synchronization and physical versus reported extension after a jam.","unknowns":"Reductions, hard stops and telescope sensor arrangement.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4"]},{"name":"Deep cage capture and moving wiring","construction":"Early active hooks. Later 2910-assisted clamp inspired by 368, plus a wider IGUS carrier and printed guide where the added hardware crosses the carrier path.","operation":"Acquire the cage, then lift through the arm package. Team reported about 1.5 seconds from contact to deep climb in practice for the newer clamp.","team_rationale":"Team considered passive capture quicker but less dependable on a moving cage. Additional wiring needed wider carrier links.","engineering_analysis":"Test capture separately from proof loading and power-off holding. A missed cage and a lost load after contact have different remedies.","interfaces":"Cage load enters the arm and chassis. The assembly shares a moving clearance boundary with the cable guide.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide wear, carrier snag points, cage engagement and positive load holding after service.","unknowns":"Exact latch geometry, retention under disable and event deployment timeline.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=3"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Hawaiian Kids adapted the 2910 Phantom telescoping arm family to carry a coral tool through floor acquisition and elevated reef placement. The arm swings relative to a low chassis mount, extends for reach, and carries a wrist whose floor angle is adjustable. The team reports both station and floor supply, scoring at every coral level, and both algae destinations. The mechanism also supports the cage apparatus, so upgrades to extension, wiring and cage engagement interact even though they address different phases of the match.","piece_flow":"Floor coral enters the arm-tip pickup when the tool is presented at the pickup angle. The team reports that driving into a piece can salvage some imperfect approaches, although a tube broadside to the intake was troublesome. The arm moves the held coral into the scoring envelope and the tool releases at the target. Station pickup supplies an alternative route into the scoring cycle. The published sources establish algae acquisition and both release destinations but leave algae contact geometry and net release settings open.","packaging_and_motion":"The base was published as 26 by 33 inches with low-offset SDS L3+ swerve. A change in arm angle changes both reach and height, while telescope extension and wrist angle add control over the tool pose. The cage device sits above the arm and shares space with the moving wiring carrier. Engineering implication: test clearance with the cable at its widest displaced position and with all cage hardware fitted. A clean CAD centerline would not bound the real harness sweep.","revisions":["Week 1 belt restriction, March 5 practice-bot outer-chain conversion, later-event improvement reported retrospectively, and April practice-bot cage clamp prepared for Champs. Internal extension and wrist belts remained according to the May clarification."],"transferable_principles":["Keep a reused arm’s geometry and its new load case separate. Verify extension at loaded scoring angles, measure pickup acceptance over random coral orientations, and cycle the full cable harness after any add-on."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A heavier tip, a different wheel footprint, repeated broadside floor supply, or an unreliable power-off hold can remove the value of a compact shared arm despite successful stationary placement."],"remaining_gaps":["Interview captions were unavailable in this pass. Motor counts, calibration logic, detailed algae contact, full competition installation history and comparative cycle data remain open."],"recommended_images":["Reveal post 1, whole-robot arm/chassis overview.","Post 63, IMG_4324 for the extension revision discussion.","Post 67, IMG_5229 for cage hardware context. Use the accompanying team text for version attribution."]}

title: 2026-7769 The CREW 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-7769","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU","title":"Team 7769 at the Michigan District Championship","locator":"0:32–1:49 intake; 2:34–3:28 hopper; 3:35–4:28 launch; 4:37–6:25 controls and climb","review_basis":"Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.","facts":["Linked rack deployment, expanding hopper and hinged belt floor.","Two launch channels initially had a center divider. The team removed it after jams.","The team described damage to rack teeth and two climb concepts that competed for space or match value."],"limitations":"Capacity is a team estimate for the interview configuration. Captions do not establish exact motor ratios or all event installations."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The CREW built around collecting a load of fuel, keeping it near a broad outlet and emptying it through a chassis-aimed shooter. The important changes followed the flow path. The collector needed to survive defense. The two launch channels did not need a divider if the divider trapped fuel. The floor needed to move for both feeding and access. The team also found that mounting an endgame mechanism could interfere with the scoring hardware it was supposed to complement.","piece_flow":["The deployed roller gathers fuel into an expanding hopper.","The powered belt floor carries the lower fuel layer toward compliant feed wheels.","The feed wheels stage fuel into the launch contacts and hood. With the divider removed, fuel can occupy a wider shared entry instead of being forced into two queues."],"packaging_and_motion":"The rack deployment and hopper extension share the collector region. A shaft ties the racks together, so side loading at one end enters both rack mounts. The belt floor can hinge to expose electrical equipment. At the exit, any divider, climb link or hook must clear both the empty mechanism and a packed fuel bed.","subsystems":[{"name":"Rack collector","construction":"Rack and pinion deploy the roller and share a cross shaft. The team describes a polycarbonate roller with a high-grip surface.","operation":"Deploy, drive through a fuel pile and return to the stowed route envelope.","team_rationale":"The team compared over-bumper and rack concepts before adopting the rack.","engineering_analysis":"A straight deployed path can preserve consistent pickup geometry. A rigid cross shaft constrains skew, while an offset defense hit can still create a concentrated tooth and bracket load.","interfaces":"Both rails need aligned supports and clearance through the hopper extension.","service_and_failure_modes":"Teeth broke under contact. The team spliced rack material when spares ran short. Check whether a loaded rack can still retract after an offset strike.","unknowns":"No measured impact load, backlash growth or deployed deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]},{"name":"Hopper and belt floor","construction":"Polycarbonate walls and a net top expand storage. A powered belt floor hinges for service.","operation":"Fuel collects in bulk before moving toward the feeder. The floor presents fuel even when the robot is stationary.","team_rationale":"The floor hinges to reach the electrical bay.","engineering_analysis":"A high capacity claim matters only for fuel that reaches the outlet. Compare the number acquired, retained over bumps and delivered within the active window.","interfaces":"Hinge and latches must keep the floor aligned with the feeder at both full and nearly empty loads.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test asymmetric loading and a deflected wall. Check wiring strain while the floor swings up.","unknowns":"The interview gives a nominal estimate around 65–70. A separate existing source reports lower typical capacity, and those conditions should stay distinct.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]},{"name":"Feeder and shooter","construction":"Compliant wheels push fuel toward a fixed chassis-mounted launch assembly and shaped hood.","operation":"Bring the shooter up to speed, advance fuel through the contact zone and aim with the drivetrain.","team_rationale":"The team removed the partition after jams between the original two channels.","engineering_analysis":"The useful width is the open feed width through the narrowest transition. A small separation feature can create a bridge even if both downstream channels can individually launch at high rates.","interfaces":"The low belt outlet, compliant wheels and hood entrance need continuous support or positive control of the fuel.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test full hopper and last-fuel conditions. Record left or right starvation, stalls and recovery after rapid reversal.","unknowns":"No synchronized shot-by-shot speed recovery or lane throughput dataset.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]},{"name":"Vision and climb","construction":"The team discusses multiple camera roles and front and side climb concepts.","operation":"Use localization for scoring and a separate camera role for climb alignment when installed.","team_rationale":"Two pose sources conflicted after a physical camera failure. The team reported leaving the side hook off in some circumstances.","engineering_analysis":"An optional mechanism earns its place through net match value after interference and setup. Low climb value alone does not explain a decision if the hardware also blocks the fuel path.","interfaces":"The front climb concept shared space with feed rollers. The side hook could interact with hopper netting.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check pose disagreement and whether an unused hook can snag storage walls when the robot is driven hard.","unknowns":"Exact competition installation and climb outcomes vary by event.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]}],"revisions":["Divider removed after jam experience.","Rack teeth damaged during competition.","Climb concepts tested and omitted at some times."],"transferable_principles":["Measure usable fuel delivered, including the last portion of the load.","Keep service access inside the packaging requirements.","Remove a separator when it narrows the actual feed path and tests show no useful benefit."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A divider can help if it prevents starvation or cross-lane wedging under a materially different feed geometry.","An independent endgame actuator can earn space if it clears the scorer and changes enough match outcomes."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact event-by-event revisions, full electrical layout, feed-current traces and jam rate under controlled conditions."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2023-2767 Snake Eyes complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-2767","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","title":"2767 Stryke Force CAD/Code Release 2023","locator":"Team posts 1, 3, 9, 11, 16 and 20","review_basis":"Read release and mechanism, revision and health-check answers.","facts":"The carbon lift pivots on printed sectors, carries a powered elbow, and sits on chromoly and custom swerve. The team identifies specific changes between St. Joe and Worlds.","limitations":"The release includes model links. This review uses the written explanations. A linked older account is described by the team as out of date."},{"url":"https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33","title":"Stryke Force Charged Up robot code","locator":"src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/RobotStateSubsystem.java, HandSubsystem.java and IntakeSubsystem.java","review_basis":"Read the cube intake and floor cone branches and hand/intake implementations in the public checkout.","facts":"Cube detection at the hand triggers a grab and intake retract. The cone branch uses a floor sweep and direct grab. The two branches coordinate different mechanisms.","limitations":"The active control path is evidence for this snapshot. Commented steps and unused routines cannot establish match execution."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Stryke Force combined a tilting carbon-fiber elevator with an articulated carriage-mounted arm and hand. The drivetrain and arm have separate responsibilities for field pose and piece pose. For a cube, a chassis-mounted intake extends and presents the piece to the hand, whose state machine gates the transfer. For a cone, the arm and hand provide a direct floor acquisition path. The team reported driver initiation of automated mechanism sequences, with manual controls available for recovery.","piece_flow":"In the reviewed floor-cube routine, intake travel reaches a sequencing threshold before the arm approaches its intake-stage pose. The collector starts running and the hand opens and spins its own roller. A cube indication at the hand commands a grab and collector retract to the pickup position. The routine waits on the hand, with an autonomous bypass of that wait, then uses a short timed phase before switching the hand roller to hold and stowing. The cone floor routine brings the hand to a floor pose, opens it, moves the arm through a sweep, closes at the sweep pose and stows when the hand move finishes. The two inputs therefore converge at the same hand for travel and placement.","packaging_and_motion":"The shoulder tilts the lift on printed sectors, the carriage moves along the carbon structure and the carriage elbow changes hand presentation. This distributes reach across three serial axes. The release also identifies left-right shoulder twist. As an engineering inference, a staged move prevents the elbow or hand from crossing the cube collector while it is still occupying the transfer envelope. The same serial chain magnifies any lost motion upstream into placement error at the hand.","subsystems":[{"name":"Carbon elevator and tilt","construction":"Single-stage carbon-fiber elevator, two carriage motors and printed Onyx pivot sectors. A carriage-mounted arm is driven by an Onyx gearbox.","operation":"Sector travel changes lift angle. Carriage travel and elbow angle change the hand's height and reach relative to the grid.","team_rationale":"The team reports enlarging the curved rack and improving elbow durability between St. Joe and Worlds. It describes iterating backlash when needed for smooth gear operation.","engineering_analysis":"A tilted lift converts some travel to horizontal reach. Measure tooth engagement at both extremes with a loaded hand, where sector backlash and carriage deflection combine.","interfaces":"Tilt load enters the chromoly chassis. The carriage carries the elbow gearbox, hand and moving electrical services.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect sector tooth contact, printed gearbox fit and carbon-to-fitting joints. Compare open-loop current and speed after repairs.","unknowns":"Carriage rigging, bonded joint strength, tilt limits and actual load margins.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]},{"name":"Ground cube collector and hand","construction":"Motorized collector travel uses a Talon SRX with a profiled setpoint. The collector roller uses a Falcon controller. The hand has separately controlled jaw and roller motors. The team identifies bevel gears in the claw.","operation":"The collector stages a cube for the open hand. The hand uses a limit-input piece indication to advance to the grab, retract and hold sequence. The floor cone uses a dedicated hand posture and arm sweep.","team_rationale":"The team describes mechanism sequencing with driver initiation and a manual fallback. It reports enlarging the claw bevel gears for Worlds.","engineering_analysis":"The pickup window requires matching roller directions, hand opening and collector pose. Time the transfer with worn cubes, including a sensor transition before the piece is fully seated.","interfaces":"The frame-mounted collector meets the moving hand at a defined arm pose. Piece confirmation ties jaw command and collector retract together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check beam-break inputs and sensor zero after an impact. Try a partial cube insertion and verify the manual controls can clear it without driving an axis into another.","unknowns":"Collector width, exact roller contact geometry and quantitative transfer tolerance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]},{"name":"Drivetrain and health checks","construction":"Chromoly frame and custom swerve with extensive printed Onyx parts. The team reports adding a 20 lb plate below the belly pan.","operation":"Drive input is limited during pickup and placement. AprilTag vision supports positioning and an open-loop health-check logs axis speed and current.","team_rationale":"Ballast was added for stability. The team uses current and speed comparisons to flag friction before closed-loop performance degrades.","engineering_analysis":"Track comparable battery voltage and test load when comparing current traces, so voltage sag does not masquerade as gearbox friction.","interfaces":"The frame supports lift pivot loads. Camera placement on the elevator can change the view as the structure moves.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare drive azimuth velocity and current against the baseline after repairs. Check camera alignment after upper-structure impacts.","unknowns":"Module hardware loads, pose-dependent vision calibration and measured ramp behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]}],"revisions":["From St. Joe to Worlds, the team reports a taller sector rack, elbow gearbox durability revisions, a camera at the top of the elevator for autonomous AprilTag viewing and larger claw bevel gears. The team also reports adding underbody ballast after an initial weight around 100 lb."],"transferable_principles":["Use explicit transfer poses with piece confirmation at the receiving mechanism. Record open-loop current and velocity together to track binding that closed-loop control can hide."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A shared hand transfer loses cycle time if collector and arm tolerances require repeated grabs. A tilting lift loses reach advantages if slope and acceleration margins force conservative motion."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-by-event component fit, collector escape geometry, cycle-time distributions, and endurance of the printed sectors and carbon joints."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"Posts 3, 7 and 20","subject":"Candidate team release illustrations for the carriage motors, composite joints and diagnostic current/velocity plots. Verify image attribution and configuration before reuse."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2022-5172 Gators 2022 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-5172","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0","title":"Behind the Bumpers 5172 Gators Robot | Rapid React","locator":"1:33–2:57 drive, 3:05–4:26 intake, 4:34–6:45 conveyor and turret, 6:53–8:11 climb","review_basis":"Read the timestamped English transcript in the public player panel. Mechanism account is from interviewed team members at Championship.","facts":["First-year swerve separated translation and rotation on the driver’s sticks. The pneumatic nonparallel intake dropped a Lexan bridge and used a foam roller with carbon core and printed mecanum elements.","One conveyor wheel set staged cargo. A sensor near the top classified color, and the turret diverted the wrong color. The flywheel stayed running with RPM set from Limelight range.","The team reverted its second regional’s four-stage climb, widened the hooks for turret clearance and replaced a single hook with two to reduce swing."],"limitations":["Automatic transcription supports sequence and rationale. Exact hardware dimensions, solenoid plumbing, angle limits and reliability sample were outside the review. The 15–20 second climb is team-reported at Worlds."]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Gators combined a compliant over-bumper collector and a short mechanically simple ramp with an independently aimed launcher. The launcher also served as the reject exit. The Worlds climber was a revised return to an earlier rung-transfer architecture, with the turret’s physical width directly shaping the hook layout.","piece_flow":"Floor cargo encounters the foam roller, whose larger angled end contacts guide it inward. On deployment a Lexan guard drops to give cargo a surface over the bumper and into the chute. A single set of conveyor wheels moves the ball up the ramp and holds it before release. The color sensor near the top decides whether to shoot toward the hub or rotate the turret to discharge away from it. The flywheel supplies launch speed and the upper compliant contacts reduce backspin. Exact locations and sequence for two simultaneously held cargo were not explained.","packaging_and_motion":"Swerve can translate while the turret changes azimuth, although the collector still has an approach side. The lift has a powered hook for reaching and lifting, then a deployable support-hook geometry for changing the suspended chassis angle. At Worlds the hooks had to clear the turret across that transition. The useful clearance check follows the suspended chassis and full turret sweep through the complete sequence, including sway and asymmetric engagement.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and operator feedback","construction":"Swerve chassis with separate translation and rotation inputs. LEDs visible to driver and operator.","operation":"Driver translates independently of heading. Dark blue denotes lined up and ready, while lighter blue denotes close to alignment.","team_rationale":"Driver emphasized the practice needed to learn the new drivetrain and valued maneuverability.","engineering_analysis":"A shared ready indication can keep the driver moving until the shot is usable. It needs to distinguish stale vision from a genuinely good alignment.","interfaces":"Chassis heading sets intake presentation and remaining turret travel. Vision and readiness states reach both operators.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck gyro orientation and sensor/LED agreement after impacts or restarts.","unknowns":"Swerve module model, heading reset and exact ready predicates.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]},{"name":"Pickup and bridge","construction":"Pneumatic nonparallel four-bar, foam roller around a carbon-fiber rod, printed angled contacts and a deployable Lexan guard.","operation":"The guard drops as the intake deploys and bridges into the chute. Larger end contacts funnel off-center cargo.","team_rationale":"The team highlighted the bridge as important to bumper crossing and valued compliance for fast pickup against a wall.","engineering_analysis":"A moving bridge removes a floor-level handoff discontinuity without another powered axis. Its loaded edge still needs overlap with the chute through linkage play.","interfaces":"First roller to bumper bridge to chute entrance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for a curled guard lip, a binding hinge or damaged end prints when pickup succeeds but handoff fails.","unknowns":"Linkage stops, roller surface speed and guard retention when stowed.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]},{"name":"Staging and rejection","construction":"Ramp, single conveyor wheel set and color sensor near the top.","operation":"The wheels hold cargo until feed. An opposing color triggers a different turret azimuth and discharge.","team_rationale":"The alternate heading keeps the rejected cargo from scoring in the hub.","engineering_analysis":"Sharing the shot path saves a second exit but can interrupt the next scoring cycle during slew, discharge and reacquisition. A color decision must stay associated with the correct cargo.","interfaces":"Sensor decision to indexing release and turret aim.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test alternating colors and closely spaced cargo, with particular attention to whether a second piece advances during reject.","unknowns":"Reject angle, sensor timing and simultaneous two-ball inventory.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]},{"name":"Turret launcher","construction":"Limelight, aluminum main wheel with blue nitrile tread and brass inertia masses, plus compliant upper wheels.","operation":"Automatically aims turret. Changes the speed of an already-spinning flywheel with observed range.","team_rationale":"Brass supports speed retention, nitrile improves grip and reducing backspin was intended to reduce bounce-outs.","engineering_analysis":"Added inertia reduces instantaneous RPM loss at release and makes large speed changes slower at a given torque. Keeping the wheel running reduces cold spin-up delay.","interfaces":"Conveyor exit, range-to-speed map, azimuth and readiness feedback.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tread and upper contact wear before recalibrating. Verify collision envelope at all useful azimuths.","unknowns":"Hood mechanism, exit-spin measurements and electrical duty cycle.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]},{"name":"Worlds climber","construction":"Powered reach hook and deployable support hooks. Wider hook placement and paired support contact distinguish the return configuration.","operation":"Reach mid, pull into support hooks, deploy to set reach angle, then reach the next bar and repeat.","team_rationale":"The four-stage replacement had mechanical issues. Wider hooks cleared the turret and paired contact reduced swing.","engineering_analysis":"Once the rung is supporting the chassis, changing hook geometry also moves the whole chassis and changes the next reach target.","interfaces":"Rung contact, suspended chassis pitch and turret envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a one-sided catch and a missed latch under load. Look for unequal contacts and interference before the next reach.","unknowns":"Exact actuator/rigging details and cause of the four-stage faults.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}],"revisions":["First regional used the earlier hook architecture. The second used the faster four-stage unit. Worlds returned to the earlier architecture with clearance and anti-swing changes."],"transferable_principles":["Evaluate climb upgrades by completed hangs per attempt and deadline margin. Test transitions with the scoring package installed."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A shared rejection exit loses its appeal if mixed-color traffic repeatedly holds up good cargo. Wider hooks only improve integration if they clear the turret and partners across the loaded sweep."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-specific reliability, electrical load and a section through the two-ball path remain open."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0","locator":"3:13–3:54 and 7:01–7:55","purpose":"Seek source stills for the deployed bridge and Worlds hook clearances. Timestamp targets are from the transcript."}]}

title: 2022-604 Octopus Prime complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-604","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/README.md","title":"Quixilver 2022 code release","locator":"Repository contents","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"The repository distinguishes the robot code from a rewrite. It includes a swerve trajectory optimizer and driver-station particle filter.","limitations":"Repository contents do not establish which optional localization tools ran at a particular event."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Intake.java","title":"Intake subsystem","locator":"Motor declarations, deploy and retract, periodic setpoint","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"Separate Falcon-controlled roller and deployment. Deployment uses a motion profile and arm feedforward.","limitations":"The code exposes actuation and target states. Installed geometry needs a physical source."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/BallPath.java","title":"Ball path subsystem","locator":"Queue, beam-break, color and launch methods","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"Two powered feed zones, three beam-break inputs, a color input, top/bottom possession states, and feed speed selection based on the upper beam.","limitations":"The switch logic reports controller intent. Sensor data and field performance are separate."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/commands/RunIntakeAndMoveToTopQueue.java","title":"Collect and move to top queue","locator":"Command lifecycle","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"The command acquires cargo and runs the path together. It monitors the bottom sensor and updates the upper state after a non-interrupted transfer.","limitations":"A state transition is not independent evidence that the cargo reached its intended pose."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Launcher.java","title":"Launcher subsystem","locator":"Speed commands, readiness and launch","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"Both launcher speed histories must be in tolerance. The launch mode checks feasible shot status.","limitations":"No measured flywheel recovery or accuracy map."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Climber.java","title":"Climber subsystem","locator":"State enum and periodic feedback","review_basis":"Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.","facts":"The published sequence includes reaches, partial lifts and intermediate handoff states. The code accepts robot tilt and tilt-rate inputs.","limitations":"Exact hook load paths and event-specific traverse performance remain unresolved."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Octopus Prime is a swerve cargo robot with a deployable intake, a managed two-position cargo path, two controlled launcher speeds and a staged climb. Its technical point is how the mechanism boundaries are made explicit in software. The collector changes the cargo’s state from outside the robot to present at the lower queue. The path advances it to a staged position. The shot logic waits for feasible, stable speed before feeding. Separate reverse and clearing commands show that handling a wrong or stuck cargo was part of the system.","piece_flow":["The deployed roller draws cargo toward the lower path. Beam-break and color input help classify and track the piece.","The lower and upper powered rollers advance and stage it. The software moves its queue state on the transfer command’s normal completion.","When the launcher is ready, the ball path changes feed speed depending on whether cargo is already near the launcher. Empty sensor states can end the feed.","The code provides clearing and rejection behavior. During climb, the robot sequences reaches, lifts and handoffs as separate states."],"packaging_and_motion":"The release describes functional interfaces rather than a dimensioned robot. A physical layout must place the first sensor after a useful capture contact, preserve control across the lower-to-upper transfer and keep cargo seated near the launcher without jamming it into the wheels. The intake must stow without trapping a staged ball or limiting approach. Climb states imply another envelope near the rungs and a structure that supports the chassis under suspended load.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector","construction":"One motor runs the acquisition contact and another deploys it. The deploy actuator uses a profiled goal with gravity-related feedforward.","operation":"Select deploy or retract, then run acquisition, reverse or clearing motion as required.","team_rationale":"Team rationale is not given in the inspected subsystem.","engineering_analysis":"Separate deploy and roller control lets the driver clear the ball while preserving the useful mouth pose. It also makes two failure paths possible.","interfaces":"Place the lower sensor where it can distinguish captured cargo from a ball merely passing across the mouth.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check the encoder zero after a hit and reversal when the mouth is blocked.","unknowns":"Exact contact width, bumper geometry and sensor alignment.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Intake.java"]},{"name":"Queue and transfer","construction":"Lower and upper powered regions have separate stored state and sensor input. Color is evaluated against an alliance-color selection.","operation":"Advance cargo to the top position and preserve separation so a second ball does not enter the shot contact early.","team_rationale":"Code comments describe staging and a different feed speed when cargo is already at the launcher.","engineering_analysis":"Tracking both occupancy and color can prevent a correct launch command from feeding the wrong physical ball. The benefit depends on synchronization between sensors and stored state.","interfaces":"Upper sensor, queue location and launcher entrance need reliable spacing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test an interrupted move while cargo spans both regions. A debounced detector may need a recovery based on the actual sensor pattern.","unknowns":"No measured jam rate, color detection accuracy or successful queue recovery data.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/BallPath.java","https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/commands/RunIntakeAndMoveToTopQueue.java"]},{"name":"Launch readiness","construction":"Separate launcher motor controls maintain the requested speed. Both histories are checked before readiness.","operation":"Convert computed exit velocity to a speed setting, wait for steady samples and feed once feasible.","team_rationale":"The implementation uses feasibility and a short speed history rather than a single sample.","engineering_analysis":"Readiness can improve repeatability, but an overly strict settling condition can waste an open shot window. Measure the time and accuracy trade.","interfaces":"Launcher entry must retain the piece while wheels accelerate, then feed cleanly without reducing speed below the tolerance band.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare single and paired shots on a partially discharged battery. Log rejected shot conditions.","unknowns":"No independently measured recovery time or field accuracy by range.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Launcher.java","https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/BallPath.java"]},{"name":"Traversal sequencing","construction":"The climb controller divides the maneuver into reaches, contact, partial lifts and handoffs with tilt inputs.","operation":"Advance through stable intermediate states while moving between rungs.","team_rationale":"Published source exposes transition structure without giving a rationale for each threshold.","engineering_analysis":"A sequence is easier to recover when each load-transfer state has an observable condition. Test each intermediate state rather than only the complete routine.","interfaces":"Hooks and rung approach must keep the next reach accessible when the chassis swings under load.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check unexpected swing and early contact. Confirm the routine has a safe response when a handoff cannot be completed.","unknowns":"No dimensioned hook or rigging data in the reviewed sections.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Climber.java"]}],"revisions":["The FRC-2022-NEW directory is a rewrite and is outside this competition-oriented source review."],"transferable_principles":["Define occupancy and recovery at each possession boundary.","Measure shot readiness over multiple launches and battery conditions.","Keep hardware and controller limits attached to their source snapshot."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Remove a transfer or independent deployment axis when it contributes little useful reach or throughput.","A less complex climb can earn more total contribution if a traversal mechanism harms the primary scoring cycle."],"remaining_gaps":["Physical packaging of the collector, feed and climb, tested acquisition limits, and match-level configuration history."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2024-1778 Zappy Feet complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-1778","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727","title":"1778 CAD/Code Release","locator":"Posts 1, 3, 5; June 2 technical replies","review_basis":"Read team release and answers.","facts":["Two lower rollers helped bend the note during acquisition and guide the Amp shot; one lower roller had sent it above the bar. Team reported 0.2-inch intake compression and 0.5-inch shooter compression without horizontal squeeze. The virtual four-bar eliminated a separate Amp-bar motor."],"limitations":"Team recollection; CAD was linked and uninspected."},{"url":"https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public","title":"Chill Out 2024 Robot Code","locator":"master: Controls.kt; IntakeWrist.kt, ShooterRollers.kt, ShooterWrist.kt, Climbers.kt, ClimberHook.kt; CenterNoteCommand, ShooterShootCommand, ShooterAmpShootCommand and climb commands","review_basis":"Read Kotlin source from team-published master archive.","facts":["Pickup runs collector and shooter feed together, then raises the intake while centering. Two digital line breaks distinguish storage and further travel. Amp uses driver approval in Amp wrist state. The two hooks each have a NEO master and follower."],"limitations":"Public release is a code snapshot. Physical dimensions, specific event deploys and climb recovery history require separate evidence."},{"url":"https://www.chillout1778.org/1778robots","title":"Chill Out robot archive","locator":"2024 Crescendo, Zappy Feet section","review_basis":"Read team season page.","facts":["Connects the robot name with the district and Championship season and identifies a separate pit interview and robot CAD."],"limitations":"Interview captions were unavailable on retry; archive text gives no additional mechanical dimensions."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Zappy Feet combines a deployable roller collector with a wristed scorer that handles acquisition, storage, and release. A shaped Amp path follows the shooter wrist through a virtual four-bar, allowing a second scoring geometry without allocating a motor to its deployment. The mechanical coupling works with a control sequence that distinguishes collecting, centering, aiming, and firing. Two independent hook sides share the chassis with these mechanisms but get their own motor pairs. The code shows where software coordinates the collector with the climbers and where the operator still decides to release a note.","piece_flow":"In the floor routine the intake is commanded down, then its rollers run alongside the shooter intake command. After acquisition the collector rises in parallel with centering. The lower line break indicates storage. The centering command pulls briefly, then feeds outward slowly while the upper beam is occupied and stops when it clears. Source loading uses a different wrist pose but reuses the shooter and centering routines. Speaker shots use flywheel spin-up plus authorization. Amp delivery uses the feed rollers after operator approval and the Amp wrist state.","packaging_and_motion":"The collector wrist has its own motor but reads an absolute sensor through the roller controller. The shooter wrist uses its master motor relative encoder and has a follower; the linkage makes bar geometry follow wrist geometry. The climb extension command explicitly demands Intake Down. That establishes a software dependency between the two motions. Whether its purpose was clearance, deployment order, or another constraint needs a geometry review.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and acquisition","construction":"Separately powered roller and wrist functions; absolute intake angle from the roller controller. Team reported 0.2-inch compression.","operation":"The floor routine waits for its angle command before starting parallel acquisition. Source loading skips the floor collector.","team_rationale":"Team published compression. The code describes the sequence but gives no prototype rationale for individual roller positions.","engineering_analysis":"Driving the collector and destination together allows an early handoff, provided the leading edge reaches the downstream nip before it loses the upstream contact.","interfaces":"Collector wrist position gates roller operation through the command sequence, and the shooter acquisition command is the deadline for parallel collection.","service_and_failure_modes":"A loose absolute sensor connection can remove angle feedback even when the wrist motor remains functional. Inspect the sensor through full collector travel.","unknowns":"Roller number, tread, and entry envelope await physical or interview review.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727","https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]},{"name":"Shooter, staging and Amp bar","construction":"Team describes two lower rollers, one top roller and a virtual four-bar. Software separates two regulated flywheel motors, a feed motor, two line breaks and a wrist.","operation":"Speaker tracking checks wrist alignment, tag availability, chassis heading and flywheel readiness before timed feeding, with separate preset branches. Amp uses the feed roller and coupled bar.","team_rationale":"The extra lower roller fixed an Amp shot above the bar and improved intake. Linkage addressed concern about notes falling into the bellypan without requiring another motor.","engineering_analysis":"Wrist-angle error affects both launch and Amp alignment. The shown speed check uses top wheel feedback despite both motor velocities being available, so test asymmetric wheel recovery.","interfaces":"Upper beam clearance terminates centering; the lower beam represents storage. The linkage maps wrist angle to bar location without a separate actuator state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check both beam transitions with worn notes. In the centering command a continuously blocked upper beam can keep slow feeding active until interrupted.","unknowns":"Exact linkage pivots, wheel diameters, and shot dispersion.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727","https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]},{"name":"Climbers and drive coordination","construction":"Two oppositely signed hook objects each use one master and one following NEO with brake mode and current limits.","operation":"Extend starts both sides and stops them individually as calculated extension passes 0.7; retraction similarly stops each side near zero.","team_rationale":"The reviewed code demonstrates independent control, while the claimed single-side field recovery remains unverified here.","engineering_analysis":"Independent stopping handles position mismatch; equal encoder readings cannot establish equal chain load or confirmed engagement.","interfaces":"Master encoder and configured drum circumference/reduction establish the travel estimate. The extend command also owns the intake wrist.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify encoder zero and paired-motor direction after service. Validate asymmetric loading separately from nominal dual-side operation.","unknowns":"Actual hook, cable and drum construction, attachment load, and trap capability.","source_urls":["https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]}],"revisions":["The team reports adding the second lower roller after the single-lower-roller Amp prototype failed. The virtual bar entered after an early archetype and remained close to the sketched geometry."],"transferable_principles":["Tie a passive scoring guide to a powered joint only after checking its pose across the full travel.","A positive sensor transition gives a stronger staging reference than fixed run time alone."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If worn notes bridge the upper beam indefinitely, centering needs a different stop condition.","If wrist or linkage play consumes Amp clearance, sharing the axis can cost more than a dedicated guide."],"remaining_gaps":["Interview-dependent collector details and any single-side climb incident remain open; public CAD was not inspected."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727/5","subject":"Team virtual four-bar design sketches and comparison"},{"url":"https://www.chillout1778.org/1778robots","subject":"2024 robot section for a floor pickup and Amp pose comparison"}]}

title: 2026-1987 Broncobots 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-1987","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","title":"Broncobots 2026 Technical Book","locator":"PDF pp. 5–13","review_basis":"Downloaded the published book and read mechanism, strategy, electrical and controls pages.","facts":"Documents drive, linear intake, coaxial rotor, floating hood and empirical moving-shot compensation. Lists 50 fuel hopper capacity and 18 fuel per second at the rotor.","limitations":"Rotor feed rate is a subsystem figure. The team season page gives 55 hopper and 10-plus through the complete path, under unspecified conditions."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1987-broncobots-2026-cad-code-resources-release/524348","title":"Cyclone release and build discussion","locator":"Posts 6, 9–11 and 14","review_basis":"Read the team explanations on prototype, hood and wiring failures, and concentric ring fabrication.","facts":"Early hook and low overhead support caused jams. Team describes a five-ring bearing stack, a six-inch through-path, and details of harness redirection and spares.","limitations":"The accounts are team observations.
