They do not provide matched rate, accuracy or durability distributions."},{"url":"https://teambroncobots.com/robots/2026Robot/","title":"Cyclone team season page","locator":"Specifications and capabilities","review_basis":"Read the team's public robot specification and capability list.","facts":"Lists 21.75-inch height, X2i swerve, 55 fuel hopper and over ten fuel per second from intake to shooter.","limitations":"No protocol explains the difference between hopper counts across team publications."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Cyclone combines trench clearance and simultaneous collection and firing with a one-stream turret. The team anticipated defense, treated 360-degree aiming and trench traversal as valuable, and saw fast singulation as necessary to make one shooter viable. It lowered the rotor with under-mounted electronics and moved the battery toward the edge with custom rails. The rotor, turret bearings and wiring occupy the same constrained central assembly.","piece_flow":"The full-width linear collector uses two powered roller stages to drive fuel front-to-back. Diverter walls guide it into a 22-inch annular rotor with eight-fuel ring capacity. The rotating hook brings fuel to the independently driven feed wheels and up the central through-path into the turret. A primary flywheel and driven hood rollers set launch velocity and spin, and the hood changes launch angle.","packaging_and_motion":"Cyclone is listed at 21.75 inches tall. Raising and shrinking the support gave fuel more space around the rotor hook. The resulting 4.25-inch shooter uses a rear-driven floating hood to achieve the angular travel the team could not fit in a short conventional rack. Wiring ascends a corner support through a protected column so the buffer can sit below the hopper.","subsystems":[{"name":"Linear collector and chassis","construction":"Polycarbonate intake structure, aluminum hub covers, large washers, silicone and grip-wrapped 1.125-inch rollers. X60 deploy at 3.6:1 and roller drive at 1.5:1. Four X2i modules and a polycarbonate skid.","operation":"Linear motion expands the hopper. Two rollers move fuel deeper and the chassis mounts carry impact load.","team_rationale":"Full width was chosen to gather five neutral-zone columns on the autonomous route. Covers spread collision loads.","engineering_analysis":"Test simultaneous arrival at several lateral positions. Reinforcement is most valuable if it preserves alignment of the moving collector and drive system.","interfaces":"Roller to hopper lip, collector to frame, and bumper-mounted hopper walls to service removal.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hub covers, tube alignment and slider motion after contact. The skid and brainpan protect or organize the vulnerable underside.","unknowns":"As-played intake travel, measured acquisition rate by approach angle and long-term wear data.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://teambroncobots.com/robots/2026Robot/"]},{"name":"Coaxial rotor and turret support","construction":"Wedge-shaped printed hook with aluminum reinforcement, separate X60 drives at 20.67:1 rotation and 1:1 feed, #25 chain and enclosed bevel gears. Five custom rings capture two seven-inch X-contact bearings around a six-inch bore.","operation":"Rotation sweeps fuel into the feed wheels. Reverse rotation helps clear jams. Independent moving assemblies share the support axis.","team_rationale":"Team wanted fast one-stream feed, a smaller hook footprint and an unobstructed route to the scorer.","engineering_analysis":"Concentricity is both structural and functional. Ring distortion or vertical stack error can tighten bearings or constrict the fuel path.","interfaces":"Hook to fuel pile, coaxial drive to feed, bearing stack and sprocket to turret, and bore to launcher inlet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early hook climbed over fuel and broke. Two fuel could jam under low structure. Rotor mounts on a separate service plate.","unknowns":"Compression and tolerance stack as built, loaded drive current, and throughput at low fill and under acceleration.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1987-broncobots-2026-cad-code-resources-release/524348"]},{"name":"Floating hood, aim and harness","construction":"Dead-axle four-inch urethane wheel, two X60s at 1.25:1, X44 hood at 80.5:1 total, 10-pound constant-force spring and a through-bore hood encoder. Separate X60 powers one-inch backspin rollers. Chain-driven azimuth has matched encoder reduction.","operation":"Hood covers 0–90 degrees per book. Controller uses empirical flight times, velocity-vector compensation and gyro latency compensation. The harness moves through a tensioned underbody route.","team_rationale":"Spring takes up cycloidal backlash. Below-floor cable buffer preserves hopper space and limits exposure to fuel impacts.","engineering_analysis":"Repeatable angle requires preloading the correct flank and measuring the output. Cable friction can change azimuth load with direction.","interfaces":"Launcher to hood rollers, hood output to encoder, underfloor cable tensioner to rotating turret.","service_and_failure_modes":"Fixed PTFE-covered redirects added friction, and tight bend at the turret caused shop failures. Team ran spare CAN and power and kept a turret/harness spare.","unknowns":"Exact position limits and bend radii, matched calibration tables, and independently measured on-move accuracy.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1987-broncobots-2026-cad-code-resources-release/524348"]}],"revisions":["Early plywood/PVC hook led to on-chassis V1 and a lower revised hook. The team also raised the support and added spring preload to address hood backlash. Final reported hopper capacity differs by team publication."],"transferable_principles":["Treat the annular feed, bearing stack and wire path as one assembly with three motions. Test emptying the last part of the hopper and feed recovery, and separate feed ceiling from actual scoring rate."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The architecture loses value if a slower serial path fails to empty a match load, or if short defended cycles make full-circle aim unnecessary relative to maintenance and calibration costs."],"remaining_gaps":["Independent throughput and scoring tests, final event configuration mapping and any endgame mechanism remain unverified."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/524348/11","locator":"Machining and stack-up attachments","purpose":"Candidate figures for marking the five rings, two bearings and shared fuel bore."},{"url":"https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf#page=11","locator":"Book pp. 10–12","purpose":"Candidate views for the enclosed rotor transmission, floating hood and harness route."}]}

title: 2023-1746 2023 rebuild (name not verified) complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-1746","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8","title":"OTTO at IRI","locator":"1:08–1:37 drive; 1:39–3:12 elevator; 3:15–5:24 intake and wrist; 5:27–8:20 controls; 8:26–10:00 autonomous preload","review_basis":"Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.","facts":["Team describes mostly stock Mk4i L1 swerve, a continuously rigged compact elevator and one cone/cube tool.","The later IRI elevator used one-inch tubing and custom guides after the team found its earlier structure carried too much mass high.","The team demonstrated cone and cube acquisition at the single substation and described a servo-triggered cube launcher for autonomous."],"limitations":"IRI is a later snapshot. The field record and interview do not establish every DCMP/Worlds component or the exact earlier mast angle."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The core OTTO design uses the same roller hand to acquire and place either game piece. In the owner’s account of the DCMP/Worlds rebuild, the hand rides a four-stage fixed inclined elevator and rotates on a wrist. The mast supplies height and reach together, while the wrist changes tool orientation. The later IRI interview confirms the compact continuously rigged lift and shared hand in that later configuration. It also describes the earlier, taller machine and the changes made to take weight out of the top. The separate autonomous cube launcher serves one preload task. The normal piece cycle can still stay in one hand.","piece_flow":["The driver aligns the mouth to the piece. The owner describes floor pickup with the wrist lowered. The IRI interview shows the single-substation method where the driver brings the robot flush to the wall and a human player supplies the piece.","The rollers pull the piece into the hand and retain it while the lift and wrist move toward the scoring pose. The hand releases the cone or cube at the target.","The lift and wrist return toward the acquisition pose. The autonomous preload launcher follows a separate path and avoids an initial chassis turn in some routines."],"packaging_and_motion":"On a fixed inclined mast, every increment of travel changes both the tool’s height and its horizontal position. Layout begins with floor, loading, transit and scoring poses with the actual piece installed. Place the mast and wrist pivots so the chassis can reach all essential poses without using extra reverse or steering moves. The early high-mass design is a useful reminder that a mechanically simple architecture still requires a loaded stability check.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis and approach","construction":"The interview describes Mk4i L1 modules with minimal modification.","operation":"Drive the single tool to the floor, station or scoring approach that its workspace can reach.","team_rationale":"The team preferred available drive torque for its reported robot weight and defense.","engineering_analysis":"Direct acquisition shifts some workload from mechanism alignment to driver positioning. Evaluate time from first sight of the piece to confirmed capture, including failed approaches.","interfaces":"The mast line and bumper face constrain how close the rollers can reach the wall and floor.","service_and_failure_modes":"A bumper offset, arm zero change or poor alignment can show up as an acquisition problem even when roller speed is unchanged.","unknowns":"No measured turning, loaded acceleration or capture tolerance comparison.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]},{"name":"Continuously rigged elevator","construction":"The IRI team describes one-inch thin-wall tubing, custom Thrifty-inspired bearing blocks and a continuous belt.","operation":"Move the roller hand along the mast and hold each scoring height with closed-loop control.","team_rationale":"The team reduced high weight after its first version was too tall and heavy.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed mast removes a shoulder axis and makes packaging easier to reason about. It couples horizontal and vertical motion, so practical reach depends on the chassis pose.","interfaces":"Guide and belt loads change with tool extension. Belt tension, carriage yaw and wrist cable clearance matter through the entire stroke.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check binding and belt tracking with an off-center cone and inspect where the mast lands under bump contact.","unknowns":"The earlier rebuild angle and stage terminology come from owner recollection. The later interview supplies different evidence.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]},{"name":"Shared wrist and roller hand","construction":"The team credits 111 for the roller intake inspiration and 1339 for the wrist approach. A Falcon drives through gearing and chain. The tool uses machined polycarbonate and printed parts.","operation":"Rotate to the pickup pose, draw a cone or cube into the tool, hold possession through the lift movement and release at the node.","team_rationale":"The team selected the intake after seeing reliable use elsewhere. The wrist reduction gives useful holding torque.","engineering_analysis":"One possession path removes the timing and alignment demands of an intake-to-gripper handoff. It still needs a workable grip on both pieces and a wrist that holds position at load without excess current.","interfaces":"Tool width and cone orientation determine the practical floor and pole approach. The wrist and carriage must support the heaviest useful extension.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect wear at the roller surface, chain tension and flex in the tool plates. Compare acquisition at multiple piece orientations.","unknowns":"The full wrist reduction and field capture envelope remain unresolved.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]},{"name":"Autonomous preload and controls","construction":"Servo releases an over-center preload launcher. The lift and wrist hold targets with closed-loop control.","operation":"The launcher scores a staged cube rearward in the chosen autonomous routine, then normal acquisition uses the shared hand.","team_rationale":"The team described saving time otherwise lost to turning.","engineering_analysis":"A narrow autonomous exception can earn its complexity when it bypasses a repeatable dead movement. Count reset time, preload reliability and changes to the starting pose.","interfaces":"The preload launcher must coexist with the lift and remain clear of the normal cycle. The wrist’s higher torque and gravity load change tuning demands.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test scoring from modest pose error and confirm a failed preload leaves the rest of the autonomous routine useful.","unknowns":"The interview reports success qualitatively. It gives no matched comparison of all autos or a measured vision upgrade effect.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]}],"revisions":["Earlier tall structure gave way to the compact lift described at IRI.","The owner describes DCMP/Worlds fixed incline and shared hand. The IRI interview has its own configuration scope.","The autonomous preload path was added to eliminate a turn in selected starts."],"transferable_principles":["Plot the required possession poses against one constrained lift path before adding an arm axis.","Compare actual failed pickups and approach correction time before deciding whether a separate collector earns a handoff.","Validate low mass and simple load paths with the piece installed at the worst pose."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Add a separate collector when its increase in capture envelope repays the time and failure risk of the handoff.","An articulated arm can earn extra motion when the robot must reach from several chassis approaches or over large obstacles."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact 2023 DCMP and Worlds geometry and revision dates, complete field acquisition statistics, independently measured performance differences."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2023-4414 Tsunami complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-4414","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584/155","title":"HighTide Tsunami elevator write-up","locator":"Post 155, June 29","review_basis":"Read team's rigging, bearing, gearbox and tensioning explanation.","facts":"Continuous belt drive, inline reduction, supported idlers, belt clamps and return springs.","limitations":"Low maintenance is team-reported. No independent endurance data or CAD review."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=6","title":"HighTide Tsunami April configuration discussion","locator":"Posts 105, 111 and 122","review_basis":"Read team motor inventory quoted in post 105, virtual four-bar explanation and chassis answer.","facts":"One inventory lists 12 swerve motors, powered cube intake, arm rollers and crawler tracks. Unequal sprockets change claw attitude.","limitations":"Motor inventory describes a specific configuration. It does not identify match settings or crawler geometry."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=11","title":"HighTide Tsunami offseason changes and fabrication discussion","locator":"Posts 212, 219 and 222","review_basis":"Read team updates on Chezy changes, intake impact and roller fabrication.","facts":"Chezy arm and wrist replacement, camera tower and ballast. Later posts detail A/B variants and common tube roller construction.","limitations":"Descriptions of later intake and roller details do not establish each part's installation at Worlds."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Tsunami combined a compact swerve base, slanted belt elevator and an arm whose virtual four-bar sets claw pitch as a function of arm angle. The April motor inventory describes separate powered cube intake deployment and rolling, plus a powered arm intake. In that architecture a cone can be carried by the scoring head, while assisted cube pickup requires an additional interface between the collector and head. The exact through-mast path reported in the corpus was not reverified in the written sources. The Chezy configuration replaced the virtual four-bar and head with a different arm-and-wrist design and should be treated separately.","piece_flow":"The arm's head is the placement mechanism. In the April version unequal sprockets change head angle as the arm swings, coupling pickup and placement attitudes to arm position. The separate cube collector provides an alternative acquisition path, with any cube delivered to the arm for elevated placement. The posts establish independent powered functions at both mechanisms. They do not establish the contact order, piece sensor, timing or whether every cube used the collector. For later variants the team documents plastic tube rollers with stretched silicone and printed, glued hubs.","packaging_and_motion":"Drive motors for the elevator are inline with its bottom 2-by-2 tube, preserving travel and overlap. The slant reduces gravity assistance along the guide rails, and the team added four constant-force springs to bring the intermediate stages down. The base is 26 by 26 inches. HighTide reports declining the one-inch module inset it had used on a larger base. Inference: the support footprint, moving mast mass and arm reach jointly constrain acceleration. A wide transfer corridor earns its volume only if the actual collector and arm can intersect safely with a held cube.","subsystems":[{"name":"Continuous belt elevator","construction":"WCP inline blocks with 0.75-inch bearings, 5.6:1 reduction, 36-tooth 18 mm HTD5 drive pulley and fiberglass Gates belt. Printed Onyx redirects are supported through their width. A toothed block and cam tension the belt.","operation":"Belt runs between the stages. Four constant-force springs help the intermediate stages return through an inclined, low-gravity-assist path.","team_rationale":"The team wanted compact packaging and more overlap. It selected larger bearings after smaller ones had cracked or worn into tubing.","engineering_analysis":"Return force must overcome worst-case loaded guide and belt friction. Extra bends and belt stiffness consume margin that would otherwise seat stages reliably.","interfaces":"Base tube carries the gearbox. The moving carriage carries arm loads. Belt clamps and redirects fit within the mast envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check smooth redirects, belt tracking and clamp slip after rebuilds. Compare repeatability on rapid reversals, where sticky stages can settle in the wrong order.","unknowns":"Belt tension target, stage travel and endurance measurements.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584/155"]},{"name":"Arm, wrist and cube intake","construction":"April arm uses an unequal-sprocket virtual four-bar and powered head rollers. The April inventory gives separate motors for cube roller and deploy. The offseason arm and wrist use lightened 7075 construction.","operation":"Arm angle determines claw pitch in April. The replacement arm and wrist use roller locations inspired by 1323. Later A/B notes distinguish some intake contact hardware.","team_rationale":"The offseason changes targeted lower moving mass and improved autonomous reliability. The team reports a roller breaking while the 7075 intake plates survived impacts.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed angular relationship simplifies actuation but constrains the pose family. Measure ground contact and high-node clearance together before changing sprocket sizes.","interfaces":"The carriage takes the linkage reaction. The collector and claw must share a transfer envelope without fouling the mast or stowed hardware.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect roller cores, glued hubs and pivot lash after contact. Test incomplete transfer and reversal.","unknowns":"April handoff geometry, linkage ratios and revision-specific pickup sequences.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=6","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=11"]},{"name":"Swerve, crawler and vision","construction":"April inventory lists 12 motors across swerve and one for crawler tracks. Chezy revisions added a vision tower and ballast low behind the elevator.","operation":"Swerve sets approach position. The tower improves sightlines to retroreflective tape and provides a rear-facing cone-tracking camera for autonomous.","team_rationale":"The team reports two high autonomous cones became possible without tipping after the changes. It also reports trading practice and readiness for the upgrades.","engineering_analysis":"Extra motors raise demand on packaging and power. Evaluate combined drivetrain and lift load with realistic batteries and loaded acceleration.","interfaces":"Wheel support polygon and mast loads bound tipping. Camera clearance competes with the slanted elevator and arm.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check approach under voltage sag and verify camera extrinsics after impacts.","unknowns":"Crawler operation, current limits and quantified vision success.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=6","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=11"]}],"revisions":["April configuration had the virtual four-bar, separate powered cube intake and crawler in the reported motor inventory. At Chezy the team changed the arm/wrist, vision placement and ballast. November posts distinguish A/B intake variants and construction."],"transferable_principles":["Preserve stage overlap when packaging a lift transmission. Validate force margin for retraction. Treat a mechanically coupled wrist as a designed pose curve."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Friction or belt bend losses can erase continuous rigging advantages. A cube collector is worthwhile only if broader capture offsets transfer time and failures."],"remaining_gaps":["Verified April transfer path, crawler function, event installation mapping, exact drivetrain current settings and independent service measurements."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"Post 155","subject":"Candidate team illustrations of inline drive, belt redirects and tensioner. Pair with a separate arm pose diagram."},{"source_index":2,"locator":"Post 222","subject":"Candidate roller construction image. Label the A/B context."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2026-125 Neutrons 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-125","review_date":"2026-11-07","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8","title":"Team 125 NUTRONs interview","locator":"0:42–1:44 frame; 2:12–3:54 collector; 4:38–5:50 serializer; 5:52–7:34 turret; 9:22–12:59 controls and autonomous","review_basis":"Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.","facts":["Trapezoidal frame gives the dish space while leaving room for modules.","The team replaced a dual-roller intake with a continuous contact drum and revised the serializer center.","A rotating capture dish and central up-feed drive independently, with a low inset turret above."],"limitations":"Some reported values are configuration-specific. Captions do not authenticate event installation or hidden geometry."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"NUTRONs shaped the entire machine around the circular serializer. The chassis gives the moving capture mechanism a large footprint. Fuel exits the dish through the center, allowing one vertical path to supply the rotating shooter. This architecture buys freedom in where and when the robot can aim. It spends chassis volume, integration time and moving-shot tuning to get it. That makes it a useful rival for a wide fixed shooter, especially when evaluating whether aiming freedom pays for the feed and packaging cost.","piece_flow":["The removable four-bar collector uses a continuous roller contact to pull fuel across the bumper.","Fuel settles into the enlarged circular working dish. The rotating pickup brings an intake point to pieces around the perimeter.","The independent center uptake captures fuel and carries it to the turret. Additional contacts close the dead region near the axis.","The turret sets yaw, the launcher establishes speed and the hood sets exit elevation. The hood has a low travel pose."],"packaging_and_motion":"The frame widens where the collector and dish need area and narrows toward the back. The interview describes a mix of stock and altered module packaging. A coaxial handoff reduces dependence on turret azimuth, but the rotating feeder, center column, wires, shooter sweep and access panels still need independent space. Keep the ground-to-dish and dish-to-column transitions serviceable after the superstructure is installed.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis around the dish","construction":"Wide front and tighter rear rails form a trapezoid around the circular fuel working volume. The rear modules are packaged around the dish.","operation":"Drive a low-profile route while leaving the center available for the serializer and launcher.","team_rationale":"The team selected the chassis shape to accommodate the enlarged dish.","engineering_analysis":"Draw the actual dish working diameter and wheel envelopes before comparing frame shapes. Chassis corners that appear unused can still carry bumper mounts, wiring, battery access or collision loads.","interfaces":"Frame rails must support the dish and leave enough room for module extraction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether a wheel or module can be replaced without disturbing dish alignment. Inspect rear mounts after side impacts.","unknowns":"Exact tolerances and installed mass distribution were not measured.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]},{"name":"Four-bar collector","construction":"Removable four-bar with a continuous roller and kicker geometry. The team describes a small set of shoulder bolts at the module interface.","operation":"Set the mouth low enough for fuel acquisition and carry fuel over the bumper into the dish.","team_rationale":"Earlier separated contact geometry jammed. The continuous roller reduces gaps in coverage.","engineering_analysis":"A broad mouth can collect more fuel per approach, but weak coverage near supports can make one edge the practical bottleneck. An accessible removal joint limits the cost of impact repairs.","interfaces":"The extended mouth and retracting bars must clear the bumper and keep the low travel profile.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare edge pickup and simultaneous arrivals, then inspect the mount after offset contacts.","unknowns":"No measured approach tolerance or durability trials.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]},{"name":"Rotating capture and up-feed","construction":"A rotating dish and a separately driven central up-feed share an axis. Additional wheels address a center dead zone.","operation":"Move the pickup point to fuel around the dish and lift it in a single stream to the turret.","team_rationale":"The team kept the serializer for moving-shot flexibility and made the working dish larger.","engineering_analysis":"Independent speeds let the mechanism tune capture availability separately from the upward feed. A jam at the central intake can still starve a ready launcher.","interfaces":"The center outlet must deliver consistent piece position across dish orientations and turret motion.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure recovery from two pieces entering together and the fraction of fuel stranded near the center.","unknowns":"Team-reported working dish counts are configuration estimates. Bulk hopper capacity is a different quantity.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]},{"name":"Turret, hood and moving shot","construction":"Inset yaw drive, multi-motor launcher and lowering hood. The team discusses interpolation and motion compensation.","operation":"Select range-based settings, move to target yaw and adjust the shot for the robot’s motion and flight time.","team_rationale":"The team chose the architecture to score or feed while moving around defense.","engineering_analysis":"Compare the fraction of usable field time when the robot can collect and shoot with an alternative that turns the chassis. The value of yaw freedom depends on maintained localization, shot readiness and a reliable single feed.","interfaces":"Hood lowering determines trench travel clearance. Cable limits constrain turret travel and where the scoring pose can resume.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify a missed camera update, a shot at a yaw limit and recovery after multiple fuel loads.","unknowns":"No independent accuracy map or matched comparison with a fixed shooter.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]}],"revisions":["Frame and serializer enlarged together.","Dual collector arrangement changed to a continuous roller.","Central uptake contacts and launcher power were revised."],"transferable_principles":["Lay out the feeder, frame and drive modules together when a large round component sets the envelope.","Compare shooting flexibility against the number of pieces delivered and scored per whole cycle.","Use a constrained test to separate a poor center handoff from a slow launch mechanism."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A fixed wide shooter can win where the scoring route naturally provides the required heading and full-bin throughput matters more.","A rotating shooter can earn its complexity when usable moving shots preserve collection routes and reduce defender control."],"remaining_gaps":["Configuration-by-event mapping, complete mechanical dimensions, measured workload, accuracy and scoring-rate distributions."],"recommended_images":[]}

title: 2022-2481 Roboteers 2022 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-2481","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","title":"Behind the Bumpers 2481 Roboteers | Rapid React","locator":"1:23–2:01 frame, 2:09–4:07 cargo path, 4:15–8:26 climb","review_basis":"Read the public timestamped English transcript from Central Illinois.","facts":["Two-roller four-bar changed from Velcro to compliant wheels, with an extra asymmetric contact to sequence two adjacent balls.","Cargo rises along Lexan into a 180-degree turret. Team reduced launcher wheel mass and used three compliant wheels to address backspin.","Front climb wheels drive against the truss while the rear set pushes from the floor. Guides center on the truss and a carabiner-like catch closes around the rung."],"limitations":["Automatic captions. No CAD or frame-by-frame inspection. Line sensors were prospective at this event."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919","title":"Roboteers Team 2481 2022 Robot Reveal","locator":"Team replies #9 and #15","review_basis":"Read indexed Chief Delphi thread text.","facts":["The team reported a 26.5-inch width and identified separate Falcon motors for the two climb wheel sets and two Redlines for shooter feed."],"limitations":["The motor list does not determine transmission or controls."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919/78","title":"Roboteers Team 2481 2022 Robot Reveal, Ben Martin follow-up","locator":"Reply #78, May 2, on page 4","review_basis":"Read indexed page 4 team reply.","facts":["Team links the 44-inch frame to the truss geometry and the fifth module to a wider stance within the cut-corner footprint."],"limitations":["The reply refers to older published swerve code as analogous. No 2022 code implementation was audited."]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Roboteers built their endgame into the chassis geometry. Floor drive uses five steerable modules on an elongated octagon, while the hangar approach deploys separately powered contact wheels fore and aft to climb the truss and catch traversal. The scoring half uses a centered, upward cargo path into a limited-travel turret.","piece_flow":"The leading four-bar roller grabs the ball and supplies compression for handoff. The second roller’s angled contacts steer inward. An extra wheel on one side advances the right-hand ball first when two arrive together. Successive rollers carry the ordered flow upward against Lexan into the turret. The heavy lower contact accelerates the ball and three green upper contacts reduce spin before release. Exact holding stations and feed permissions remain unresolved.","packaging_and_motion":"The two deployed wheel contacts and truss face define a geometric system with the chassis length. The team cites 16-inch reach at both ends and a roughly 44-inch chassis. Once the front wheels grip the truss, the rear wheels push on the carpet as chassis pitch changes. Field traction and guide capture replace intermediate rung handoffs. Chassis yaw and turret rotation remain distinct scoring motions, and the dedicated climb drives add two more powered functions.","subsystems":[{"name":"Elongated chassis and swerve","construction":"Cut-corner frame and five Falcon-powered swerve modules.","operation":"Each module takes a vector based on its position on the chassis.","team_rationale":"Five increased usable wheelbase over four and saved mass and motor allocation relative to six.","engineering_analysis":"A wider support polygon can help lateral stability on a long frame. Unequal normal loads can limit how much five drives contribute during acceleration.","interfaces":"Outer shape fixes module stations and climb contact reach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check loaded contact on uneven flooring and steering zero after climb impacts.","unknowns":"Module model, exact coordinates and load split.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919/78"]},{"name":"Pickup and singulation","construction":"Four-bar with two rollers, compliant wheels replacing Velcro and one extra green wheel on the angled second roller.","operation":"The biased contact advances one of a side-by-side pair so the other can follow.","team_rationale":"The Velcro grabbed well but did not compress enough at transfer. The extra contact addressed simultaneous arrival jams.","engineering_analysis":"Passive priority reduces simultaneous occupation of the throat. It depends on enough timing separation under drive acceleration.","interfaces":"Front nip, second roller lateral centering, then feeder mouth.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch whether worn contact or a side hit changes which ball gets through.","unknowns":"Roller gaps, timing and actuator details.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY"]},{"name":"Transfer and turret","construction":"Lexan-backed lift, roller sets, half-turn turret, one heavy main wheel and three compliant upper wheels.","operation":"Lifts into the turret and launches with reduced backspin. Team described an annular shooting area and launchpad use.","team_rationale":"Reduced heavy-wheel count saved mass. Upper contacts reduce bounce-out.","engineering_analysis":"Half-turn azimuth decouples aim over part of the approach space. Outside that sweep the chassis still has to turn or the route must change.","interfaces":"Lift exit must remain aligned with the rotating inlet. Upper contact and main wheel condition jointly set release.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check turret limits and scuffs at the rotating entry before tuning RPM.","unknowns":"Staging sensors, turret cable accommodation and range map.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919"]},{"name":"Truss-driving traversal","construction":"Deployable front and rear drive wheels, guide rollers and self-closing rung hook.","operation":"Align to the truss, drive up using floor and truss reactions and close the hook after the rung moves past center.","team_rationale":"Truss geometry offered a promising path for triple climbs. Wheel size, grip and contact height were prototyped.","engineering_analysis":"If either contact runs out of traction or guide margin, the support geometry can disappear before the hook closes.","interfaces":"Rear carpet contact, front truss face and guide engagement followed by rung retention.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect wheel tread, guide damage and free hook return. Trial a yaw error and approach with partners already hanging.","unknowns":"Contact forces, current draw, recovery procedure and later line-sensor deployment.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919/78"]}],"revisions":["Central Illinois used manual lineup. Line sensing was planned for St. Louis. Velcro and multiple heavy shooter wheels describe prior configurations."],"transferable_principles":["Build a full-scale geometry and traction fixture before committing chassis dimensions. Validate passive singulation with two simultaneous arrivals."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A narrow guide capture window, shared truss interference or contaminated contact surface can erase the benefit of avoiding intermediate rung transfers."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-by-event alignment changes, swept partner clearance and distributions of approach-to-hook time."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","locator":"2:17–3:09 and 4:24–5:42","purpose":"Seek stills of the asymmetric intake contact and floor/truss/rung load paths."}]}

title: 2026-604 Toploader complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-604","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289","title":"Quixilver Toploader mechanical and software release","locator":"Posts 1, 6–7, 13, 15, 18–20 and 24","review_basis":"Read the complete team overview and later construction and service answers in the public post stream.","facts":"Team chose a single turret despite higher full-width prototype feed rates. It details the split bucket, above-mounted turret, separately driven intake arms, and elastic sliding hopper.","limitations":"Prototype comparisons are team-reported. Release does not quantify collision loads or match throughput."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/SerializerSubsystem.java","title":"Toploader serializer implementation","locator":"setRollerVelocity and periodic","review_basis":"Read the pinned Java source for roller commands, rotor following and jam state transitions.","facts":"Rotor command follows filtered measured roller speed with a 1.2 surface-speed relationship. A persistent high-current and low-speed condition triggers a timed unjam command with the rotor stopped.","limitations":"Public source defines logic and thresholds at this commit. It supplies neither as-played logs nor recovery success rates."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/quixlib/math/LaunchCalculator.java","title":"Toploader launch calculator implementation","locator":"CSV load, computeLaunchInfo and computeInstantaneousLaunchInfo","review_basis":"Read the pinned Java source for interpolated launch parameters and motion correction.","facts":"Projects with a 50 ms latency term, evaluates velocity at the offset turret base, subtracts planar turret velocity and rotates into the tilted body frame.","limitations":"The source does not establish calibration error under defense, nor validate the offline model against match shots."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Toploader is a single-stream moving scorer designed around its dynamic point of capture serializer. Quixilver identifies serialization as its limiting stage. It reports roughly 15 BPS in a single-stream serializer prototype and 23 in full width, then chose the turret for scoring and feeding flexibility on the move. A single driver controls the robot with automated scoring and passing logic. Its bump-only autonomous routes were designed around traffic and partner timing.","piece_flow":"The front rollers deliver fuel into a sliding hopper over the circular bucket. A rotating scoop brings the capture point around the stored pile. Side omni rollers and a separately driven upfeed push successive fuel items into a corrugated-plastic tube with printed ends. New arrivals push fuel already in the column into the overhead-supported turret. The launcher uses silicone-covered PETG rollers, with recessed ties to hold the sleeve.","packaging_and_motion":"A 27-inch square frame preserves bucket diameter with standard-form swerve packaging. Crossbars isolate battery and module compartments and the rear bumper mount carries serializer armor. The inset turret hangs from the superstructure to keep its swept volume small and the bucket entrance open. A two-piece plywood bucket and removable rear wall section provide battery and electronics access.","subsystems":[{"name":"Independent intake and sliding hopper","construction":"Separate X44 deploy on each polycarbonate arm, belt-driven silicone-covered dead-axle rollers and TPU belt supports and pulley plugs. Laminated corrugated hopper has polycarbonate slot reinforcement.","operation":"Intake deployment pushes the hopper outward and surgical tubing retracts it. The single-deploy kicker uses an elastic drive and a string-retained, loosely fitted cross tube.","team_rationale":"Independent arms addressed chain failure on the linked 2024 design. The team wanted belt centers to recover after a hit and avoided a rigid through-bolt at the flexible tube.","engineering_analysis":"Decouple impact compliance from belt retention and hopper guidance. Confirm the mechanism still closes when either side takes an off-axis hit.","interfaces":"Deploy motors to arm travel, deflecting arm to belt support, kicker plugs to string, intake to hopper slide.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports TPU pulley tooth wear after one to two events and brittle PETG predecessors. Inspect the string, tooth roots and slot laminate together.","unknowns":"Deploy synchronization tolerances, force on slides and measured impact durability.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289"]},{"name":"Dynamic capture and column feed","construction":"Split plywood bucket, separately motorized rotating scoop and upfeed, side omni rollers, printed ends and corrugated tube.","operation":"Code averages ten roller speed samples, divides modeled roller surface speed by 1.2 and converts to rotor command. After 0.3 seconds of detected jam it stops the rotor, commands unjam velocity and resumes after 0.1 seconds.","team_rationale":"Separate drives allow tuning while omni rollers reduce lateral forces. Split bucket preserves access.","engineering_analysis":"Following actual roller speed limits overdelivery during droop, but a jam downstream can leave fuel trapped above the detection point. Test with a fully packed column and minimum fill.","interfaces":"Scoop and bucket to roller, upfeed to tube, column to turret entry, and roller current and velocity to recovery state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Code logs target and actual velocities and jam state. Inspect tube ends for distortion, and correlate retries with current and column fill.","unknowns":"Compression, full-scale success rate, wear-driven threshold drift and event firmware parity.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/SerializerSubsystem.java"]},{"name":"Turret support and automated launch","construction":"Segmented polycarbonate ring, aluminum gear, PETG spacers and lubricated slider. Camera localization uses four viewpoints and multi-tag observations.","operation":"The team gates serializer feed on launch speed, elevation and yaw tolerances plus recent tag evidence. The solver interpolates a distance table for scoring, then compensates for turret motion and chassis attitude.","team_rationale":"Small swept volume protects hopper flow. Offline trajectory selection reduces onboard computation and seeks launch pairs less sensitive to errors.","engineering_analysis":"Mechanical clearance and camera availability both affect firing duty cycle. Evaluate where ready-to-feed interruptions cluster before altering the table.","interfaces":"Overhead ring to rotating turret, tube to scorer, pose and velocity to aim, readiness to serializer enable.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect slider friction and play after contamination or spacer replacement. A camera view blocked by field geometry can interrupt the gate.","unknowns":"Loaded angle and speed errors, observed vision dropout and endgame hardware.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/SerializerSubsystem.java","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/quixlib/math/LaunchCalculator.java"]}],"revisions":["The team moved to TPU plugs after PETG impact failures. Earlier rigid aluminum tube plugs remained in one location, while cracking at another bolted tube drove the flexible TPU and string design."],"transferable_principles":["Compare serializers at equivalent game-piece supply and aim duty cycle. Treat service access and moving envelopes as part of the piece path."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A full-width approach can win the comparison if aiming opportunities are plentiful and serial delivery limits scored fuel. Pose-dependent feed gates lose value if availability is too low in intended field zones."],"remaining_gaps":["Controlled match-rate comparisons, as-played current traces and clearances throughout intake and turret motion remain open."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/524289/15","locator":"Team bearing stack views","purpose":"Candidate annotation for how the top plate captures the turret."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/524289/1","locator":"Serializer and hopper sections","purpose":"Candidate overview and sectional figure for the scoop-to-tube handoff and service split."}]}

title: 2019-1323 2019 competition robot (name sources conflict) complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2019-1323","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379","title":"1323 Elevator","locator":"Post 17","review_basis":"Read the team explanation of internal continuous rigging.","facts":"Two pull and two return runs have individual ratchet adjustment on half-inch hex. Two geared bottom spools counterrotate. Return runs loosened when only the pull side was tensioned. Three stages supply overlap and travel for high rocket scoring.","limitations":"A 3310 image earlier in the thread is a different robot. No complete rigging drawing is established."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379?page=3","title":"1323 Elevator, page 3","locator":"Posts 44, 45, 52","review_basis":"Read team material and current discussion including the correction.","facts":"Machined blocks replaced poorly performing plastic blocks. Two 775pros and no constant-force springs were used. A tentative five-amp hold estimate was followed by two amps total.","limitations":"No trace, load condition, or meter location for the current report."},{"url":"https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018","title":"MadTown 2019DeepSpace source","locator":"13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018, Superstructure, BallIntake, BallCarriage, DiskIntake, DiskScorer and Jacks","review_basis":"Read selected state handlers and request methods from pinned checkout.","facts":"Ball intake uses motor current for capture while the carriage uses a banner input. Disk handoff has separate delivery, scorer detection and lift states. Jacks uses the disk-intake motor with a solenoid shift.","limitations":"Static public code snapshot, not tied to a specific event or robot image."},{"url":"https://team1323.com/first/frc/2019-frc-season/","title":"Team 1323 2019 FRC Season","locator":"Robot introduction","review_basis":"Read the team season account.","facts":"Team calls the 2019 robot ETR 16.","limitations":"Identity and season context only."},{"url":"https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2019/team/1323","title":"FIRST FRC Event Web, team 1323","locator":"2019 team summary","review_basis":"Read the official robot registration field.","facts":"FIRST calls the 2019 robot ETR13.","limitations":"Registration field alone cannot reconcile the name."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"MadTown combined a swerve chassis, an internally rigged elevator, a wrist-controlled floor ball intake and carriage receiver, separate disk handling, and a shared-motor jack system. Floor mechanisms put pieces into a known transfer pose before the elevator delivers them. Selected vision routines make lift height part of the approach, since a mechanically reachable score pose can obstruct tracking. The jack mode changes which subsystem owns a motor controller and also reuses the ball-intake wrist and rollers.","piece_flow":["Ball intake detects a current threshold held for a dwell period. The feed routine commands intake height, wrist feed angle, carriage receive and intake feed, and waits for carriage possession before ending feed. The carriage uses separate sensing.","Disk intake detects acquisition, delivers to a scorer in ground-intaking state, and waits for scorer detection before shutting off intake and moving through handoff height. The scorer can also receive directly from the station. The eject routine pairs disk release with a backing trajectory."],"packaging_and_motion":"Internal ropes and machined blocks leave the lift's working volume useful while making tension access important. The lift and wrist must share a transfer pose and a collision-free scoring path. Chassis and lift cannot be planned independently when camera visibility depends on height. Jack deployment adds contact geometry and software ownership constraints to hardware already serving the disk and ball systems.","subsystems":[{"name":"Continuous lift","construction":"Three stages, four separately tensioned runs, opposed geared spools, machined bearing blocks and two 775pros.","operation":"Paired up and return runs move the assembly through the required stage travel. The team reports about one amp per motor at hold in an unspecified condition.","team_rationale":"The team sought overlap at level three, preferred the internal design to its earlier cascades and wanted to avoid repeatedly engaging a brake.","engineering_analysis":"Maintain preload on both rope directions. Effective spool radius and return slack affect reversal accuracy, while guide play and overlap affect extended stiffness.","interfaces":"Opposed spools must preserve compatible line payout. Carriage pose sets both transfer alignment and the useful vision window.","service_and_failure_modes":"Expose adjusters and inspect rope abrasion, block wear and changes after reversals.","unknowns":"Full reeving map, drum geometry and tested loads.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379?page=3","https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]},{"name":"Cargo and vision","construction":"Wristed collector with grabber and feeder, separate carriage motor and banner input, and swerve target tracking.","operation":"After receiving cargo, selected tracking logic moves through vision-visible heights, waits for tracking, commands scoring height and ejects.","team_rationale":"The code records the order and separate possession signals. It gives limited reasons for the physical construction.","engineering_analysis":"A current spike can also indicate a jam. Confirming possession at the receiver limits the consequences of an incorrect inference at the collector.","interfaces":"Wrist angle and lift height align the two assemblies. Target acquisition depends on camera line of sight and chassis heading.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check incomplete transfers, false current detections and stale vision before committing lift or eject.","unknowns":"Roller geometry, optical calibration and measured transfer robustness.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]},{"name":"Disk intake and scorer","construction":"Motorized ground intake and separate scorer, with possession checks and stowed, receiving, detecting and holding states.","operation":"Ground intake current is used in acquisition. Scorer detection has distinct modes for station and floor paths, and the two transfers converge on retention for scoring.","team_rationale":"The state split records different source interfaces. Physical rationale is sparsely documented.","engineering_analysis":"Owner changes should be explicit so lift motion cannot pull an incompletely received disk away.","interfaces":"Disk intake delivery, scorer state and elevator handoff height must agree.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sensing through partially delivered panels and recovery with mechanisms engaged.","unknowns":"Contact geometry and version-specific installation.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]},{"name":"Jacks and PTO","construction":"Solenoid-controlled takeoff and shared disk-intake motor controller; feedback source depends on configuration.","operation":"Jacks applies position control when power is shifted to it and its sensor is connected. Climb sequences coordinate wrist gearing, roller pull and chassis motion.","team_rationale":"Motor sharing is explicit. A team comparative weight or reliability assessment was not found.","engineering_analysis":"Shared actuation saves a motor at the cost of interlocks and a reliable mechanical shift under the expected load.","interfaces":"Shift state must coordinate controller ownership and feedback selection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test wrong feedback, incomplete shifts and a stopped climb under load.","unknowns":"Physical lock, shift confirmation and exact competed macro.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]}],"revisions":["Return-only slack prompted independent tensioning of all runs. Team reports moving from plastic to machined blocks. Hold-current correction is evidence refinement, separate from hardware revision."],"transferable_principles":["Treat the receiving assembly as the authority on handoff completion. Specify pose-dependent sensor visibility before optimizing motion timing."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Reject PTO reuse if a failed shift compromises both endgame and piece control, or if a dedicated motor yields a simpler qualified load path."],"remaining_gaps":["Naming remains unresolved. No event-specific software mapping, rope drawing, complete climb load path, or narrated interview review."],"recommended_images":[{"path":"images/history_2019-1323_source.jpg","reason":"Team season photograph for the swerve, elevator and wrist relationship."}]}

title: 2025-180 S.P.A.M. 2025 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-180","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","title":"S.P.A.M. 2025 public robot code","locator":"README, RobotContainer, Auto, IntakeCoral, elevatorArm, elevatorArmAlgae and climber Java packages","review_basis":"Read controller bindings, real hardware I/O and transition logic in public snapshot","facts":["Floor intake, indexer and arm sensors coordinate handoff. Station feeds in reverse at a separate receiving pose. Cage capture and winch have separate motor commands and two digital latch inputs."],"limitations":["Code establishes configuration and commanded behavior, with no measurement of physical geometry or event-specific deployment."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667","title":"FRC 180 S.P.A.M. 2025 Code Release","locator":"Posts 1 and 4, Ryan_S","review_basis":"Read team release and technical follow-up","facts":["The one-driver setup led to cross-subsystem triggers. Dynamic floor coral targeting shifted most motion toward DriveToPose, and simulation was used for early driver practice and logic validation."],"limitations":["Team reports simulation and field use without publishing a timed comparison or reliability dataset."]}],"subsystems":[{"name":"Floor acquisition and coral registration","construction":"Pivoted intake with separate bottom-roller command, LaserCan, driven indexer and three discrete inputs on the arm tool.","operation":"Gate the transfer on receiver pose, stage at the arm, and suppress coral deployment while a piece is entering. The arm also has passive indexing as a default command.","team_rationale":"The team described coordinating many subsystems centrally for one driver. Haptic feedback tells the driver when floor coral is acquired.","engineering_analysis":"The intake sensor can justify driving away from the pickup sooner than arm staging alone. Keep downstream release gated separately so an intake detection cannot be mistaken for a scoring-ready piece.","interfaces":"Intake sensor to autonomous transition, indexer to arm, and receiving height and angle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test out-of-order sensor events, stalled transfer and damage to the bottom-roller mount. Rumble reports software state and should be checked against physical possession.","unknowns":"Roller contact geometry, material, preload and station funnel geometry.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]},{"name":"Scoring and dynamic alignment","construction":"Elevator, arm pivot, coral and algae drive channels, and camera-based target selection. Algae tool I/O includes a CANrange.","operation":"Branch and level input select a reef target. Auto combines pose-based travel to a seen floor piece with separate scoring and intake triggers. PathPlanner retains the curved exit from the first score.","team_rationale":"Most moves were straight or depended on observed piece positions. The team used simulation to reuse behavior across teleop and auto and used field time to refine vision and auto-align.","engineering_analysis":"Target-dependent motion cuts dead travel if detection is timely. Occlusion and erroneous detection can erase that gain, so test with clutter and partially visible reef tags.","interfaces":"Camera to drivetrain target, drivetrain tolerance to scoring, and lift and pivot release geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for alignment timeouts, camera dropout and interrupted scoring reset. Team reports pulsed rumble for slow alignment and separate completion feedback.","unknowns":"Field-calibrated pose tolerances across events, mechanical lift rigging and tool dimensions.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]},{"name":"Cage capture and lift","construction":"Separate Talon FX outputs for winch and grabber, absolute position feedback and two digital inputs.","operation":"Deployment advances to a position threshold. In deployed state the grabber runs until both sensors have tripped and cleared. A separate driver command winches toward the climb limit.","team_rationale":"The team used distinct rumbles for deployed and latched conditions because the mechanism is difficult to see from the driver station.","engineering_analysis":"Two completed sensor transitions can distinguish entry from settled engagement. Confirm that a skewed cage or bounce cannot produce the same sequence with poor retention.","interfaces":"Grabber inputs to capture confirmation, winch feedback to travel limit, and climb pose to arm and floor-intake clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sensor sequence, mount alignment and load holding after disable, which motor neutral mode alone cannot establish.","unknowns":"Physical hook and retention geometry, winch reeving, cage load path and proof test.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Anemone coordinates a floor intake and intermediate indexer with a coral roller tool on a pivoting elevator arm. The lift and arm also present an independently driven algae tool. A station receive pose runs the coral tool in reverse, providing another supply path. The one-driver interface can align to a branch while issuing lift and pivot commands. Late in the match, a separate powered cage capture and winch operate while the elevator, arm and floor intake move into climb-specific positions.","piece_flow":"For floor coral, the code moves the lift to stow, extends the intake and sets the arm to receive. Once lift and arm are ready it starts the indexer and intake on the arm. An intake LaserCan detects a piece, and three arm inputs distinguish partial, entering and staged coral. The intake stops feeding once coral enters the arm. Station input commands reverse intake and indexing with the arm at a different height and angle. Coral is released at the selected branch or L1 pose. The code also exposes reef algae removal, floor or lollipop pickup poses, and processor and barge modes through the arm's algae tool.","packaging_and_motion":"Elevator height, arm pivot and floor-intake deployment must agree before coral crosses the handoff gap. The code also uses a closer reef deployment gate in situations where the arm can block a vision target. The resulting motion constraint is partly optical. A pose can clear the reef physically and still obscure the camera needed to finish lining up. In climb mode the arm and elevator take separate positions while the coral intake uses an extreme-stow command.","revisions":["Team documents a shift from broader PathPlanner use to dynamic DriveToPose with a retained first-exit curve. Hardware installation dates remain unresolved in the released code."],"transferable_principles":["Treat early piece detection and scoring-ready confirmation as different states. Simulate trigger ordering and validate contact and occlusion on a real field."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Dynamic pickup loses value if the first reliable piece observation arrives late, alignment is often obstructed, or the handoff prevents driving away promptly."],"remaining_gaps":["Mechanical drawing and dimensional review, event-specific software revisions, cage retention hardware and field cycle distributions."],"recommended_images":["Team code-release post 1 for the labeled Anemone overview.","AdvantageScope simulation illustration in the same post for state visualization, explicitly identified as simulation."]}

title: 2022-125 Freefall complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-125","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8","title":"Behind the Bumpers 125 NUTRONs | Rapid React","locator":"1:19–3:13 intake/feed, 3:20–5:12 shooter, 5:20–7:49 climb and autonomous","review_basis":"Read timestamped English transcript of team members at Week Zero.","facts":["Pneumatic intake uses a dead axle and metal printed pulleys. Retraction actively pushes cargo into the feeder. The S-curve preserves a low robot and leaves an open path for bouncing cargo.","Light grippy main wheels, two powered contacts and adjustable hood support range and backspin control. The climb uses contact against another rung to change hanging attitude.","Full climb automation, a five-ball auto and the Velcro bounce-pickup roller were plans at the interview."],"limitations":["Automatic transcript contains inconsistent ordinal descriptions of the rungs. The reaction principle is clearer than the exact sequence."]},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2022-frc125-reveal-the-nutrons-present-freefall/405399","title":"2022 FRC125 Reveal — The NUTRONs present Freefall","locator":"March 11, posts 1 and 9 by Brandon Holley","review_basis":"Read the team’s reveal and explanatory follow-up in the indexed thread.","facts":["Sorting was added after Week Zero. Once two desired balls are held and the inner feed stops, arriving cargo exits through the top of the intake. The team credits Citrus as an influence."],"limitations":["No sensor placement, software or exact path dimensions are given. The team’s rules interpretation is not an official ruling."]}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Freefall pairs a low, open-front cargo system with a two-contact adjustable shooter. Its intake deploys briefly for acquisition and then retracts to complete the transfer. The early climb is a rung-reacting traversal mechanism that changes chassis pitch during the hang to make the final hooks reachable. The March sorting system adds a distinct way for surplus cargo to escape upstream of the launcher.","piece_flow":"With the collector down, the roller gets the first purchase on floor cargo. As the collector retracts, its roller pushes the ball into the feeder contact, accelerating the first handoff. The S-curve connects that low entrance to the hooded launcher while leaving a possible route for balls bouncing above the normal floor intake. The shooter applies powered contacts to control both velocity and spin. In the later sorting account, stopping the inner feed when two desired balls are staged leaves a top-of-intake ejection route. Exact Week Zero staging sensors and March color-dependent routing through the lower path remain unresolved.","packaging_and_motion":"Collector angle changes entry and transfer geometry, so stow timing is part of cargo handling. The offset between low entrance and raised shot is covered by a curved feeder. On the climb, the hanging angle governs the final hook reach. Pushing on another rung rotates the suspended chassis, making the field contact a load-bearing interface rather than a timing cue.","subsystems":[{"name":"Intake and entrance","construction":"Pneumatic retracting collector with dead axle, metal printed pulleys and a separate roller identified for prospective Velcro.","operation":"Deploys near a ball and retracts essentially immediately to push it into the next roller.","team_rationale":"Fast acquisition and resistance to hits were priorities. Prototypes suggested Velcro could capture low-bouncing cargo otherwise missed.","engineering_analysis":"Retraction can increase handoff force without another actuator, but the two contacts must overlap in time. A late retract can leave cargo riding at the bumper.","interfaces":"Floor contact, retraction stroke, feeder inlet and open upper entry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect dead-axle supports and handoff gap after side impacts. Test bounced and grounded balls separately.","unknowns":"Roller diameters, dead-axle bearing stack and later Velcro installation.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]},{"name":"Feeder and March sorter","construction":"S-shaped roller path. Later sorting architecture provides an ejection path through the intake.","operation":"Moves cargo through the low package to the shooter. Once two desired balls are held, stopped inner feed allows incoming cargo to be ejected above the intake.","team_rationale":"Low height and open front drove the curve. Hunting for alliance cargo in mixed piles took too much time at Week Zero.","engineering_analysis":"An alternate exit can save the approach turn and a shooter cycle. The release path must stay clear with a worn or partially compressed ball already staged.","interfaces":"Retracting collector, curved feeder compression, desired cargo count and shooter inlet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure whether a rejected ball disturbs either held ball. Check surfaces for wedging at changes in curvature.","unknowns":"Sorting sensor type, lower exit geometry and command sequencing.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2022-frc125-reveal-the-nutrons-present-freefall/405399"]},{"name":"Launcher and range control","construction":"Light grippy wheels, powered front and rear contacts, adjustable hood and Limelight.","operation":"With the hub in view, software adjusts hood and shooter settings. Team favored the edge of the tarmac.","team_rationale":"Prior wheels gave useful grip at lower weight. Tests favored reduced spin and enough energy to enter without bouncing out.","engineering_analysis":"The two contact speeds jointly determine energy and spin. A faster shot can reduce successful retention even if it enters the opening more often.","interfaces":"Feeder output, traction, vision range and hood angle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare first and second exit conditions, then check for tread slip and hood backlash.","unknowns":"Wheel construction details, setpoint curves and chassis aim routine.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]},{"name":"Rung-reacting climber","construction":"Primary deployment arms, reaction bars and final capture hooks.","operation":"After initial engagement and pull, reaction bars press on an intermediate rung to flatten the robot enough for the final hooks to catch traversal. Week Zero sequencing was manual after arm deployment.","team_rationale":"The team sought a faster route that skipped an intermediate hang and added the reaction bars after finding an unfavorable hanging angle.","engineering_analysis":"The extra contact changes pitch and local rung load. One-sided contact can twist the chassis and leave one hook short.","interfaces":"Initial suspension, reaction contact and final hook capture.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test loaded skew, contact slip and recovery after a missed final catch.","unknowns":"Exact rung ordinals from a corroborating diagram, actuator details and later automation deployment.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]}],"revisions":["Week Zero interview establishes early manual climb and no active sorting. March reveal follow-up establishes later ejection behavior. Five-ball and automated climb were future work at the earlier snapshot."],"transferable_principles":["Use a deployment mechanism for handoff where its controlled sweep can maintain contact. Measure hub retention as well as entry, and design the loaded reach geometry before committing the climber."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Retraction-assisted transfer is weaker if multiple balls block the same throat. The pitch reaction works only if intermediate contact stays stable across setup errors."],"remaining_gaps":["Chassis drive model, event-specific sorting revision, full sensor state machine and verified climb contact sequence."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8","locator":"2:19–3:13 and 5:36–6:52","purpose":"Seek stills showing retraction handoff and the rung reaction contact."}]}

title: 2023-125 NUTRONs 2023 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-125","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","title":"NUTRONs 2023 Code and CAD Release","locator":"Brandon Holley posts 1, 7 and 18","review_basis":"Read team's release and follow-up answers.","facts":"Split rack collector and its removal, iterative printed arm guides, offline trajectories, and central battery/sideways PDH layout are described.","limitations":"Mechanism dimensions beyond the written specifications and the deployed program revision were not audited."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639","title":"Behind the Bumpers | 125 NUTRONs, team replies","locator":"Brandon Holley posts 3, 7, 9 and 11","review_basis":"Read team replies on extension, cable routing and electrical limits.","facts":"Arm collapse and available travel, helical cable spool, separate power and CAN slip rings, elastic slack compensation and 30 A limits.","limitations":"February weight is a pre-ballast snapshot. August replies describe the hardware but do not date its installation."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Duality combined a long telescoping arm and powered wrist with a chassis packaged around a central battery. The early cube collector was divided across the front so the arm could pass between its two sides. The team eventually removed that collector. The arm's electrical services are part of the mechanism design: as the arm changes length, the extension gearbox pays out or retrieves the harness through a helical drum. That interface lets the wrist and roller retain powered control at either end of the stroke.","piece_flow":"The early ground-cube configuration used a deployed roller ahead of the arm's wrist and claw. The two collector halves left a path for the arm to approach or pass through the front. The release describes automatic selection of cone versus cube scoring position from the most recent intake selection and a toggle between single-station poses. After deletion of the ground intake, the documented hardware retained the wrist and claw for direct piece handling. The exact full set of post-deletion pickup locations and the early collector-to-claw timing were not established from these posts.","packaging_and_motion":"The team measured the collapsed arm at 23 inches with 52 inches of additional linear travel available. The stance and base packaging must accommodate a large change in reach. The release documents a side-mounted PDH between center frame bars, front swerve and intake connections on one side and rear swerve and arm on the other. Snap-in printed grommets protect the wires through the frame. The team chose this layout to retain a central battery and low, balanced mass. Its offline trajectory solver incorporated velocity, acceleration, jerk and obstacle constraints for the peg and shelf.","subsystems":[{"name":"Arm extension, guides and planning","construction":"Multi-stage telescope with printed bearing blocks. The final blocks reported by the team were printed on Markforged Onyx Ones. The shoulder and extension are coordinated by offline trajectories.","operation":"Guide fit is tuned after assembly and powder coating. The team measured play, moved bearing locations in the print and reprinted on the same machine.","team_rationale":"The team optimized part breakup and fit and wanted to move quickly between poses with obstacle and motion constraints.","engineering_analysis":"At long extension, small guide gaps can become large wrist errors. Test side load, joint reversal and repeated extension with the assembled coating stack.","interfaces":"The telescope carries the powered wrist. The extension gearbox also drives harness payout. The early collector shares the arm's swept corridor.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep printed spare guides matched to real tube lots and coatings. Recheck clearance and endpoint calibration after installing a replacement.","unknowns":"Final bearing preload, telescope section sizes, shoulder drive geometry and trajectory deployment by event.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]},{"name":"Wrist, rollers and harness","construction":"Compact printed wrist and end-effector parts, two NEOs with Spark MAX controllers, a helical cable drum driven from the extension gearbox, and separate four-wire power and CAN slip rings. Surgical tubing tensions an approximately eight-inch cable section.","operation":"The drum winds or pays out with extension. The elastic section takes up mismatch at direction changes. Wrist and intake circuits each use a 30 A breaker and controller current limit.","team_rationale":"The team used reduction to make the wrist controllable while holding position and prototyped the roller to preserve adequate acquisition and ejection with the current cap.","engineering_analysis":"A spool phase error accumulates with stroke. The elastic section needs enough travel to absorb reversals without concealing excessive tension at full reach.","interfaces":"Power and CAN cross the rotating drum boundary. Harness motion is mechanically tied to extension rather than to a separate motor.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check strand condition, slip-ring continuity and voltage at the tip through repeated reversals. Validate that the roller clears a jam under its current limit.","unknowns":"Slip-ring models, spool ratio, harness fatigue life and roller compression.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]},{"name":"Split collector and base","construction":"Early roller split across the front. Aluminum and printed rack assemblies ride on printed bearing blocks. The chassis routes front and rear swerve wiring to opposite PDH sides.","operation":"The deployed roller collects while leaving room for the arm to swing through its center. The later robot dispensed with that intake.","team_rationale":"The team states the split was for arm clearance. February plans included 26 lb of low steel ballast after a 78 lb pre-ballast weigh-in.","engineering_analysis":"A centered corridor exchanges usable roller width for collision clearance. An offset strike can bind one rack while the other still moves.","interfaces":"The racks and arm compete for front-frame space.
