The base distributes arm and ballast loads to the wheels.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check both racks after unilateral impact and reproduce handoff with the real bumpers and held piece before copying the arrangement.","unknowns":"Collector synchronization hardware in the final early-season revision, the date of removal, and final official weight.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]}],"revisions":["Ground collector removed during the season. The team reports nearly a dozen telescope bearing-block iterations, including final post-coating fit correction. The February ballast plan and August cable explanation are separately dated reports."],"transferable_principles":["Design telescoping cable travel with the extension transmission and include a tolerance absorber. Measure printed guide fit after finishing the real assembly."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A synchronized cable spool offers little benefit if full-stroke electrical reliability is worse than a routed harness. A dedicated intake earns its space only if its acquisition advantage survives transfer and recovery time."],"remaining_gaps":["Installed event-by-event mechanisms, direct-pickup pose coverage after collector deletion, measured cycle times and endurance of the slip-ring path."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":1,"locator":"Post 7, two linked photographs","subject":"Candidate close-ups for the cable drum, slip-ring interfaces and elastic take-up."},{"source_index":0,"locator":"Post 1 overview and post 14 bearing-block illustration","subject":"Candidate overview and guide comparison. Identify the depicted revision before captioning."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2023-973 Greybots 2023 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2023-973","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","title":"Greybots robot archive and MudSlide photograph","locator":"2023 – MudSlide section, linked myponc7_orig.jpeg","review_basis":"Read the primary team season entry and visually inspected its full robot photograph.","facts":"Team identifies MudSlide as its 2023 robot. The photo shows an inclined two-rail elevator, paired horizontal light-covered rollers, a wide low forward assembly and a pivot transmission adjacent to the head.","limitations":"The archive has no robot-specific build narrative. One pose cannot establish motor identities, rigging sequence or chronology."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","title":"FIRST Updates Now, 973 Cube Rolling Strategy and Robot Overview","locator":"Post 1, March 7","review_basis":"Read the host's published interview summary. The linked video's captions could not be downloaded.","facts":"The host identifies the cascade elevator, swerve and a wrist-enabled cube rolling strategy.","limitations":"This is the host's summary, not a review of the team's spoken explanations. The historical first-swerve claim is contested in the thread."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607","title":"Charged Up robot comparison and intake discussion","locator":"Posts 1, 4, 6 and 12","review_basis":"Read thread and inspected both 973 images. The MudSlide image in post 6 duplicates the team archive view.","facts":"A peer reports a wider cube intake at Champs. Another contributor describes 973's two-roller choice and aluminum wrist attachment as influences on 972.","limitations":"Peer testimony, with a team archive photo supporting visible geometry. Image dates and exact part changes are not independently established."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"MudSlide pairs a swerve base and an inclined cascading elevator with a rotating roller head. The 2023 archive identifies the robot and supplies an unusually clear view of how the low head and large transverse assembly sit ahead of the rails. The host's contemporary account links wrist articulation to rolling cubes. That combination is the most defensible architectural finding. Team 973's own archive calls the 2023 machine MudSlide and uses WildFire for 2022, despite the name in FIRST's 2023 event record.","piece_flow":"The team photo shows two closely spaced, transverse roller surfaces in the low wrist area. A second published view shows a cone held low and ahead of the mast. This establishes the location of cone retention in that pose, while the published interview summary establishes a cube rolling capability. The likely geometric division is that wrist pitch presents the roller contact while carriage movement provides height and fore-aft reach. Whether the wide lower assembly separately acquires and hands cubes to the head, or primarily assists ground contact in a particular pose, remains unresolved. Exact piece entry, transfer and release actions require spoken or visual sequence evidence.","packaging_and_motion":"The mast leans back from its lower mounting area. Accordingly, any straight travel up the visible rail direction shifts the carriage horizontally as well as vertically. Below the roller pair, the photograph shows a broader assembly occupying the low front space. Inference: these parts compete for envelope near a retracted mast, and the wide collector may create better cube approach tolerance only if the receiving pose clears the rail spacing and bumpers. Bench validation should include wrist sweep at intermediate lift heights and with a retained cone.","subsystems":[{"name":"Cascade elevator","construction":"Inclined, paired metal rails with nested members visible. The interviewer identifies cascade rigging in the written overview.","operation":"The elevator changes manipulator height and, because of the incline, changes horizontal offset as it travels.","team_rationale":"Robot-specific selection and manufacturing rationale could not be newly verified.","engineering_analysis":"A narrow span can increase sensitivity to racking from an off-center piece. Measure diagonal movement and carriage error on abrupt reversal with the wrist extended.","interfaces":"The mast bolts into the chassis and the lower moving head occupies space directly in front of the rails.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect both sides for unequal stage travel and contact marks after lateral hits. Confirm harness clearance across moving stages.","unknowns":"Stage count, gearbox and motor specification, rigging details and exact commercial kit fit.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]},{"name":"Wrist and roller head","construction":"Paired cylindrical rollers and a side pivot transmission are visible. A peer identifies the wrist attachment as aluminum.","operation":"Wrist motion changes piece presentation. The host associates that motion with rolling cubes. A published photo shows a low carried cone.","team_rationale":"The peer reports that the two-roller and wrist attachment details influenced 972. Greybots' own rationale for contact count was not newly accessible.","engineering_analysis":"Independent wrist orientation can compensate for the fixed mast angle. If rolling is used for release, surface friction and approach pitch can affect the result even at the same wrist setpoint.","interfaces":"Roller head attaches to the lift carriage. Low pitch brings it close to the bumper and wider front assembly.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check backlash, roller grip and symmetry. Test worn cube surfaces and cone flange deformation across the pickup and release envelopes.","unknowns":"Wrist ratio, roller drive and compliance, sensor confirmation and documented release poses.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]},{"name":"Wide front assembly and swerve","construction":"The team image shows a transverse lower assembly. A peer reports a wider cube intake for Champs. The host identifies swerve.","operation":"Swerve controls the field approach while the intake hardware sets the physical capture window.","team_rationale":"The wider cube intake is peer-reported. No primary design rationale or quantitative trade study was found.","engineering_analysis":"Wider coverage can reduce centering demands while increasing leverage from side impact. Compare capture rates with actual approach error distributions.","interfaces":"Frame rail and bumper clearance govern how far the wider assembly can reach and retract.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect alignment after one-sided strikes and test for partial capture at the outer edges.","unknowns":"Module variant, collector drive, handoff sequence and as-built date.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]}],"revisions":["A peer dates a wider cube intake to Champs. The photos corroborate the presence of a broad front assembly in one view. Prototype roller deletion and kit adaptation details from the corpus were not promoted to newly reviewed facts."],"transferable_principles":["Evaluate wrist pitch and mast angle jointly at contact and release. Judge a wider collector against measured alignment gains, swept clearance and service burden."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Wider ground coverage offers little if edge captures cannot be transferred consistently. Wrist-led cube rolling loses value if floor and piece variation make the final resting position unreliable."],"remaining_gaps":["Primary interview content, stage and motor details, direct versus assisted cube pickup sequence and dated verification of prototype changes."],"recommended_images":[{"source_index":0,"locator":"MudSlide linked image","subject":"Inspected front three-quarter view of rail incline, roller head and transverse assembly."},{"source_index":2,"locator":"Post 1, second robot image","subject":"Inspected field view of the low cone-carry pose. Confirm original credit before reuse."}],"review_date":"2026-11-09"}

title: 2018-2898 V1 scale robot / V2 switch rebuild complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-2898","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf","title":"Flying Hedgehogs 2018 Technical Binder","locator":"Physical pp. 5–21 and 22–27","review_basis":"Re-read both robot designs, results, manufacturing and control pages from the team PDF.","facts":"V1 combined a fixed-role collector, mixed-rigging elevator and bucket. V2 retained the drivetrain and intake but changed to a lower-scoring arm. Four range sensors and a model fit assisted pickup, and an encoder-equipped miniature arm provided operator commands.","limitations":"Self-reported outcomes. No exact failure chronology, code execution, or independent timed trial."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Flying Hedgehogs document two materially different robots. V1 targeted scale, switch and exchange with a separate floor collector and a bucket on an elevator. It ran into coupled lift, alignment and sensing failures. V2 traded away scale reach and became a switch and exchange specialist with the V1 intake mounted to a powered arm. Building and testing the conversion on the practice chassis let the team reuse drive and pickup hardware in the limited unbag window. Lower reach was a deliberate strategy choice as well as a mechanical simplification.","piece_flow":["V1 pulls in a cube using off-center pivoting intake wheels and feeds a separate, pivoting bucket. The bucket rides the lift and tips to release. The binder reports both collector and manipulator misalignment, so the transfer is a documented weak interface.","V2 carries the intake on the 120-degree arm and can place in the switch from behind. The sensor assist fits cube orientation from four ranges and varies intake speed to align it during capture. The binder does not specify how possession gates arm motion or whether the exchange uses a distinct release sequence."],"packaging_and_motion":"The six-wheel chassis uses cantilevered West Coast wheels and sliding chain-tension blocks. A flipped intake gearbox reduces the local footprint. V2 retains that chassis and intake, moves motors to manage the arm's center of gravity, and uses an adjustable belt drivetrain for the pivot. The team machined V2 on CNC after reporting poor tolerances in manually made V1 assemblies, and pocketed components to meet the 30-pound withholding allowance.","subsystems":[{"name":"Chassis and collector","construction":"Six 6-inch nitrile wheels, four CIMs, single speed, sliding chain-tension blocks. Intake uses pivoting wheels and a flipped 10:1 775pro gearbox.","operation":"Intake contacts offset from the pivots and is specified for half-inch compression. V2 changes wheel durometer to improve alignment.","team_rationale":"Team wanted sprint speed and ramp traversal and reports 14.9 ft/s drivetrain top speed and 32.3 ft/s intake surface speed.","engineering_analysis":"Contact compliance should accommodate the cube diagonal and asymmetric fabric deformation. Surface speed alone cannot ensure retention or a successful transfer.","interfaces":"V1 collector exit must match the bucket. V2 bolts the collector to the moving arm, making belt routing and wire travel part of the pivot envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check block position, chain tension and intake pivot friction after bumps.","unknowns":"Loaded wheel slip, wiring envelope and measured approach tolerance.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"V1 elevator and bucket","construction":"Continuous first stage and cascading second stage, 2 × 1 aluminum, custom slides, two 775pros at 50:1, and constant-force springs. A 775pro pivots the bucket.","operation":"Elevator presents the bucket at scoring height. The binder lists 0.75 seconds for lift but reports reduced maximum height from the cascade design.","team_rationale":"The team sought a light bucket and speed, and retained a possible future climb path.","engineering_analysis":"Guide or termination error can change both achievable height and bucket-to-intake alignment. A mechanical datum for the transfer matters independently of controller repeatability.","interfaces":"Transfer depends on the intake, bucket geometry and bottom elevator pose. The upper rigging limits scale reach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Documented V1 failures include cascade, sensor and misalignment problems. Check them independently to isolate each cause.","unknowns":"The binder does not isolate exact cascade failure physics or verify full-load travel.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"V2 arm and operator control","construction":"Four 775s, roughly 96:1 through planetary, gears and belt, with sliding gearboxes and absolute plus relative encoding. A magnetic encoder and Arduino instrument a miniature arm controller.","operation":"Robot mirrors the operator's input angle. The intake follows the arm through the range used to place forward or behind.","team_rationale":"The team found presets insufficient in practice and chose direct pose control. The absolute encoder was intended to remove the need to zero the arm.","engineering_analysis":"Output backlash, belt stretch and gravity torque vary across the sweep. A networked input also needs a defined stale-command response.","interfaces":"Arm base and reused intake attachment establish the geometry. Network messages carry requested pose to the robot controller.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep access for belt tension and inspect encoder disagreement. text: {"robot_id":"2026-9483","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383","title":"Team 9483 Presents: Enigma","locator":"Posts 1, 23, 26, 30, 33, 35, 41 and 47","review_basis":"Read the reveal and later team answers through the published discussion and its public post stream.","facts":"Team replies describe intake version three, curved rack packaging, independently driven cone and uptake, flywheel construction, empirical shot modeling and close-range illumination.","limitations":"Third-party post 44 is conjecture. The written replies give neither final ratios nor a measured CAD envelope."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Enigma puts a rotating-floor conical spindexer below a compact turret. Its intake has to cross the bumper and return inside the robot without raising the rear of the deployment rack through the stored fuel. Separate motors at the rotating floor and uptake provide independent authority over bulk circulation and delivery. The team reports intermittent jams and automatic recovery, making recovery part of the delivered architecture.","piece_flow":"The front collector passes floor fuel into bulk storage. The cone and spinning floor circulate it toward the uptake, then the feeder presents fuel to the turret flywheel. The team describes the feeder as imparting no spin in its reply about perpendicular turret orientation. The launch arrangement lacks a powered top roller, and the aiming model accounts for spin. No final measured throughput curve is provided.","packaging_and_motion":"The curved rack keeps its inboard section low while allowing the front roller to descend below the top of the bumper. The team says the articulated secondary kicker barely cleared the depot and encountered no issues at the bump. Those comments support a tight moving envelope at the intake. Clearance through the entire turret sweep at high hopper fill remains an engineering question.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and rack","construction":"Curved rack and pinion, front roller, kicker and articulating secondary kicker in the third intake.","operation":"Rack travel lowers the front roller for acquisition. The secondary kicker can move relative to the primary kicker.","team_rationale":"The team chose the curve to avoid an elevated inboard rack and preserve hopper capacity.","engineering_analysis":"The path links reach, bumper crossing and stowed intrusion. Impact deflection can change effective gear alignment and field clearance.","interfaces":"Rack to pinion support, intake-to-bumper clearance and final roller to hopper lip.","service_and_failure_modes":"The initial intake was troublesome. Check rack mesh and guide wear through deployment, especially after lateral impact.","unknowns":"Rack pitch radius, backing material, guide clearance and exact roller stack.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]},{"name":"Spindexer and vertical indexer","construction":"Cone with spinning floor. One Kraken X44 powers each of the spindexer and vertical indexer.","operation":"Bulk circulation supplies a separately driven uptake. The robot clears occasional jams automatically.","team_rationale":"The team iterated ratios and feeder wheels within season time constraints. It reports no designed compression against the hopper walls.","engineering_analysis":"Cone circulation has to keep the pickup supplied without packing a bridge at its entry. Feeder grip and floor velocity are coupled even with independent drives.","interfaces":"Cone and floor to wall, floor to feeder wheels and feeder outlet to rotating scorer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Log failed feeds and recovery duration. The team reports seven or eight feeder-wheel changes and denies cone-to-shooter-corner jams in its account.","unknowns":"Wheel geometry, final ratio, throat compression, detection signal and retry sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]},{"name":"Turret launcher and targeting","construction":"Three X44 flywheel motors, roughly half-pound three-inch printed wheel and one Thrifty Bot flywheel disc kit per team replies. No powered top roller. Camera has a nearby flood-pattern truck LED.","operation":"Empirically tuned tables and iterative physics jointly solve moving shots with spin compensation. The light fills close shadows.","team_rationale":"The light helped close-range tag observations where the net shadowed a tag. The team reports little long-range benefit.","engineering_analysis":"Supplemental inertia can reduce transient droop at the cost of slower setpoint changes. Characterize those effects separately from shot-model residuals.","interfaces":"Feeder exit to wheel compression, camera to pose estimate and pose/velocity to launch solution.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check printed-wheel balance and fastening after impacts. Measure tag availability with and without the light at representative poses.","unknowns":"Turret support, hood travel, total inertia and the solver inputs and gains.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]}],"revisions":["First intake was problematic. Version three added the kicker and a movable secondary kicker. The team also tuned uptake ratios and changed feeder wheels repeatedly without replacing the overall feed architecture."],"transferable_principles":["Lay out the complete deployment path against the occupied hopper volume. Test rotating bulk feed and throat traction independently at several fill levels."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The rack benefit shrinks if an equally low linear path fits the same structure. The spindexer transfer case weakens if recoverable jams still consume substantial scoring time at match fill and acceleration."],"remaining_gaps":["Final drive modules, climbing hardware, gear ratios, recovery logic, and repeatable feed and shot rates by operating state remain unverified."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515383/35","locator":"Team attachments labeled topdown and kickerer","purpose":"Review and annotate these candidate figures for the cone-to-feeder path and articulated kicker respectively."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515383/41","locator":"Curved-rack explanation","purpose":"Pair with measured deployed and retracted profiles if a drawing becomes available."}]}

title: 2018-148 Drive and control package
text: {"name":"Drive and control package","construction":"Configurable single-speed drivetrain, two-sided electronics panel and Talon SRX encoder breakout.","operation":"The team reports an 18 ft/s top speed and describes trajectory correction and lift scoring presets.","team_rationale":"Compact footprint and light drive package support rapid cube cycling and passage under the scale.","engineering_analysis":"High straight-line speed only helps when acceleration, braking and lift clearance allow it. Constrain transit speed by raised center of mass and position confidence.","interfaces":"Mast stow envelope, chassis approach and preset release positions interact in an automatic placement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep encoder and electronics access compatible with module changes. Verify the eject/back-away sequence after reassembly.","unknowns":"Wheel and gearing configuration at specific events, acceleration and control abort behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]}

title: 2018-148 Boot and cube intake
text: {"name":"Boot and cube intake","construction":"Lexan intake, orientation boot and passive drinking-bird preload retention.","operation":"Acquisition moves the cube across the boot to convert different starting orientations into a narrow, tall output. The carried assembly then places it.","team_rationale":"The team chose orientation control early because it wanted more cubes to fit on the target. It reports six pre-bag intake revisions.","engineering_analysis":"The important interface is the distribution of final cube poses after fast floor pickups, including diagonal contact and fabric deformation. A righting feature can become a jam point if entry force stalls below its tipping threshold.","interfaces":"Rollers and boot govern the pose presented to the target. Fold/stow geometry also affects the preload retainer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect boot wear, fastener holes and reliable release of the passive retainer. Verify that a failed flip can be reversed.","unknowns":"Actuator and roller specs, boot profile and documented revision differences.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]}

title: 2018-148 Cascading elevator
text: {"name":"Cascading elevator","construction":"Two 775pros, chain on the bottom stage, tensioned Dyneema on the top two stages, constant-force springs and printed rollers.","operation":"The pamphlet reports a floor-to-90-inch cube lift under half a second and collapsed height under 42 inches.","team_rationale":"The team used lightweight guide and tube construction and spring assist to reduce active lift load.","engineering_analysis":"A spring reduces some gravity burden, while acceleration and stopping still load every stage. Compare full loaded travel and settling rather than treating reported lift time as cycle time.","interfaces":"The carriage takes the intake and the top of the elevator temporarily carries the climb hook.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect chain and rope tension, spring attachments and high-stage guide wear. Confirm hook separation before lowering.","unknowns":"Drum or reeving dimensions, spring force, feedback geometry and repeatability.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]}

title: 2018-148 Hook winch and Robot Wrangler
text: {"name":"Hook winch and Robot Wrangler","construction":"Three 775pros and a four-stage winch reduction, central A-frame, deployable one-way roller and underbody forks.","operation":"The hook is carried up on a hook-and-loop mount and the separate winch lifts after bar engagement. A partner rope positions the partner onto the forks.","team_rationale":"Team designed to keep both robots balanced and reports lifting itself and a full-weight partner in under three seconds.","engineering_analysis":"Treat rope capture and structural support as distinct load cases. An off-center partner adds overturning torque and lateral loads even after successful capture.","interfaces":"Bar, hook, line, winch and A-frame form the main load path. Rope location and fork engagement determine partner alignment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hook retention versus release, verify fork seating, and assess failure to stop backdrive after interruption.","unknowns":"Fork geometry, winch holding mechanism, measured loads and partner compatibility list.","source_urls":["https://www.robowranglers148.com/uploads/1/0/5/4/10542658/judges_pamphlet-compressed.pdf"]}

title: 2018-1610 Six-wheel West Coast drivetrain
text: {"name":"Six-wheel West Coast drivetrain","construction":"2 × 1.5-inch rails enclose chains from the driven center axle to front and rear axles. A custom gearbox developed with 2363 puts Mini-CIMs over the wheels. Flipping the Versa Block orientation creates a small center drop.","operation":"One Talon SRX leads two Victor SPX followers per side. Quadrature feedback goes to the master, and voltage compensation caps full command at 10.5 V.","team_rationale":"The team wanted useful turning and platform clearance while maximizing room for mechanisms. Mini-CIMs let the folded gearbox stay inside the perimeter.","engineering_analysis":"Enclosed chain routing trades central volume for visibility and tool access. Exhaust routed through 5/32-inch inlets and vented motor bolts may cool motors intermittently, depending on cylinder activity.","interfaces":"Rail bore alignment sets chain tracking. Wheel clearance, gearbox body and bumper brackets share the side envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Plan for chain replacement and motor access with the intake installed. The binder itself flags difficult chain maintenance.","unknowns":"Chain tension limits, temperature benefit and measured speed under load.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]}

title: 2018-1610 Pivoting cube intake
text: {"name":"Pivoting cube intake","construction":"Green compliant wheels on powered arms, with belts and pulleys internal to the tubing. Pneumatic cylinders apply pressure to the cube. The arms were changed to plastic tubing.","operation":"Wheels draw the cube between the arms. Arm pressure maintains contact while the cube faces present different dimensions and stiffness. The assembly flips upright for hook presentation.","team_rationale":"Wheel testing and a wood prototype helped tune the intake for both cube orientations and the loose fabric on the open face. Inboard belt routing reduced package thickness.","engineering_analysis":"Grip should tolerate uneven compression without rotating the cube out of the intake. Internal pulleys and lighter arms improve envelope and mass but concentrate bearing, wear and repair requirements in the arm.","interfaces":"Elevator carriage takes the intake mount and vertical pivot; wheel motors sweep next to the uprights. Hook loads enter the underside during climb.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pulley alignment, buried belts, arm joints and hook attachment. A soft fabric panel can increase compression without proportionally increasing retention.","unknowns":"Pivot actuator details, working pressure, roller speeds, grip forces and release sensing.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]}

title: 2018-1610 Elevator and integrated climb
text: {"name":"Elevator and integrated climb","construction":"Two-stage mast in 2 × 1-inch aluminum with custom R4 linear bearing mounts. Two 2 × 1 tubing hooks are beneath the intake. A pneumatic pin locks the elevator.","operation":"The intake rotates upright and the elevator raises the hooks above the bar. The reused lift drive takes robot weight with the added motor and gearbox. The pin is the documented backdrive countermeasure.","team_rationale":"With about ten pounds remaining, the team rejected the separate winch gearbox and a more complicated tape-measure hook deployment.","engineering_analysis":"Treat bar capture, load transfer and locking as distinct events. The carriage, pivot, hook joint and mast guides see climb loads with a different magnitude and direction from scoring.","interfaces":"Bar to hooks to intake structure to elevator and chassis. The pin must line up under the actual loaded deflection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check pin engagement and support before releasing motor torque. Inspect guide binding and hook load symmetry.","unknowns":"Rigging topology, pin engagement sensing and validated climb capacity.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2018_Rev_2.pdf"]}

title: 2018-254 Two-speed drivetrain
text: {"name":"Two-speed drivetrain","construction":"Six-wheel differential chassis with compact gearboxes and low-mounted hardware.","operation":"Select the useful ratio for the route and preserve a predictable approach while the elevator moves.","team_rationale":"Short-cycle acceleration and driving across the field impose different demands.","engineering_analysis":"A repeatable stopping pose makes the wrist and lift more useful. A faster top speed matters only where the route gives room to accelerate and decelerate.","interfaces":"Lift reactions and partner loads pass through the chassis. Driver approach heading interacts with the choice of front or rear release.","service_and_failure_modes":"A frame hit can change approach accuracy without obvious failure in the scoring hardware. Inspect gearbox and wheel retention after contact.","unknowns":"Source-reported speed is not loaded measured cycle performance.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]}

title: 2018-254 Roller intake and wrist
text: {"name":"Roller intake and wrist","construction":"Opposed powered roller groups on a wristed cube manipulator with movable jaws.","operation":"Acquire from the floor, retain the cube while the wrist rotates, then drop or eject at the target.","team_rationale":"Front and rear releases widen the useful scoring poses.","engineering_analysis":"Maintaining possession across transit removes a transfer boundary. The mouth still needs to tolerate off-center cubes and the hold geometry must survive reversal and acceleration.","interfaces":"The cube envelope, wrist linkage and jaw opening compete for the same pass-through opening.","service_and_failure_modes":"A loaded cube can move under reversal or crowding. Gentle release is a separate operating condition from maximum ejection.","unknowns":"No complete tested capture envelope or independently measured hold reliability is available.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-frc-2018-code/166514"]}

title: 2018-254 Pass-through elevator
text: {"name":"Pass-through elevator","construction":"Two-stage lift with rigging and a clear center between the lift rails.","operation":"Raise the same cube tool to the target, then lower it and restore the floor pickup pose.","team_rationale":"One structure serves multiple scoring heights and works with the reversible tool.","engineering_analysis":"A short mechanical path still requires careful motion planning. Rail spacing, cable pretension and torsion become more important if the tool is extended and the piece sits off center.","interfaces":"The clear passage also needs room for cable motion and harness bend radius, while the elevator is the structural support for endgame loads.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check carriage binding, rigging wear and access to replace a cable without stripping unrelated mechanisms.","unknowns":"Source figures establish arrangement and selected dimensions, with dynamic deflection and friction unresolved.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]}

title: 2018-254 Hook and partner forks
text: {"name":"Hook and partner forks","construction":"Upper hook and deployable fork assembly integrated with the scoring lift.","operation":"Enter the climbing configuration, engage the bar and support an alliance partner when the setup allows.","team_rationale":"The endgame function made use of the same major lifting structure.","engineering_analysis":"Shared hardware saves a separate lift volume, but it raises design loads and demands a distinct mode. Partner geometry and alignment can dominate endgame reliability.","interfaces":"Bar, hook, carriage, forks and frame make one coupled load path. Folded hardware cannot obstruct normal cube cycles.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check fork alignment, unequal partner loading and whether the driver can abandon a slow setup.","unknowns":"No universal partner fit or verified safety factor follows from published renderings.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://www.team254.com/frc/2018/"]}

title: 2018-254 Controls and autonomous
text: {"name":"Controls and autonomous","construction":"Spline trajectory following, coordinated lift and wrist commands, and a scale-attitude sensing account.","operation":"Schedule acquisition and lift states around the route, then release once possession and pose allow. Choose autonomous tasks with partner capability in mind.","team_rationale":"A useful start required early cube scoring and enough flexibility to cover uncertain switch capability.","engineering_analysis":"The closest transfer is making possession, target pose and return path explicit. Copying a controller does little if the robot cannot repeat the physical transition it is commanding.","interfaces":"A path can pass only if the tool and cube clear the route at the actual lift and wrist states.","service_and_failure_modes":"A missed acquisition or stale target estimate needs an explicit fallback. End-stop and transition checks need validation with the actual mechanism.","unknowns":"The binder names pure pursuit. The pinned release defaults to nonlinear feedback. The Houston binary remains unauthenticated.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2018-Public/blob/2c06c1ea5c81b6ed970fa8bc2611f69467a08075/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2018/planners/DriveMotionPlanner.java#L28-L36","https://blog.team254.com/2018cmp/"]}

title: 2018-2898 Chassis and collector
text: {"name":"Chassis and collector","construction":"Six 6-inch nitrile wheels, four CIMs, single speed, sliding chain-tension blocks. Intake uses pivoting wheels and a flipped 10:1 775pro gearbox.","operation":"Intake contacts offset from the pivots and is specified for half-inch compression. V2 changes wheel durometer to improve alignment.","team_rationale":"Team wanted sprint speed and ramp traversal and reports 14.9 ft/s drivetrain top speed and 32.3 ft/s intake surface speed.","engineering_analysis":"Contact compliance should accommodate the cube diagonal and asymmetric fabric deformation. Surface speed alone cannot ensure retention or a successful transfer.","interfaces":"V1 collector exit must match the bucket. V2 bolts the collector to the moving arm, making belt routing and wire travel part of the pivot envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check block position, chain tension and intake pivot friction after bumps.","unknowns":"Loaded wheel slip, wiring envelope and measured approach tolerance.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}

title: 2018-2898 V1 elevator and bucket
text: {"name":"V1 elevator and bucket","construction":"Continuous first stage and cascading second stage, 2 × 1 aluminum, custom slides, two 775pros at 50:1, and constant-force springs. A 775pro pivots the bucket.","operation":"Elevator presents the bucket at scoring height. The binder lists 0.75 seconds for lift but reports reduced maximum height from the cascade design.","team_rationale":"The team sought a light bucket and speed, and retained a possible future climb path.","engineering_analysis":"Guide or termination error can change both achievable height and bucket-to-intake alignment. A mechanical datum for the transfer matters independently of controller repeatability.","interfaces":"Transfer depends on the intake, bucket geometry and bottom elevator pose. The upper rigging limits scale reach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Documented V1 failures include cascade, sensor and misalignment problems. Check them independently to isolate each cause.","unknowns":"The binder does not isolate exact cascade failure physics or verify full-load travel.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}

title: 2018-2898 V2 arm and operator control
text: {"name":"V2 arm and operator control","construction":"Four 775s, roughly 96:1 through planetary, gears and belt, with sliding gearboxes and absolute plus relative encoding. A magnetic encoder and Arduino instrument a miniature arm controller.","operation":"Robot mirrors the operator's input angle. The intake follows the arm through the range used to place forward or behind.","team_rationale":"The team found presets insufficient in practice and chose direct pose control. The absolute encoder was intended to remove the need to zero the arm.","engineering_analysis":"Output backlash, belt stretch and gravity torque vary across the sweep. A networked input also needs a defined stale-command response.","interfaces":"Arm base and reused intake attachment establish the geometry. Network messages carry requested pose to the robot controller.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep access for belt tension and inspect encoder disagreement. Limit travel if input goes stale.","unknowns":"Collision guards, angle limits in code and measured pose accuracy.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}

title: 2018-2898 Cube alignment and diagnostics
text: {"name":"Cube alignment and diagnostics","construction":"Four range sensors in the backing bar, Jetson TX1 model fitting and roboRIO roller control.","operation":"Least-squares cube orientation is converted to differential speed commands. Reported diagnostics can enable fallback autonomous or disable a subsystem.","team_rationale":"Team aimed to reduce acquisition alignment burden and protect equipment after faults.","engineering_analysis":"Fit confidence depends on what surfaces the four rays hit. A clipped corner or background return can produce plausible but incorrect alignment.","interfaces":"Sensor aiming, model geometry and roller sign conventions must agree.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test partial views and disagreement with acquisition behavior, then provide a manual fallback.","unknowns":"Quantified improvement and fit rejection criteria.","source_urls":["https://bpsrobotics.github.io/2898/files/2018-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}

title: 2018-2910 Swerve and azimuth feedback
text: {"name":"Swerve and azimuth feedback","construction":"Custom modules with thin-section X-contact bearings and MA3 absolute sensors. The steering output and encoder branch have equivalent gearing.","operation":"The sensor reports module orientation across power cycles. The team confirmed that an effectively one-to-one encoder relationship avoids routine re-zeroing.","team_rationale":"The team wanted freedom to maneuver around field obstacles and considered the game suitable for swerve.","engineering_analysis":"Absolute angle preserves the datum only while the keyed or geared relationship holds. Offset changes or encoder gear slip can bias both steering and any inferred chassis motion.","interfaces":"The bearing carries steering-axis loads, while calibration ties encoder angle to the actual wheel direction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck the mechanical and software datum after module replacement. Check wheel clearance at full steering sweep near bumper brackets.","unknowns":"Drive motor feedback and quantitative accuracy under load.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://frcteam2910.org/competition-history/"]}

title: 2018-2910 Cube collector and carriage claw
text: {"name":"Cube collector and carriage claw","construction":"Through-bumper floor rollers and a separate belt-and-wheel roller claw visible at the lowered mast, described in the handbook.","operation":"The floor mechanism orients the incoming cube and the claw takes it vertically to the switch or scale.","team_rationale":"The handbook ties this arrangement to varied cube orientations. A firsthand team comparison for this choice was not located.","engineering_analysis":"A transfer can reduce raised collector mass but needs a stable orientation after asymmetric contact. A miscentered cube can wedge between stationary rollers and the moving receiver.","interfaces":"Bumper gap, roller contact height and carriage home position jointly define admission and handoff.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect roller compliance and repeat the transfer after collision or carriage service.","unknowns":"Wheel revision chronology, retention force, home sensing and recovery behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://www.frc-handbook.com/ref/28"]}

title: 2018-2910 Belt lift and climb
text: {"name":"Belt lift and climb","construction":"Continuous two-stage lift with belt routed around bearing pulleys through tubes. Separate pneumatic cylinders shift range and lock the elevator. Upper hooks visible in the release render.","operation":"High range handles cube placement. Low range handles climbing, and the separate lock holds after climb.","team_rationale":"Team favored belt protection and avoiding spool-tracking concerns.","engineering_analysis":"The hard-stop event shows why clamp-edge radius and terminal impact matter independently of nominal belt strength. A climb changes loads at the carriage attachment, mast guides and lock.","interfaces":"The fixed end on the carriage, internal pulley path, gearbox and lock share responsibility for load transfer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports about 45 minutes to replace a belt, including removing guide bearings, separating stages and threading without twist.","unknowns":"Lock geometry, full belt specification, climb qualification and confirmed climb states.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095","https://www.frc-handbook.com/ref/28"]}

title: 2018-2910 Sideways platform clearance
text: {"name":"Sideways platform clearance","construction":"Two waterjet-cut 6061-T6 free rollers at the base of the elevator.","operation":"They provide rolling contact at the platform rather than letting the chassis settle on a fixed low surface.","team_rationale":"Team reports fewer instances of bottoming out, with occasional sticking still possible.","engineering_analysis":"A passive roller only helps while driven wheels retain normal force and torque.","interfaces":"Wheel vector, platform edge and roller axis must align with the crossing direction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check roller bearings and mounts for strikes and inspect whether damage reduces floor clearance.","unknowns":"Tested crossing angles and loaded ground clearance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pic-2910-cad-release-2018/167095"]}

title: 2018-971 Drivetrain
text: {"name":"Drivetrain","construction":"Six 5-inch Colsons, belt-driven clamshell layout with dead axles and a two-speed ball shifter.","operation":"Workshop lists 9.1 and 16.7 ft/s for low and high and identifies encoder, gyro, IMU and potentiometer signals in a state-space drive controller.","team_rationale":"The binder emphasizes maneuverability to avoid defense.","engineering_analysis":"Grip, shift timing and raised arm mass all affect path following. The binder gives different rounded speed figures, with low gear listed at 11 ft/s.","interfaces":"Belt tensioners, wheel pulleys and modular gearboxes share access with chassis electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect bonded pulley interfaces and tension before blaming steering error on estimation.","unknowns":"Cause of speed discrepancy and loaded shift behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]}

title: 2018-971 Series-elastic floor intake
text: {"name":"Series-elastic floor intake","construction":"Four-inch webbed Fairlane wheels, pivot gearboxes with series elasticity, magnetic spring encoder, absolute encoder, potentiometer, beam breaks and LIDAR.","operation":"The pivot loop incorporates measured spring deflection. Roller geometry and sensing align the cube for the claw.","team_rationale":"Prototype oscillations and a desire for active intake angle led the team to put an actuator in series with the spring.","engineering_analysis":"Deflection is meaningful only with known spring behavior and calibrated limits. Control must distinguish intentional contact from blocked motion.","interfaces":"The arm can acquire consistently only across the residual yaw and position spread at the floor intake.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check encoder zero, spring travel limits and a stalled cube with a blocked beam.","unknowns":"Spring stiffness, force limits and automatic recovery logic.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]}

title: 2018-971 Two-link arm and claw
text: {"name":"Two-link arm and claw","construction":"Carbon fiber tubes and CNC joints, proximal chain, distal cable, dedicated motors in a shared gearbox and disk brake. Printed claw body uses pulley-and-string actuation from hidden pistons.","operation":"Arm profiles independently drive joints, while the claw converts cylinder motion into linear grasp. A claw beam monitors the piece.","team_rationale":"Early aluminum links were structurally inadequate. Pulley actuation reduced claw package and inertia, and shorter fingers reduced zipper jams at the cost of some control.","engineering_analysis":"Joint angle error and compliance translate into endpoint error according to configuration. With crossed workspace and a retained cube, verify the sweep around mast, intake and bumpers.","interfaces":"Claw shape must accept the oriented cube. Capstan anchoring and guide stiffness govern distal position repeatability.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope preload, bonded inserts and air lines; test zipper snag and beam false positives.","unknowns":"Joint gains, load limits and exact arm motor designation given the overview's different shorthand.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]}

title: 2018-971 Hanger and partner lift
text: {"name":"Hanger and partner lift","construction":"Separate hook, two 775pros for the hanger in the combined gearbox, proximal-tube winch-line exit, spring-deployed partner fork with expansion stage.","operation":"The hanger loads the robot through the winch system. Fork deployment enlarges the partner's boarding area, and its low-friction underside permits exchange traffic.","team_rationale":"The team wanted a balanced quick hang with an alliance robot.","engineering_analysis":"Changing partner position changes fork bending and the moment around the hoist line. The historical prototype load label cannot qualify the competed system.","interfaces":"Hook, winch, chassis and partner support require independent attachment and retention checks.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify latching, unintended movement and release under asymmetric load.","unknowns":"Load rating, version differences and event use.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_8ddb7c2844de4500b0e2fb88ebab7742.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2018.pdf"]}

title: 2019-1323 Continuous lift
text: {"name":"Continuous lift","construction":"Three stages, four separately tensioned runs, opposed geared spools, machined bearing blocks and two 775pros.","operation":"Paired up and return runs move the assembly through the required stage travel. The team reports about one amp per motor at hold in an unspecified condition.","team_rationale":"The team sought overlap at level three, preferred the internal design to its earlier cascades and wanted to avoid repeatedly engaging a brake.","engineering_analysis":"Maintain preload on both rope directions. Effective spool radius and return slack affect reversal accuracy, while guide play and overlap affect extended stiffness.","interfaces":"Opposed spools must preserve compatible line payout. Carriage pose sets both transfer alignment and the useful vision window.","service_and_failure_modes":"Expose adjusters and inspect rope abrasion, block wear and changes after reversals.","unknowns":"Full reeving map, drum geometry and tested loads.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1323-elevator/358379?page=3","https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]}

title: 2019-1323 Cargo and vision
text: {"name":"Cargo and vision","construction":"Wristed collector with grabber and feeder, separate carriage motor and banner input, and swerve target tracking.","operation":"After receiving cargo, selected tracking logic moves through vision-visible heights, waits for tracking, commands scoring height and ejects.","team_rationale":"The code records the order and separate possession signals. It gives limited reasons for the physical construction.","engineering_analysis":"A current spike can also indicate a jam. Confirming possession at the receiver limits the consequences of an incorrect inference at the collector.","interfaces":"Wrist angle and lift height align the two assemblies. Target acquisition depends on camera line of sight and chassis heading.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check incomplete transfers, false current detections and stale vision before committing lift or eject.","unknowns":"Roller geometry, optical calibration and measured transfer robustness.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]}

title: 2019-1323 Disk intake and scorer
text: {"name":"Disk intake and scorer","construction":"Motorized ground intake and separate scorer, with possession checks and stowed, receiving, detecting and holding states.","operation":"Ground intake current is used in acquisition. Scorer detection has distinct modes for station and floor paths, and the two transfers converge on retention for scoring.","team_rationale":"The state split records different source interfaces. Physical rationale is sparsely documented.","engineering_analysis":"Owner changes should be explicit so lift motion cannot pull an incompletely received disk away.","interfaces":"Disk intake delivery, scorer state and elevator handoff height must agree.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sensing through partially delivered panels and recovery with mechanisms engaged.","unknowns":"Contact geometry and version-specific installation.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]}

title: 2019-1323 Jacks and PTO
text: {"name":"Jacks and PTO","construction":"Solenoid-controlled takeoff and shared disk-intake motor controller; feedback source depends on configuration.","operation":"Jacks applies position control when power is shifted to it and its sensor is connected. Climb sequences coordinate wrist gearing, roller pull and chassis motion.","team_rationale":"Motor sharing is explicit. A team comparative weight or reliability assessment was not found.","engineering_analysis":"Shared actuation saves a motor at the cost of interlocks and a reliable mechanical shift under the expected load.","interfaces":"Shift state must coordinate controller ownership and feedback selection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test wrong feedback, incomplete shifts and a stopped climb under load.","unknowns":"Physical lock, shift confirmation and exact competed macro.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Team1323/2019DeepSpace/tree/13d5d4ac56c2da11d112ab9ab84241c8b6878018"]}

title: 2019-1610 Eight-wheel chassis and gearbox
text: {"name":"Eight-wheel chassis and gearbox","construction":"West Coast rails are 2 × 1.5-inch tube with internal chain and sprockets. The two central axles have a small drop made by flipping Versa Blocks. Custom two-stage gearboxes use Mini-CIMs and vented mounting bolts.","operation":"Center drop assists turning; wheel traction becomes the HAB drive once the wedges establish a contact angle. Talon masters use quadrature encoders and a 10.5 V compensated command ceiling.","team_rationale":"Team retained the narrow internal chain packaging and compact 2363 collaboration gearbox from earlier seasons.","engineering_analysis":"More wheels can help bridge the step only if the needed driven contacts have sufficient normal force throughout the transition.","interfaces":"Wedge geometry determines first-wheel engagement; rail and gearbox tolerances determine chain tracking. Cylinder exhaust is routed through 5/32-inch gearbox inlets.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check chains through accessible inspection points and plan disassembly for replacements. Cooling depends on available exhaust flow.","unknowns":"Wheel loading through climb and measured cooling benefit.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]}

title: 2019-1610 Cargo transfer and scoring lift
text: {"name":"Cargo transfer and scoring lift","construction":"One over-bumper collector and one carriage gripper. Elevator uses 1/16-inch-wall aluminum and 1 × 1-inch tubing in its first stage; two carriage cylinders extend the scoring tools.","operation":"The collector and gripper overlap at the handoff pose. The elevator motor gearbox encoder sets an upper travel constraint, and a lower magnetic limit switch resets encoder position at the bottom.","team_rationale":"The team accepted added total hardware weight to cut vertically moving weight, and reports nearly 50 percent less elevator mechanism weight than the prior design.","engineering_analysis":"A low moving mass can improve acceleration and stability. The benefit depends on reliably transferring a soft sphere between independently mounted systems despite carriage error or intake deflection.","interfaces":"The collector exit, gripper throat and elevator home position define the transfer window. Carriage slide stroke also controls bumper and target clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"A failed bottom switch can undermine the datum. Check switch brackets, carriage play, hoses and interference during partial extension.","unknowns":"Rigging topology, measured handoff window, cargo release actuator sequence and jam recovery.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]}

title: 2019-1610 Expanding hatch tool
text: {"name":"Expanding hatch tool","construction":"A cylinder drives a plunger into pivoting triangular fingers with torsion-spring return. Team shows first and second printed versions.","operation":"The contracted tool fits the center opening, then deploys fingers internally. Removal depends on withdrawing the fingers cleanly after the target supports the hatch.","team_rationale":"Suction trials fell short. The team adapted an inside-gripping mechanism from 2363's 2015 recycling-can design.","engineering_analysis":"Internal engagement separates locating from clamping. Hole tolerance and angled approach determine whether the fingers catch the intended surface.","interfaces":"Carriage extension, center-hole registration and spring force set acquisition and release limits.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect printed pivot bores and spring return. A finger held open by a tilted panel can impede clean release.","unknowns":"Finger materials, deployed dimensions, grip force and partial-capture sensing.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]}

title: 2019-1610 HAB2 wedge climb
text: {"name":"HAB2 wedge climb","construction":"Paired wedges stow beside the intake with pancake-cylinder pins.","operation":"Pins release the wedges; the intake lowers and the pins extend into the wedge centers. The robot drives up once the first wheel contacts the HAB.","team_rationale":"The team dropped direct cylinder-lift prototypes to avoid bending a cylinder and skipped HAB3 to prioritize rocket scoring.","engineering_analysis":"Use the ramp face and chassis reaction points to carry the step encounter, then verify how much side load reaches the retaining pins.","interfaces":"Both sides must reach the intended support geometry before the front of the frame or bumpers contact the platform.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pin seating and symmetry after impacts. An unlatched wedge can skew the robot or fail to lift a wheel.","unknowns":"Pin-load distribution, feedback and failed-deploy recovery.","source_urls":["https://blackwaterrobotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1610_Technical_Binder_2019_rev2.pdf"]}

title: 2019-2910 Swerve and bumper mounting
text: {"name":"Swerve and bumper mounting","construction":"Four wheels, protected NEO locations at bumper cutouts, chassis standoffs and captured 1/4-20 bumper fasteners.","operation":"Drive encoder feedback returns over CAN for odometry. Steering commands use PWM and roboRIO control.","team_rationale":"Guards addressed recurring motor clipping. Captive fasteners support repeatable bumper changes.","engineering_analysis":"A guard needs a stiff load path and a deflection margin to the motor throughout the module sweep.","interfaces":"Bumper wood transfers load to its 1 × 1 frame, then to spacers and threaded chassis standoffs.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bent guards and trapped fasteners after contact; retain tool access past the guard.","unknowns":"Impact load cases and calibrated travel.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2019/359697"]}

title: 2019-2910 Cargo arm and rollers
text: {"name":"Cargo arm and rollers","construction":"Arm gearbox with long chain run, inline tensioner and keyed/bolted sprocket-to-gear hub. Lower pulley shares roller width with a narrow compliant wheel.","operation":"Beam states and arm pose determine drive, centering and soft hold. The code changes roller bias at the rocket because cargo could ride up the target.","team_rationale":"The team prioritizes backlash near the output and limits current while stalled in hold.","engineering_analysis":"Output lost motion multiplied by arm reach shifts the contact point. Centring confidence should be distinguished from detection by one beam.","interfaces":"Roller contact width, target approach and arm angle set ejection behavior.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect chain tension, hub fasteners and optical alignment; a false beam condition can drive a stall.","unknowns":"Loaded endpoint error and retained force.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]}

title: 2019-2910 Hatch system
text: {"name":"Hatch system","construction":"Floor gatherer and placer with distinct extension, gripper and placement solenoid outputs, plus two limit switches.","operation":"The floor gatherer rotates the hatch into the extended placer's capture zone. Station pickup avoids the extra transfer.","team_rationale":"Team reports the floor system was alignment-sensitive; the competition design replaced the reveal's wheeled hatch tool.","engineering_analysis":"A timer after grab does not establish possession. Verify overlap through partial capture before reversing the gatherer.","interfaces":"Hatch presentation angle, gatherer axis and placer stroke define the transfer pose.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect switches, gatherer stow and hose paths. Partial seating can appear valid on one switch.","unknowns":"Finger geometry and version-specific clearances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2019/359697","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]}

title: 2019-2910 HAB climb and supports
text: {"name":"HAB climb and supports","construction":"Code declares separate climber and kickstand solenoids. Team describes rear support plus two forward supports.","operation":"The climb macro requests extension, forward drive, bottom roller and pitch correction together. Supports hold bumpers above the platform with rear wheels off.","team_rationale":"Forward supports were added for sharing HAB3 with 1323 in practice.","engineering_analysis":"Analyze transitions and partner reactions at the support polygon, including partial deployment.","interfaces":"The bumper and chassis carry partner contact loads. Pitch control depends on attitude sensing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Confirm support deployment before adding partner load. Protect lines and valves from chassis contact.","unknowns":"Main actuator dimensions, qualified loads and deployment verification.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-release-2019/357461","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2019CompetitionRobot-Public/tree/137b803b4dc3e14d68a0c1ed9ae072ae42320ffe"]}

title: 2019-971 Chassis and approach sensing
text: {"name":"Chassis and approach sensing","construction":"Six-wheel single-speed West Coast drive, four 4-inch outer Colsons, two center tread wheels, and two CIMs per side. Five JeVois cameras support localization with infrared illumination; the workshop identifies another driver camera.","operation":"Encoder-based drivetrain motion and a vision extended Kalman filter support field approach. The cameras estimate target distance, heading and skew.","team_rationale":"The team chose a compact robot to evade defense and shorten cycles.","engineering_analysis":"Track width, moving mass and stilt placement constrain lateral stability. Camera utility depends on usable views across wrist and lift motion.","interfaces":"Camera extrinsics and illumination need repeatable mounts. Encoder scale and image timestamps affect pose agreement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect mounts and wheels after impacts, and test recovery when the lift or cargo obscures a camera.","unknowns":"Pose accuracy and high-lift stability under defense.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/971-spartan-robotics-2019/350389"]}

title: 2019-971 Elevator and pass-through wrist
text: {"name":"Elevator and pass-through wrist","construction":"Carbon-fiber two-stage continuous lift, Dyneema and printed pulleys, one 775pro at reported 10.25:1. Onyx carriage with Delrin bearings, BAG wrist at reported 175:1 and spring-loaded telescoping aluminum.","operation":"A potentiometer and absolute encoder support lift positioning. The dead-axle wrist swings the tool past the offset elevator.","team_rationale":"Team sought low center of gravity and wrist motion fast enough to keep up with the lift.","engineering_analysis":"Fast extension is useful only if cable routing, carried mass and swing settle within the placement tolerance.","interfaces":"Offset mast and carriage travel must clear the loaded wrist through the entire cross-chassis path.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect printed pulleys, rope, carbon joints, bearing wear and hose snag during telescoping.","unknowns":"Mass boundary, joint construction and loaded timing.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]}

title: 2019-971 Floor intake and vacuum tooling
text: {"name":"Floor intake and vacuum tooling","construction":"Polycarbonate four-bar, BAG VersaPlanetary pivot, current-limited 775pro roller drive with two-inch omnis, commercial pump driven by a 775pro and compliant cups.","operation":"Omnis provide a centering surface for the ball. Bellows improve station contact and a smaller cup stabilizes a hatch. Valves help unseat the tool.","team_rationale":"The collector addressed weak direct depot pickup. Bellows improve compliance at the station.","engineering_analysis":"Vacuum area alone cannot predict resistance to peeling. Preserve seal under acceleration, surface defects and partial contact.","interfaces":"Roller centerline, wrist extension and pump/valve timing must present the ball to the cup before carrying it away.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check seals, hoses, pump and contamination. Test roller stalls and early lift after imperfect contact.","unknowns":"Leak margin, force conditions and acquisition interlocks.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]}

title: 2019-971 HAB3 stilts
text: {"name":"HAB3 stilts","construction":"One 775pro at reported 31:1, over-center spring ankles and feet with one-way bearing wheels.","operation":"Feet hold their geometry through lift, then pivot to move the robot onto the platform. Stilts retract and the drivetrain completes entry.","team_rationale":"The design targets a short late-match climb with room for another robot on HAB3.","engineering_analysis":"A passive transition depends on the center of mass crossing the intended boundary and one-way wheels resisting backslip.","interfaces":"Stilt foot, step edge, bumper and wheel contacts determine each support change.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect spring and bearing behavior under asymmetric loads, including incomplete ankle transition.","unknowns":"Qualification loads and partner envelope.","source_urls":["https://www.spartanrobotics.org/_files/ugd/00c1f8_39beba9b690d48febf9f90fa267cdf93.pdf","https://docs.lynkrobotics.org/technicalBinders/971/971-TB-2019.pdf"]}

title: 2022-125 Intake and entrance
text: {"name":"Intake and entrance","construction":"Pneumatic retracting collector with dead axle, metal printed pulleys and a separate roller identified for prospective Velcro.","operation":"Deploys near a ball and retracts essentially immediately to push it into the next roller.","team_rationale":"Fast acquisition and resistance to hits were priorities. Prototypes suggested Velcro could capture low-bouncing cargo otherwise missed.","engineering_analysis":"Retraction can increase handoff force without another actuator, but the two contacts must overlap in time. A late retract can leave cargo riding at the bumper.","interfaces":"Floor contact, retraction stroke, feeder inlet and open upper entry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect dead-axle supports and handoff gap after side impacts. Test bounced and grounded balls separately.","unknowns":"Roller diameters, dead-axle bearing stack and later Velcro installation.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]}

title: 2022-125 Feeder and March sorter
text: {"name":"Feeder and March sorter","construction":"S-shaped roller path. Later sorting architecture provides an ejection path through the intake.","operation":"Moves cargo through the low package to the shooter. Once two desired balls are held, stopped inner feed allows incoming cargo to be ejected above the intake.","team_rationale":"Low height and open front drove the curve. Hunting for alliance cargo in mixed piles took too much time at Week Zero.","engineering_analysis":"An alternate exit can save the approach turn and a shooter cycle. The release path must stay clear with a worn or partially compressed ball already staged.","interfaces":"Retracting collector, curved feeder compression, desired cargo count and shooter inlet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure whether a rejected ball disturbs either held ball. Check surfaces for wedging at changes in curvature.","unknowns":"Sorting sensor type, lower exit geometry and command sequencing.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2022-frc125-reveal-the-nutrons-present-freefall/405399"]}

title: 2022-125 Launcher and range control
text: {"name":"Launcher and range control","construction":"Light grippy wheels, powered front and rear contacts, adjustable hood and Limelight.","operation":"With the hub in view, software adjusts hood and shooter settings. Team favored the edge of the tarmac.","team_rationale":"Prior wheels gave useful grip at lower weight. Tests favored reduced spin and enough energy to enter without bouncing out.","engineering_analysis":"The two contact speeds jointly determine energy and spin. A faster shot can reduce successful retention even if it enters the opening more often.","interfaces":"Feeder output, traction, vision range and hood angle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare first and second exit conditions, then check for tread slip and hood backlash.","unknowns":"Wheel construction details, setpoint curves and chassis aim routine.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]}

title: 2022-125 Rung-reacting climber
text: {"name":"Rung-reacting climber","construction":"Primary deployment arms, reaction bars and final capture hooks.","operation":"After initial engagement and pull, reaction bars press on an intermediate rung to flatten the robot enough for the final hooks to catch traversal. Week Zero sequencing was manual after arm deployment.","team_rationale":"The team sought a faster route that skipped an intermediate hang and added the reaction bars after finding an unfavorable hanging angle.","engineering_analysis":"The extra contact changes pitch and local rung load. One-sided contact can twist the chassis and leave one hook short.","interfaces":"Initial suspension, reaction contact and final hook capture.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test loaded skew, contact slip and recovery after a missed final catch.","unknowns":"Exact rung ordinals from a corroborating diagram, actuator details and later automation deployment.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/O5ZSv-1vbJ8"]}

title: 2022-2046 Collector and service joint
text: {"name":"Collector and service joint","construction":"Early printed hubs with belting flaps. At Chezy a smaller griptape tube, mecanum centering and polycarbonate breakaways with a thicker inner piece.","operation":"Drops to pick up and feeds directly to the superstructure. Crew swaps breakaways or the complete spare collector.","team_rationale":"Early flap and Velcro configuration pushed too many balls away. Inner breakaway was thickened because it broke more often.","engineering_analysis":"A deliberate weak joint can protect the downstream frame if the failure load stays above ordinary pickup loads and below the load that bends the frame.","interfaces":"Roller centering, mounting plates and repeatable handoff to lift.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reported swapping the full assembly if breakaway repair would take more than about three minutes. A hard hit can still bend metal plates.","unknowns":"Actual joint failure load and spare swap procedure.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-robot-rapid-react/405155"]}

title: 2022-2046 Two-ball lift and feedback
text: {"name":"Two-ball lift and feedback","construction":"Custom printed tracking rollers, poly belts, ultrasonic sensing and driver controller haptics.","operation":"A detected ball advances the lift a set distance. Detecting the next creates room and updates driver feedback.","team_rationale":"The team describes acquisition notification and limiting held cargo to two.","engineering_analysis":"Distance indexing depends on traction and repeatable sensor placement. Slip can create a mismatch between count and actual stage position.","interfaces":"Collector exit, first/second cargo spacing and shooter feed nip.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking and run a stopped/restarted feed with two worn balls.","unknowns":"Encoder basis, exact detection location and count recovery logic.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM"]}

title: 2022-2046 Fixed launcher
text: {"name":"Fixed launcher","construction":"Fixed hood and chassis-relative heading, shooter and feed wheels, backspin contacts and Limelight.","operation":"Shoots from a preferred ring around the hub and farther when needed. Chassis provides azimuth.","team_rationale":"Team cited weight and serviceability. Field-house testing provided coverage within the fixed geometry.","engineering_analysis":"Removing hood motion trades an alignment degree of freedom for a more limited shot corridor. Route availability is part of measured shooter throughput.","interfaces":"Lift feed, chassis pose and vision target.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check fixed mount reference and rear-contact wear before retuning distance settings.","unknowns":"Exact exit angle, range-to-speed map and accuracy distribution.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-robot-rapid-react/405155"]}

title: 2022-2046 Belt telescopes
text: {"name":"Belt telescopes","construction":"Four continuously belt-routed telescoping arms arranged as inner and outer pairs.","operation":"Starts from mid. The inner pair catches high and lifts off mid. Chassis swing brings the outer arms to traversal.","team_rationale":"The team favored belt travel for speed and fewer spring problems, and added two arms to speed the sequence.","engineering_analysis":"Belt timing and hanging dynamics are coupled. A slightly different initial pitch changes the outer hook’s path at the transfer.","interfaces":"Arm hooks, rung loading, belt travel and chassis swing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking, hook closure and left-right asymmetry. Record missed-transfer recovery as well as clean cycles.","unknowns":"Rigging, sensors and onseason vs. Chezy timing changes.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/1zQLypCgjSM"]}

title: 2022-2481 Elongated chassis and swerve
text: {"name":"Elongated chassis and swerve","construction":"Cut-corner frame and five Falcon-powered swerve modules.","operation":"Each module takes a vector based on its position on the chassis.","team_rationale":"Five increased usable wheelbase over four and saved mass and motor allocation relative to six.","engineering_analysis":"A wider support polygon can help lateral stability on a long frame. Unequal normal loads can limit how much five drives contribute during acceleration.","interfaces":"Outer shape fixes module stations and climb contact reach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check loaded contact on uneven flooring and steering zero after climb impacts.","unknowns":"Module model, exact coordinates and load split.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919/78"]}

title: 2022-2481 Pickup and singulation
text: {"name":"Pickup and singulation","construction":"Four-bar with two rollers, compliant wheels replacing Velcro and one extra green wheel on the angled second roller.","operation":"The biased contact advances one of a side-by-side pair so the other can follow.","team_rationale":"The Velcro grabbed well but did not compress enough at transfer. The extra contact addressed simultaneous arrival jams.","engineering_analysis":"Passive priority reduces simultaneous occupation of the throat. It depends on enough timing separation under drive acceleration.","interfaces":"Front nip, second roller lateral centering, then feeder mouth.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch whether worn contact or a side hit changes which ball gets through.","unknowns":"Roller gaps, timing and actuator details.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY"]}

title: 2022-2481 Transfer and turret
text: {"name":"Transfer and turret","construction":"Lexan-backed lift, roller sets, half-turn turret, one heavy main wheel and three compliant upper wheels.","operation":"Lifts into the turret and launches with reduced backspin. Team described an annular shooting area and launchpad use.","team_rationale":"Reduced heavy-wheel count saved mass. Upper contacts reduce bounce-out.","engineering_analysis":"Half-turn azimuth decouples aim over part of the approach space. Outside that sweep the chassis still has to turn or the route must change.","interfaces":"Lift exit must remain aligned with the rotating inlet.
