Upper contact and main wheel condition jointly set release.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check turret limits and scuffs at the rotating entry before tuning RPM.","unknowns":"Staging sensors, turret cable accommodation and range map.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919"]}

title: 2022-2481 Truss-driving traversal
text: {"name":"Truss-driving traversal","construction":"Deployable front and rear drive wheels, guide rollers and self-closing rung hook.","operation":"Align to the truss, drive up using floor and truss reactions and close the hook after the rung moves past center.","team_rationale":"Truss geometry offered a promising path for triple climbs. Wheel size, grip and contact height were prototyped.","engineering_analysis":"If either contact runs out of traction or guide margin, the support geometry can disappear before the hook closes.","interfaces":"Rear carpet contact, front truss face and guide engagement followed by rung retention.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect wheel tread, guide damage and free hook return. Trial a yaw error and approach with partners already hanging.","unknowns":"Contact forces, current draw, recovery procedure and later line-sensor deployment.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/oG17jVYqORY","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/roboteers-team-2481-2022-robot-reveal/405919/78"]}

title: 2022-4499 Chassis and aiming
text: {"name":"Chassis and aiming","construction":"Square tube chassis, standardized mounting holes, inner electronics routing, MK4 L2 modules with four-inch nitrile-tread wheels.","operation":"Swerve accepts planar and angular velocities. Hub vision contributes position information alongside gyro heading and odometry.","team_rationale":"The team valued agile movement around the hub, straightforward integration and early time for other subsystems.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed-azimuth launcher makes chassis yaw accuracy a shot variable. Swerve can set yaw while translating, although intake approach still constrains where the chassis points.","interfaces":"Drive mounting, common feeder and climb references, hub camera and gyro.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tread and verify yaw references after contact. Camera bias or wheel slip can shift both path following and the shot setup.","unknowns":"Full aiming gate and camera calibration parameters.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}

title: 2022-4499 Intake
text: {"name":"Intake","construction":"Two belt-driven aluminum rollers on a pneumatic nonparallel four-bar with quarter-inch polycarbonate plates. One Falcon drives the rollers.","operation":"Compliant wheels collect and rear mecanum ends steer cargo inward before the handoff.","team_rationale":"Survive impacts, collect at speed and retract around defenders.","engineering_analysis":"Soft wheel contact and yielding links address different disturbances. The rear lateral component only helps if the second roller still has traction as the ball clears the bumper.","interfaces":"Bumper clearance, feeder inlet and paired cylinder linkage.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect both sides for skew and the shared belt for damage after corner impacts.","unknowns":"Deployed gaps and any cylinder synchronization procedure.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}

title: 2022-4499 Feeder
text: {"name":"Feeder","construction":"Flat deck, printed double-sided bump, flaps, two-inch entrance wheels, three-inch compliant index wheels and two beam breaks.","operation":"The bump lifts cargo into the indexing nip just upstream of the launcher.","team_rationale":"Preserve a low two-ball package and stable grip while allowing a possible second collector.","engineering_analysis":"A localized rigid rise makes indexing compression less sensitive to long-deck flex. Too much squeeze can turn two-ball acquisition into a stall.","interfaces":"Intake exit, two sensor stations, launcher throat and feeder frame supporting the climber.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check ramp fasteners, sensor alignment and wheel wear before changing control timing.","unknowns":"Compression tolerance for worn cargo and exact occupancy state machine.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}

title: 2022-4499 Shooter
text: {"name":"Shooter","construction":"Two six-inch nitrile-tread flywheels, two Falcon motors, a geared hood and a two-inch backspin roller driven from the flywheel.","operation":"Changes RPM and elevation for range, with the chassis positioning for the shot.","team_rationale":"Repeatable fast shots from multiple ranges.","engineering_analysis":"Coupling rear contact speed to the main wheel reduces independent tuning variables. Wear can still change the effective ratio at the ball.","interfaces":"Indexer entry, camera-derived pose and hood position.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tread, belt and hood play when a range-map correction fails to repeat.","unknowns":"Measured exit spin, per-range settings and accuracy under contact.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}

title: 2022-4499 Climber
text: {"name":"Climber","construction":"Two-stage elevator on tube rails, #25H chain drive, two Falcons, one-way carriage hooks and separately geared NEO 550 rotating arm.","operation":"Carriage and arm reach and transfer rung contact. Ratcheting hooks retain the robot after the match.","team_rationale":"Compact packaging and centering near the center of mass to reduce lateral swing.","engineering_analysis":"Rail alignment and chain tension matter under off-axis loading. The feeder structure is part of the climb load path.","interfaces":"Rung to hooks, rails and feeder/chassis tubes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bearing preload, chain slack, hook closure and hard-stop damage after an asymmetric catch.","unknowns":"Full rung transfer state sequence, swing feedback implementation and loaded approach statistics.","source_urls":["https://www.highlandersfrc.com/Documents/EngineeringBinder/2022/TechnicalBinder.pdf"]}

title: 2022-5172 Drive and operator feedback
text: {"name":"Drive and operator feedback","construction":"Swerve chassis with separate translation and rotation inputs. LEDs visible to driver and operator.","operation":"Driver translates independently of heading. Dark blue denotes lined up and ready, while lighter blue denotes close to alignment.","team_rationale":"Driver emphasized the practice needed to learn the new drivetrain and valued maneuverability.","engineering_analysis":"A shared ready indication can keep the driver moving until the shot is usable. It needs to distinguish stale vision from a genuinely good alignment.","interfaces":"Chassis heading sets intake presentation and remaining turret travel. Vision and readiness states reach both operators.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck gyro orientation and sensor/LED agreement after impacts or restarts.","unknowns":"Swerve module model, heading reset and exact ready predicates.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}

title: 2022-5172 Pickup and bridge
text: {"name":"Pickup and bridge","construction":"Pneumatic nonparallel four-bar, foam roller around a carbon-fiber rod, printed angled contacts and a deployable Lexan guard.","operation":"The guard drops as the intake deploys and bridges into the chute. Larger end contacts funnel off-center cargo.","team_rationale":"The team highlighted the bridge as important to bumper crossing and valued compliance for fast pickup against a wall.","engineering_analysis":"A moving bridge removes a floor-level handoff discontinuity without another powered axis. Its loaded edge still needs overlap with the chute through linkage play.","interfaces":"First roller to bumper bridge to chute entrance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for a curled guard lip, a binding hinge or damaged end prints when pickup succeeds but handoff fails.","unknowns":"Linkage stops, roller surface speed and guard retention when stowed.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}

title: 2022-5172 Staging and rejection
text: {"name":"Staging and rejection","construction":"Ramp, single conveyor wheel set and color sensor near the top.","operation":"The wheels hold cargo until feed. An opposing color triggers a different turret azimuth and discharge.","team_rationale":"The alternate heading keeps the rejected cargo from scoring in the hub.","engineering_analysis":"Sharing the shot path saves a second exit but can interrupt the next scoring cycle during slew, discharge and reacquisition. A color decision must stay associated with the correct cargo.","interfaces":"Sensor decision to indexing release and turret aim.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test alternating colors and closely spaced cargo, with particular attention to whether a second piece advances during reject.","unknowns":"Reject angle, sensor timing and simultaneous two-ball inventory.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}

title: 2022-5172 Turret launcher
text: {"name":"Turret launcher","construction":"Limelight, aluminum main wheel with blue nitrile tread and brass inertia masses, plus compliant upper wheels.","operation":"Automatically aims turret. Changes the speed of an already-spinning flywheel with observed range.","team_rationale":"Brass supports speed retention, nitrile improves grip and reducing backspin was intended to reduce bounce-outs.","engineering_analysis":"Added inertia reduces instantaneous RPM loss at release and makes large speed changes slower at a given torque. Keeping the wheel running reduces cold spin-up delay.","interfaces":"Conveyor exit, range-to-speed map, azimuth and readiness feedback.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tread and upper contact wear before recalibrating. Verify collision envelope at all useful azimuths.","unknowns":"Hood mechanism, exit-spin measurements and electrical duty cycle.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}

title: 2022-5172 Worlds climber
text: {"name":"Worlds climber","construction":"Powered reach hook and deployable support hooks. Wider hook placement and paired support contact distinguish the return configuration.","operation":"Reach mid, pull into support hooks, deploy to set reach angle, then reach the next bar and repeat.","team_rationale":"The four-stage replacement had mechanical issues. Wider hooks cleared the turret and paired contact reduced swing.","engineering_analysis":"Once the rung is supporting the chassis, changing hook geometry also moves the whole chassis and changes the next reach target.","interfaces":"Rung contact, suspended chassis pitch and turret envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a one-sided catch and a missed latch under load. Look for unequal contacts and interference before the next reach.","unknowns":"Exact actuator/rigging details and cause of the four-stage faults.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/5pX6RHlKFR0"]}

title: 2022-604 Collector
text: {"name":"Collector","construction":"One motor runs the acquisition contact and another deploys it. The deploy actuator uses a profiled goal with gravity-related feedforward.","operation":"Select deploy or retract, then run acquisition, reverse or clearing motion as required.","team_rationale":"Team rationale is not given in the inspected subsystem.","engineering_analysis":"Separate deploy and roller control lets the driver clear the ball while preserving the useful mouth pose. It also makes two failure paths possible.","interfaces":"Place the lower sensor where it can distinguish captured cargo from a ball merely passing across the mouth.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check the encoder zero after a hit and reversal when the mouth is blocked.","unknowns":"Exact contact width, bumper geometry and sensor alignment.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Intake.java"]}

title: 2022-604 Queue and transfer
text: {"name":"Queue and transfer","construction":"Lower and upper powered regions have separate stored state and sensor input. Color is evaluated against an alliance-color selection.","operation":"Advance cargo to the top position and preserve separation so a second ball does not enter the shot contact early.","team_rationale":"Code comments describe staging and a different feed speed when cargo is already at the launcher.","engineering_analysis":"Tracking both occupancy and color can prevent a correct launch command from feeding the wrong physical ball. The benefit depends on synchronization between sensors and stored state.","interfaces":"Upper sensor, queue location and launcher entrance need reliable spacing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test an interrupted move while cargo spans both regions. A debounced detector may need a recovery based on the actual sensor pattern.","unknowns":"No measured jam rate, color detection accuracy or successful queue recovery data.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/BallPath.java","https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/commands/RunIntakeAndMoveToTopQueue.java"]}

title: 2022-604 Launch readiness
text: {"name":"Launch readiness","construction":"Separate launcher motor controls maintain the requested speed. Both histories are checked before readiness.","operation":"Convert computed exit velocity to a speed setting, wait for steady samples and feed once feasible.","team_rationale":"The implementation uses feasibility and a short speed history rather than a single sample.","engineering_analysis":"Readiness can improve repeatability, but an overly strict settling condition can waste an open shot window. Measure the time and accuracy trade.","interfaces":"Launcher entry must retain the piece while wheels accelerate, then feed cleanly without reducing speed below the tolerance band.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare single and paired shots on a partially discharged battery. Log rejected shot conditions.","unknowns":"No independently measured recovery time or field accuracy by range.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Launcher.java","https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/BallPath.java"]}

title: 2022-604 Traversal sequencing
text: {"name":"Traversal sequencing","construction":"The climb controller divides the maneuver into reaches, contact, partial lifts and handoffs with tilt inputs.","operation":"Advance through stable intermediate states while moving between rungs.","team_rationale":"Published source exposes transition structure without giving a rationale for each threshold.","engineering_analysis":"A sequence is easier to recover when each load-transfer state has an observable condition. Test each intermediate state rather than only the complete routine.","interfaces":"Hooks and rung approach must keep the next reach accessible when the chassis swings under load.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check unexpected swing and early contact. Confirm the routine has a safe response when a handoff cannot be completed.","unknowns":"No dimensioned hook or rigging data in the reviewed sections.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc604/2022-public/blob/2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d/FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/subsystems/Climber.java"]}

title: 2023-118 Floor intake and scoring arm
text: {"name":"Floor intake and scoring arm","construction":"Bent-polycarbonate dustpan intake with waterjet grout-sponge wheels over a pool-noodle roller. Falcon reductions are 6.25:1 for the two-motor roller, 60:1 for pivot and 40:1 for flappers. Arm pivot and telescope are 118:1 and 15.58:1 respectively.","operation":"Waterjet sectors deploy the floor intake. A camera supports cone detection. A pivoting telescopic arm moves a double-roller head with silicone surfaces.","team_rationale":"The team specifies polycarbonate for impact resistance, shimmed hex interfaces to reduce backlash, and light arm/head materials to reduce moving mass.","engineering_analysis":"A soft roller may widen the capture window while changing centering under compression. Verify custody overlap and clearance before increasing axis speeds.","interfaces":"Dustpan delivery pose meets the arm head. Printed clamps attach the head to the carbon telescope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sponge adhesion, flapper clearance, shim wear and head clamp alignment after collision. Exercise transfer with skewed cones.","unknowns":"Handoff triggers, arm calibration, cube capture limits and cycle times.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-robonauts-118-2023-video/429565?page=3"]}

title: 2023-118 Partner forks and swerve
text: {"name":"Partner forks and swerve","construction":"Backwards-mounted Mk4 L2 modules in a sheet-metal and billet chassis. Forks use 3/4-inch solid carbon rods, nonparallel four-bar, 230:1 lift, 28:1 deployment, over-center linkage and servo pawl release.","operation":"A driver camera aids alignment. Forks reach under the partner and lift and tilt it away from the floor.","team_rationale":"The team cites increased stability for its module placement and sufficient clearance under the partner for the slender rods.","engineering_analysis":"The support reaction depends on where the rods engage the partner. Test the full loaded system, including stance and station pitch.","interfaces":"Fork loads enter the carriage and chassis. Partner underbody geometry and pawl release affect recovery.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check ratchet engagement, fork damage and over-center geometry after load. Recheck frame squareness after contact.","unknowns":"Qualified partner envelope, fork load data and exact red/blue revision geometry.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-robonauts-118-2023-video/429565?page=3"]}

title: 2023-118 Blooper, Swiper and avionics
text: {"name":"Blooper, Swiper and avionics","construction":"Blooper uses an extension spring, adjustable stop and servo pin puller. Swiper has two in-perimeter cups with independent 775 Redline-driven vacuum pumps. Custom avionics include a ten-channel CAN node and switchable low-current power.","operation":"Blooper fires once from the preload position. Swiper applies independent vacuum at its two contacts. Lua scripts coordinate selected autonomous and driver sequences, with gyro PID for station balance.","team_rationale":"The binder identifies a dedicated preload shot and a cube pickup developed in three days between Houston and Space City.","engineering_analysis":"Separate pumps can limit shared leakage effects, but seals still depend on cube surface. A separate preload shot saves arm sequencing only if launch consistency is maintained.","interfaces":"Spring preload and hard stop set release geometry. Vacuum and digital controls share chassis space and electrical supply with the main scorer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check latch reset, spring setting, seal integrity and device wiring after repairs.","unknowns":"Catapult trial count, vacuum retention and release sequence, and Swiper match use.","source_urls":["https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf"]}

title: 2023-125 Arm extension, guides and planning
text: {"name":"Arm extension, guides and planning","construction":"Multi-stage telescope with printed bearing blocks. The final blocks reported by the team were printed on Markforged Onyx Ones. The shoulder and extension are coordinated by offline trajectories.","operation":"Guide fit is tuned after assembly and powder coating. The team measured play, moved bearing locations in the print and reprinted on the same machine.","team_rationale":"The team optimized part breakup and fit and wanted to move quickly between poses with obstacle and motion constraints.","engineering_analysis":"At long extension, small guide gaps can become large wrist errors. Test side load, joint reversal and repeated extension with the assembled coating stack.","interfaces":"The telescope carries the powered wrist. The extension gearbox also drives harness payout. The early collector shares the arm's swept corridor.","service_and_failure_modes":"Keep printed spare guides matched to real tube lots and coatings. Recheck clearance and endpoint calibration after installing a replacement.","unknowns":"Final bearing preload, telescope section sizes, shoulder drive geometry and trajectory deployment by event.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]}

title: 2023-125 Wrist, rollers and harness
text: {"name":"Wrist, rollers and harness","construction":"Compact printed wrist and end-effector parts, two NEOs with Spark MAX controllers, a helical cable drum driven from the extension gearbox, and separate four-wire power and CAN slip rings. Surgical tubing tensions an approximately eight-inch cable section.","operation":"The drum winds or pays out with extension. The elastic section takes up mismatch at direction changes. Wrist and intake circuits each use a 30 A breaker and controller current limit.","team_rationale":"The team used reduction to make the wrist controllable while holding position and prototyped the roller to preserve adequate acquisition and ejection with the current cap.","engineering_analysis":"A spool phase error accumulates with stroke. The elastic section needs enough travel to absorb reversals without concealing excessive tension at full reach.","interfaces":"Power and CAN cross the rotating drum boundary. Harness motion is mechanically tied to extension rather than to a separate motor.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check strand condition, slip-ring continuity and voltage at the tip through repeated reversals. Validate that the roller clears a jam under its current limit.","unknowns":"Slip-ring models, spool ratio, harness fatigue life and roller compression.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]}

title: 2023-125 Split collector and base
text: {"name":"Split collector and base","construction":"Early roller split across the front. Aluminum and printed rack assemblies ride on printed bearing blocks. The chassis routes front and rear swerve wiring to opposite PDH sides.","operation":"The deployed roller collects while leaving room for the arm to swing through its center. The later robot dispensed with that intake.","team_rationale":"The team states the split was for arm clearance. February plans included 26 lb of low steel ballast after a 78 lb pre-ballast weigh-in.","engineering_analysis":"A centered corridor exchanges usable roller width for collision clearance. An offset strike can bind one rack while the other still moves.","interfaces":"The racks and arm compete for front-frame space. The base distributes arm and ballast loads to the wheels.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check both racks after unilateral impact and reproduce handoff with the real bumpers and held piece before copying the arrangement.","unknowns":"Collector synchronization hardware in the final early-season revision, the date of removal, and final official weight.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc125-the-nutrons-2023-code-and-cad-release/438641","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-125-nutrons/427639"]}

title: 2023-1727 Swerve and base
text: {"name":"Swerve and base","construction":"24 by 28 inch aluminum MaxTube chassis with REV MAXSwerve, four NEO 1.1 drive motors and four NEO 550 steering motors. Drive reduction is 5.08:1. A 1/8-inch aluminum belly pan and 15 lb of steel rail ballast sit low.","operation":"Independent steering permits translation around obstacles and a wheel-lock configuration for station use.","team_rationale":"REX sought strafe mobility and a low center of gravity. Toggle clamps are specified for rapid bumper swaps.","engineering_analysis":"Test downhill braking and direction reversals with a representative high extension, where wheel load transfer can undermine pose control.","interfaces":"Arm and ballast loads enter the frame. The belly pan protects and carries electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect clamps, wheel steering zero and rail retention after hard impacts.","unknowns":"Loaded speed and measured stability margin.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]}

title: 2023-1727 Arm and telescope
text: {"name":"Arm and telescope","construction":"Arm uses one NEO 1.1 with 100:1 MaxPlanetary and two 30 lb gas springs. A turnbuckle adjusts the fixed-center chain. The two-stage Thrifty Bot lift uses custom string and pulleys, a 9:1 planetary and a 2:1 external gear stage.","operation":"The two axes can travel simultaneously to a preset. The shared axle and removable lift attachment integrate the drives.","team_rationale":"REX cites shorter piece transit and straightforward removal of the arm from the elevator.","engineering_analysis":"Gas assist varies with geometry. Check shoulder tracking across extension because both gravity leverage and reflected inertia change.","interfaces":"Shared axle, lift mount, string path and protected cable chain all cross the pivot-to-extension boundary.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check string tracking and tension, chain slack and spring mounts before retuning. Confirm the lift can be removed without losing alignment.","unknowns":"String anchoring and event-specific tension settings.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]}

title: 2023-1727 Roller head and controls
text: {"name":"Roller head and controls","construction":"Six four-inch VEXpro flex wheels, four 30A and two 45A, in quarter-inch polycarbonate. One NEO drives the head. Lift and arm use PID position control.","operation":"Preset scoring poses coordinate both axes. PathPlanner event markers run subsystem commands during autonomous travel.","team_rationale":"The team prioritized positive capture despite variable piece compliance and reduced driver input.","engineering_analysis":"A failed grab ties up the scoring axes. Measure acquisition tolerance in yaw, height and piece deformation before extending the concept to crowded approaches.","interfaces":"Head rides the moving lift. Electrical leads must traverse the pivot and the extension track.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check polycarbonate hole elongation, wheel wear, wire strain and whether an interrupted preset can be recovered cleanly.","unknowns":"Exact head reduction convention and acquisition confirmation method.","source_urls":["https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6174237f356d2538b2cf482d/t/665390d5e89cf80f9ae28234/1716752598746/1727%2BTechnical%2BBinder%2B2023.pdf"]}

title: 2023-1746 Chassis and approach
text: {"name":"Chassis and approach","construction":"The interview describes Mk4i L1 modules with minimal modification.","operation":"Drive the single tool to the floor, station or scoring approach that its workspace can reach.","team_rationale":"The team preferred available drive torque for its reported robot weight and defense.","engineering_analysis":"Direct acquisition shifts some workload from mechanism alignment to driver positioning. Evaluate time from first sight of the piece to confirmed capture, including failed approaches.","interfaces":"The mast line and bumper face constrain how close the rollers can reach the wall and floor.","service_and_failure_modes":"A bumper offset, arm zero change or poor alignment can show up as an acquisition problem even when roller speed is unchanged.","unknowns":"No measured turning, loaded acceleration or capture tolerance comparison.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]}

title: 2023-1746 Continuously rigged elevator
text: {"name":"Continuously rigged elevator","construction":"The IRI team describes one-inch thin-wall tubing, custom Thrifty-inspired bearing blocks and a continuous belt.","operation":"Move the roller hand along the mast and hold each scoring height with closed-loop control.","team_rationale":"The team reduced high weight after its first version was too tall and heavy.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed mast removes a shoulder axis and makes packaging easier to reason about. It couples horizontal and vertical motion, so practical reach depends on the chassis pose.","interfaces":"Guide and belt loads change with tool extension. Belt tension, carriage yaw and wrist cable clearance matter through the entire stroke.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check binding and belt tracking with an off-center cone and inspect where the mast lands under bump contact.","unknowns":"The earlier rebuild angle and stage terminology come from owner recollection. The later interview supplies different evidence.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]}

title: 2023-1746 Shared wrist and roller hand
text: {"name":"Shared wrist and roller hand","construction":"The team credits 111 for the roller intake inspiration and 1339 for the wrist approach. A Falcon drives through gearing and chain. The tool uses machined polycarbonate and printed parts.","operation":"Rotate to the pickup pose, draw a cone or cube into the tool, hold possession through the lift movement and release at the node.","team_rationale":"The team selected the intake after seeing reliable use elsewhere. The wrist reduction gives useful holding torque.","engineering_analysis":"One possession path removes the timing and alignment demands of an intake-to-gripper handoff. It still needs a workable grip on both pieces and a wrist that holds position at load without excess current.","interfaces":"Tool width and cone orientation determine the practical floor and pole approach. The wrist and carriage must support the heaviest useful extension.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect wear at the roller surface, chain tension and flex in the tool plates. Compare acquisition at multiple piece orientations.","unknowns":"The full wrist reduction and field capture envelope remain unresolved.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]}

title: 2023-1746 Autonomous preload and controls
text: {"name":"Autonomous preload and controls","construction":"Servo releases an over-center preload launcher. The lift and wrist hold targets with closed-loop control.","operation":"The launcher scores a staged cube rearward in the chosen autonomous routine, then normal acquisition uses the shared hand.","team_rationale":"The team described saving time otherwise lost to turning.","engineering_analysis":"A narrow autonomous exception can earn its complexity when it bypasses a repeatable dead movement. Count reset time, preload reliability and changes to the starting pose.","interfaces":"The preload launcher must coexist with the lift and remain clear of the normal cycle. The wrist’s higher torque and gravity load change tuning demands.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test scoring from modest pose error and confirm a failed preload leaves the rest of the autonomous routine useful.","unknowns":"The interview reports success qualitatively. It gives no matched comparison of all autos or a measured vision upgrade effect.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PhlmMCOir8"]}

title: 2023-1756 Shoulder and extension
text: {"name":"Shoulder and extension","construction":"Ball-screw linear actuator with custom gearbox raises the arm. Sprocket teeth engage a CNC-routed hole pattern in a nested tube as a modified rack and pinion.","operation":"The shoulder moves the inner tube's line of action, while extension sets radial reach. Position requests are converted to coordinated shoulder and extension motion.","team_rationale":"Argos documents configurable conversion from sensor readings to physical units and preset movement through a kinematic model.","engineering_analysis":"Actuator leverage changes through the pivot arc. A perforated rack also concentrates load at the hole edges. Test both for play and tracking in loaded reversals.","interfaces":"The shoulder pivot transmits reach and piece loads to the chassis. The extending tube carries wrist, rollers and their harness.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect actuator pivots, hole wear and tube guides. Verify virtual retract reference after changing guide fit or disassembling the transmission.","unknowns":"Actuator force curve, sprocket geometry and tube-guide stack.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]}

title: 2023-1756 Wrist and roller head
text: {"name":"Wrist and roller head","construction":"Dual axles with compliant wheels, rigid aluminum tube and a powered flipping wrist.","operation":"The intake controls the piece while it changes orientation. The pose command distinguishes roller-up and roller-down targets and restricts early flips to a defined arm envelope.","team_rationale":"The integrated head serves both acquisition and placement. LEDs communicate intent and intake status.","engineering_analysis":"Cone flange engagement and cube compression impose different contact requirements. A current spike can also come from an obstruction, so evaluate it together with distance and retention.","interfaces":"Wrist and intake wiring follow the extending arm. The pose command reads piece orientation when selecting an end attitude.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check time-of-flight range with dirty sensors and crushed or skewed pieces. Validate reverse and interrupted wrist transitions with an actual piece.","unknowns":"Roller durometers, speed, field-side release accuracy and sensor false-positive rates.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]}

title: 2023-1756 Bash guards and chassis
text: {"name":"Bash guards and chassis","construction":"Paired guard tubes driven by a sprocket and hex shaft. Guards tilt downward and the drivetrain is swerve.","operation":"Guard deployment is operator-selectable. The subsystem has soft limits after homing, and pose command initialization can exclude guard motion when guard home has failed.","team_rationale":"The team wanted extra intake protection and specified a downward deployment angle to keep the guards in the bumper zone.","engineering_analysis":"Guard contact can redirect load into the chassis and a bent tube may consume clearance even when encoder position reads correctly.","interfaces":"Guard targets are included in the arm motion command. Chassis pose determines clearance to the grid and field structures.","service_and_failure_modes":"After side contact, check both tubes for unequal travel and rehome. Exercise the homing-failure branch before relying on degraded operation.","unknowns":"Guard material, impact ratings, exact event fit and measured scoring-wall clearance.","source_urls":["https://www.teamargos.org/assets/files/2023_Judge_Handout-24cf2061b65da71c4282727cf68a4f64.pdf","https://github.com/FRC1756-Argos/2023-Robot/tree/6375116c9331d3840823979990460ac4b9a83bfb"]}

title: 2023-2767 Carbon elevator and tilt
text: {"name":"Carbon elevator and tilt","construction":"Single-stage carbon-fiber elevator, two carriage motors and printed Onyx pivot sectors. A carriage-mounted arm is driven by an Onyx gearbox.","operation":"Sector travel changes lift angle. Carriage travel and elbow angle change the hand's height and reach relative to the grid.","team_rationale":"The team reports enlarging the curved rack and improving elbow durability between St. Joe and Worlds. It describes iterating backlash when needed for smooth gear operation.","engineering_analysis":"A tilted lift converts some travel to horizontal reach. Measure tooth engagement at both extremes with a loaded hand, where sector backlash and carriage deflection combine.","interfaces":"Tilt load enters the chromoly chassis. The carriage carries the elbow gearbox, hand and moving electrical services.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect sector tooth contact, printed gearbox fit and carbon-to-fitting joints. Compare open-loop current and speed after repairs.","unknowns":"Carriage rigging, bonded joint strength, tilt limits and actual load margins.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]}

title: 2023-2767 Ground cube collector and hand
text: {"name":"Ground cube collector and hand","construction":"Motorized collector travel uses a Talon SRX with a profiled setpoint. The collector roller uses a Falcon controller. The hand has separately controlled jaw and roller motors. The team identifies bevel gears in the claw.","operation":"The collector stages a cube for the open hand. The hand uses a limit-input piece indication to advance to the grab, retract and hold sequence. The floor cone uses a dedicated hand posture and arm sweep.","team_rationale":"The team describes mechanism sequencing with driver initiation and a manual fallback. It reports enlarging the claw bevel gears for Worlds.","engineering_analysis":"The pickup window requires matching roller directions, hand opening and collector pose. Time the transfer with worn cubes, including a sensor transition before the piece is fully seated.","interfaces":"The frame-mounted collector meets the moving hand at a defined arm pose. Piece confirmation ties jaw command and collector retract together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check beam-break inputs and sensor zero after an impact. Try a partial cube insertion and verify the manual controls can clear it without driving an axis into another.","unknowns":"Collector width, exact roller contact geometry and quantitative transfer tolerance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]}

title: 2023-2767 Drivetrain and health checks
text: {"name":"Drivetrain and health checks","construction":"Chromoly frame and custom swerve with extensive printed Onyx parts. The team reports adding a 20 lb plate below the belly pan.","operation":"Drive input is limited during pickup and placement. AprilTag vision supports positioning and an open-loop health-check logs axis speed and current.","team_rationale":"Ballast was added for stability. The team uses current and speed comparisons to flag friction before closed-loop performance degrades.","engineering_analysis":"Track comparable battery voltage and test load when comparing current traces, so voltage sag does not masquerade as gearbox friction.","interfaces":"The frame supports lift pivot loads. Camera placement on the elevator can change the view as the structure moves.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare drive azimuth velocity and current against the baseline after repairs. Check camera alignment after upper-structure impacts.","unknowns":"Module hardware loads, pose-dependent vision calibration and measured ramp behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2767-stryke-force-cad-code-release-2023/437202","https://github.com/strykeforce/chargedup/tree/25e9168de2f9dd8a88c31a6025508adb10421b33"]}

title: 2023-4414 Continuous belt elevator
text: {"name":"Continuous belt elevator","construction":"WCP inline blocks with 0.75-inch bearings, 5.6:1 reduction, 36-tooth 18 mm HTD5 drive pulley and fiberglass Gates belt. Printed Onyx redirects are supported through their width. A toothed block and cam tension the belt.","operation":"Belt runs between the stages. Four constant-force springs help the intermediate stages return through an inclined, low-gravity-assist path.","team_rationale":"The team wanted compact packaging and more overlap. It selected larger bearings after smaller ones had cracked or worn into tubing.","engineering_analysis":"Return force must overcome worst-case loaded guide and belt friction. Extra bends and belt stiffness consume margin that would otherwise seat stages reliably.","interfaces":"Base tube carries the gearbox. The moving carriage carries arm loads. Belt clamps and redirects fit within the mast envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check smooth redirects, belt tracking and clamp slip after rebuilds. Compare repeatability on rapid reversals, where sticky stages can settle in the wrong order.","unknowns":"Belt tension target, stage travel and endurance measurements.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584/155"]}

title: 2023-4414 Arm, wrist and cube intake
text: {"name":"Arm, wrist and cube intake","construction":"April arm uses an unequal-sprocket virtual four-bar and powered head rollers. The April inventory gives separate motors for cube roller and deploy. The offseason arm and wrist use lightened 7075 construction.","operation":"Arm angle determines claw pitch in April. The replacement arm and wrist use roller locations inspired by 1323. Later A/B notes distinguish some intake contact hardware.","team_rationale":"The offseason changes targeted lower moving mass and improved autonomous reliability. The team reports a roller breaking while the 7075 intake plates survived impacts.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed angular relationship simplifies actuation but constrains the pose family. Measure ground contact and high-node clearance together before changing sprocket sizes.","interfaces":"The carriage takes the linkage reaction. The collector and claw must share a transfer envelope without fouling the mast or stowed hardware.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect roller cores, glued hubs and pivot lash after contact. Test incomplete transfer and reversal.","unknowns":"April handoff geometry, linkage ratios and revision-specific pickup sequences.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=6","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=11"]}

title: 2023-4414 Swerve, crawler and vision
text: {"name":"Swerve, crawler and vision","construction":"April inventory lists 12 motors across swerve and one for crawler tracks. Chezy revisions added a vision tower and ballast low behind the elevator.","operation":"Swerve sets approach position. The tower improves sightlines to retroreflective tape and provides a rear-facing cone-tracking camera for autonomous.","team_rationale":"The team reports two high autonomous cones became possible without tipping after the changes. It also reports trading practice and readiness for the upgrades.","engineering_analysis":"Extra motors raise demand on packaging and power. Evaluate combined drivetrain and lift load with realistic batteries and loaded acceleration.","interfaces":"Wheel support polygon and mast loads bound tipping. Camera clearance competes with the slanted elevator and arm.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check approach under voltage sag and verify camera extrinsics after impacts.","unknowns":"Crawler operation, current limits and quantified vision success.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=6","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-4414-hightide-2023-robot-tsunami/428584?page=11"]}

title: 2023-604 Floor intake and reorienter
text: {"name":"Floor intake and reorienter","construction":"Pasta-style paired rollers, powered rotating roller assembly and linear intake slider. Roller power passes through the reorienter coaxially.","operation":"The rollers grip the piece and constrain cone direction to one of two states. The rotating assembly makes a pose suitable for transfer.","team_rationale":"Quixilver sought ground acquisition regardless of cone orientation, with the motor mass and exposure reduced at the intake's leading edge.","engineering_analysis":"The two-state assumption is valuable only if skewed cones settle into one of those states with predictable range readings.","interfaces":"Coaxial transmission crosses a moving pivot. Slider alignment fixes the receiver's fore-aft and height window.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect slider travel after frontal contact. Test roller grip and range separation with folded flanges, soft cubes and parts shifted by impact.","unknowns":"Roller materials, exact reductions and capture probability by approach angle.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]}

title: 2023-604 Sensing, cross-slide and transfer
text: {"name":"Sensing, cross-slide and transfer","construction":"Time-of-flight ranging, powered transverse scoring slide, vertical elevator and coordinated transfer commands.","operation":"Orientation selects the measurement pose. Filtered range plus an offset sets the lateral position. Roller release and receiving commands overlap as the system clears the exchange.","team_rationale":"The lateral slider was added because the piece can land anywhere across the roller span. The team wanted handoff across that span.","engineering_analysis":"A clamped axis target can still be unreachable for the jaw. Test the edges for transfer completion, not just encoder arrival.","interfaces":"Sensor line of sight couples piece geometry to axis position. The gripper, elevator, arm and intake are all command requirements during handoff.","service_and_failure_modes":"After replacing sensors or guides, verify tip-in/out readings and transverse offset. Try an interrupted exchange with a half-seated piece.","unknowns":"Drop detection and recovery rates, precise sensor mounting and calibration tolerances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]}

title: 2023-604 Scoring linkage and operator interface
text: {"name":"Scoring linkage and operator interface","construction":"Non-parallel four-bar with an Everybot-style roller gripper on the elevating assembly. The original driver-station keyboard selected scoring location.","operation":"The linkage extends to the mid and high rows. The driver later aligned manually while the operator selected piece type and row.","team_rationale":"The team chose the linkage for reach and lower weight. It reports the driver eventually outperformed the automatic location-scoring sequence.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate both manual and automatic release against total time and repeatability once the drive team has practiced. Tip grip makes cone attitude sensitive to contact slip.","interfaces":"Four-bar, elevator and transverse slide stack loads between the claw and chassis.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check joint play at extended poses and verify that a slipped cone still clears the node during retract.","unknowns":"Arm transmission, grid clearance under load and measured manual-versus-automatic performance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255","https://github.com/frc604/2023-public/tree/7a43ff85694409364cbf79a422728d0f9b3bf4eb/FRC-2023"]}

title: 2023-6328 Ground cube collector
text: {"name":"Ground cube collector","construction":"Independent deployed collector and powered roller are represented in the released code. Deployment is profiled and zeroed using absolute and relative angle information.","operation":"Drive into a cube with the collector deployed and present it near the gripper.","team_rationale":"The release documents a dedicated route alongside direct pickup. It does not provide a controlled comparison of the two.","engineering_analysis":"A wider collector can improve approach tolerance, but a cube sent out skewed still needs to be recoverable at the receiver. The same alignment question moves from driver-to-mouth to collector-to-hand.","interfaces":"Collector pivot, roller outlet and receiving gripper pose must align while the chassis and arm may be moving.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for cube corners that stick at the exit and for false stow following impact.","unknowns":"Exact contact widths, loaded transfer speed and event-specific hardware not established by the code.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/cubeintake/CubeIntake.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]}

title: 2023-6328 Arm reach and sweep
text: {"name":"Arm reach and sweep","construction":"The released arm interfaces command preplanned poses and direct tool targets. The floor sweep varies horizontal reach while holding a low target height.","operation":"Approach the floor pose, sweep for acquisition and return home on command termination.","team_rationale":"The direct route offers another acquisition option without routing every piece through the cube collector.","engineering_analysis":"More reach and orientation freedom can save chassis repositioning. Evaluate the price in moving inertia and slower transition margins with the tool loaded.","interfaces":"The direct sweep needs space outside the frame and a path back from both front and rear.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether a pose is available near a wall after a bump or steering error. Test blocked path recovery with the piece retained.","unknowns":"Setpoint limits do not establish reachable physical contact under load.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeFromFloorSweeper.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/arm/Arm.java"]}

title: 2023-6328 Handoff coordination
text: {"name":"Handoff coordination","construction":"The collector is the deadline for concurrent arm and gripper commands. The arm targets the cube handoff preset and an indicator marks readiness.","operation":"Keep the receiver active during transfer, then command the arm to return toward home when the operation ends.","team_rationale":"The command comments specify an immediate cube handoff.","engineering_analysis":"The design benefits from overlapping motions, so handoff time is not automatically the sum of both actuator times. Still test early arrival, late arrival, interrupted input and asymmetric compression.","interfaces":"The collector-to-gripper gap, vertical approach and roller direction all affect whether the cube remains controlled through the interface.","service_and_failure_modes":"An interrupted command can leave a piece between contacts. Verify a recovery or clear-out route that does not force the arm through an occupied region.","unknowns":"The software does not establish transfer completion probability or all clearance assumptions.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]}

title: 2023-6328 Gripper and scoring release
text: {"name":"Gripper and scoring release","construction":"Motor-driven gripper with holding, intake and multiple eject requests. The code monitors roller speed and temperature.","operation":"Intake until the timed velocity sequence concludes, then hold. Choose an eject behavior based on the scoring objective.","team_rationale":"Separate release settings fit different scoring interactions.","engineering_analysis":"Speed-based detection is available even without an extra detector, but friction, an obstruction and true possession can all slow a roller. Verify which signals remain reliable after wear.","interfaces":"The gripper shares position targets with the articulated arm, and its own operating state determines whether the game piece will stay put during transit.","service_and_failure_modes":"The release includes high-temperature protection. Compare retention after a protective stop and after a stalled attempt.","unknowns":"No measured possession accuracy, scoring reliability or installed friction coefficients.","source_urls":["https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/subsystems/gripper/Gripper.java","https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java"]}

title: 2023-973 Cascade elevator
text: {"name":"Cascade elevator","construction":"Inclined, paired metal rails with nested members visible. The interviewer identifies cascade rigging in the written overview.","operation":"The elevator changes manipulator height and, because of the incline, changes horizontal offset as it travels.","team_rationale":"Robot-specific selection and manufacturing rationale could not be newly verified.","engineering_analysis":"A narrow span can increase sensitivity to racking from an off-center piece. Measure diagonal movement and carriage error on abrupt reversal with the wrist extended.","interfaces":"The mast bolts into the chassis and the lower moving head occupies space directly in front of the rails.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect both sides for unequal stage travel and contact marks after lateral hits. Confirm harness clearance across moving stages.","unknowns":"Stage count, gearbox and motor specification, rigging details and exact commercial kit fit.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]}

title: 2023-973 Wrist and roller head
text: {"name":"Wrist and roller head","construction":"Paired cylindrical rollers and a side pivot transmission are visible. A peer identifies the wrist attachment as aluminum.","operation":"Wrist motion changes piece presentation. The host associates that motion with rolling cubes. A published photo shows a low carried cone.","team_rationale":"The peer reports that the two-roller and wrist attachment details influenced 972. Greybots' own rationale for contact count was not newly accessible.","engineering_analysis":"Independent wrist orientation can compensate for the fixed mast angle. If rolling is used for release, surface friction and approach pitch can affect the result even at the same wrist setpoint.","interfaces":"Roller head attaches to the lift carriage. Low pitch brings it close to the bumper and wider front assembly.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check backlash, roller grip and symmetry. Test worn cube surfaces and cone flange deformation across the pickup and release envelopes.","unknowns":"Wrist ratio, roller drive and compliance, sensor confirmation and documented release poses.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]}

title: 2023-973 Wide front assembly and swerve
text: {"name":"Wide front assembly and swerve","construction":"The team image shows a transverse lower assembly. A peer reports a wider cube intake for Champs. The host identifies swerve.","operation":"Swerve controls the field approach while the intake hardware sets the physical capture window.","team_rationale":"The wider cube intake is peer-reported. No primary design rationale or quantitative trade study was found.","engineering_analysis":"Wider coverage can reduce centering demands while increasing leverage from side impact. Compare capture rates with actual approach error distributions.","interfaces":"Frame rail and bumper clearance govern how far the wider assembly can reach and retract.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect alignment after one-sided strikes and test for partial capture at the outer edges.","unknowns":"Module variant, collector drive, handoff sequence and as-built date.","source_urls":["https://www.greybots.com/the-robots.html","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-973-greybots-cube-rolling-strategy-robot-overview/429317","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/very-strange-coincidence/435607"]}

title: 2024-1778 Collector and acquisition
text: {"name":"Collector and acquisition","construction":"Separately powered roller and wrist functions; absolute intake angle from the roller controller. Team reported 0.2-inch compression.","operation":"The floor routine waits for its angle command before starting parallel acquisition. Source loading skips the floor collector.","team_rationale":"Team published compression. The code describes the sequence but gives no prototype rationale for individual roller positions.","engineering_analysis":"Driving the collector and destination together allows an early handoff, provided the leading edge reaches the downstream nip before it loses the upstream contact.","interfaces":"Collector wrist position gates roller operation through the command sequence, and the shooter acquisition command is the deadline for parallel collection.","service_and_failure_modes":"A loose absolute sensor connection can remove angle feedback even when the wrist motor remains functional. Inspect the sensor through full collector travel.","unknowns":"Roller number, tread, and entry envelope await physical or interview review.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727","https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]}

title: 2024-1778 Shooter, staging and Amp bar
text: {"name":"Shooter, staging and Amp bar","construction":"Team describes two lower rollers, one top roller and a virtual four-bar. Software separates two regulated flywheel motors, a feed motor, two line breaks and a wrist.","operation":"Speaker tracking checks wrist alignment, tag availability, chassis heading and flywheel readiness before timed feeding, with separate preset branches. Amp uses the feed roller and coupled bar.","team_rationale":"The extra lower roller fixed an Amp shot above the bar and improved intake. Linkage addressed concern about notes falling into the bellypan without requiring another motor.","engineering_analysis":"Wrist-angle error affects both launch and Amp alignment. The shown speed check uses top wheel feedback despite both motor velocities being available, so test asymmetric wheel recovery.","interfaces":"Upper beam clearance terminates centering; the lower beam represents storage. The linkage maps wrist angle to bar location without a separate actuator state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check both beam transitions with worn notes. In the centering command a continuously blocked upper beam can keep slow feeding active until interrupted.","unknowns":"Exact linkage pivots, wheel diameters, and shot dispersion.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1778-cad-code-release/466727","https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]}

title: 2024-1778 Climbers and drive coordination
text: {"name":"Climbers and drive coordination","construction":"Two oppositely signed hook objects each use one master and one following NEO with brake mode and current limits.","operation":"Extend starts both sides and stops them individually as calculated extension passes 0.7; retraction similarly stops each side near zero.","team_rationale":"The reviewed code demonstrates independent control, while the claimed single-side field recovery remains unverified here.","engineering_analysis":"Independent stopping handles position mismatch; equal encoder readings cannot establish equal chain load or confirmed engagement.","interfaces":"Master encoder and configured drum circumference/reduction establish the travel estimate. The extend command also owns the intake wrist.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify encoder zero and paired-motor direction after service. Validate asymmetric loading separately from nominal dual-side operation.","unknowns":"Actual hook, cable and drum construction, attachment load, and trap capability.","source_urls":["https://github.com/FIRST1778/2024-Robot-Code-Public"]}

title: 2024-2075 Floor pickup and higher roller assembly
text: {"name":"Floor pickup and higher roller assembly","construction":"Visible green and gray wheel groups on a transverse shaft; underside inspection frames expose multiple roller and support groups below the blue bumper.","operation":"Pickup hardware can be presented low or in a raised position. The team reveal identifies a separate start-of-match release action.","team_rationale":"The Kentwood update explicitly targeted reliability and robustness. Spring rate and wall pickup rationale were not verified in the primary material reviewed.","engineering_analysis":"Compliance would allow a narrow entry to accept differently worn rings, but if roller sections deflect unevenly the downstream handoff can arrive skewed.","interfaces":"Bumper opening, first nip and clear deck must overlap at entry. The raised roller assembly also needs clearance from the central scoring frame.","service_and_failure_modes":"After front impact, test both sides and the center with a loaded note. Inspect release hardware and roller alignment as distinct checks.","unknowns":"Exact segmentation and spring arrangement, wall pickup envelope and as-built change details.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]}

title: 2024-2075 Transfer and scoring pivot
text: {"name":"Transfer and scoring pivot","construction":"A tall panel with a transverse roller at its foot is visible below opposing large launcher wheels. Close-ups show lateral sprocket and chain hardware.","operation":"The upper assembly changes pitch relative to the chassis. The team reported a dedicated shuttling mode and automatic pickup.","team_rationale":"Team update records the functions. The reason for two-sided drive and any protected feedback transmission still needs primary confirmation.","engineering_analysis":"A two-sided support can resist twist only if the frame remains square and transmission loads stay balanced. A narrow beam condition can confirm occupancy while missing a skewed rim.","interfaces":"Lower pickup must hand off across the base of the panel. Pivot position governs the launch direction and alters adjacent clearances.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for side-to-side lash and clear-deck interference at loaded angle limits. Recheck sensing after chain tension changes.","unknowns":"Feeder timing, shot settings and exact pivot motor and encoder topology.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]}

title: 2024-2075 Climb, Trap and controls
text: {"name":"Climb, Trap and controls","construction":"Visible upright structure and a field segment with the chassis suspended. Team reported a complete climb redesign plus LED and LL3G changes.","operation":"Michigan state results demonstrate repeated Trap use as reported by the team. The team tuned pickup and localization before that event.","team_rationale":"The update gives timing and capability changes but does not specify why each climb part was replaced.","engineering_analysis":"A stable chain-supported pose is required for a repeatable Trap delivery. Success counts do not isolate hook engagement from note delivery failures.","interfaces":"The suspended base, scoring structure and Trap opening must line up under load. Vision and feedback changes affect acquisition and approach independently.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check hook capture and Trap placement separately. A Kentwood roboRIO failure required replacement; the post does not establish its cause.","unknowns":"Actuator, hook linkage, shared pivot load path and measured Trap repeatability by failure category.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/5","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/7","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2075-enigma-robotics-presents-masquerade/456972/8","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DEHi3v9PK90"]}

title: 2024-2974 Protected intake and transfer
text: {"name":"Protected intake and transfer","construction":"Carbon-fiber rollers with end adapters, 1/4-inch polycarbonate side plates and later replaceable guide pieces. Curved guide and dedicated NEO-powered upper conveyor roller.","operation":"The roller captures off-center notes and the driven curved transfer lifts the note into the shooter throat.","team_rationale":"Wide capture let drivers collect without slowing for precise alignment. The longer PVC/tubing conveyor was slower and marked notes in prototyping.","engineering_analysis":"A short handoff reduces residence time but amplifies interference between the roller drive, guide supports and launcher cross members.","interfaces":"An added shooter brace collided with the earlier power-transfer belt path, so the team installed a dedicated conveyor motor above the intake. The cover above the front assembly protected the path from notes and wheel contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"A crowned pulley free-spun as the polybelt overheated; timing drive and additional axle support replaced it. Keep a complete spare intake and inspect bent frame stock, side plates and bumper brackets after contact.","unknowns":"Final roller gap under impact and event-specific guide dimensions.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/15","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/18","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21"]}

title: 2024-2974 Shooter, pivot and sensing
text: {"name":"Shooter, pivot and sensing","construction":"Carbon-roller top/bottom shooter with grip treatment and guides; pivot transmission with external CANCoder, hard stops and a friction damper added around the lower axle.","operation":"The sensors stage the note out of the accelerating nip; wheel spin-up and physical pivot settling precede feeding. Team later logged request-to-exit time.","team_rationale":"The first flywheel layout lacked desired velocity. A tread-loaded damper reduced the seconds spent waiting for the pivot to settle. The 125:1 to 100:1 ratio change targeted faster motion.","engineering_analysis":"A high-resolution motor trace is only an indirect angle estimate when compliant transmission stages can slip. Compare it with the output sensor while loaded.","interfaces":"The shooter base, bottom transfer roller, front swerve modules and pivot shaft occupy intersecting service paths. Access holes reduced the amount of hardware removed to extract the lower axle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tension at both sides, matching stop heights and encoder agreement. Noisy bearings were found during a District Championship ops check.","unknowns":"Final loaded-angle repeatability, full current draw, and exact World Championship shot calibration.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/15","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/27","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/28","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/32"]}

title: 2024-2974 Winch and Trap development
text: {"name":"Winch and Trap development","construction":"Team built a winch module and reported changing hook guides and materials in development. A shooter-mounted two-pivot door opener with rotary servo release was reported in April testing.","operation":"The winch was tested on the defense base. Door-opening tests subsequently used a fully climbed, stabilized setup to obtain initial shot angles.","team_rationale":"Planar polycarbonate guides were selected to stabilize hook travel relative to rods; a second door pivot provided needed reach.","engineering_analysis":"Loaded suspension pose determines the door contact location and release angle. Bench-stabilized shots omit swing and chain compliance.","interfaces":"Mini PC and panel clearance affect installation of the winch; Trap requires door pressure, stable chassis pose and a viable shooter angle at once.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hook support material, module insertion clearance and release function as separate checks.","unknowns":"Exact event installation and competitive Trap outcomes remain open.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/21","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/27","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2974-walton-robotics-build-blog-2024/452466/28"]}

title: 2024-359 Arm-end collector and note guide
text: {"name":"Arm-end collector and note guide","construction":"Two prominent full-width tubular rollers, clear guide surfaces and side plates; the orange ring is visible across the roller opening.","operation":"Low arm poses bring the roller opening to the carpet. The guide and rollers support the ring until the opposing wheel rows can take it.","team_rationale":"The team reveal demonstrates several uses of the head. The specific reason for avoiding a separate Amp handoff remains a prior interview lead.","engineering_analysis":"Retention depends on contact continuity as the arm accelerates. A guide wide enough for acquisition must still prevent the ring from migrating into one-sided launch contact.","interfaces":"Collector rollers and guide lead into the flywheel opening on the moving head. Their relative alignment must survive head motion and impacts.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide mounting and roller-to-roller gap after floor contact, then test note retention with the head sweeping through its normal pitch range.","unknowns":"Driven versus passive roller assignments, compression and detection sensors.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]}

title: 2024-359 Launcher and moving arm
text: {"name":"Launcher and moving arm","construction":"The top/bottom wheel rows have visibly unequal lateral wheel coverage. Nested members and shoulder sprockets are visible in the interview images.","operation":"Shoulder motion changes presentation angle. The arm also reaches farther in the practice scoring poses than in the floor pose.","team_rationale":"Team credits 2910 broadly. The claimed choice to eliminate an extension stage awaits a readable primary account.","engineering_analysis":"A longer reach increases leverage on the shoulder and magnifies angular play at the outlet. Unequal wheel coverage may affect spin and lateral sensitivity, but the intended effect was not established here.","interfaces":"Shoulder transmission, sliding members and end assembly all contribute to exit position. Route the head harness for the combined angular and extension limits.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check shoulder play under load, cable strain near the nested members and contact symmetry on a centered note.","unknowns":"Actuators, reeving, travel, launch settings and whether or how wheel spin was tuned.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2024-robot-reveal/455664","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]}

title: 2024-359 Drivebase and Stage interface
text: {"name":"Drivebase and Stage interface","construction":"Low rectangular base with corner module hardware, upright structure and protruding endgame hardware visible in practice.","operation":"Reveal frames around the Stage show a raised head and the base lifted off the floor during the same montage.","team_rationale":"No chain-load rationale established by the reviewed text.","engineering_analysis":"A repeatable suspended pose matters because the Trap opening fixes the outlet location independently of robot coordinate zero.","interfaces":"Chain engagement and chassis reaction determine reach to the opening. A note can remain in the head while this geometry changes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the suspension contact and arm position after a skewed engagement before judging placement consistency.","unknowns":"Module variant, chain attachment load path and field alignment logic.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_hxATpue968","https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0QAU0Ql9xy4"]}

title: 2024-368 Chassis, bumpers and acquisition
text: {"name":"Chassis, bumpers and acquisition","construction":"31.5 by 26 inch frame with Falcon SDS L4 and black neoprene. One 1.5-inch collector roller uses silicone tubing and modified flex wheels. Passive rollers center the note.","operation":"Floor pickup threads the note under the bumper, then passive guidance brings it into the feeder corridor.","team_rationale":"Team selected the protected layout to limit driving damage and passive centering for quick feeding. It strengthened the front after stage contact.","engineering_analysis":"The bumper protects the roller from direct horizontal contact only where its deflection and the obstacle geometry leave clearance. Test a low oblique impact as well as head-on driving.","interfaces":"Floor and bumper gap determine ring entry, while collector support stiffness maintains alignment to the passive guide and feeder.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the front-end support and bumper fit after a stage hit. Test pickup with an off-center ring before returning it to play.","unknowns":"Actual entry opening and front-end material changes between events.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/11"]}

title: 2024-368 Feeder and Amp/Trap elevator
text: {"name":"Feeder and Amp/Trap elevator","construction":"Three 1.25-inch rollers wrapped with self-fusing electrical tape, side precompression rollers and a double-stage extrusion elevator.","operation":"The feeder guides a note toward Speaker launch and can present and eject it for Amp or Trap.","team_rationale":"Team attributes the side rollers to precompressing the note for the shooter. The spec sheet identifies the feeder as the Amp and Trap scorer.","engineering_analysis":"The note changes support and width at the shooter mouth. Variable precompression may shift the first wheel engagement to one side, changing spin or yaw.","interfaces":"Feeder exit must overlap the shooter inlet at the transfer pose, and the elevated outlet must clear the respective scoring lip.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tape wear and extrusion alignment, then test the handoff at both loaded and unloaded extension positions.","unknowns":"Elevator drive, extension, sensor layout and note routing timing.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1"]}

title: 2024-368 Pivoting Speaker shooter
text: {"name":"Pivoting Speaker shooter","construction":"3-inch Colsons in a 3–1 lateral split, dual Falcons with 1.67× speed increase, 10 DP rack. Team lists 0.5 inch compression and 2 inches of side compression.","operation":"Automatic ranging selects a shot using the pivot and launcher. The documented range extends from bumper to wing line.","team_rationale":"The asymmetric wheel contact intentionally imparts spin for shot stability. The second motor and higher speed targeted a better wing-line shot, especially in auto.","engineering_analysis":"A spin-inducing offset is only repeatable if the feeder stages the note laterally. Motor count and speed alone cannot establish dispersion.","interfaces":"Rack stiffness and support affect release elevation; pivot movement also acts on the climber ratchet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rack play and tooth contact after endgame loading. Compare left/right rim wear after an extended shot test.","unknowns":"Shot map, sensor feedback and rack mesh adjustment procedure.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/6"]}

title: 2024-368 Independent climbers and reaction bar
text: {"name":"Independent climbers and reaction bar","construction":"Falcon on each side with 18.75:1 reduction, UHMWPE rope on a 1.5-inch-diameter pulley, ratchet actuated by shooter pivot and delayed reaction-bar deployment.","operation":"Team describes automatic alignment and Trap sequencing, with hook predeployment and later reaction bar timing.","team_rationale":"Delay and higher speed were pursued to shorten climb and Trap cycle time.","engineering_analysis":"Hook load asymmetry can roll the suspended robot and shift the feeder away from its target despite correct extension.","interfaces":"Chain, hook, rope pulley, ratchet and reaction bar define the suspended pose while the feeder presents the note.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope winding and ratchet engagement individually, including off-center chain contact.","unknowns":"Ratchet phase, reaction bar timing and event-level Trap timings.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-kika-mana-368-2024-robot/460883/3"]}

title: 2024-9483 Collector and transfer
text: {"name":"Collector and transfer","construction":"Several transverse rollers are visible in the upper assembly; the pit image exposes clear side material and a white transverse roller near the note.","operation":"Visible contacts give the ring successive surfaces along its width.
