Its direction through them and which are driven are unresolved in the stills.","team_rationale":"No collector design rationale in the reviewed team season text.","engineering_analysis":"Spanning the note width gives room for an off-center capture, but a flexible ring can cock if one rim reaches the next nip first. Compression should be measured with the arm loaded.","interfaces":"Outer roller to inner roller, then the clear guide and the launcher throat; guide edge height controls whether the leading rim dives below the next contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide edges and roller traction after impacts. Witness marks on one guide wall can reveal a biased feed before it becomes a jam.","unknowns":"Roller count, material, deployment geometry and drive routing from the old synopsis remain unconfirmed.","source_urls":["https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg"]}

title: 2024-9483 Launcher and angular positioning
text: {"name":"Launcher and angular positioning","construction":"Two conspicuous upper/lower shafts carry paired, thick, textured contact bands. Side drive elements are visible beside the roller assembly.","operation":"An opposing contact pair can compress and accelerate a ring. The side transmission is visible, but exact rotation direction and assignment of each drive element remain unknown.","team_rationale":"The reviewed primary photo supplies geometry only.","engineering_analysis":"A split left/right contact surface can feed a flexible ring asymmetrically if it is off center; check exit yaw and speed at multiple lateral offsets before adjusting a range map.","interfaces":"The upstream note position defines first contact; the frame-side transmission and its supports define how repeatably the exit direction can be held.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare physical release direction with commanded angle after side transmission service, especially at opposite ends of travel.","unknowns":"Pivot range, feedback, wheel speeds, and ready-to-fire logic require primary verification.","source_urls":["https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg"]}

title: 2024-9483 Base and endgame packaging
text: {"name":"Base and endgame packaging","construction":"The portrait shows front corner drive hardware below the roller frame, inclined supports and two upright side structures.","operation":"Drive hardware carries the moving upper assembly. Endgame engagement sequence is unresolved by these sources.","team_rationale":"No endgame rationale in the reviewed team publication.","engineering_analysis":"Pitch and chassis roll alter the world-space exit angle and would also change the approach of a chain hook.","interfaces":"Corner modules, upright bases and the swing envelope share the same bounded chassis volume.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bumper access and wiring strain after moving the upper structure through its full travel.","unknowns":"A one-shot ratchet is a corpus lead only; its load path, reset and release are unverified.","source_urls":["https://www.frc9483.com/robots","https://www.frc9483.com/img/snapfire.png","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9fc1bf7d9f026a0e88e392e040a4a97e95d9172.jpeg"]}

title: 2025-111 Direct-handoff floor intake
text: {"name":"Direct-handoff floor intake","construction":"Asymmetric compliant polycarbonate flaps, bottom roller, and spring-loaded floating leading roller pivoting about the middle shaft. Separate drive groups support L1.","operation":"Bottom contact lifts awkward orientations and the floating roller opens the throat. Flaps guide the piece into the existing gripper. Rear feed waits on receiver readiness.","team_rationale":"Small station funnel and skilled human-player loading made rerouting under defense hard. Team selected an intake that preserved the arm.","engineering_analysis":"Break bilateral symmetry to move a crosswise pipe away from a stable jam. Validate the acceptance map with skew and edge entry.","interfaces":"Leading roller clearance, gripper readiness, and shared climb sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team added bearing hats and wheel spacers after bearings escaped and wheels migrated. Check flank compliance and shaft fit after contact.","unknowns":"Final roller preload and stage-specific collection rates.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716/331","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]}

title: 2025-111 Elevator arm and two tools
text: {"name":"Elevator arm and two tools","construction":"Two-stage lift with separate coral roller gripper and algae claw. V5 coral tool uses aluminum gears and recessed wheels; later algae sensing uses LaserCAN.","operation":"Select arm and lift poses for source, reef and algae. The 6.5-inch tool center spacing was chosen to combine algae removal and branch placement from one drive pose.","team_rationale":"Team abandoned pass-through complexity. Later it adjusted algae compression and reduction after high holding current and unreliable seating.","engineering_analysis":"The hybrid cycle depends on bumper standoff, tool registration and algae compression at the same pose.","interfaces":"Funnel and ground feed converge on one coral tool. The algae load acts off the coral centerline.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch stripped pulleys, off-center algae pickup and gear impacts from the coral. Recheck claw compression after wheel swaps.","unknowns":"Full elevator rigging and final algae-contact stack across events.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716/139","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=13","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]}

title: 2025-111 Lightweight cage climb
text: {"name":"Lightweight cage climb","construction":"Redesigned climb uses Spectra bracing tied to frame rails, a 1 by 1 structural member and a single-bar grabber. Team reinforced or replaced composite pieces with aluminum.","operation":"Capture cage and pivot to lift. Intake moves to its climb position once the superstructure reaches its prerequisite pose.","team_rationale":"Old climb and added intake exceeded mass allowance together. Single-bar grabber reduced mass and eased alignment.","engineering_analysis":"Beyond 90 degrees the load reverses in affected pieces. A part sized for tension can buckle in compression.","interfaces":"Brace to frame rails, cage to grabber and intake stow to climb sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect brace anchors, compressed parts and capture alignment after overload.","unknowns":"Final reduction and power-off retention details.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2025/477716?page=19","https://github.com/wildstang/2025_111_robot_software/tree/4cb46cedf183a41e9f00d44f76bebf23d385d195"]}

title: 2025-1771 Continuous elevator and dual-axis carriage
text: {"name":"Continuous elevator and dual-axis carriage","construction":"Two-stage continuous elevator inspired by 4414's 2023 lift, carrying a pivot and separate wrist.","operation":"The pivot alternates between floor handoff and station angles, including station approaches from either side. Wrist sets the L1 shelf angle.","team_rationale":"The team targeted quick L1 and all coral levels, floor and station supply, and shorter or less predictable approaches under defense.","engineering_analysis":"An additional axis can recover release geometry lost to short lift stroke. It also raises the number of intermediate poses that need clearance and overshoot testing.","interfaces":"Lift height controls cross-brace clearance. Pivot and wrist determine both the receiving pose at handoff and placement pitch at L1.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck homing, mechanical stops and clearance on every allowed transition after a carriage impact or motor replacement.","unknowns":"Lift reeving, motors, reductions, mass and path coordinates.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]}

title: 2025-1771 Shared roller claw and centering
text: {"name":"Shared roller claw and centering","construction":"Passive opening against surgical tubing, upper pull-in rollers, a transverse positioning wheel and two CANrange sensors.","operation":"Pull coral into the claw. Jog the tube toward dual detection, or deliberately shift it back for the L4 route. The claw can open around algae and retain it under elastic preload.","team_rationale":"The team wanted repeatable tube placement at release and explained that L4 needed an approach around the corner with its available lift height.","engineering_analysis":"Two binary observations can define an acceptance window without estimating continuous tube position. Their overlap must survive range thresholds, tube skew and changing grip force.","interfaces":"Upper rollers accept both station feeds and floor handoff. The piece position couples directly to the collision margin at L4.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for stretched tubing, seized positioning rollers, and a sensor stuck on or off. Test a timeout or manual recovery if dual detection never occurs.","unknowns":"Roller diameters, tubing preload, sensor thresholds and exact L4 offset.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]}

title: 2025-1771 Transition and reef-state controls
text: {"name":"Transition and reef-state controls","construction":"Allowed-state graph for the mechanism and a reef occupancy dashboard with operator entry and automatic tracking of robot actions.","operation":"The graph routes tested moves. The dashboard can mark coral placement and removed algae and use a selected goal to choose the next target.","team_rationale":"The team wanted to reduce target-selection time on short cycles and switch between ranking-point and playoff priorities.","engineering_analysis":"Mechanical pose safety and scoring intent are separate state problems. A failed score or partner action can invalidate the dashboard even when the motion graph remains correct.","interfaces":"The target policy requests a pose and alignment, while the mechanism graph governs how the robot reaches it.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check behavior after an interrupted transition and after a failed score gets credited to occupancy. The interview included a dashboard restart, with no root cause given.","unknowns":"Fallback logic, position tolerances, homing recovery, and how driver overrides were implemented.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W807-oy25U"]}

title: 2025-180 Floor acquisition and coral registration
text: {"name":"Floor acquisition and coral registration","construction":"Pivoted intake with separate bottom-roller command, LaserCan, driven indexer and three discrete inputs on the arm tool.","operation":"Gate the transfer on receiver pose, stage at the arm, and suppress coral deployment while a piece is entering. The arm also has passive indexing as a default command.","team_rationale":"The team described coordinating many subsystems centrally for one driver. Haptic feedback tells the driver when floor coral is acquired.","engineering_analysis":"The intake sensor can justify driving away from the pickup sooner than arm staging alone. Keep downstream release gated separately so an intake detection cannot be mistaken for a scoring-ready piece.","interfaces":"Intake sensor to autonomous transition, indexer to arm, and receiving height and angle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test out-of-order sensor events, stalled transfer and damage to the bottom-roller mount. Rumble reports software state and should be checked against physical possession.","unknowns":"Roller contact geometry, material, preload and station funnel geometry.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]}

title: 2025-180 Scoring and dynamic alignment
text: {"name":"Scoring and dynamic alignment","construction":"Elevator, arm pivot, coral and algae drive channels, and camera-based target selection. Algae tool I/O includes a CANrange.","operation":"Branch and level input select a reef target. Auto combines pose-based travel to a seen floor piece with separate scoring and intake triggers. PathPlanner retains the curved exit from the first score.","team_rationale":"Most moves were straight or depended on observed piece positions. The team used simulation to reuse behavior across teleop and auto and used field time to refine vision and auto-align.","engineering_analysis":"Target-dependent motion cuts dead travel if detection is timely. Occlusion and erroneous detection can erase that gain, so test with clutter and partially visible reef tags.","interfaces":"Camera to drivetrain target, drivetrain tolerance to scoring, and lift and pivot release geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check for alignment timeouts, camera dropout and interrupted scoring reset. Team reports pulsed rumble for slow alignment and separate completion feedback.","unknowns":"Field-calibrated pose tolerances across events, mechanical lift rigging and tool dimensions.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]}

title: 2025-180 Cage capture and lift
text: {"name":"Cage capture and lift","construction":"Separate Talon FX outputs for winch and grabber, absolute position feedback and two digital inputs.","operation":"Deployment advances to a position threshold. In deployed state the grabber runs until both sensors have tripped and cleared. A separate driver command winches toward the climb limit.","team_rationale":"The team used distinct rumbles for deployed and latched conditions because the mechanism is difficult to see from the driver station.","engineering_analysis":"Two completed sensor transitions can distinguish entry from settled engagement. Confirm that a skewed cage or bounce cannot produce the same sequence with poor retention.","interfaces":"Grabber inputs to capture confirmation, winch feedback to travel limit, and climb pose to arm and floor-intake clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sensor sequence, mount alignment and load holding after disable, which motor neutral mode alone cannot establish.","unknowns":"Physical hook and retention geometry, winch reeving, cage load path and proof test.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc180/2025-public/tree/258ad38164b5cbfba7371a3dbdca83b448f1151c","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-180-s-p-a-m-2025-code-release/501667"]}

title: 2025-190 Station funnel and coral release
text: {"name":"Station funnel and coral release","construction":"Belts in the closing funnel, an Allen-Bradley photoelectric sensor identified in discussion, and star wheels at the V2 outtake.","operation":"Guide the coral, close for transport or temporary storage, and transfer to the scoring tool. The star wheel lifts the pipe lip on exit.","team_rationale":"The same funnel motion was already needed for climb clearance. The star wheels helped when the release tool was slightly too low.","engineering_analysis":"A hard reference upstream can stabilize release. A soft capture envelope is still needed if a misaligned pipe reaches a closing funnel.","interfaces":"Funnel-to-tool feed, retracted intake as hard stop, and reef branch contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check asymmetric closure, sensor visibility and star wheel wear after repeated mis-height releases.","unknowns":"Belt ratios, sensor thresholds and full control sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/10"]}

title: 2025-190 Elevator and algae mechanisms
text: {"name":"Elevator and algae mechanisms","construction":"Four lift motors. Floor algae intake uses a synchronized rack and pinion with a belted 3:1 reduction from an X44. The revised claw uses a deeper C, X60 roller power and an extra grip-taped tube.","operation":"The intake extends for algae and retracts as a stop. The extension motor current can indicate that a coral has reached the stop. Claw pressure and driven rollers retain and move algae.","team_rationale":"Six lift motors offered an estimated 20 ms benefit. The linear intake met stop, camera and weight constraints. The claw needed greater holding torque.","engineering_analysis":"The intake's two jobs make its retracted position a scoring datum. Treat current rise as an indirect measurement, which a bind or crash may mimic.","interfaces":"Shared intake stop and coral tool, cross-shaft and two racks, camera clearance, and claw belt engagement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports plate fractures from collisions and rapid stops, and printed idlers to address belt skipping. Inspect synchronized travel and replace damaged plates before recalibrating the stop.","unknowns":"Control thresholds, claw reductions, field release poses and stage rigging.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/10"]}

title: 2025-190 Rope grapple climber
text: {"name":"Rope grapple climber","construction":"40 lb rated pulling gas spring, spool-gear release bearing, deployed-arm lock, redirect pulley and five-bar over-center grapple coupling.","operation":"Reel to release the arm, let the lock seat, then take up slack until line tension frees the grapple from the stow blocks. Guides route load into the surrounding plates.","team_rationale":"Magnets failed to hold through the deployment shock. The redirect controls fleet angle and helps the grapple rise within the cage under tension.","engineering_analysis":"Deployment and hoisting have distinct load paths. Repeatable slack stow is needed to avoid triggering grapple release before arm deployment.","interfaces":"Funnel clearance, reel, guides, release coupling and frame attachment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope stacking and abrasion, release timing, and guide or lock wear. The team used button heads and guide blocks to reduce snagging and gear ingestion.","unknowns":"Winch reduction and ultimate and repeated load capacity.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/190-cad-release/503355/8"]}

title: 2025-359 Coral acquisition and wrist
text: {"name":"Coral acquisition and wrist","construction":"Arm-mounted pickup and belt-driven wrist. Team reports additional tensioners for the wrist belts.","operation":"Present the tool to the floor or feeder, retain the piece through arm motion and release at the reef.","team_rationale":"The team reported that angled floor coral was easier to grab and that incorrect wrist angle made acquisition harder.","engineering_analysis":"Pickup tolerance should be plotted against both tube angle and lateral offset. Driver translation may turn a missed entry into capture while lengthening the cycle.","interfaces":"Wrist position affects roller-to-carpet and tube-to-tool contact. Telescope and shoulder set the gross scoring pose.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt preload and wrist reference after nose strikes. The reported broadside miss is a real acquisition boundary.","unknowns":"Wheel spacing, sensor logic and station receiving geometry.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4"]}

title: 2025-359 Arm extension and chassis
text: {"name":"Arm extension and chassis","construction":"The 2910-derived mechanism retains an internal extension belt. 359 replaced the outer belt with chain using a WCP spline adapter for the pinion sprocket.","operation":"Shoulder and telescope carry the tool to branches, including L3 and L4. Team says it capped extension to roughly 50–60 percent power early to avoid slipping.","team_rationale":"Team attributes extension speed limits to longer reach and intake weight, and reports better operation after the chain retrofit.","engineering_analysis":"A slip that changes actual tool travel relative to feedback can appear as inconsistent placement. Positive drive can restore usable acceleration while introducing tension, lash and shock-load considerations.","interfaces":"Arm reaction feeds the base through the pivot. The wired tool moves with the telescope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Track chain tension, sprocket retention, stage synchronization and physical versus reported extension after a jam.","unknowns":"Reductions, hard stops and telescope sensor arrangement.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4"]}

title: 2025-359 Deep cage capture and moving wiring
text: {"name":"Deep cage capture and moving wiring","construction":"Early active hooks. Later 2910-assisted clamp inspired by 368, plus a wider IGUS carrier and printed guide where the added hardware crosses the carrier path.","operation":"Acquire the cage, then lift through the arm package. Team reported about 1.5 seconds from contact to deep climb in practice for the newer clamp.","team_rationale":"Team considered passive capture quicker but less dependable on a moving cage. Additional wiring needed wider carrier links.","engineering_analysis":"Test capture separately from proof loading and power-off holding. A missed cage and a lost load after contact have different remedies.","interfaces":"Cage load enters the arm and chassis. The assembly shares a moving clearance boundary with the cable guide.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guide wear, carrier snag points, cage engagement and positive load holding after service.","unknowns":"Exact latch geometry, retention under disable and event deployment timeline.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=4","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-team-359-2025-robot-pic-reveal/492663?page=3"]}

title: 2025-3663 Sideways lift and arm structure
text: {"name":"Sideways lift and arm structure","construction":"Elevator presented sideways with a pivoting arm mounted on its carriage. The interview identifies 2 by 2 aluminum on the arm.","operation":"The lift supplies height and the arm reaches past the lift to move between intake and scoring presentations.","team_rationale":"The team wanted pass-through-style access and judged passing through the elevator itself unsuitable. They also aimed for a low center of gravity.","engineering_analysis":"If the carried arm and piece load the carriage off center, check guide loading and wrist deflection at reach. The benefit depends on access around the upright throughout the motion, including with a loaded tool.","interfaces":"Carriage reacts arm loads, and lift height sets the clearance available for pivoting near the bellypan.","service_and_failure_modes":"After impact, compare the measured tip path to its taught path before commanding an aggressive low transition.","unknowns":"Stage count, carriage guides, reduction, motor placement and exact motion limits.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U"]}

title: 2025-3663 Wrist, grabber and scoring controls
text: {"name":"Wrist, grabber and scoring controls","construction":"Internal belts drive the wrist and grabber. The same tip handles coral and algae.","operation":"Present the tool for collection, keep the piece through the arm swing, then place it at the chosen target using the level-specific software pose and speed.","team_rationale":"External belts in early design were exposed to snagging on the reef. Software work emphasized avoiding robot and field collisions and placing pieces precisely.","engineering_analysis":"Enclosing transmission reduces exposure to reef contact and can complicate belt inspection. A protective tube only helps if the service route permits restoring belt tension and wrist zero repeatably.","interfaces":"The 2 by 2 arm is both structure and transmission enclosure. Wrist orientation and chassis approach determine release geometry together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect belt tracking and exits after contact. Exercise collision limits with a real coral and algae, since each enlarges the moving envelope differently.","unknowns":"Internal reduction, grabber contact materials, sensing, calibration and release settings.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U","https://www.cpr3663.com/cpr-blog"]}

title: 2025-3663 Deep cage latch
text: {"name":"Deep cage latch","construction":"Elevated pivot and latch that flips the cage; the final described holding method is drivetrain gearing within the climber, with a planned ratchet omitted.","operation":"Latch into the cage, rotate to move the suspended chain toward the robot middle and lower the scoring arm clear.","team_rationale":"Deep climb mattered for ranking points. CPR wanted a small package and designed around battery and elevator balance. The team reported gearing held long enough in its use.","engineering_analysis":"Measure the suspension point relative to the loaded center of mass. Small offsets change hanging angle and the loads on the latch and structure.","interfaces":"Climb rotation shares space with the arm. Battery location and mast mass influence hang attitude.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check gear backdrive after disable, with wear and the least favorable loading. Inspect cage pin and latch engagement after repeated off-center capture.","unknowns":"Gear reduction, latch actuation details and timed retention under varied loads.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lY_t0Ueh7U"]}

title: 2025-5990 Ground intake and handoff
text: {"name":"Ground intake and handoff","construction":"Two sets of compliant wheels, independent intake and funnel drive, folding polycarbonate and printed guides, and a pivot. Binder specifies three screws at the main plate-to-axis attachment.","operation":"Gearbox sets contact direction and speed. Sensors distinguish early contact, centered possession and gripper receipt. Loading retries briefly with different commands after the intake beam clears.","team_rationale":"Team sought rapid orientation, protected low motor placement and modular access.","engineering_analysis":"Measure centering time across initial angles and test obstruction with a second tube. A downstream beam going clear can mean travel or loss, so confirm with the receiving sensor.","interfaces":"Ground contacts to funnel, intake pivot to wrist, and wrist readiness to transfer at elevator rest.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check guide edges, wheel wear, pivot zero and recurring retries after impact.","unknowns":"Exact contact widths, material stiffness and jam rate.","source_urls":["https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vQDmuOuYko6tsqzaVRxMaeidCp3j22V8D6hehm5MjMr2mTX2qjtZM0GDTF_Q82WCff1eS-U3_bndLev/pub","https://github.com/Programming-TRIGON/RobotCode2025/tree/c4582360ce8200a7d76610bd5a825d532fa4b58d","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/trigon-5990-2025-robot-reveal-tridog/493284"]}

title: 2025-5990 Lift, wrist and algae add-on
text: {"name":"Lift, wrist and algae add-on","construction":"Two-stage rope lift with two motor channels, custom guide blocks, ratchet tension adjustment, and quick-swap printed overload pulley. Tight gear spacing and direct pulley at wrist. Algae add-on uses a custom rack and pinion.","operation":"Set lift and wrist for transfer, reef release, or algae removal and scoring. Code opens wrist for reef clearance during certain elevation moves.","team_rationale":"Team wanted low lash and straightforward rope service, and designed the sacrificial pulley to protect the lift.","engineering_analysis":"Rope stretch or tension imbalance can shift the handoff and scoring references. Validate where the sacrificial link fails and what restrains the carriage afterward.","interfaces":"Guide block tolerances, rope tension, wrist pitch and chassis pose all contribute to release accuracy.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope tracking, pulley damage, wrist lash and printed guides. Reverify rest pose after servicing the lift.","unknowns":"Load capacity, rope specification, proof testing and exact algae force.","source_urls":["https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vQDmuOuYko6tsqzaVRxMaeidCp3j22V8D6hehm5MjMr2mTX2qjtZM0GDTF_Q82WCff1eS-U3_bndLev/pub","https://github.com/Programming-TRIGON/RobotCode2025/tree/c4582360ce8200a7d76610bd5a825d532fa4b58d","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/trigon-5990-cad-release-2025-tridog/500664"]}

title: 2026-1114 Collector and folding kicker
text: {"name":"Collector and folding kicker","construction":"The main roller and kicker send fuel up into the hopper. The kicker retracts with linked hopper motion.","operation":"Deploy for acquisition. Retract the hopper to fold the kicker before crossing.","team_rationale":"The earlier kicker could drop and stay extended. The linked version addresses that route problem.","engineering_analysis":"A mechanical dependency avoids requiring a separately timed command. The design still needs hard stops and enough freedom to retract with debris or misalignment.","interfaces":"The folded kicker must clear the frame and loaded hopper. The collector can also become a contact point during recovery from an obstacle.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check partial stow after a hit and a stalled extension actuator. Look for a positive indication that the route envelope has been restored.","unknowns":"No exact linkage dimensions or clearance tolerance in the interview.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]}

title: 2026-1114 Hopper and powered floor
text: {"name":"Hopper and powered floor","construction":"Extending storage supplies a rolling floor with side agitators and passive contact elements.","operation":"Use agitation to move fuel out of side and rear dead spots and into the floor’s direction of travel.","team_rationale":"The team added passive rollers and high-grip surfaces after finding collection dead spots.","engineering_analysis":"The floor cannot pull fuel that is supported by its neighbors above the active contacts. Side agitation can destabilize a bridge while avoiding a steep drop or additional transfer.","interfaces":"Wall and floor positions must maintain a usable exit at all fill levels. A twisted belt drive couples motions and imposes belt routing constraints.","service_and_failure_modes":"Use a transparent mockup to locate stationary fuel during sustained output. Check belt tracking after impact and compare full with nearly empty behavior.","unknowns":"No measured live inventory or jam rate.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]}

title: 2026-1114 Up-feed and drum
text: {"name":"Up-feed and drum","construction":"A compliant-wheel feeder drives fuel into a belt-coupled rising roller path and drum launcher.","operation":"Capture the floor output, raise the stream and place fuel into the launch contact.","team_rationale":"Added grip helped drive fuel down into the feed entrance.","engineering_analysis":"The most consequential gap may be a transition before the shooter, even when the shooter has ample acceleration. The rise should control the piece rather than counting on the next roller to recover a bouncing feed.","interfaces":"The floor angle, feeder nip and rising path need matched speeds and overlapping control.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch for a stalled feed wheel under bulk pressure and whether reversing can clear the same path without backing the hopper up.","unknowns":"Exact shooter angle, reductions and current limits unresolved.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]}

title: 2026-1114 Driving and operator controls
text: {"name":"Driving and operator controls","construction":"The team describes multi-camera localization and intake states that change agitation behavior.","operation":"Stage the robot for scoring, signal readiness and use the known bump route with the hopper stowed as needed.","team_rationale":"The team selected the bump and a drum design for its expected traffic and preferred play.","engineering_analysis":"More inventory shifts the choice toward fewer trips. Driving around defense and aligning from a useful heading can still dominate the cycle.","interfaces":"Localization, vehicle heading and feed-ready logic determine whether a full mechanism produces a timely scoring burst.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a bad localization update, blocked route and beach recovery with a loaded bin.","unknowns":"No independent telemetry for shot pose, ready-state accuracy or route times.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ksvuenS2gGY"]}

title: 2026-125 Chassis around the dish
text: {"name":"Chassis around the dish","construction":"Wide front and tighter rear rails form a trapezoid around the circular fuel working volume. The rear modules are packaged around the dish.","operation":"Drive a low-profile route while leaving the center available for the serializer and launcher.","team_rationale":"The team selected the chassis shape to accommodate the enlarged dish.","engineering_analysis":"Draw the actual dish working diameter and wheel envelopes before comparing frame shapes. Chassis corners that appear unused can still carry bumper mounts, wiring, battery access or collision loads.","interfaces":"Frame rails must support the dish and leave enough room for module extraction.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether a wheel or module can be replaced without disturbing dish alignment. Inspect rear mounts after side impacts.","unknowns":"Exact tolerances and installed mass distribution were not measured.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]}

title: 2026-125 Four-bar collector
text: {"name":"Four-bar collector","construction":"Removable four-bar with a continuous roller and kicker geometry. The team describes a small set of shoulder bolts at the module interface.","operation":"Set the mouth low enough for fuel acquisition and carry fuel over the bumper into the dish.","team_rationale":"Earlier separated contact geometry jammed. The continuous roller reduces gaps in coverage.","engineering_analysis":"A broad mouth can collect more fuel per approach, but weak coverage near supports can make one edge the practical bottleneck. An accessible removal joint limits the cost of impact repairs.","interfaces":"The extended mouth and retracting bars must clear the bumper and keep the low travel profile.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare edge pickup and simultaneous arrivals, then inspect the mount after offset contacts.","unknowns":"No measured approach tolerance or durability trials.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]}

title: 2026-125 Rotating capture and up-feed
text: {"name":"Rotating capture and up-feed","construction":"A rotating dish and a separately driven central up-feed share an axis. Additional wheels address a center dead zone.","operation":"Move the pickup point to fuel around the dish and lift it in a single stream to the turret.","team_rationale":"The team kept the serializer for moving-shot flexibility and made the working dish larger.","engineering_analysis":"Independent speeds let the mechanism tune capture availability separately from the upward feed. A jam at the central intake can still starve a ready launcher.","interfaces":"The center outlet must deliver consistent piece position across dish orientations and turret motion.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure recovery from two pieces entering together and the fraction of fuel stranded near the center.","unknowns":"Team-reported working dish counts are configuration estimates. Bulk hopper capacity is a different quantity.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]}

title: 2026-125 Turret, hood and moving shot
text: {"name":"Turret, hood and moving shot","construction":"Inset yaw drive, multi-motor launcher and lowering hood. The team discusses interpolation and motion compensation.","operation":"Select range-based settings, move to target yaw and adjust the shot for the robot’s motion and flight time.","team_rationale":"The team chose the architecture to score or feed while moving around defense.","engineering_analysis":"Compare the fraction of usable field time when the robot can collect and shoot with an alternative that turns the chassis. The value of yaw freedom depends on maintained localization, shot readiness and a reliable single feed.","interfaces":"Hood lowering determines trench travel clearance. Cable limits constrain turret travel and where the scoring pose can resume.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify a missed camera update, a shot at a yaw limit and recovery after multiple fuel loads.","unknowns":"No independent accuracy map or matched comparison with a fixed shooter.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8"]}

title: 2026-1706 Intake and stow transition
text: {"name":"Intake and stow transition","construction":"Sloped plate between front intake and indexing region. Bumpers use formed 1/8-inch 5052-H32 backing stock with holes on a one-inch pattern, PE foam and a sewn cover.","operation":"The transition guides fuel out of the pinch region while the intake pulls in. Local foam displacement permits the mechanism to travel past the bumper edge.","team_rationale":"Fuel formerly lodged below the transition, dented the spindexer wall and prevented retraction. Iterating the plate substantially improved the behavior.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate stow with fuel deliberately left at the interface, including dented walls and aged foam. Clearance measured with an empty robot can miss this failure.","interfaces":"Intake plate to foam, mounting holes to edge, slope to spindexer wall.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect for a fresh witness mark or dent and check that repair foam has comparable compliance. The team’s alternative XPE was still under evaluation.","unknowns":"Plate angle, roller transmission and allowable interference.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1706-ratchet-rockers-2026-cad-release-mirage-champs-version/522276"]}

title: 2026-1706 Twin launch modules and turret services
text: {"name":"Twin launch modules and turret services","construction":"Two turret assemblies, dual CANcoders on each, and spring-retracted cable chains running through blue pulleys. Shooter drivetrain preserves distinct speeds and rotation directions for front and rear rollers.","operation":"The team describes residue-based angle reconstruction using the Chinese remainder method. The spring takes up returning cable carrier during rotation.","team_rationale":"Fit the complete path in a 12-inch A-bot cylinder while preserving the fuel path and speed relationships.","engineering_analysis":"The two angle signals extend the uniquely measurable range if their ratios and offsets are suitable. Offset consistency after service and cable reaction torque under motion matter to repeatability.","interfaces":"Fuel entrance to accelerator rollers, encoder gearing to azimuth estimate, and fixed wiring to moving carrier.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect cable tracking over full permitted travel and compare both raw absolute angles after a repair. Belt and shaft alignment were cited as possible contributors to B-bot behavior.","unknowns":"Encoder tooth counts, sensor reconciliation, cable travel limits and actual hood calibration.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1706-ratchet-rockers-2026-cad-release-mirage-champs-version/522276","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/522276/13"]}

title: 2026-1768 Four-bar intake and expandable hopper
text: {"name":"Four-bar intake and expandable hopper","construction":"Two two-inch polycarbonate rollers with silicone grip, static half-hex kicker bars, SRPP upper links, aluminum lower links and a MaxSpline jackshaft under the floor. Slides describe one X60 at 90:1 deploy reduction.","operation":"Cross-shaft and chains drive both sides. The lower links provide a repeatable hard stop and the hopper changes volume with deployment.","team_rationale":"Team optimized trench clearance while keeping the intake inside perimeter at start and leaving useful internal space.","engineering_analysis":"Flexible plates that survive impact may still move transmission centers enough to lose tooth engagement. A rigid load path across the transmission can be sized separately from the rest of the side plate.","interfaces":"Deploy shaft to links, kicker to bumper, moving wall to collector, roller motor to first roller.","service_and_failure_modes":"After Worlds a chain replaced a skipping motor belt. A thrown chain prompted polycarbonate flanges. Team suspected plate flex and poor wrap on a 12-tooth pulley. Roller-to-roller belt had no reported skipping.","unknowns":"Resolve upper-versus-lower hopper attachment wording by build version and measure belt-center displacement under torque.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]}

title: 2026-1768 Floor and entry
text: {"name":"Floor and entry","construction":"WCP stubs and custom plugs, three through-shafts of squish wheels, thin aluminum tube rollers with silicone, and shortened belt center distances by 0.030 inch. April entry had its own X60.","operation":"Floor conveys fuel toward the entry. Offseason revisions combined floor and entry drives, then increased floor speed as launch consistency improved.","team_rationale":"The team shortened centers to reduce current and tried spaced entry wheels to separate fuel into lanes.","engineering_analysis":"Speed increases shift load downstream. Compare full-width trajectories before increasing floor command, and log chain motion as well as average current.","interfaces":"Hopper to floor, floor rollers to compliant entry, entry to drum compression zone.","service_and_failure_modes":"The combined chain could contact itself in long operation. Confirm chain clearance with warmed hardware and accumulated slack.","unknowns":"Loaded current by version and whether all lanes feed equally at low fill.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]}

title: 2026-1768 Drum and hood
text: {"name":"Drum and hood","construction":"Four X60s drive a four-inch aluminum drum with CatTongue tape. Slides specify powered hood rollers, a roughly three-pound external steel flywheel, and a 20-DP printed hood rack flanked by aluminum plates.","operation":"The hood pivots under X44 power. A later ratio brought kicker surface speed closer to the drum. Team reports spinning up from zero for each shot.","team_rationale":"Flanking rack plates resist tooth shear. The team matched surfaces more closely to improve shot consistency and regarded continuous spin as poor value given inertia and kicker friction.","engineering_analysis":"Reducing surface speed mismatch can narrow launch variation, but fast feed and a lower-angle, higher-power shot can erode voltage headroom.","interfaces":"Entry release to drum, drum to hood contact, rack mesh to hood position, shared electrical supply to drivetrain.","service_and_failure_modes":"Offseason flywheel belt slack caused shredding and led to a sliding tensioner. Team reports late-match brownouts after faster tuning.","unknowns":"Onseason exit-speed distribution, power traces, hood angle map and initial versus final flywheel ratios.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-nashoba-robotics-2026-robot-reveal-nightshift/519386","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1768-2026-cad-release/525192","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/cSkTBJjJHHz68cz8b3rYZHDueja.pdf"]}

title: 2026-1987 Linear collector and chassis
text: {"name":"Linear collector and chassis","construction":"Polycarbonate intake structure, aluminum hub covers, large washers, silicone and grip-wrapped 1.125-inch rollers. X60 deploy at 3.6:1 and roller drive at 1.5:1. Four X2i modules and a polycarbonate skid.","operation":"Linear motion expands the hopper. Two rollers move fuel deeper and the chassis mounts carry impact load.","team_rationale":"Full width was chosen to gather five neutral-zone columns on the autonomous route. Covers spread collision loads.","engineering_analysis":"Test simultaneous arrival at several lateral positions. Reinforcement is most valuable if it preserves alignment of the moving collector and drive system.","interfaces":"Roller to hopper lip, collector to frame, and bumper-mounted hopper walls to service removal.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect hub covers, tube alignment and slider motion after contact. The skid and brainpan protect or organize the vulnerable underside.","unknowns":"As-played intake travel, measured acquisition rate by approach angle and long-term wear data.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://teambroncobots.com/robots/2026Robot/"]}

title: 2026-1987 Coaxial rotor and turret support
text: {"name":"Coaxial rotor and turret support","construction":"Wedge-shaped printed hook with aluminum reinforcement, separate X60 drives at 20.67:1 rotation and 1:1 feed, #25 chain and enclosed bevel gears. Five custom rings capture two seven-inch X-contact bearings around a six-inch bore.","operation":"Rotation sweeps fuel into the feed wheels. Reverse rotation helps clear jams. Independent moving assemblies share the support axis.","team_rationale":"Team wanted fast one-stream feed, a smaller hook footprint and an unobstructed route to the scorer.","engineering_analysis":"Concentricity is both structural and functional. Ring distortion or vertical stack error can tighten bearings or constrict the fuel path.","interfaces":"Hook to fuel pile, coaxial drive to feed, bearing stack and sprocket to turret, and bore to launcher inlet.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early hook climbed over fuel and broke. Two fuel could jam under low structure. Rotor mounts on a separate service plate.","unknowns":"Compression and tolerance stack as built, loaded drive current, and throughput at low fill and under acceleration.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1987-broncobots-2026-cad-code-resources-release/524348"]}

title: 2026-1987 Floating hood, aim and harness
text: {"name":"Floating hood, aim and harness","construction":"Dead-axle four-inch urethane wheel, two X60s at 1.25:1, X44 hood at 80.5:1 total, 10-pound constant-force spring and a through-bore hood encoder. Separate X60 powers one-inch backspin rollers. Chain-driven azimuth has matched encoder reduction.","operation":"Hood covers 0–90 degrees per book. Controller uses empirical flight times, velocity-vector compensation and gyro latency compensation. The harness moves through a tensioned underbody route.","team_rationale":"Spring takes up cycloidal backlash. Below-floor cable buffer preserves hopper space and limits exposure to fuel impacts.","engineering_analysis":"Repeatable angle requires preloading the correct flank and measuring the output. Cable friction can change azimuth load with direction.","interfaces":"Launcher to hood rollers, hood output to encoder, underfloor cable tensioner to rotating turret.","service_and_failure_modes":"Fixed PTFE-covered redirects added friction, and tight bend at the turret caused shop failures. Team ran spare CAN and power and kept a turret/harness spare.","unknowns":"Exact position limits and bend radii, matched calibration tables, and independently measured on-move accuracy.","source_urls":["https://teambroncobots.com/robots/Technical%20Books/Technical%20Book%202026.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1987-broncobots-2026-cad-code-resources-release/524348"]}

title: 2026-2046 Slapdown collector and hopper
text: {"name":"Slapdown collector and hopper","construction":"Two X44 deploy motors drive a sprocket and pivot arm on a stationary axle. Three dead-axle polycarbonate rollers use a one-side gearbox and belt train. Printed links couple the collector to the hopper extension.","operation":"Collector pivots down to pick up fuel and moves the hopper plate along slides. A net limits escape.","team_rationale":"The team picked a familiar simple deploy, iterated compression and added metal reinforcement at stub axles.","engineering_analysis":"A loaded hopper can increase deploy forces through the printed linkage and slider friction. Validate asymmetric hit recovery with a filled extension.","interfaces":"Pivot axle to arm, roller stubs to reinforced structure, linkage to slider, net to fuel envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt and stub retention after impacts, plus slider alignment and print cracking. Hopper detachment was a service objective.","unknowns":"Exact deployed and stowed margins, linkage force and net fatigue.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]}

title: 2026-2046 Staged floor and powered S-path
text: {"name":"Staged floor and powered S-path","construction":"Binder lists ten 1.25-inch horizontal tubes with silicone and CatTongue grip, 21:20 stages, two X44s, and two X60s on the compact S-curve superstructure.","operation":"Speed steps upward toward the exit. A backed transition actively draws fuel from the floor into the shooter.","team_rationale":"Rollers displaced a difficult belt bed. After DCMP the team added a floor motor to stay in a better efficiency band and increase usable speed.","engineering_analysis":"Motor count and bus draw can move in opposite directions when a loaded motor leaves its efficiency band. Evaluate energy across an entire burst.","interfaces":"Floor-to-S-curve roller traction and clearance, molded backing to drum entry, drivetrain and scoring shared battery.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early belt tension loaded axles and fuel could spin in place. Inspect roller grip, backing and timed accumulation at the intake to the S-curve.","unknowns":"Binder gives 1410 to 2297 RPM. Confirm the actual number of speed stages, including transition rollers, before recreating the ratio stack.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]}

title: 2026-2046 Drum, hood and aim
text: {"name":"Drum, hood and aim","construction":"Four-inch aluminum drum with grip tape. Passive printed hood backing and commanded angle from −10 to 60 degrees. The binder lists 3000 RPM.","operation":"Normal shots depend on chassis heading and hood selection. Negative angle enables the special reverse shot while pressed against the hub. Lookup-table trim is available to the operator.","team_rationale":"The team credits smooth backing with reducing unpredictable bounce and identifies idle speed oscillation as an early tuning issue without supplemental flywheel inertia.","engineering_analysis":"Measure loaded and idle response separately. The reverse shot is useful only where alignment and release conditions stay repeatable under contact.","interfaces":"Powered S-path to drum nip, hood setting to exit, localized pose to heading and lookup table.","service_and_failure_modes":"Monitor drum velocity recovery during a full burst and inspect backing wear for lane-dependent changes.","unknowns":"True field shot distribution, power traces, and controlled reverse-shot results.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YBlY312kMTiV29boVv6xRt87foDIU9lk/view","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2046-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2026/523823"]}

title: 2026-2481 Collector and pressure relief
text: {"name":"Collector and pressure relief","construction":"Three-inch grip-covered intake roller with two motors in the reported later setup. A plate limits fuel weight pressing directly on the intake.","operation":"Keep the intake running while fuel accumulates just inside the mouth.","team_rationale":"The team added the second motor after stall problems.","engineering_analysis":"Separate lack of available torque from an unfavorable contact load. A pressure barrier can prevent bulk inventory from continuously loading a roller intended to accelerate one layer at a time.","interfaces":"The roller opening must stay useful across a wide mouth while walls retract and extend.","service_and_failure_modes":"A pressure-relief feature can become a pinch point if fuel wedges under it. Test new and worn balls while pushing against a full bin.","unknowns":"Precise gaps, currents and endurance data are unresolved.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]}

title: 2026-2481 Expanding hopper and floor
text: {"name":"Expanding hopper and floor","construction":"Flexible side structure and a roller floor feed the four-wide launch section. The team revised wall support geometry.","operation":"Deploy the hopper for bulk collection. The floor presents lower fuel while the rest of the load settles.","team_rationale":"The team changed supports after racking and catches.","engineering_analysis":"More static volume gives diminishing returns if the added fuel bridges above the floor, spills during travel or takes longer than the active scoring window to clear.","interfaces":"The floor must coexist with electronics and route-clearance requirements. The stowed wall envelope sets bump clearance and access to the drivetrain.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure load retention over repeated crossings and examine where a bent wall first intrudes into the roller path.","unknowns":"The 115-fuel estimate is a source claim under unspecified packing conditions.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]}

title: 2026-2481 Four-wide launcher
text: {"name":"Four-wide launcher","construction":"Multiple accelerator contacts feed a wide launch assembly. A passive upper contact and electric hood actuation are described.","operation":"Build fuel speed over successive contacts, then launch at the selected angle and flywheel speed.","team_rationale":"The extra upper contact improved the entrance without adding a powered roller in that location.","engineering_analysis":"If launch contact force varies by lane, equal speed commands do not imply equal release speed or trajectory. Measure misses by lane and shooter speed recovery during a full burst.","interfaces":"The floor and shooter need equal flow across the width. A single loaded lane can reduce consistency even if the motor has ample total power.","service_and_failure_modes":"Bracket repairs and actuator changes show the value of replacing a high-load mounting point without rebuilding the floor.","unknowns":"Reported BPS lacks a confirmed measurement window and scoring conversion rate.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]}

title: 2026-2481 Loaded drivetrain and routes
text: {"name":"Loaded drivetrain and routes","construction":"The team describes custom adjustable-gearing swerve, large wheels and a chassis shaped to cross the bump.","operation":"Approach in the planned direction, climb the obstacle loaded and return to a scoring position.","team_rationale":"The team chose gearing for loaded current and the crossing rather than maximum possible speed.","engineering_analysis":"Compare the obstacle route with the alternative under realistic traffic. More fuel per trip can still lose if repeated turns, beaching or queueing consume the scoring window.","interfaces":"Drive tuning, fuel retention and the approach geometry are coupled. Electrical demand rises when the drivetrain and feeder operate together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test from a partially discharged battery and a poor entry angle. The team credited practice as well as mechanical changes.","unknowns":"No controlled timing across routes, configurations and driver practice levels.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc"]}

title: 2026-604 Independent intake and sliding hopper
text: {"name":"Independent intake and sliding hopper","construction":"Separate X44 deploy on each polycarbonate arm, belt-driven silicone-covered dead-axle rollers and TPU belt supports and pulley plugs. Laminated corrugated hopper has polycarbonate slot reinforcement.","operation":"Intake deployment pushes the hopper outward and surgical tubing retracts it. The single-deploy kicker uses an elastic drive and a string-retained, loosely fitted cross tube.","team_rationale":"Independent arms addressed chain failure on the linked 2024 design. The team wanted belt centers to recover after a hit and avoided a rigid through-bolt at the flexible tube.","engineering_analysis":"Decouple impact compliance from belt retention and hopper guidance. Confirm the mechanism still closes when either side takes an off-axis hit.","interfaces":"Deploy motors to arm travel, deflecting arm to belt support, kicker plugs to string, intake to hopper slide.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team reports TPU pulley tooth wear after one to two events and brittle PETG predecessors. Inspect the string, tooth roots and slot laminate together.","unknowns":"Deploy synchronization tolerances, force on slides and measured impact durability.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289"]}

title: 2026-604 Dynamic capture and column feed
text: {"name":"Dynamic capture and column feed","construction":"Split plywood bucket, separately motorized rotating scoop and upfeed, side omni rollers, printed ends and corrugated tube.","operation":"Code averages ten roller speed samples, divides modeled roller surface speed by 1.2 and converts to rotor command. After 0.3 seconds of detected jam it stops the rotor, commands unjam velocity and resumes after 0.1 seconds.","team_rationale":"Separate drives allow tuning while omni rollers reduce lateral forces. Split bucket preserves access.","engineering_analysis":"Following actual roller speed limits overdelivery during droop, but a jam downstream can leave fuel trapped above the detection point. Test with a fully packed column and minimum fill.","interfaces":"Scoop and bucket to roller, upfeed to tube, column to turret entry, and roller current and velocity to recovery state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Code logs target and actual velocities and jam state. Inspect tube ends for distortion, and correlate retries with current and column fill.","unknowns":"Compression, full-scale success rate, wear-driven threshold drift and event firmware parity.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/SerializerSubsystem.java"]}

title: 2026-604 Turret support and automated launch
text: {"name":"Turret support and automated launch","construction":"Segmented polycarbonate ring, aluminum gear, PETG spacers and lubricated slider. Camera localization uses four viewpoints and multi-tag observations.","operation":"The team gates serializer feed on launch speed, elevation and yaw tolerances plus recent tag evidence. The solver interpolates a distance table for scoring, then compensates for turret motion and chassis attitude.","team_rationale":"Small swept volume protects hopper flow. Offline trajectory selection reduces onboard computation and seeks launch pairs less sensitive to errors.","engineering_analysis":"Mechanical clearance and camera availability both affect firing duty cycle. Evaluate where ready-to-feed interruptions cluster before altering the table.","interfaces":"Overhead ring to rotating turret, tube to scorer, pose and velocity to aim, readiness to serializer enable.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect slider friction and play after contamination or spacer replacement. A camera view blocked by field geometry can interrupt the gate.","unknowns":"Loaded angle and speed errors, observed vision dropout and endgame hardware.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/SerializerSubsystem.java","https://github.com/frc604/2026-public/blob/5c050ac2b0370f65c5b349c592cde8b90af68323/FRC-2026/src/main/java/frc/quixlib/math/LaunchCalculator.java"]}

title: 2026-6329 Four-bar acquisition
text: {"name":"Four-bar acquisition","construction":"Four-bar with SRPP and polycarbonate at pivots, 3/8-inch spacers, SplineXL drive, and a 95A TPU connector at the polycarbonate kicker arm. Custom compliant wheels were cast from VytaFlex 30.","operation":"Front impact can fold the linkage, while long arms can flex laterally. The collector delivers into either the circular or wide storage architecture.","team_rationale":"The team expected frequent midfield impacts, knew this linkage family and could make it with available equipment.","engineering_analysis":"Design the load path and recovery motion together. Side bending can still shift shaft alignment or change the stowed envelope.","interfaces":"Four-bar pivot stack, collector-to-hopper opening, kicker tube to TPU connector.","service_and_failure_modes":"Older two-inch wheels walked along dead axle tubes. Team reports the cast wheels lasted about one event plus practice and would consider commercial wheels for longevity.","unknowns":"Exact contact loads, wheel retention dimensions, return behavior and clearance in impact deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/19"]}

title: 2026-6329 Roman I indexing and turret
text: {"name":"Roman I indexing and turret","construction":"20.75-inch outer drum, roughly six-inch center, polycarbonate and printed center construction, integrated spur gearbox and cantilevered uptake wheels. Printed turret pulley and bearing stack around 3/16-inch aluminum base.","operation":"Floor and center move fuel outward. The upkicker engages the fuel at the raised fixed bar and transfers it into the turret.","team_rationale":"Small center preserves space for fuel to drop into the spindexer. The team highlights service panels and low turret part count.","engineering_analysis":"Bulk agitation, bar height and uptake traction jointly determine whether an arriving item rises or stalls.","interfaces":"Rotating floor to bar and wheels, uptake to rotating turret, removable floor to electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check cantilever shaft deflection and bar clearance when replacing wheels. Team reports the turret bearing stack gave no issues.","unknowns":"Floor speed, wheel compression at the throat, turret launch settings and as-played current.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342"]}

title: 2026-6329 Roman II wide feed and drum
text: {"name":"Roman II wide feed and drum","construction":"Roller floor with flex wheels and grip tape, 47-tooth belts and one motor, with about 3:1 at the front roller and 2:1 elsewhere. Bolted, bent UHMW feed sheet and aluminum tube drum with drilled radial holes.","operation":"Double feed rollers guide fuel into the drum. A hood sector gear adjusts the launch geometry.","team_rationale":"Team chose rollers over concern a belt floor would sag under full load. Drill guides allowed drum work without a large lathe. Tape was repairable and available.","engineering_analysis":"The reductions can keep the single motor within a usable efficiency band. Verify this at full fill and when the front and downstream rollers load simultaneously.","interfaces":"Intake dead shaft to pivoting floor, feed pair to UHMW guide, guide to drum and adjustable hood.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tape cuts, belt tracking and guide retention. The floor pivot gives underfloor access without dismantling the feed train.","unknowns":"Matched loaded current, feed compression and widthwise shot variation.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-bucks-wrath-robot-reveal-2026-roman/515342","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515342/19"]}

title: 2026-7769 Rack collector
text: {"name":"Rack collector","construction":"Rack and pinion deploy the roller and share a cross shaft. The team describes a polycarbonate roller with a high-grip surface.","operation":"Deploy, drive through a fuel pile and return to the stowed route envelope.","team_rationale":"The team compared over-bumper and rack concepts before adopting the rack.","engineering_analysis":"A straight deployed path can preserve consistent pickup geometry. A rigid cross shaft constrains skew, while an offset defense hit can still create a concentrated tooth and bracket load.","interfaces":"Both rails need aligned supports and clearance through the hopper extension.","service_and_failure_modes":"Teeth broke under contact. The team spliced rack material when spares ran short. Check whether a loaded rack can still retract after an offset strike.","unknowns":"No measured impact load, backlash growth or deployed deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]}

title: 2026-7769 Hopper and belt floor
text: {"name":"Hopper and belt floor","construction":"Polycarbonate walls and a net top expand storage. A powered belt floor hinges for service.","operation":"Fuel collects in bulk before moving toward the feeder. The floor presents fuel even when the robot is stationary.","team_rationale":"The floor hinges to reach the electrical bay.","engineering_analysis":"A high capacity claim matters only for fuel that reaches the outlet. Compare the number acquired, retained over bumps and delivered within the active window.","interfaces":"Hinge and latches must keep the floor aligned with the feeder at both full and nearly empty loads.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test asymmetric loading and a deflected wall. Check wiring strain while the floor swings up.","unknowns":"The interview gives a nominal estimate around 65–70. A separate existing source reports lower typical capacity, and those conditions should stay distinct.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]}

title: 2026-7769 Feeder and shooter
text: {"name":"Feeder and shooter","construction":"Compliant wheels push fuel toward a fixed chassis-mounted launch assembly and shaped hood.","operation":"Bring the shooter up to speed, advance fuel through the contact zone and aim with the drivetrain.","team_rationale":"The team removed the partition after jams between the original two channels.","engineering_analysis":"The useful width is the open feed width through the narrowest transition. A small separation feature can create a bridge even if both downstream channels can individually launch at high rates.","interfaces":"The low belt outlet, compliant wheels and hood entrance need continuous support or positive control of the fuel.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test full hopper and last-fuel conditions. Record left or right starvation, stalls and recovery after rapid reversal.","unknowns":"No synchronized shot-by-shot speed recovery or lane throughput dataset.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]}

title: 2026-7769 Vision and climb
text: {"name":"Vision and climb","construction":"The team discusses multiple camera roles and front and side climb concepts.","operation":"Use localization for scoring and a separate camera role for climb alignment when installed.","team_rationale":"Two pose sources conflicted after a physical camera failure. The team reported leaving the side hook off in some circumstances.","engineering_analysis":"An optional mechanism earns its place through net match value after interference and setup. Low climb value alone does not explain a decision if the hardware also blocks the fuel path.","interfaces":"The front climb concept shared space with feed rollers. The side hook could interact with hopper netting.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check pose disagreement and whether an unused hook can snag storage walls when the robot is driven hard.","unknowns":"Exact competition installation and climb outcomes vary by event.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU"]}

title: 2026-9483 Collector and rack
text: {"name":"Collector and rack","construction":"Curved rack and pinion, front roller, kicker and articulating secondary kicker in the third intake.","operation":"Rack travel lowers the front roller for acquisition. The secondary kicker can move relative to the primary kicker.","team_rationale":"The team chose the curve to avoid an elevated inboard rack and preserve hopper capacity.","engineering_analysis":"The path links reach, bumper crossing and stowed intrusion. Impact deflection can change effective gear alignment and field clearance.","interfaces":"Rack to pinion support, intake-to-bumper clearance and final roller to hopper lip.","service_and_failure_modes":"The initial intake was troublesome. Check rack mesh and guide wear through deployment, especially after lateral impact.","unknowns":"Rack pitch radius, backing material, guide clearance and exact roller stack.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]}

title: 2026-9483 Spindexer and vertical indexer
text: {"name":"Spindexer and vertical indexer","construction":"Cone with spinning floor. One Kraken X44 powers each of the spindexer and vertical indexer.","operation":"Bulk circulation supplies a separately driven uptake. The robot clears occasional jams automatically.","team_rationale":"The team iterated ratios and feeder wheels within season time constraints. It reports no designed compression against the hopper walls.","engineering_analysis":"Cone circulation has to keep the pickup supplied without packing a bridge at its entry. Feeder grip and floor velocity are coupled even with independent drives.","interfaces":"Cone and floor to wall, floor to feeder wheels and feeder outlet to rotating scorer.","service_and_failure_modes":"Log failed feeds and recovery duration. The team reports seven or eight feeder-wheel changes and denies cone-to-shooter-corner jams in its account.","unknowns":"Wheel geometry, final ratio, throat compression, detection signal and retry sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]}

title: 2026-9483 Turret launcher and targeting
text: {"name":"Turret launcher and targeting","construction":"Three X44 flywheel motors, roughly half-pound three-inch printed wheel and one Thrifty Bot flywheel disc kit per team replies. No powered top roller. Camera has a nearby flood-pattern truck LED.","operation":"Empirically tuned tables and iterative physics jointly solve moving shots with spin compensation. The light fills close shadows.","team_rationale":"The light helped close-range tag observations where the net shadowed a tag. The team reports little long-range benefit.","engineering_analysis":"Supplemental inertia can reduce transient droop at the cost of slower setpoint changes. Characterize those effects separately from shot-model residuals.","interfaces":"Feeder exit to wheel compression, camera to pose estimate and pose/velocity to launch solution.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check printed-wheel balance and fastening after impacts. Measure tag availability with and without the light at representative poses.","unknowns":"Turret support, hood travel, total inertia and the solver inputs and gains.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-9483-presents-enigma/515383"]}

title: 2026-9496 Passive intake and hopper
text: {"name":"Passive intake and hopper","construction":"Two powered intake rollers, passively deployed collector, sliding hopper and retention net. The team reports using roller pulses while shooting.","operation":"Intake collects fuel and its roller direction can alternate for agitation. Hopper retention and exposure depend on deployed geometry.","team_rationale":"LYNK prioritized fewer active degrees of freedom while operating near its mass limit.","engineering_analysis":"Verify deployment from low traction and varying battery state. Measure whether pulsing recovers low-fill feed or interrupts entry pickup.","interfaces":"Rollers to hopper opening, deployment travel to stowed geometry, and collector extent to path and contact exposure.","service_and_failure_modes":"The team noted poor agitation and situations where it wanted to fold the intake. Check end stops, net tears and slide contamination.","unknowns":"Exact passive deployment sequence and slide construction, reset method and mass budget.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]}

title: 2026-9496 Roller floor and uptake
text: {"name":"Roller floor and uptake","construction":"Early build specified 7/8-inch tubes with 1/16-inch silicone, roughly 2.125-inch centers and ten-degree inclination. Two motors were tried on the floor after single-motor issues. Printed side guides narrow the path 0.85 inch per side.","operation":"Floor and indexer move fuel into the drum. The guides keep fuel away from pulleys. Team reported faster feed improved range spread.","team_rationale":"Removing the divider increased observed BPS. Team judged the wider path acceptable for accuracy in its tests.","engineering_analysis":"Electrical limits, loaded ratio and traction can masquerade as mechanical jams. Compare time to deliver at low and full fill using current and speed traces.","interfaces":"Floor to indexer compression, indexer to drum and side guides to pulleys.","service_and_failure_modes":"Early testing exposed low-voltage and current-limit sensitivity. Team used tape to enlarge a slightly loose idler and reported cracking at the CANcoder cover.","unknowns":"Final installed ratio, loaded current, definitive idler arrangement and late-season lane distribution.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]}

title: 2026-9496 Fixed drum and shot control
text: {"name":"Fixed drum and shot control","construction":"Four motors on one shaft, supplemental brass and steel flywheel masses in the early build, fixed hood, and PhotonVision on Orange Pi 5 with Arducam OV2311. Side camera supplements the front.","operation":"Pose estimate selects field-relative heading. Distance lookup with interpolation sets RPM. The team describes continuous corrections and a readiness gate before feed.","team_rationale":"Simplicity left tuning time for drum PIDF, heading control and calibrated distance. The driver can still aim from pose when a fresh hub view is briefly unavailable.","engineering_analysis":"A one-variable range map works only across its tested launch envelope. Pose drift, RPM recovery, or lane interaction can produce systematic misses.","interfaces":"Drivetrain yaw to shot line, floor enable to readiness, and front camera field of view to hopper load.","service_and_failure_modes":"Log loaded RPM droop, alignment errors and vision loss before changing calibration. The bumper kit also needed an internal latch after impact dismounts.","unknowns":"Final hood angle, inertia, deployed code and shot envelope by distance.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/lynk-9496-build-log-2026/511797","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/511797/144"]}

title: 2018-1678 Lemon Zest complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2018-1678","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.citruscircuits.org/2018-robot","title":"Citrus Circuits 2018 robot","locator":"Scoring, Drivetrain, Operating Interface, Electrical","review_basis":"Read full team page prose","facts":"Front or rear cube scoring, pneumatic gripping and climb deployment, wrist camera, and protected moving services.","limitations":"Retrospective overview lacks dated configurations and timed comparisons."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1678-citrus-circuits-2018-cad-release/166149","title":"Lemon Zest CAD release","locator":"Team posts 1, 3, 8, 12, 14","review_basis":"Read team announcement and replies","facts":"Later 1323-derived intake withheld. Team details ramp forming, hook latch, differential winding drums and printed supports.","limitations":"GrabCAD returned 403. Model geometry and photo dimensions were unavailable."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/blob/master/c2018/subsystems/score_subsystem/score_subsystem.cpp","title":"2018 scoring coordinator","locator":"BoundGoal; SetGoal; RunStateMachine, lines 21–41 and 90–247","review_basis":"Read team C++ source","facts":"Profiles estimate time to clearance. Low ground acquisition can trigger automatic stow. Front and rear scale goals are distinct.","limitations":"Public master code is a snapshot with no match deployment or clearance test evidence."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/blob/master/c2018/subsystems/climber/climber.cpp","title":"2018 climber controller","locator":"Climber::Update, lines 16–82","review_basis":"Read team C++ source","facts":"Separate commands expose approach, ramp deployment and powered climb states.","limitations":"Command outputs alone do not establish hook engagement feedback or holding behavior."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Lemon Zest combined a six-wheel drive, two-stage cascading elevator and rotating cube tool with a separate buddy climb. The chassis could keep its heading when the scale was behind it, while the driver still had to align the shot. Endgame changed the main load path from the wheels to a detachable hook and winch that also carried a partner on a ramp.","piece_flow":"The powered jaws capture and clasp a Power Cube. The coordinator distinguishes intake at a selected pose from ground intake followed by stow on possession. Front scoring raises the tool and runs its wheels outward. Rear scoring raises the wrist to clear the elevator structure, flips the held cube and ejects it behind the chassis.","packaging_and_motion":"A camera above the intake follows the moving tool. The linked conduit carries electrical and pneumatic services down the lift. The release distinguishes unreinforced Onyx elevator braces from carbon-fiber-reinforced printed ramp-pivot supports. The bumper mount bolts through an extrusion into chassis rivet nuts.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and alignment","construction":"Four Colson wheels, two front omnis and a two-speed gearbox per the team page.","operation":"Steering wheel and vertical joystick split heading and speed.","team_rationale":"Front omnis were chosen to improve turning.","engineering_analysis":"Measure turning benefit with the lift raised.
