The omni end changes lateral scrub and may reduce disturbance resistance.","interfaces":"Wheel encoders, bumper mounts, hook approach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect bumper fasteners and compare repeatability on worn omnis.","unknowns":"Loaded traction and acceleration by gear.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2018-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1678-citrus-circuits-2018-cad-release/166149"]},{"name":"Cube tool and lift","construction":"Pneumatic arms, powered wheels, a rotating wrist and two cascading stages.","operation":"The software floors the elevator goal when the wrist is beyond its safe angle and can defer wrist motion based on predicted arrival times.","team_rationale":"Team describes two-sided placement and camera-assisted acquisition.","engineering_analysis":"Validate the loaded cube envelope, conduit and stopping margin through the transition. A late lift or false possession signal can invalidate the planned motion.","interfaces":"Hall sensors, proximity sensing, release wheels, lift/wrist coordinator.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a skewed or partly held cube, slow lift and failed position reference.","unknowns":"Installed late-intake dimensions, clamp force and per-event settings.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2018-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1678-citrus-circuits-2018-cad-release/166149","https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/blob/master/c2018/subsystems/score_subsystem/score_subsystem.cpp"]},{"name":"Buddy climb","construction":"Detachable latched hook, ribbed formed sheet ramp and three cable contacts driven by unequal-diameter drums on one winch output.","operation":"Deploy and latch the hook, lower the ramp for a partner, then wind the ramp cable and two hook-side cables.","team_rationale":"Latch addressed rung slip. Drum diameters were chosen to synchronize different cable take-up requirements.","engineering_analysis":"Model winding radius as layers accumulate and evaluate an off-center partner. Hatch score sequences the backplate and flutes. Buddy mode enables separate winch outputs. Comment records removal of ground hatch intake.","limitations":"Static read of public master. Code contains branches for hardware absent from competition."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Buzz Lime-year coupled a fixed-plane pass-through lift and wrist with separate contact mechanisms for the two game pieces. Front or rear placement reduced the need to reverse heading on some routes. The scoring elevator also participated in endgame, with crawlers for the platform transition and deployable forks and winches in the buddy sequence.","piece_flow":"The station tool pilots through the hatch center, retains the disk for transport and releases it at the target. Code separates the retaining flutes from a backplate used in the scoring sequence. A cargo roller draws in the ball and uses reduced holding drive with possession detected. The coordinator can stow after cargo acquisition. Cargo and hatch follow separate contact paths into scoring poses.","packaging_and_motion":"Six wheels with omnis at both ends and three MiniCIMs per side support point turns. Printed combined electronics mounts preserve bellypan space, and conduit follows the moving lift. In the released flip routine, the lift is driven down and the wrist stays on its current side until clearance, with cargo deployment suppressed and the hatch backplate forced in. That direction of travel matters when comparing this design to the 2018 robot.","subsystems":[{"name":"Hatch and cargo acquisition","construction":"Arrowhead station tool with two double-acting cylinders and a separate powered cargo intake.","operation":"The arrowhead guides entry, then retention expands. Cargo feedback transitions intake toward holding.","team_rationale":"Fast station engagement and early cargo capture.","engineering_analysis":"Lead-in tolerance, secure retention and clean release need separate tests. Payload size changes clearance even with identical wrist angles.","interfaces":"Center hole, backplate, flutes, proximity feedback, cargo roller and elevator wrist.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test skewed panels, loose retention and a ball detected before fully seated.","unknowns":"Capture envelope, forces and failure rates.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2019-robot","https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/tree/master/c2019"]},{"name":"Pass-through elevator and wrist","construction":"Spectra cable with threaded looped-bolt tensioning, tube inserts and a Hall switch/magnet at the bottom.","operation":"The interface zeros the elevator encoder on first Hall detection. Profiled axes are coordinated by positional bounds.","team_rationale":"Provide two-sided placement and usable position references.","engineering_analysis":"Check the swept volume in both directions, including end-effector hardware and payload. A home reference alone cannot distinguish a slack line from stage binding.","interfaces":"Wrist, carriage, moving conduit and position signals.","service_and_failure_modes":"Provide access to cable terminations and test recovery from false zero or unequal cable tension.","unknowns":"Full cable reeving, loaded deflection and actual clearances.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2019-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1678-citrus-circuits-2019-cad-release/359101","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-1678-2019-code-release/357185","https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/tree/master/c2019"]},{"name":"HAB climb","construction":"Folded partner hardware, elevator, crawler outputs and independently commanded buddy winches in the release.","operation":"Climb commands coordinate lift height, gear and crawler deployment. Buddy mode enables fork deployment and independent winching.","team_rationale":"Team reports reaching HAB3 with two partners and says the elevator held that load without the contemplated brake.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate eccentric partner loading, platform contact, motor heating and holding through power loss before reusing a scoring elevator as a climber.","interfaces":"Partner geometry, HAB edge, drivetrain and operator sequencing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test partial docking and a stalled or mismatched winch.","unknowns":"Physical fork geometry, full climb chronology and success distribution.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2019-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1678-citrus-circuits-2019-cad-release/359101","https://github.com/frc1678/robot-code-public/tree/master/c2019"]}],"revisions":["CAD post 16 explicitly says the modeled elevator brake never reached the competition robot. Released brake commands do not override that statement.","The competition code retains ground-hatch and handoff logic, with a source comment explicitly saying the ground intake was removed before competition."],"transferable_principles":["Treat possession, retraction and measured axis clearance as prerequisites to a loaded flip."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Slow lowering or incompatible payloads can erase the heading advantage. Partner variability can erase the value of shared climb hardware."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. A compact traction chassis carries a yawing turret with a single-stage lift and pitch joints at shoulder and wrist. The team reserved endgame for its own HAB3 climb, leaving partners simpler tasks in qualification strategy. At Championship the elevator pulled against a suction-supported carriage instead of transmitting climb loads through the scoring arm.","piece_flow":"With the Championship jaws open, the top roller feeds floor cargo into horizontal compliant wheels for centering and retention. With jaws closed, those wheels engage the hatch center hole. The published state machine distinguishes disk and cargo capture and qualifies possession before changing state. The elevator and arm present the chosen piece to a rocket or cargo ship, with turret tracking assisting alignment.","packaging_and_motion":"The square chassis helps short turns and HAB coexistence. Yaw rotates the lift and arm together. A horizontal reverse-bend carrier routes services across the yaw joint, and the shoulder and wrist gearboxes sit together on the elevator carriage. The shorter Championship tool carries pieces inside the bumper perimeter during turret rotation, expanding usable approaches.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and alignment","construction":"Six-wheel dropped-center West Coast drive, 4-inch nitrile tread and two NEOs per side with two-speed gearboxes.","operation":"Low gear favors control and defense. High gear reduces travel time on longer legs.","team_rationale":"Accelerate between station and rocket and minimize HAB footprint.","engineering_analysis":"Measure time over complete short sprints including braking. Axle encoders remove upstream drivetrain play from measurement while still reporting wheel slip as motion.","interfaces":"Bumpers, HAB edge, front axle encoders and pose estimator.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tread and check carpet-direction odometry under load.","unknowns":"Loaded sprint and defense measurements.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/resources/Team_254_Tech_Binder_2019.pdf"]},{"name":"Scoring axes and planner","construction":"Double-supported turret, chain-driven elevator, shoulder and chain-driven wrist with gas spring counterbalance.","operation":"Vision can aim yaw. The released setpoint method applies tuck conditionally, with a separate direct-goal vision path.","team_rationale":"Coordinate four axes to save drive turns and fit inside the robot.","engineering_analysis":"Validate every mode transition with payload and stopping margin. Offboarding the wrist motor reduces distal inertia, but chain stretch changes angle accuracy.","interfaces":"Camera transforms, turret cable carrier, chain tension, tool and climb carriage.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test target loss, invalid calibration and cable clearance at yaw limits.","unknowns":"Measured timing and per-mode minimum clearance.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/resources/Team_254_Tech_Binder_2019.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2019-Public/tree/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2019"]},{"name":"Dual-piece tool","construction":"Polycarbonate pivoting jaws, top roller, compliant flex wheels and a cargo sensor.","operation":"One jaw position centers balls and the other uses the wheels to grip disk centers.","team_rationale":"Reduce moving mass and preserve shock tolerance.","engineering_analysis":"Check grip and release with worn wheels and mixed approach offsets. Compactness can still benefit a fixed-plane design even if it gains no yaw workspace.","interfaces":"Wrist, pneumatic cylinder, roller drives and detection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Watch for flex-wheel wear, jaw play and premature possession.","unknowns":"Force and compression ranges.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/resources/Team_254_Tech_Binder_2019.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2019-Public/tree/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2019"]},{"name":"Suction climb","construction":"Foam-sealed pad, pivot foot, over-center deployment, kickstand hooks and elevator ratchet.","operation":"Contact and pressure precede pulling the climber carriage down. The ratchet holds elevator position.","team_rationale":"Use the HAB edge while leaving platform area for partners.","engineering_analysis":"Pressure threshold and ratchet address different failures. The ratchet cannot preserve platform attachment if the pad peels or leaks.","interfaces":"Platform surface, vacuum check valve, carriage and elevator load path.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test contamination, edge offset, pressure loss and hook seating.","unknowns":"Seal margin and field reliability.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/resources/Team_254_Tech_Binder_2019.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2019-Public/tree/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2019"]}],"revisions":["Regional dual-roller intake, 16.5-inch arm and stinger became a 10.2-lb tool in place of 15.7 lb, a lighter 21-inch arm and suction climb. New geometry required inversion for the second-level rocket hatch and improved top cargo reach."],"transferable_principles":["Evaluate reach, moving mass, current and swept volume together when revising a scoring arm."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A fixed-plane electric-only design must remeasure approach savings and redesign jaw and climb actuation. An unreliable seal surface defeats the HAB edge strategy."],"remaining_gaps":["Dossier used for navigation. No event-by-event build or full video caption review."],"recommended_images":["images/history_2019-254_p24.jpg and images/history_2019-254_p28.jpg for labeled tool versions.","images/history_2019-254_p26.jpg and images/history_2019-254_p27.jpg for the climb load path and carriage."]}

title: 2022-987 HIGHROLLERS 2022 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-987","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40","title":"Behind the Bumpers with the High Rollers at Las Vegas","locator":"1:35–3:17 collector and popper; 3:30–4:55 hood and turret; 5:05–6:27 climber; 6:35–8:25 status and targeting","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":["The compliant-wheel collector followed an Orange County version that kicked cargo away.","A three-finger popper presented cargo to the shooter. The team drew on its 2012 design.","A rack-and-pinion adjustment replaced the two-position pneumatic hood. The team also changed the climb sequence."],"limitations":"The interview describes Las Vegas and retrospects Orange County. Some transmission wording is ambiguous. Color sorting was a planned Champs addition."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Las Vegas High Rollers robot used a four-bar pickup, a two-position inventory in its transport, and a deliberate final upward presentation into a separately aimed launcher. That final presentation is the unusual choice. A staged cargo waits for an actuator to put it into the shooting contacts. The pickup and hood revisions address different failures: bouncing off the robot before possession and limited control of release after possession.","piece_flow":["The four-bar places compliant wheels in contact with floor cargo and passes it into the indexer.","Inventory sensing distinguishes one and two cargo. The second waits for the first to clear.","The three fingers lift the staged ball into the treaded main and smaller upper wheels. The turret and adjustable hood establish the shot."],"packaging_and_motion":"The popper needs a clear approach below the shooting contacts while the turret yaws through its reported full-turn sweep from one limit to the other. The interviews describe a fixed sensor used to signal cargo at the popper and a camera mounted to the turret. Check the overlap between the moving shooter and fixed presentation throughout yaw, along with the cable sweep and climber travel.","subsystems":[{"name":"Compliant four-bar","construction":"Four-bar deployment with compliant pickup wheels.","operation":"Capture the ball with compression and pass it into the indexer.","team_rationale":"Earlier contacts could send cargo across the field instead of collecting it.","engineering_analysis":"Wheel compliance can absorb a poor approach, but a soft wheel may still kick a fast ball if the entry path lacks a closing contact.","interfaces":"The last pickup contact must keep custody until the indexer accepts the ball.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test centered and glancing approaches with stationary and rolling cargo. Inspect wheel wear and asymmetric deployment.","unknowns":"Wheel material, preload and changes to links are unverified.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40"]},{"name":"Indexer and three-finger popper","construction":"Sensors distinguish inventory and an ultrasonic sensor reports cargo at the popper. Three fingers support the staged ball.","operation":"Raise the ball into the launcher after the first piece clears.","team_rationale":"The team recalled jams with its 2020 uptake and cited consistent presentation on its 2012 popper.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed launch entry can improve repeatability, but the popper return adds a time and clearance constraint.","interfaces":"A second cargo must remain out of the fingers’ return path. Presence and shooter-ready states are distinct.","service_and_failure_modes":"Observe short lifts and check whether the next piece can be staged after a weak or interrupted shot.","unknowns":"Actuator geometry and fault recovery are unknown.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40"]},{"name":"Launcher and vision","construction":"Treaded six-inch main wheels, smaller upper wheels and rack-and-pinion adjustment in the interview configuration.","operation":"Use camera-derived range and tuned speed and hood settings, with separate moving and stationary indications.","team_rationale":"The team found treaded contacts consistent and wanted more range control than the earlier hood gave.","engineering_analysis":"A range table is sensitive to consistent entry and contact compression. Dynamic shots add sensitivity to velocity estimates and latency.","interfaces":"The popper, wheel recovery, turret position and vision validity must agree before release.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test loss of target just after a feed command and inspect binding near the yaw limits.","unknowns":"No verified speed maps, wire routing or shot dispersion.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40"]},{"name":"Windmill climb","construction":"Rotating traversal geometry with gas-shock assistance and a piston reported for deployment.","operation":"Deploy and transfer between bars by rotating through the climb.","team_rationale":"The team replaced much of the earlier complex pneumatic sequence and reported a faster deployment.","engineering_analysis":"Fewer sequential actions help only if hook engagement remains tolerant of bar approach and chassis swing.","interfaces":"Plot climb sweep against the shooter and neighboring hang positions.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check incomplete deployment and a single-side catch on a fixture.","unknowns":"Load paths and capture tolerances are unverified.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40"]}],"revisions":["Orange County pickup, hood and climb preceded the Las Vegas versions."],"transferable_principles":["Use positive presentation where a repeatable launch entry is worth an extra indexing motion.","Display possession and shot readiness independently."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A continuously supported roller path may cycle faster if it matches popper presentation repeatability.","A fixed shooter changes the approach and readiness timing, so remeasure the entire cycle."],"remaining_gaps":["Worlds sorting installation, climb geometry and as-built yaw limits."],"recommended_images":["Request a side view with popper down and fully raised, plus the turret at both yaw limits."]}

The compact pickup narrows cargo immediately, and a separate feeder drive can reverse a local section during rejection. The simplicity of the mechanical yaw solution moved substantial work into finding the target, turning the chassis and correcting the robot’s estimate of its own pose.","piece_flow":["Mecanum contacts guide the ball into the narrow over-bumper throat.","Two compliant entrance rollers and a larger lower contact carry cargo through the feeder, against a Lexan guide. The compact build also has to preserve a useful center of mass for the alternating climb and let each arm swing far enough to catch the next bar.","subsystems":[{"name":"Vector collector and feeder","construction":"Nominal ball-width throat, mecanum contacts, independent compliant entrance pair, large bottom roller and passive Lexan on one side.","operation":"Center the ball immediately and use the local drive to reverse the relevant contacts for rejection.","team_rationale":"The team chose a compact throat after prototypes and wanted a faster handoff than its 2019 hopper.","engineering_analysis":"A passive guide removes transmission complexity if the opposite contact supplies enough traction at the least favorable compression.","interfaces":"Collection direction and rejection timing share the same throat.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test grazing entries, worn cargo and a reject with a second ball at the mouth. Bound accepted residuals and specify how stale vision can be before a shot is withheld.","interfaces":"Pose, path following and shot authorization share data across processors.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test stale messages, false reflections and recovery after odometry drift.","unknowns":"No source code or recorded estimator residuals reviewed.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/JhFD4KO5HRU"]},{"name":"Alternating climb","construction":"Two commercial-style reaching arms with hook pairs, restrained using wire and elastic material.","operation":"Take mid, use favorable robot tilt to reach high and repeat for traversal.","team_rationale":"The original Waco climb hung up and needed frequent maintenance. text: {"robot_id":"2022-5940","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/GbeIEkqZO9Q","title":"Behind the Bumpers with BREAD at Chezy Champs","locator":"1:20–3:38 collection and passthrough; 3:40–4:52 controls and moving shots; 4:54–6:29 offseason climb","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. The main benefit was keeping the driver or autonomous routine on a useful heading while collecting and rejecting. The architecture depends on the center selector pulling a wanted piece up before it travels out, and on clean sensing when either end can be the entrance.","piece_flow":["Select the near-side wide intake and vector the piece toward the center.","Read the lower presence and color sensors. Move a wanted ball up to storage or pass an unwanted one through to the far side.","Upper presence sensing confirms staging. The shooter uses separate hood and flywheel targets."],"packaging_and_motion":"The central belt path must leave both ends clear, while the upper storage and shooter sit above it. Two deployable collectors occupy both chassis edges and create two sets of service points. The team kept two climb belts inside a large tube, and the original extension exceeded the intended frame allowance according to its release.","subsystems":[{"name":"Dual intake and bidirectional selector","construction":"Two wide vectoring collectors, single-sided belts, lower color and beam-break sensing and upper beam-break sensing. Public intake code has distinct idle, acquire and reverse states with independent deployment state.","operation":"Choose intake side, then pass through or raise cargo based on sensor state.","team_rationale":"Dual entry made the planned drive-by autonomous easier. The team reports many intake iterations and expressed reservations about transferring its mecanum implementation.","engineering_analysis":"Judge whether heading flexibility actually removes a turn over a complete route. Dual collection can double the service burden without doubling throughput when both mouths share one selector.","interfaces":"A staged ball must remain isolated when the floor path reverses or rejects.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test both entry directions and interruptions with a correct ball staged above a rejection.","unknowns":"Exact selector geometry, fault recovery and simultaneous-entry behavior remain unknown.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/GbeIEkqZO9Q","https://github.com/BREAD5940/2022-Onseason/blob/0a322ca98a559c411e19f7ac19c5a8149b4a4c8b/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/statemachines/Intake.java"]},{"name":"Launcher and moving shot","construction":"Adjustable hood and flywheel with separate feedback checks. The onseason shooter code has homing, idle, approach, stabilization and at-setpoint states.","operation":"Shift to a virtual target based on chassis motion in the reported later strategy. In the reviewed code, enter stabilization once both setpoints agree, wait 0.25 seconds and subsequently leave ready if either drifts.","team_rationale":"The team added moving shots to reduce time spent stopping near clusters.","engineering_analysis":"The stabilization timer shows why a shot can be mechanically capable yet delayed. In the reviewed state machine the timer itself does not require continuous in-tolerance feedback before entering at-setpoint. Verify the downstream feed gate before treating that as a shot authorization bug.","interfaces":"Estimated chassis velocity and launch readiness must be aligned in time.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test speed drop after a shot, a hood rehome and command changes during stabilization.","unknowns":"Release orchestration and event-deployed software were not audited.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/GbeIEkqZO9Q","https://github.com/BREAD5940/2022-Onseason/blob/0a322ca98a559c411e19f7ac19c5a8149b4a4c8b/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/statemachines/Shooter.java"]},{"name":"High-bar and traversal climb","construction":"Onseason belted assembly packaged two belts inside its tube. The Chezy traversal version uses static hooks, pneumatic pivot and a rear hook.","operation":"Transfer from mid to high, then catch traversal in the later version.","team_rationale":"The team cites extension overshoot in CAD and unreliable swing in a flipped pre-Champs setup. It kept high during the season and spent saved time scoring when partners could traverse.","engineering_analysis":"The full envelope and success probability can outweigh extra points from nominal reach.","interfaces":"Check belt adjustment access, path interference and the reach at actual suspended attitude.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure stretch and alignment with unequal side loads.","unknowns":"Exact offseason changes and field success distribution remain unknown.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/GbeIEkqZO9Q","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/412602/6"]}],"revisions":["Single intake concept replaced by dual intake. Moving shot added before Worlds. High-bar onseason choice and later Chezy traversal remain distinct."],"transferable_principles":["A pass-through is valuable when it preserves travel direction.","Budget for state settling and calibration in cycle time."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If route geometry rarely calls for the second entrance, its mass and maintenance can outweigh time saved.","If later reach requires reliable swing that the field cannot provide, favor a lower verified climb."],"remaining_gaps":["Selector code, match configuration details, as-built CAD and measured throughput."],"recommended_images":[{"source_url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/412602/1","image_url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/f/6/f620967c192354e5ea55836049c2804458061179.jpeg","caption":"Team release attachment. Inspect to identify installed climb configuration."}]}

text: {"robot_id":"2022-1690","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/rnpB8KXTd7U","title":"Behind the Bumpers with Orbit at Championship","locator":"1:37–3:05 drive and intake; 3:12–5:26 conveyors and turret; 5:30–7:50 climb; 8:00–12:06 shot model and state estimation","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":["Rigid intake arms yield rearward through surgical tubing in the deployment linkage.","The turret gearbox sits low and transmits torque up the structure. A new shooter with a top roller followed observed bounce-outs.","The climb reacts against the truss and uses a deployed line camera. The team models moving shots and combines encoders, gyro and vision for pose."],"limitations":"These are descriptions of the championship machine and earlier revisions. The calibration, model source code and shot statistics were not reviewed."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/403533/1","title":"Orbit introduces Parker","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read team reveal text and attachment metadata.","facts":["Names Parker and announces the first and third Israel district events."],"limitations":"Attachment located, with no visual mechanism verification."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Parker joined a rigid collection mechanism to a deliberately yielding deployment, and a wide-yaw shooter to an estimator that could account for chassis motion. Both choices move the hardest problems to interfaces. The intake needs to fold without losing the capture geometry after impact. The shooter needs fresh velocity and a model that predicts the ball’s behavior over a range of entry conditions.","piece_flow":["The collector captures the ball and shares its drive with the horizontal conveyor.","A separate vertical drive meters cargo to the shooter. Three infrared positions and color sensing track staged balls.","The hood, top roller and main launcher release while turret aim and shot setpoints compensate for robot motion."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team wanted low mass distribution and mounted the turret gearbox near the bottom, with torque sent up the tower. Printed guides manage the long cable as yaw passes through a full turn. The truss reactor sweeps outside its stowed volume, and deploys a small camera arm whose view of the floor line helps place the chassis before lift.","subsystems":[{"name":"Impact-tolerant collector","construction":"Rigid arms with a driven sprocket lever and surgical-tubing coupling.","operation":"Pull down to deploy. Under a rearward hit the assembly can yield and fold toward the robot.","team_rationale":"The team’s prior flexible intake worked but needed frequent replacement. It wanted rigidity in normal use without transmitting full impact to the motor and frame.","engineering_analysis":"A compliant actuator coupling can protect the drive while keeping the roller stiff. Verify that yielding stops short of belts, cables and hard structure.","interfaces":"After an impact the horizontal conveyor still needs its original entry geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test angled hits and repeatability after many folds. Inspect tubing for loss of force.","unknowns":"Actual release force and geometry unknown.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/rnpB8KXTd7U"]},{"name":"Transport and turret launcher","construction":"Shared collector/horizontal drive, independent vertical conveyor, adjustable hood, added top roller and low-mounted turret drive.","operation":"Stage independently of the floor path. Set yaw and hood, then release with the intended wheel states.","team_rationale":"A top roller was added after early balls bounced out of the hub. The team describes dual turret motors for responsiveness under launcher motion.","engineering_analysis":"Elevated cable drag and reflected inertia can change control across yaw. Measure release under speed and yaw changes rather than inferring it from static tuning.","interfaces":"The tower shaft, cable guides and moving ball entry have to remain aligned after service.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check wire abrasion at limits, ball entry under yaw and top-wheel speed after consecutive launches.","unknowns":"Torque margin and measured spin remain open.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/rnpB8KXTd7U"]},{"name":"Moving-shot controls","construction":"Trajectory simulation includes gravity, drag and Magnus force. The team describes selecting less sensitive combinations and correcting for chassis velocity. Pose estimation combines wheel encoders, gyro and vision.","operation":"Estimate radial and transverse motion, choose the shot and shift aim to compensate. The team also logs skids and limits reliance on drive estimates during them.","team_rationale":"A distance-by-velocity test grid was judged impractical. The team wanted a shot less sensitive to mechanical variation.","engineering_analysis":"Compare model residuals under representative wear and speeds. A low-sensitivity choice in the model only helps if it matches actual release behavior.","interfaces":"Targeting and pose share vision and velocity estimates.","service_and_failure_modes":"Exercise skid, delayed vision and a rapid acceleration immediately before release.","unknowns":"No model coefficients, validation set or latency budget.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/rnpB8KXTd7U"]},{"name":"Truss-reacting climb","construction":"Telescopic lift, V-shaped reactor, traversal hooks and a spring-deployed line camera on a small arm.","operation":"Lift while the reactor contacts the truss and changes body attitude. Capture traversal, then release the lower rung.","team_rationale":"The team wanted few actions and found initial alignment took a large share of total time.","engineering_analysis":"Using field contact saves actuation only if real approach error and field tolerances still allow the intended reaction.","interfaces":"Camera alignment must correspond to the hook and reactor pose, not just chassis heading.","service_and_failure_modes":"Try lateral offsets, missed floor line and contact near truss joints.","unknowns":"Measured load and capture margins unresolved.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/rnpB8KXTd7U"]}],"revisions":["Shooter replaced after the first Israeli event. Team added climb alignment and reports later skid detection."],"transferable_principles":["Include approach time in climb optimization.","Use model-based compensation where input quality and repeatable release justify it."],"disconfirming_conditions":["If field contact is unavailable or inconsistent, the reactor geometry loses its simplifying benefit.","Variable piece properties or noisy speed estimates can undermine moving-shot compensation."],"remaining_gaps":["Geometry, measured shot validation and control source."],"recommended_images":[{"source_url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/403533/1","image_url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/default/original/3X/1/c/1ca3bda7a564f4ec62b593aadf96ba7f5b46fd0f.jpeg","caption":"Team reveal overview. Verify whether shooter predates the new upper roller."}]}

title: 2022-971 Buckets complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-971","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/znrVtVZgQwY","title":"Behind the Bumpers with Spartan Robotics at Championship","locator":"1:26–3:25 pickup and flippy arms; 3:25–6:43 turret, retention and launch; 6:47–9:13 vision and sorting; 9:16–11:14 climb","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":["Front and rear pickups compensate for a differential chassis that cannot reorient as quickly as the team wanted.","Transfer rollers actively oscillate a staged ball around a beam break. Spring-loaded flippy arms retain and release the piece around the firing motion.","Turret position is coordinated with intake clearance. The team uses predictive control for catapult release speed and angle."],"limitations":"The full captions describe the Championship machine and include team timing claims. The binder provides construction and design rationale. Neither provides independent scoring or endurance measurements."},{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view","title":"Spartan Robotics 2022 Technical Documentation","locator":"PDF pp. 2–13, printed pp. 1–11 after overview","review_basis":"Read extracted text from the complete team PDF.","facts":["Explains six-wheel drive, successive pickups, turret bearing and cable carrier, flippy arms, catapult comparison, high-bar climb, vision and predictive control."],"limitations":"Text extraction only. Figures and hidden CAD dimensions were not measured."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Buckets uses two fixed entry directions and a rotating structure that carries both its launcher and climber. That gives the driver two ways to collect without turning the chassis around, but also requires the turret to meet the correct pickup before it can aim for the shot. A motor-driven carbon-fiber catapult replaces the usual flywheel discharge, and the flippy arms preserve custody during turret rotation and defensive contact.","piece_flow":["A front or rear mecanum pickup centers the ball and transfers it to driven staging contacts. Wrong color can reverse back out.","The transfer motor alternates direction around a beam break to retain the second ball until the turret can receive it.","Flippy arms transfer the ball into the catapult and hold it as the turret aims. Reversing the flippy rollers opens the arms so the catapult can release at the selected angle and speed."],"packaging_and_motion":"The six-wheel West Coast drive provides a short, familiar base. Above it, the turret’s bearing pair carries catapult firing and climb loads. The cable carrier routes up through the assembly. The software can move the intakes outward for turret clearance, which makes intake position part of the safe rotation state. The launcher and climb rotate together, so they keep their relative geometry while adding inertia and support loads to the same axis.","subsystems":[{"name":"Dual pickup and staged retention","construction":"Chain-tensioned pickup geometry with mecanum centering and extra upper guide rollers. Transfer rollers are controlled by a beam break.","operation":"Center cargo from either end and hold a staged ball by reversing around the detection point.","team_rationale":"The team wanted quicker acquisition without turning the differential chassis and reused lessons from its 2016 intake.","engineering_analysis":"Oscillating retention can hold a ball without a latch, but distance traveled each reversal depends on traction, sensor latency and speed.","interfaces":"Intake side and ball state tell the turret where to pick up. Deployment can also create turret clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Try sensor chatter, a failed detector and a ball displaced by a hit. Verify safe rotation before commanding intake movement.","unknowns":"Actual staging excursion and pickup performance are unresolved.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/znrVtVZgQwY","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view#page=6"]},{"name":"Flippy arms","construction":"Two opposed arms with torsion springs and a one-way bearing. The binder reports 0.75-inch cargo compression.","operation":"Roll the ball into the cup and retain it until reversed rollers open the arms for release.","team_rationale":"The team wanted continuous custody under heavy defense.","engineering_analysis":"One motor coordinating gripping, feed and release removes independent control of those functions. The release must remain synchronized as spring load and contact friction change.","interfaces":"The catapult must clear both arms throughout its stroke.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare opening symmetry and repeatability with different ball sizes and arm wear.","unknowns":"Release timing tolerance and actual spring force are unknown.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/znrVtVZgQwY","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view#page=8"]},{"name":"Catapult, yaw and localization","construction":"Vacuum-bagged carbon-fiber arm made in a printed mold, driven by two Falcons. Turret bearing stack and spring-managed cable carrier. Four Pi camera stations with custom lighting.","operation":"Use predictive voltage control to reach release angle and velocity, with target pose from vision and onboard sensing.","team_rationale":"The team found its catapult less sensitive to ball condition than its flywheel prototype. Custom vision allowed control of software and hardware.","engineering_analysis":"The release shifts dependence toward arm inertia, position sensing and timing. Verify voltage margin during combined yaw and launch.","interfaces":"Vision, turret aiming, ball retention and catapult release must agree in one shot state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test low battery, stale pose and off-center ball seating. Inspect the cup and bearing mounts after impacts.","unknowns":"No reviewed solver traces or controlled dispersion comparison.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/znrVtVZgQwY","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view#page=9","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view#page=13"]},{"name":"Turret-carried high climb","construction":"Mid-bar latching hooks and a chain/cable system. Servo release and constant-force springs extend the high-bar stage, with torsion-assisted folding hooks.","operation":"Latch mid, deploy the high stage and transfer by swinging into position.","team_rationale":"Binder identifies weight savings from the mixed chain/cable drive and an original mid-bar objective.","engineering_analysis":"Sharing turret support keeps relative clearances but concentrates hang loads in rotating joints.","interfaces":"Account for off-axis loads and cable clearance throughout positioning and hanging.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check one-hook capture and latch retention under disabled conditions.","unknowns":"No certified bearing loads or climb rate sample.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/znrVtVZgQwY","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view#page=10"]}],"revisions":["Collector prototypes progressed from flex contacts to mecanum/chain geometry and then added guide rollers. Binder distinguishes earlier climb concepts from the current high-bar mechanism."],"transferable_principles":["Preserve positive piece custody through aiming under contact.","Treat turret travel clearance as a state machine requirement when intakes share the sweep."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A catapult loses its advantage if release timing and cup fit vary more than a flywheel’s compression.","Dual entry may lose time when turret handoff is slower than chassis repositioning."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact competition software, launch traces, event-by-event configuration and turret load margins."],"recommended_images":["Request binder figures for the flippy arms and catapult, then a wide view showing both intake clearance poses."]}

text: {"name":"Catapult, yaw and localization","construction":"Vacuum-bagged carbon-fiber arm made in a printed mold, driven by two Falcons. Turret bearing stack and spring-managed cable carrier. text: {"robot_id":"2023-3538","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-3538-robojackets-1-fim-epa/433780","title":"3538 RoboJackets | Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Posts 1 and 3","review_basis":"Read the publisher's introduction and AlexZ's fabrication reply.","facts":"The introduction identifies Colson swerve, auto intake, arm placement and Helix Navigator. The introduction is a secondary summary."},{"url":"https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA","title":"3538 RoboJackets interview","locator":"Older dossier and focused supplement","review_basis":"Inherited interview synopsis. Full captions not available for this review.","facts":"The dossier describes a curved roller tool, virtual four-bar with extension, gravity compensation and pitch-based balancing.","limitations":"Inherited details are provisional. No independent visual or full-caption review."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The RoboJackets' retained interview account describes a single tool that picks up cones and cubes and carries them all the way to the node. The important mechanical distinction is that the tool's angle is tied to the arm geometry, while extension adds reach. This couples the design of the gripper mouth to the poses the arm can reach. The separate fabrication reply directly establishes how the team made its Colson wheel hardware compatible with commercial swerve modules.","piece_flow":["Present the curved tool at the floor or station. The older account describes a wide opening intended to tolerate station alignment error.","Draw the piece into the tool and hold it during arm motion. The focused supplement describes reducing roller speed in the previous useful direction.","Move the loaded linkage and extension to the scoring pose, release and recover to a travel pose. The older account describes direct grip without an intermediate transfer."],"packaging_and_motion":"Treat the mechanism's swept volume as the union of the arm, extension, tool, harness and the retained cone or cube. Mechanically coupled tool angle can simplify commands, but it removes a free adjustment for clearing the bumper or approaching a node at a different angle. A configuration that works at both endpoints can still intersect the grid during the transition.","subsystems":[{"name":"Virtual four-bar and extension","construction":"Older dossier describes a virtual four-bar and telescoping reach.","operation":"The linked motion carries the same tool from pickup to scoring poses.","team_rationale":"Older synopsis reports fast cycles as a design priority. The exact choice of linkage is unexplained.","engineering_analysis":"Compare load-dependent tip sag and endpoint error at high reach with error at floor height. Extension can multiply angular play into translational error.","interfaces":"Linkage geometry sets the tool approach angle, while extension changes reach and the loaded moment on the arm.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect joint play, phase/indexing and carriage travel after impacts. These are proposed checks.","unknowns":"Link ratios, actuators, travel and event configurations.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA"]},{"name":"Curved direct gripper","construction":"Older dossier describes a curved dual-piece roller tool.","operation":"Acquire, hold at reduced output and release with the same mechanism.","team_rationale":"Older account reports that the wide opening reduced station alignment demand and that the first prototype acquired better than it placed.","engineering_analysis":"A broad entrance helps only if it leads to a repeatable seat. Compare cone yaw and cube offset at pickup against actual release error.","interfaces":"Needs tool clearance and roller contact across floor, shelf and node poses.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test restarts after reversing direction and retention during chassis braking. A direction remembered from the previous action could become wrong after an interrupted cycle.","unknowns":"Exact profile, compression and state logic.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA"]},{"name":"Colson swerve and station control","construction":"Machined hubs and wheels were reported by AlexZ. Older account associates gyro pitch with balance.","operation":"Swerve aligns the collector and traverses the station. The reported balancing loop uses pitch.","team_rationale":"Older dossier attributes traction selection in part to the station surface.","engineering_analysis":"Test wheel retention and braking on the relevant surface. Wheel compatibility alone does not establish grip, wear or stop distance.","interfaces":"Changing wheels may alter approach behavior and odometry scale.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check hub attachment and tread wear before attributing variation to software.","unknowns":"Installed module, wheel dimensions and measured traction.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-3538-robojackets-1-fim-epa/433780","https://youtu.be/wmEajgIojAA"]}],"revisions":["Older synopsis separates the week-one pickup prototype from the later curved placement geometry. July reply dates wheel documentation, not installation."],"transferable_principles":["Prototype pickup, carried pose and release on a single fixture before freezing the virtual-linkage geometry."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Reject the transfer if tight release-angle tolerances require a separate wrist adjustment or if loaded extension shifts the gripper outside the placement tolerance."],"remaining_gaps":["Full interview captions, arm CAD and measured repeatability."],"recommended_images":["Retrieve a source-linked side view with the linkage and extension visible and a close-up of the Colson hub. text: {"robot_id":"2023-1325","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-1325-inverse-paradox/437023","title":"1325 Inverse Paradox | Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read full interview publisher introduction.","facts":"Identifies wrist iterations, custom VP gearbox additions, multiple Limelights, custom pathing UI, and first use of swerve.","limitations":"Publisher summary only. No team explanation transcribed in the post."},{"url":"https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk","title":"1325 Inverse Paradox pit interview","locator":"Base dossier and focused technical supplement","review_basis":"Inherited interview synopsis. Captions were not recovered in this review.","facts":"Reports a compact square chassis, two-joint arm, aircraft-cable wrist transmission and a final fixed-spacing roller gripper.","limitations":"Specific geometry, transmission and chronology remain inherited claims."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The 1325 dossier describes a small swerve robot that uses the same tool to acquire and score. The arm moves through shoulder and elbow joints, with a separate wrist for orienting the piece. The noteworthy iteration is at the contact interface. The retained account says the team removed a gripping degree of freedom after learning that fixed spacing could accommodate both 2023 pieces. The interview announcement independently confirms wrist iterations and custom gearbox work at a broad level.","piece_flow":["Present the tool at the supply pose and draw the piece into the roller gap. In the final configuration described by the dossier the gap is fixed.","Hold the piece in the same tool while shoulder, elbow and wrist move the piece toward the grid. The earlier collector concept is a prototype lineage.","Orient and release at the node, then retract while keeping the tool and retained piece clear of field and robot structure."],"packaging_and_motion":"The older description puts the gearboxes low and drives the wrist remotely with aircraft cable. This can keep mass out of the distal assembly and reduce shoulder inertia. It introduces a cable route whose effective length and tension must remain stable as other joints move. On the reported 26-inch square base, extension moves the loaded center of mass toward the edge quickly, especially under braking.","subsystems":[{"name":"Fixed-spacing roller tool","construction":"Older dossier describes a static final gap and powered rollers.","operation":"Capture either piece with contact geometry and roller compliance, then carry it directly.","team_rationale":"The retained account says testing showed fixed spacing worked after opening and closing versions were tried.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed gap removes a clamp action and its controls. That benefit depends on the two pieces sharing a usable compression range at their actual orientations.","interfaces":"Wrist angle controls approach and release. Contact geometry determines where the piece sits relative to wrist presets.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether wear and deformation cause loss of retention at one end of the size range. Test recovery from a half-seated cone.","unknowns":"Roller profile, compression, sensor and release logic.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk"]},{"name":"Shoulder, elbow and remote wrist","construction":"Low gearbox packaging and cable drive are inherited. The publisher explicitly mentions gearbox additions.","operation":"Move the elbow and shoulder to position the wrist while the wrist adjusts the tool angle.","team_rationale":"Specific rationale for the transmission layout needs the team interview or drawings.","engineering_analysis":"A distal mass reduction trades against cable stretch, friction and pretension. Measure tool angle at the same command after reversing direction under load.","interfaces":"Shoulder and elbow motion can change cable routing clearance and loads on the distal joint.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check cable anchoring and tension before retuning a controller that appears to have pose-dependent error.","unknowns":"Cable routing, reductions, joint stops and counterbalance mounting.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-1325-inverse-paradox/437023","https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk"]},{"name":"Approach and path controls","construction":"The publisher identifies first-season swerve, multiple Limelights and a custom pathing UI.","operation":"Older synopsis assigns vision to AprilTag and cone-node alignment.","team_rationale":"Exact camera placement rationale remains inherited and incompletely documented.","engineering_analysis":"Different camera viewpoints can address different occlusion cases. Measure target visibility with the arm up and the piece seated.","interfaces":"Tool reach and yaw tolerance determine how much chassis alignment error the arm can absorb.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify camera alignment after remount and compare against repeatable manual fallback approaches.","unknowns":"Camera layout, steering logic and station engagement.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-1325-inverse-paradox/437023","https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk"]}],"revisions":["The inherited account places slider and pivot prototypes before a spring-closing competition design, then fixed spacing after the second event and a later gas-spring counterbalance. Exact installation dates remain open."],"transferable_principles":["Compare cycle time and release scatter on a fixed tool before allocating a clamp actuator. Test remote wrist accuracy at several arm angles with the piece installed."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Fixed spacing loses its advantage if worn contacts cannot retain the smallest piece while still admitting the largest. Remote drive loses value if loaded hysteresis consumes the placement tolerance."],"remaining_gaps":["Team-authored mechanism text, full captions, installed version dates and station behavior."],"recommended_images":["Seek a side view of the complete cable route and side-by-side images of opening and fixed grippers."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2023-2468","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-2468-team-appreciate-fit-dallas-winners-ei/429455","title":"2468 Team Appreciate | Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read the complete interview publisher introduction.","facts":"Publisher describes a cascading elevator, wrist intake, custom dashboard and path planning.","limitations":"Secondary summary. No fresh full-caption or visual review.","facts":"Reports a fixed-angle two-stage lift, narrow dual-piece tool, floor supply, and wrist transmission changes.","limitations":"Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Appreciate's older interview record describes a robot that gets its scoring reach from a lift set at a fixed angle. The wrist on its rigid arm makes the contact angle adjustable while the lift changes height and horizontal reach together. The team reportedly made the pickup tool narrow enough to work between hybrid-node dividers. This is a useful case where access to a crowded scoring space dictates the geometry of the collector.","piece_flow":["Use the wrist to bring the narrow tool to a floor-fed piece. The older account describes direct acquisition.","Raise the tool on the tilted lift, carrying the same piece to the node. Choose the wrist angle for the selected piece and target.","Release, withdraw along a clear path, then lower the lift and return the wrist to pickup."],"packaging_and_motion":"Tilting the rail gives a repeatable relationship between lift height and horizontal approach distance. The tradeoff is fewer independent ways to reach an obstructed target. Chassis placement takes up the remaining horizontal error, and high extension moves the loaded mass farther toward the node. Test the stowed and extended envelope with the bumper and the largest retained piece installed.","subsystems":[{"name":"Cascading elevator and rigid arm","construction":"Publisher identifies a cascade. Fixed tilt, two stages and wide layout come from the older dossier.","operation":"Lifting simultaneously advances the end tool along the tilted axis.","team_rationale":"The older account says the angle follows cone-node geometry.","engineering_analysis":"Cascade motion can reduce time to height, but an off-center piece loads the guides in twist and can alter the release pose.","interfaces":"The lift defines the tool approach line. The wrist and chassis make the remaining corrections.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure rail alignment after contact and cycle with representative off-center loads. Check access to inspect and replace rigging.","unknowns":"Rigging, angle, motor sizing and release tolerances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-2468-team-appreciate-fit-dallas-winners-ei/429455","https://youtu.be/LvGNxp2PQ7I"]},{"name":"Narrow wrist and gripper","construction":"Publisher identifies wrist intake. Narrow geometry and direct retention are inherited.","operation":"Rotate into pickup or placement pose and carry the piece in the same tool.","team_rationale":"The older interview synopsis attributes tool width to clearance between hybrid dividers and the ability to retrieve or rescore.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate capture rate against approach offset and score/recovery rate beside dividers. Optimizing just one end of the cycle would favor different widths.","interfaces":"Operator mode selection reportedly sets piece behavior. A mismatch can pick the wrong preset.","service_and_failure_modes":"Older dossier reports a belt-to-chain change. Inspect backlash and retention after impact and check whether wrist position has drifted under load.","unknowns":"Contact geometry, final wrist hardware and exact reason for each revision.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-2468-team-appreciate-fit-dallas-winners-ei/429455","https://youtu.be/LvGNxp2PQ7I"]},{"name":"Dashboard and approach","construction":"Publisher confirms a custom dashboard and path planning.","operation":"The older dossier describes remembered piece selection and pitch/roll display for autonomous engage.","team_rationale":"The source introduction gives no rationale for the operator interface.","engineering_analysis":"A displayed selection is operator intent. Verify that the next command is recoverable when the physical piece or pose differs.","interfaces":"Chassis alignment, wrist presets and display state affect the same placement task.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test wrong selection and interrupted approach recovery with a human player and operator.","unknowns":"Auto balance logic, path implementation and recovery inputs.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-2468-team-appreciate-fit-dallas-winners-ei/429455","https://youtu.be/LvGNxp2PQ7I"]}],"revisions":["Older dossier reports belt-to-chain wrist transmission and half-inch hex to REV MAXSpline changes. Event installation dates are unresolved."],"transferable_principles":["Size the collector against the tightest scoring or recovery clearance, then measure whether drivers can reliably feed the resulting opening."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A fixed-tilt lift loses its advantage if new targets require substantially different horizontal approaches at the same height. The underside clearance has to be checked with bumper compression, drivetrain deflection and station angle included.","subsystems":[{"name":"Roller claw and collection stop","construction":"Older dossier reports three rollers and a hard reference at a bumper support.","operation":"The tool captures both pieces and retains them through arm motion.","team_rationale":"The retained account describes a repeatable collection pose and several claw iterations.","engineering_analysis":"A structural stop can set pickup height reproducibly, provided it takes the load without bending the tool or unloading the wheels.","interfaces":"The stop and bumper mount share the collection interface. text: {"robot_id":"2023-6329","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-the-bucks-wrath-2023-robot-shock/428274","title":"6329 presents Shock","locator":"Team posts 1 and 4","review_basis":"Read team reveal and reply on frame dimensions.","facts":"Team identifies MK4i swerve, two-position tipping elevator, dual-motor intake with wrist and a 24 by 24 inch design requirement that drove layout.","limitations":"Reveal gives architecture and packaging target. No fresh full-caption or visual review.","facts":"Describes a two-stage cascade, Everybot-derived tool with different contact regions and cube-retaining netting, cone/cube presets and switch from NEO to Falcon drive.","limitations":"Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Shock fits swerve, a tipping lift and a dual-piece tool on a chassis whose stated design requirement was a 24-inch square. The lift changes its orientation between two positions. Its wrist then adjusts the piece's local angle for acquisition and scoring. This breaks the problem into a small number of coarse reach configurations and finer tool motion. The release confirms those main mechanisms, while the contact geometry and controls below come from the retained interview synopsis.","piece_flow":["Bring the wrist to the piece. The older account describes different contact regions for cones and cubes within the same tool, plus netting that helps retain cubes.","Keep possession in the gripper while selecting lift tip position, height and wrist orientation. The older account describes direct handling.","Place and release at the grid, then return to the travel or collection pose. Preserve clearance for a cone that is slightly off its nominal seat."],"packaging_and_motion":"The compact square frame leaves less internal space for a mast pivot, actuator and cables, and gives a smaller wheel support polygon for extended work. Moving the lift from one tip position to another sweeps the carriage and tool as well as the rails. A second fixed tip position can deliver more reach without full continuous articulation, provided each position has a repeatable reference and the loaded transition fits.","subsystems":[{"name":"Tipping elevator","construction":"Reveal identifies two tip positions. Two-stage cascading construction comes from the older interview.","operation":"Tip the lift as a unit and move the carriage to height, while the wrist sets final tool angle.","team_rationale":"The team explicitly says its compact frame requirement drove design. The post does not explain the tilt mechanism choice.","engineering_analysis":"The positions simplify the command space, but the structure must locate consistently under changing bending moments.","interfaces":"Mast, lift and wrist have intersecting motion envelopes. A raised piece increases the lever arm on the tipping structure.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare repeatability at both stops and after a reversal. Inspect play and test recovery from a stopped intermediate posture.","unknowns":"Tilt actuator, locking method, rail spacing and rigging.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-the-bucks-wrath-2023-robot-shock/428274","https://youtu.be/uLgGPEvMAqA"]},{"name":"Dual-motor wrist intake","construction":"Reveal confirms dual motors and a wrist. Retaining netting and contact-region layout are inherited.","operation":"Acquire and score directly with the same tool.","team_rationale":"No contact-geometry rationale in the reveal.","engineering_analysis":"A cone needs stable orientation while a cube can need containment across open spaces. Separate contact zones allow tuning each while sharing an envelope.","interfaces":"The wrist's sweep and load depend on where each piece sits. An off-center cone can also affect the mast moment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check worn roller compression and snagging or slack in the retaining netting. Test cube retention under braking.","unknowns":"Motor assignments, current limits and grip detection.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-the-bucks-wrath-2023-robot-shock/428274","https://youtu.be/uLgGPEvMAqA"]},{"name":"Swerve and presets","construction":"MK4i modules directly confirmed. Motor swap and heading snaps are inherited.","operation":"Older synopsis describes piece-specific lift and wrist presets with cardinal heading snaps.","team_rationale":"Older account attributes the motor change to control difficulties.","engineering_analysis":"Heading snap helps only if the mast and gripper reproduce the lateral pose accurately enough for the node.","interfaces":"Approach heading and extension interact with available support and bumper clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check whether changed steer behavior or wheel calibration shifts autonomous approach. Test loaded and unloaded docking separately.","unknowns":"Exact drive configuration by event and station sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/6329-the-bucks-wrath-2023-robot-shock/428274","https://youtu.be/uLgGPEvMAqA"]}],"revisions":["Team reveal describes February configuration. Older synopsis reports an initial NEO implementation and later Falcons. No complete event chronology."],"transferable_principles":["Use a discrete posture change when the task separates into distinct approach families and each can be reached with repeatable stops."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The benefit shrinks if obstacle avoidance needs many intermediate tip angles or extended-load stability sets a low chassis speed limit."],"remaining_gaps":["Full interview, stop geometry, loaded reach and charge-station method."],"recommended_images":["Seek side views of both lift positions with the same carriage height and a close-up of the separate roller regions."]}

Event installation and mechanism purpose by match are unresolved."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Team 930's CAD release directly documents the lift's continuous belt and its protected route. The older interview account explains how that lift fits into the scoring machine. An arm moves through the opening between the structural members while carrying a piece in a belt-based tool. The layout gives the tool access to useful approach directions while the stage structure remains tall enough to serve the grid.","piece_flow":["Acquire into the gripper and retain the piece in the same tool. The older synopsis describes polyurethane belts and stand-offs to keep the belts clear of carpet.","Move the arm and carriage through a collision-free sequence. Pass-through gives a potential route to the other side while keeping the original grip.","Release at the selected node and retract. The proposed auxiliary cube intake in the interview is a separate route whose deployment status remains unresolved."],"packaging_and_motion":"The two bolted tubes support and enclose a useful routing volume. Internal belt runs protect the transmission from contact and free external clearance, but hidden belt edges and anchors must remain inspectable. The pass-through opening has to clear the carried piece, not just the arm CAD. Grid, bumper, elevator and wrist also bound how much directional flexibility the drive team can actually use.","subsystems":[{"name":"Continuously rigged elevator","construction":"Team describes a belt routed inside aluminum tubes, with its ends connected to the top and bottom of the carriage.","operation":"Belt motion controls carriage position while the rail stack supports the scoring arm.","team_rationale":"Team states packaging and protection as reasons for internal routing.","engineering_analysis":"Internal routing can make a belt serviceable only if there is a path to fish, tension and anchor a replacement with the arm installed. The bolted stage can also accumulate alignment error.","interfaces":"The elevator sets arm height and carries bending and torsional load when the gripper extends or reverses.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tube-edge clearance and belt tracking through the entire stroke. Time belt replacement before assuming internal routing improves service.","unknowns":"Belt pitch, detailed pulley geometry, tension settings and loaded deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-930-mukwonago-bears-cad-and-code-release/438584"]},{"name":"Pass-through arm and gripper","construction":"Carbon-fiber arm and belt-based gripper are from the older interview. The belt elevator is a distinct subsystem.","operation":"Carry the retained piece through the arm's working envelope and release from a selected direction.","team_rationale":"Older account attributes stand-offs to keeping intake belts off carpet.","engineering_analysis":"Reducing arm mass can improve motion at the expense of sensitivity to joint attachment and impact. Check the complete loaded envelope and end-tool sag after reversal.","interfaces":"Pickup height depends on wrist angle and stand-off position. The lift opening limits allowable piece yaw during reversal.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check bonded or fastened interfaces using actual construction details when available. Inspect worn belts and floor stand-offs after a hard landing.","unknowns":"Tube layup, joint attachments, compression and capture envelope.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/wzWFWZzy9C8"]},{"name":"Preset and auxiliary route","construction":"Older dossier describes the proposed auxiliary route. Released code declares an intake extension motor, roller motor and a driver binding for the ground intake sequence.","operation":"The code positions the elevator and arm for intake after collector extension, uses manipulator current in the sequence, then stows the arm before collector retraction.","team_rationale":"The auxiliary route's link value is an engineering interpretation of the older account.","engineering_analysis":"Time the actual low-link cycle and compare with the main arm before assigning the volume, wiring and driver inputs to a second mechanism.","interfaces":"A low intake can occupy the arm's collection sweep and change the possession logic.","service_and_failure_modes":"Exercise wrong preset and delayed retraction scenarios before integrating an auxiliary path.","unknowns":"Actual competition installation and whether the proposed direct low-scoring function was fielded.","source_urls":["https://github.com/FRC930/Robot2023/blob/master/src/main/java/frc/robot/utilities/CommandFactoryUtility.java","https://github.com/FRC930/Robot2023/blob/master/src/main/java/frc/robot/RobotContainer.java","https://youtu.be/wzWFWZzy9C8"]}],"revisions":["Older interview reports aluminum-to-carbon-fiber arm evolution and presents the low route as future work at filming. June release and July reply establish publication dates only."],"transferable_principles":["For a pass-through lift, route protected drive elements and harnesses outside the volume occupied by the retained piece."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The layout loses value if piece or harness clearance forces a stop-and-regrip, or if the alternate route rarely saves a chassis turn."],"remaining_gaps":["Full captions, release branch deployment by event, and mechanical validation of the auxiliary intake. FIRST records Benedict Cargohub while the older dossier uses Cubert Conelius. This makes the tower tube part of both the structure and the transmission alignment scheme.","piece_flow":["Set the wrist for the intended piece. text: {"robot_id":"2023-2910","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2023/436653","title":"2910 Phantom CAD and tech binder release","locator":"Posts 1, 8 and 9","review_basis":"Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.","facts":"Team confirms internal Falcon encoders, tight-fitting REV ION gears, dead-axle main pivot, delayed extension near shoulder setpoint, and cone centering using intake-wall time-of-flight measurement. Team says the compensation reduced translation direction error while rotating. The release discussion also documents recharacterizing path feedforward after three gearing changes.","limitations":"The default drive command is a separate implementation from cone scoring alignment. The gain is tuned to that chassis and version."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Phantom uses a compact telescoping arm to reach a piece at the floor or shelf and carry it directly to the grid. The team documented a useful tradeoff between moving joints together and staying stable. Extending early increased tip tendency, so extension waits until the shoulder is near its target. The team also measured where the cone sat within the gripper so automatic alignment aimed the piece at the node instead of assuming it was centered on the chassis.","piece_flow":["Select the source posture and acquire the piece with the wristed roller tool. The older account lists several floor and shelf poses.","Keep the piece in the tool as the shoulder moves. In the team-described stability sequence, delay extension until the shoulder is within an allowed distance of its target.","During assisted cone scoring, use the measured cone offset and localized chassis pose to select a scoring column. The driver advances to confirm. Release when position and orientation checks pass."],"packaging_and_motion":"A telescope allows a compact stow and significant loaded reach. The worst overturning moment can occur during transition when the arm is extended at an unfavorable angle. Deferring extension reduces that moment at the expense of overlap. Tight gear fits and a stiff A-frame let the team use motor-side encoders, which still require a consistent reference and minimal lost motion at the tool.","subsystems":[{"name":"Shoulder and telescope","construction":"Team confirms dead-axle main pivot, stiff A-frame, REV ION gear fits and internal Falcon encoders. The older dossier identifies a two-stage telescope.","operation":"Rotate shoulder, extend and adjust wrist. Team reports sequencing extension based on shoulder progress.","team_rationale":"Team explicitly addresses tipping and mechanical backlash.","engineering_analysis":"Measure loaded tip error from both motion directions and quantify wheel unloading with a piece while braking. Motor position can be accurate even while a compliant joint moves.","interfaces":"The shoulder-to-extension gate determines how much mass moves forward during rotation.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check startup reference, tension and backlash after maintenance. Test a missed gate and a stalled intermediate posture.","unknowns":"Actual gating threshold, current limits and observed wheel loads.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2023/436653","https://youtu.be/7ETEf__nD1I"]},{"name":"Roller tool and offset sensing","construction":"Older account describes dead-axle roller contacts. Team confirms a time-of-flight sensor inside the intake wall.","operation":"Capture and retain both pieces. For cone alignment, estimate its lateral position inside the tool.","team_rationale":"Team says an off-center cone could miss when aligned using the drivebase center alone.","engineering_analysis":"Measure sensor error across cone orientation, surface condition and partial seating. Center measurement is useful only when it predicts the cone's placement contact.","interfaces":"Tool offset measurement feeds node selection and lateral chassis control.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test dirty optics, no-return values and side-seated cones. Manual release needs predictable behavior if automated checks are unavailable.","unknowns":"Sensor calibration, mounting tolerances and cube behavior.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2023/436653","https://youtu.be/7ETEf__nD1I"]},{"name":"Chassis alignment","construction":"Team describes two angled cameras for relocalization and a release gate across X, Y, yaw and pitch.","operation":"Close the lateral and angular error, then let the driver's forward command confirm the approach.","team_rationale":"Team reports strict thresholds cut false positives and sometimes made manual scoring faster.","engineering_analysis":"Compare both workflows on full scoring time and misses, including reacquisition after a rejected gate.","interfaces":"Localization and in-tool measurement must share the same coordinate conventions.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check camera calibration and degraded-field visibility. Test manual field-relative driving at varied turn rates after any drivetrain change because the published compensation coefficient was tuned empirically.","unknowns":"Exact threshold settings, timeouts and configuration dates.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2023/436653","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2023CompetitionRobot-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/frcteam2910/c2023/commands/DefaultDriveCommand.java","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2910-code-release-2023/443663"]}],"revisions":["Older record describes several tool prototypes. Team describes automatic scoring late in the season and release publications afterward.","The code-release Q&A reports three drivetrain gearings and a shift from concatenating PathPlanner segments to independent trajectories."],"transferable_principles":["Measure the piece in the tool when centering error is comparable to target tolerance. Sequence axes against the loaded stability envelope."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Automatic release loses value when conservative thresholds cost more cycles than they save. Motor-only sensing becomes inadequate when wear or deflection exceeds placement tolerance."],"remaining_gaps":["Binder access, full captions, source inspection of arm and alignment logic, and event-specific threshold history."],"recommended_images":["Team release robot render and a close-up showing the intake-wall sensor relative to a loaded cone."]}
