text: {"robot_id":"2023-111","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2023/420243?page=9","title":"WildStang 2023 build blog","locator":"Team 111 posts 167, 172, 174 and 179","review_basis":"Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.","facts":"Team describes carriage popping out under strafing or rotation with a horizontal arm, captive floating DryLin sliders with cam followers carrying vertical loads, a serviceable hot-melt composite plug and bolt-on spare-arm interface. Posted code and text distinguish arm delay, lift delay, wrist carry and simple moves.","limitations":"February development snapshot. The post gives a static slider rating, not shock validation. Team 112 posts are separate."},{"url":"https://youtu.be/iKxRiTgii4k","title":"111 interview","locator":"Base dossier and focused supplement","review_basis":"Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.","facts":"Older synopsis describes open-top continuous lift, symmetric roller tool and both-face pickup, plus stays and spring/magnet stage retention.","limitations":"Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"WildStang's open-top lift allows its arm to cross the center of the robot while keeping the game piece in one tool. The same opening creates two design problems the February posts make concrete. A loaded or horizontal arm can put enough torque into the carriage to pull it away from the rail. Crossing the opening also requires the wrist to orient so it clears the fixed stage. The team addressed those problems with a mechanically captured carriage and explicit axis sequencing.","piece_flow":["Present the symmetric tool at a supply pose. Older interview describes cube and upright or tipped cone acquisition from either face.","Hold the piece and select a lift, arm and wrist transition. The posted controller keeps the wrist in a carry orientation during side changes and delays axes when clearance requires it.","Place at the node from the selected side, then return to collection using the applicable sequence."],"packaging_and_motion":"The open top makes a useful central path for the arm. Lateral chassis acceleration loads that opening through the long arm, and the reaction becomes more severe as the carriage rises. Captive side guidance helps keep the carriage installed. Allowing the guides to float in selected directions prevents the new constraint from fighting vertical cam followers on imperfectly parallel rails.","subsystems":[{"name":"Open-top lift and carriage","construction":"Team reports switching side rollers to captive DryLin sliders with different float directions while retaining cam followers in the vertical plane. Continuous rigging, stays and stage retention are inherited.","operation":"Raise the arm while rails guide the carriage and sliders react side loads.","team_rationale":"Team wanted to withstand impacts without relying solely on drive speed limits. Float was added to avoid binding.","engineering_analysis":"Separate vertical support, lateral capture and alignment. Check what happens under a side load at maximum height and extension, including permanent rail misalignment.","interfaces":"Horizontal arm torque enters carriage guides and frame. Cable tension and rail parallelism affect the same stroke.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check rail play and binding after a hit. Test replacement of a slider without losing the carriage reference.","unknowns":"Later guide specification, shock testing and exact sequencing hardware.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2023/420243?page=9","https://youtu.be/iKxRiTgii4k"]},{"name":"Composite arm and direct gripper","construction":"Team describes carbon tube, printed plugs retained with hot melt, increased tube support near wrist and a bolted base joint. The symmetric roller tool is inherited.","operation":"Acquire and hold through transfer across the robot, then release with the same tool.","team_rationale":"Team wanted replaceable end caps, improved wrist stiffness and a whole-arm swap that avoids heating the robot.","engineering_analysis":"Adhesive serviceability is separate from bond reliability. Test loaded torsion and creep under belt tension with realistic part fit and temperature.","interfaces":"Arm, wrist and belt loads converge at the plug. The whole assembly must retain its encoder reference after a swap.","service_and_failure_modes":"Time arm replacement and check wrist angle, bond movement and belt tracking.","unknowns":"Installed adhesive lots, validated shock limits and final tool compression.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2023/420243?page=9","https://youtu.be/iKxRiTgii4k"]},{"name":"Collision sequencing","construction":"Team posted a February control excerpt and identifies lift motor encoder plus through-bore arm and wrist encoders.","operation":"Use different axis waits for floor, height and fixed-stage clearance. The wrist points upward during side changes.","team_rationale":"Team says the wrist would strike the fixed stage in another orientation.","engineering_analysis":"Side changes require both a legal swept volume and predictable abort handling. Test a command change while one axis is waiting.","interfaces":"Piece size, wrist angle and lift height constrain transition choice.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test sensor misreference and a command interrupted near the frame or floor.","unknowns":"Full program, final thresholds and stage-specific revisions.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2023/420243?page=9"]}],"revisions":["February posts report a carriage retention redesign and arm plug service changes. Older account reports stays and bottom-stage magnet changes without exact event dates."],"transferable_principles":["Assign side load capture and vertical support to different features where an open lift must stay tolerant of rail misalignment."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Transfer fails if a larger piece makes the side-change clearance dependent on many more states, or if shock load exceeds capture capacity."],"remaining_gaps":["Full captions, season chronology, load test results and charge-station behavior."],"recommended_images":["Team post 167 slider diagrams and post 174 arm/wrist joint images."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2023-3467","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-3467-2023-build-blog/417264?page=10","title":"3467 Windham Windup 2023 build blog","locator":"Posts 184, 186–187 and 189–191","review_basis":"Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.","facts":"Team abandoned side climber concept after Week 0 given 24-inch-square packaging, electronics access and lower priority. The build blog documents a decision that the small chassis forced. A separate side climber consumed too much space and interfered with electronics access, so the team abandoned the concept after Week 0. The early event posts also show that software and spare robots only help when mechanical reference points and hardware revisions are consistent.","piece_flow":["The early-season account emphasizes double-substation loading. text: {"robot_id":"2023-1323","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://team1323.com/first/frc/2023-season-2/","title":"MadTown 2023 season","locator":"ETR 19 and competitive-concept sections","review_basis":"Read team season page.","facts":"Team labels the competition robot ETR 19 and separately describes two COTS-focused CAD concepts intended to help other teams.","limitations":"The COTS statement applies to the concept program. In the retained account, the floor cube intake delivers to the same scoring claw that takes cones. The independent axes then position that claw for the grid. This gives the machine the chance to start some motions before others finish, but it makes successful timing and repeatable handoff part of the mechanical architecture. The team’s season page identifies ETR 19 separately from its two shared competition concepts.","piece_flow":["Use the wide cube collector and funnel the cube to a transfer pose. The older interview account describes rollers and star wheels guiding it through a tunnel.","Coordinate the claw with the tunnel for cube handoff. For cones, use the claw's direct acquisition route. The inherited account describes a separate recovery move for tipped cones.","Lift, extend and orient to place the piece. The older account describes some joints moving simultaneously within collision limits. Withdraw and make the claw available for the next load."],"packaging_and_motion":"The tunnel needs enough clearance for cube rotation, guide deflection and release while sitting under or near moving scoring hardware. The claw has to be in position during cube transfer and then be free to leave. Independently driven height and reach improve access to placement poses but occupy space and increase moving mass and electrical demand when accelerating together.","subsystems":[{"name":"Cube collector and tunnel","construction":"The broad double-intake architecture is reported by the publisher. Rollers, star wheels and the tunnel are from the older interview account.","operation":"Collect a cube at the floor and center it for claw transfer.","team_rationale":"The older synopsis describes acquisition breadth and a guided handoff. Precise mechanism rationale needs fuller team text.","engineering_analysis":"Measure lateral and angular exit error and use that to set the claw window. A wide entrance is ineffective if off-center cubes jam downstream.","interfaces":"Collector, guides and claw share one timing and alignment interface.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test a cube pinned diagonally and a delayed claw. Establish whether the collector can reverse without jamming the arm.","unknowns":"Roller drive, tunnel throat, sensors and cycle distributions.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-1323-madtown-robotics/435870","https://youtu.be/hz3MolcRe2M"]},{"name":"Positioning axes and claw","construction":"Older dossier describes a vertical belt lift, horizontal chain/rope extension and an articulated arm with shared claw.","operation":"Move joints together where allowed and use the same claw for scoring cubes and cones.","team_rationale":"Older account associates independent motions with rapid cycles. Exact component choices need team confirmation.","engineering_analysis":"Quantify cycle improvement from motion overlap against peak current, deflection and stability. Presets must tolerate cube and cone seating differences.","interfaces":"The tunnel is a fixed receiver/sender interface. The arm and claw must visit it repeatably before travel toward the grid.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test one slow axis, a late homing event and recovery from a partially transferred cube.","unknowns":"Axis geometry, limit logic, stow envelope and deployed revisions.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/hz3MolcRe2M"]},{"name":"Cone acquisition and perception","construction":"Publisher identifies object detection. Inherited account describes Limelight correction for autonomous cone pickup.","operation":"Approach and take a cone into the claw directly, using a distinct recovery sequence if tipped.","team_rationale":"Older account reports a later preference for reliable station loading as loose cones became less available in advanced play.","engineering_analysis":"An autonomous detector can help only if it resolves a pose early enough for the claw to reach it safely. The value of floor cone recovery depends on usable supply.","interfaces":"Vision adjustment, arm pose and chassis heading affect first contact.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test off-center and occluded cones, with a deterministic recovery if the detection is lost.","unknowns":"Vision code, station balance and chronology.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-1323-madtown-robotics/435870","https://youtu.be/hz3MolcRe2M"]}],"revisions":["Separate ETR 19 from the team's COTS concepts. Older synopsis describes tipped-cone recovery and evolving station preference without installed dates."],"transferable_principles":["Compare both supply paths at the same gripper and measure the cost of waiting for handoff. text: {"robot_id":"2023-254","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2023-breakdown-technical-binder-code-q-a/443167","title":"254 BREAKDOWN technical release","locator":"Team posts 1, 6 and 8","review_basis":"Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.","facts":"Team chose a repeatable feeder approach, then rear vertical elevator, slightly upward three-stage Laterator and dual-piece claw. Same-face pickup/score complicated autonomous turns. Floor intake translates on printed blocks lined with PTFE tape. Team cites light PEEK rollers on Laterator pins and less need for forks by Championship.","limitations":"The Q&A is team retrospective. PDF text was unavailable in this review. Exact load margins and event installations need separate evidence."},{"url":"https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2023-Public/blob/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2023/subsystems/Superstructure.java","title":"Team 254 Superstructure.java","locator":"GoalState and enabled-loop control, blob 0dae282181b7ef7b4965fe37edf491f2a546195c","review_basis":"Read published Java through repository contents.","facts":"Separate feeder, floor and node goals specify lift and Laterator positions. Mid/high cone actions include lowering, with a distinct autonomous high-cone action. Feeder mode conditionally limits extension current in position. Ground intake logic commands extension and roller states.","limitations":"Released source establishes implemented logic and setpoints. It does not establish use in a given match."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"BREAKDOWN used a rear-mounted vertical elevator and a slightly rising telescoping Laterator to move a dual-piece claw up and forward. Team 254 started from a preferred cycle at the feeder. Its driver could drive firmly into the station with the claw up and in, then capture the piece repeatably. That decision shaped the lift and claw layout. Using the same robot face at pickup and scoring made the driver’s station task predictable but made turn-and-drive autonomous paths harder to tune.","piece_flow":["Raise the claw to a feeder pose and approach the station. The published code includes a lower-current extension mode once the feeder goal is in range.","For floor cubes, deploy the auxiliary translating intake and use the roller to guide the cube toward the claw. Floor and feeder goals use separate states in the release.","Carry the piece in the claw and position the elevator and Laterator for the node. The release distinguishes mid/high cone lowering from cube placement. Withdraw and return toward travel pose."],"packaging_and_motion":"Keeping the mast at the back gives the tool room to rise while retracted, but the Laterator must then reach from that rear support to the node. A slight upward angle couples extension to height even though both axes are driven separately. A long reach puts torque into the mast and changes stability. The team’s repeated use of a hard feeder approach also makes front frame and bumper load paths part of the scoring design.","subsystems":[{"name":"Elevator and Laterator","construction":"Team describes a vertical elevator with radial ball bearings and a three-stage slightly rising Laterator with light PEEK rollers on dowel pins in metal end caps.","operation":"Raise the assembly and extend for target reach. Release logic uses separate paired goals and different placement actions.","team_rationale":"Team traces the layout to feeder clearance and high-cone reach. It chose PEEK to reduce moving mass.","engineering_analysis":"Model deflection at loaded reach and after the mast sees an impact. Axis separation simplifies targeting while coupling remains through rail angle, deflection and chassis pitch.","interfaces":"Distal gripper mass and guide preload affect the mast and horizontal stages. Hall references are at retracted/bottom hard stops.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect stage tracking, surface wear and homing after bumps. Verify the system can recover after losing encoder position away from the normal starting pose.","unknowns":"Exact loaded stiffness, PEEK wear and current logs.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2023-breakdown-technical-binder-code-q-a/443167","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2023-Public/blob/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2023/subsystems/Superstructure.java"]},{"name":"Claw and translating collector","construction":"Team reports dead-axle claw rollers and floor extension on printed linear blocks lined with low-friction tape.","operation":"The claw receives directly at the station. The floor intake aids pickup, with deploy and roller actions coordinated in code.","team_rationale":"Team chose reliable station cone centering and liked the translation approach inspired by another published robot.","engineering_analysis":"A fixed feeder stop can reduce approach variation but raises impact loads. Floor handoff still needs the roller and claw to agree on where the cube is.","interfaces":"Claw current and Laterator position affect station contact. Floor roller and claw need overlapping reach.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check block contamination, roller retention and low-current behavior after impacts. Test partial cube capture recovery.","unknowns":"Collector fit tolerance and fielded setpoint chronology.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2023-breakdown-technical-binder-code-q-a/443167","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2023-Public/blob/master/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2023/subsystems/Superstructure.java"]},{"name":"Station forks","construction":"Team season specifications and Q&A identify separate deployable forks and a travel-end Hall input.","operation":"The forks allow hanging with robots on the balanced station. Team says quick triple balancing reduced use late in the season.","team_rationale":"Team retained the forks at Chezy Champs and cites rear ballast as a side benefit.","engineering_analysis":"Compare setup reliability and partner compatibility against the frequency of occasions where ordinary docking is insufficient.","interfaces":"Forks have an independent actuation path but share frame, mass and stow volume.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check clearance and recovery from uneven contact before adopting the concept.","unknowns":"Force path details, deployment frequency and partner geometry.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2023-breakdown-technical-binder-code-q-a/443167"]}],"revisions":["Older dossier describes frame-rail and elevator bracing changes after impacts. Team Q&A documents late-season reduction in fork utility."],"transferable_principles":["Start from the driver's repeatable supply interaction. Trace the resulting reach, homing, structure and autonomous rotation requirements before freezing the lift."],"disconfirming_conditions":["This layout loses value if feeder contact is inconsistent, turn time dominates, or extended-stage deflection consumes the placement tolerance."],"remaining_gaps":["Full binder text, event-specific variants, measured handoff performance and fork deployment history."],"recommended_images":["Binder figures for elevator, Laterator and floor intake, plus a source-linked loaded station pose."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2023-1678","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.citruscircuits.org/2023-robot","title":"Tangerine Tumbler","locator":"Scoring, Drivetrain, Operating Interface and Electrical","review_basis":"Read full team robot page.","facts":"Continuous three-stage elevator with MAXTube and WCP bearing blocks. Team specifies 26-inch square frame, MK4i swerve and rear battery placement near the arm pivot.","limitations":"Team page does not date the gripper or fork configurations."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1678-citrus-circuits-2023-cad-and-code-release/437632","title":"1678 CAD and code release","locator":"Team posts 1 and 20","review_basis":"Read team publication and rope termination reply.","facts":"Team tied the lift rope to spacers on the spool and through a shaft hole on the inner stage. Other commenters' roller descriptions are not treated as confirmed."},{"url":"https://youtu.be/r6JDy85dax8","title":"1678 pit interview","locator":"Base dossier and supplement","review_basis":"Inherited synopsis. Full captions unavailable in this review.","facts":"Older account describes the pivoting lift assembly, intake revisions and shortened arm-mounted forks.","limitations":"Installed dates and load limits remain unresolved."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Tangerine Tumbler used one roller tool for cones and cubes on a continuously rigged pivoting elevator assembly. The team robot page explains how the tool contacts both pieces and how most heavy components were placed low in a compact frame. The older interview describes forks that reuse the scoring structure for a station task. A service detail in the written release adds a practical constraint. The lift rope stretched in use and the team periodically retied it to remove slack.","piece_flow":["The front roller pair acquires an upright cone. A cube sits lower, where the rear roller helps hold it.","The same tool retains the piece while the pivot and lift move to the scoring pose. The team reports node selection updates the scoring goal.","Release and return to pickup. LEDs communicate the desired piece to the human player. The fork sequence described in the older account is separate from scoring."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team kept most motors near the bellypan and the battery toward the rear near the arm pivot. This can help preserve wheel contact as the tool swings and rises. The raised carriage and loaded tool still move the center of mass. The compact chassis must fit the pivot, moving rope, electrical routing and retained piece, with enough room to retension the lift in the pit.","subsystems":[{"name":"Pivoting continuous elevator","construction":"Team confirms three stages, MAXTube and WCP blocks. Release reply describes spool spacers and rope termination through a shaft hole. Pivot architecture comes from the older account.","operation":"Raise the tool continuously while the pivot sets reach direction. Restore rope tension as needed.","team_rationale":"Team links the low packaging to center of gravity and agility.","engineering_analysis":"Rope stretch can change stage coordination and reference repeatability. A fast loaded stroke needs guide alignment and predictable rope tracking.","interfaces":"Lift reactions pass through the pivot to the frame. Rope and tool wiring share the structure.","service_and_failure_modes":"Time rope retensioning and verify knots, repeatability and full travel after service. Inspect exposed wiring and guides after impact.","unknowns":"Rigging path, tension target and loaded deflection.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2023-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/1678-citrus-circuits-2023-cad-and-code-release/437632","https://youtu.be/r6JDy85dax8"]},{"name":"Three-roller tool","construction":"Team specifies layered silicone on polycarbonate rollers and separate front and rear roles.","operation":"Acquire either piece and retain it directly for scoring.","team_rationale":"Team distinguishes roller roles by piece. Older dossier reports multiple iterations and a crossbar material change.","engineering_analysis":"A shared floor pose can still require different compression and seating for each piece. Check tip force and lateral release error separately.","interfaces":"Tool mass and capture geometry affect stability, node clearance and approach tolerance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the roller layers and crossbars after side hits. Test whether damaged floor contacts still allow a station route.","unknowns":"Final version, contact forces and release timing.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2023-robot","https://youtu.be/r6JDy85dax8"]},{"name":"Forks and station interface","construction":"Arm-mounted forks and shortening are inherited. Team page separately reports fast docking with LED assistance.","operation":"Older account describes engagement and lifting the chassis with existing scoring actuators.","team_rationale":"Older synopsis associates shorter forks with easier alignment and access from either side.","engineering_analysis":"Shared actuators save space but see different loads when lifting the chassis. Check support transitions and uneven contact.","interfaces":"Forks share the arm and frame force path. Stow affects scoring clearance.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test asymmetric contact and safe return to standard docking after a failed setup.","unknowns":"Installed dates, measured loads and actual use.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2023-robot","https://youtu.be/r6JDy85dax8"]}],"revisions":["Older synopsis reports aluminum replacing carbon fiber in intake crossbars and shorter forks. Written release directly confirms periodic rope retensioning."],"transferable_principles":["Treat rope termination as a routine service interface. Evaluate both load paths when scoring actuators double as endgame hardware."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The shared lift loses value when partner or station geometry creates loads outside the scoring structure's capacity. In the team's account, a full-width hex shaft would have bent permanently under impacts that the roller tube itself could survive. The design therefore separates the roller's local axle supports from the cross-robot synchronization path. The observed failures show where durability moved next. Both the bolts at the roller supports and the chain in the deployment mechanism remained vulnerable. The public release is unusually explicit about the differences between the assembly drawing and the machine the team actually serviced.","piece_flow":["The compliant collector pulls a floor note into the protected feed area described in the older dossier.","The inherited path stages the note for the asymmetric launcher or the separate endgame delivery mechanism. The release discussion does not specify the complete routing sequence."],"packaging_and_motion":"The pickup's rigid cross shaft sits inside the frame while the roller spans the exposed mouth. That frees the outer roller to bow without relying on a long shaft. Ensure the bow envelope clears the bumper and internal rollers, and check whether a bent or partially displaced roller can retract. At the upper mechanism, use the as-built shaft length and actual surgical tubing when checking clearance, not the release image alone.","subsystems":[{"name":"Compliant intake rollers","construction":"Polycarbonate tube, short end axle segments, tube plugs and bolted side supports. Later supports used purchased 3/8-inch OD spacers.","operation":"Roll to acquire while elastically deflecting during a hit.","team_rationale":"The team wanted resilience and low weight. Larger bolts could shift failure into the plug or mount.","interfaces":"Axial retention, tube clearance, side plate spacing and replaceable roller ends.","service_and_failure_modes":"Axle bolts sheared in use. Compare change time, repeat alignment and whether an impact can pull the plug out of the tube.","unknowns":"Wall thickness, bolt grade, actual peak deflection and frequency.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2024-robot-cad-and-code-release/477799"]},{"name":"Deployment and chassis","construction":"Chain and an in-frame cross shaft mechanically link left and right.","operation":"Deploy and retract both sides together.","team_rationale":"A cross link ties the sides without needing a rigid crossbar in the exposed collector.","engineering_analysis":"An offset collision can drive load into both sides of the linkage. Proposed check: hit one side at an angle and try to stow before realigning it.","unknowns":"Chain load and whether a sacrificial coupling or alternate drive would maintain useful recovery.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2024-robot-cad-and-code-release/477799"]},{"name":"Elevator, shooter and service","construction":"Older dossier describes asymmetric launch and trap hardware. The release confirms elevator shaft reuse for surgical tubing and shortened actual shooter shafts.","operation":"Move the scorer and operate the chain assist without contacting nearby structure.","team_rationale":"The team reused available hardware and suppressed electronics in CAD for performance.","engineering_analysis":"A visible shaft may be an obsolete design remnant or a useful assist mounting point. A service plan needs the actual machine and wiring view.","interfaces":"Verify tubing travel, shaft clearance and access to the drill pattern and electronics.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare release geometry to actual repairs and hardware before deriving clearances or spares.","unknowns":"Event-specific wire routing, shot settings and complete feed sequence.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2024-robot-cad-and-code-release/477799","https://youtu.be/bGivb7bY7kI"]}],"revisions":["Team confirmed spacer substitution, shorter installed shooter shafts and reuse from an earlier climber. The repository separates end-of-Champs and offseason software."],"transferable_principles":["Trace impact loads beyond the flexible part and check whether the robot can still stow after failure. Release CAD and pit configuration should be reconciled before copying."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The flex design loses its advantage if it causes roller-to-frame contact or an unrecoverable deployment-chain failure. A stiffer assembly may be preferable when replaceable supports can absorb impacts at lower repair cost."],"remaining_gaps":["Championship state logic, installed geometry at the note handoff and fault-rate measurements."],"recommended_images":["Release post 3 electronics layout and climber assist images","Intake roller plug and protected cross-shaft view"]}

This makes the important trade visible. The machine saves mechanical couplings but must deliver four coordinated wheel speeds while the transfer presents a note with repeatable compression.","piece_flow":["The two entrances converge on a common path. Older material describes sensing and supporting the note on a low-friction plate.","The inherited pivoting handoff maintains compression while delivering the note to the launcher.","The launcher sets angle and wheel speeds. text: {"robot_id":"2024-1678","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://github.com/frc1678/C2024-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team1678/frc2024/subsystems/Superstructure.java","title":"Nik public Superstructure.java","locator":"Beam-break declarations, updateShootingSetpoints, intakeToHoldTransition, fireState and elevator transitions","review_basis":"Read Java implementation","facts":["The release declares separate serializer, feeder and amp beam breaks. Feeder detection triggers intake clearing and stops the serializer in the hold sequence.","Fire waits on the shooter request then feeds until the feeder beam clears. Amp extension waits on the amp beam and uses a motion plan.","Speaker targeting passes measured chassis velocity to its shooting solution. The published command uses the same setpoint on both shooter outputs in the reviewed method."],"limitations":"Code on main is not pinned to an event. A declared sensor does not authenticate all physical installations."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc1678/C2024-Public","title":"Citrus Circuits 2024 public robot code","locator":"README and package descriptions","review_basis":"Read team release documentation","facts":["Team calls the 2024 robot Nik. A request system coordinates intake, index rollers and elevator. The motion planner is intended to avoid intake/elevator interference."],"limitations":"The older corpus uses Epsilon. No source reviewed here establishes its scope as a separate version name."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Nik combines a deployed intake, chassis-aimed variable-angle shooting and a distinct elevated placement route. The public software makes the coordination visible. Different beam breaks identify a note at the serializer, feeder or amp stage. Once the feeder sees a note, separate requests clear the intake and stop the transfer. The elevator is a second destination, with software ordering to make space around the deployed collector. Together these details explain why this machine can share volume without assuming every mechanism can move simultaneously.","piece_flow":["Older corpus describes a full-width over-bumper collector and guides into the serializer. The code starts the pickup and serializer while the feeder is idle.","Feeder beam interruption causes the serializer to idle and the intake to clear and tuck. The note can wait short of the shooter.","Fire waits for the shooter, runs the serializer/feeder and watches for feeder clearance. The alternate placement route uses amp beam confirmation before extension and during release."],"packaging_and_motion":"The vertical scorer and deployed intake overlap enough that motion order matters. In the amp score transition, intake clearance precedes elevator retraction and final intake tuck. That is a geometric constraint expressed as a sequence. If the robot loses its reference on one axis, simply replaying the nominal sequence may be insufficient. Draw safe escape directions at each state, including a note trapped at the boundary.","subsystems":[{"name":"Deployed intake and staging","construction":"Inherited over-bumper collector, centering blocks and replaceable side assemblies. Code confirms deploy actuator, serializer, feeder and three declared beam breaks.","operation":"Acquire until feeder occupancy, then clear and tuck the collector and stop the path.","team_rationale":"Published controls distinguish a note held for a shot from one in the elevator.","engineering_analysis":"Sensor distinctions let the drive team or state machine recover based on where the note actually is. A clear beam through the open center of a ring does not necessarily mean empty unless sensor placement and timing support that interpretation.","interfaces":"Intake clearance, feeder datum and sensor threshold need to stay valid when the rollers or funnel are serviced.","service_and_failure_modes":"Exercise partial capture, skewed notes and failure to clear a beam. Inspect whether an operator can interrupt and recover without losing a held note.","unknowns":"Physical sensor brackets, false readings and event-installed versions.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc1678/C2024-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team1678/frc2024/subsystems/Superstructure.java"]},{"name":"Elevator and amp rollers","construction":"Separate elevator, roller stage and amp beam break are visible in the code.","operation":"Verify occupancy, move using a clearance plan, release and order the return motions.","team_rationale":"README identifies avoiding contact between the elevator and intake as the planner's purpose.","engineering_analysis":"A short commanded path is only safe if it lies inside a clearance region with backlash, flex and sensor drift included. A timed recovery on one axis may need a slower or mechanically bounded route.","interfaces":"Overlap of intake, elevator, held note and stowed chassis envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test start from an interrupted state and replace one damaged intake side, then rerun the clearance check.","unknowns":"Geometric margins, state timeouts outside reviewed methods and trap success.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc1678/C2024-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team1678/frc2024/subsystems/Superstructure.java"]},{"name":"Speaker aim and feed readiness","construction":"Code computes heading, hood and shooter setpoints from field pose and passes measured velocity for speaker targeting.","operation":"Coordinate chassis heading and release after shooter readiness.","team_rationale":"README describes a heading override during auto-align and separate shooting/ferry maps.","engineering_analysis":"Motion compensation should be validated by shot residual versus chassis velocity and pose age. A drive-induced error can look like a hood calibration error.","interfaces":"Pose timestamps, hood position, wheel readiness and feeder edge timing.","service_and_failure_modes":"Log all four during moving shots and after localization loss.","unknowns":"Actual tuned map range, camera occlusion and hit rates by pose.","source_urls":["https://github.com/frc1678/C2024-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team1678/frc2024/subsystems/Superstructure.java"]}],"revisions":["Team release names Nik. The older dossier name and hardware history remain distinct from the source revision studied here."],"transferable_principles":["Model collision-safe motion ordering explicitly. Use distinct sensing for a captured note, a ready feed and a loaded secondary scorer."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A shared envelope is a poor transfer if damage or lost reference leaves no safe recovery path. Moving shots lose value when localization age or heading lag exceeds the release tolerance."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-pinned code, primary mechanical assembly sections, caption review and logged shot outcomes."],"recommended_images":["Side elevation showing intake clearance poses and amp travel","Feeder and amp beam locations with a note present"]}

title: 2024-1690 Doppler complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-1690","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838","title":"Orbit releases Doppler CAD","locator":"Release and low-profile discussion","review_basis":"Read team release and technical response","facts":["Orbit released CAD for Doppler. The team emphasized its low height and described tradeoffs against other robots' intake, shooter, amp and trap concepts."],"limitations":"Team comparison is qualitative. It does not establish outcomes under a common test."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838?page=5","title":"Orbit CAD technical replies","locator":"Posts on lower kicker, pass control, service joint and arm homing","review_basis":"Read team replies","facts":["Orbit says a lower roller lifts the note first. Top-first compression tended to drag the note on carpet and draw more current in testing.","Field location selects one of two preset passing angles. The compact pivot uses relative motor sensing and a closed-position Hall check at startup.","Interlocking shooter mount features add rigidity for service. The complete shooter still requires removal of a belt-coupled shaft."],"limitations":"No current traces or fixture measurements. No CAD geometry or full video captions re-read."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Doppler prioritized a very low travel profile. The robot therefore had to acquire a flat, compliant ring without pinning it to the carpet, guide it through a constrained path and aim by moving the shooter in pitch and the chassis in yaw. Orbit's technical answers identify a specific acquisition choice that helped. The bottom roller made the first contact and lifted the note into the next contacts. The compact package also drove a sensing compromise at the arm pivot and a mechanical joint intended to preserve stiffness while permitting removal.","piece_flow":["The bottom roller catches the approaching rim and lifts it into the feed. The alternative top-first pinch caused carpet drag in the team's tests.","The inherited record routes the note into the pivoted launcher and alternate placement functions. The exact contact sequence beyond acquisition was outside the reviewed replies.","The public answer identifies separate flat and high passing trajectories selected using field position. This describes passing modes, distinct from the normal speaker calibration."],"packaging_and_motion":"A low robot can preserve a route under the stage, but the usable space between carpet, bumper, first roller and electronics is small. That makes the leading contact, suspension deflection and service stack-up critical. The pivot is compact enough that Orbit chose a Hall reference at its closed position instead of an absolute angle sensor. Two travel barriers physically support the shooter near its edges in the team explanation.","subsystems":[{"name":"Bottom-first floor pickup","construction":"A low leading roller encounters the note before the upper roller can pinch it against carpet.","operation":"Kick the rim upward and immediately capture it with the rest of the intake.","team_rationale":"The team reported less carpet drag, lower current and favorable capture compared with its top-compression trial.","engineering_analysis":"The roller must apply enough upward impulse for the next contact to take over without pushing the note ahead. Required grip and surface speed will depend on note stiffness and vehicle speed.","interfaces":"Carpet, bumper lip, note edge, lower roller and second contact define the capture envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Compare current and successful capture across approach speed and worn notes. Watch first contact in slow motion after a bracket replacement.","unknowns":"Actual operating clearances and current distribution.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838?page=5"]},{"name":"Pivot, aiming and homing","construction":"Compact shooter pivot with relative motor feedback, closed-position Hall sensor and mechanical travel supports.","operation":"Start from a known closed condition. Aim the chassis and set pitch for the shot. Select a preset passing pitch from field position.","team_rationale":"The team cited space as the reason for omitting an absolute sensor at that pivot.","engineering_analysis":"An at-home check can be robust while adding an operational dependency after a reset. A robot disabled mid-travel needs a way to restore the datum without forcing the arm against an obstacle.","interfaces":"Pivot stops, hall alignment, pass zones and chassis aim.","service_and_failure_modes":"Reboot at home, off home and after a Hall bracket shift. Verify the fault and recovery path independently.","unknowns":"Angle tolerances, deployed event code and handoff alignment.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838?page=5"]},{"name":"Launcher mounting and service","construction":"Interlocking plates and clamshell around blocks supporting the main shaft. A belt still couples a shaft to the assembly.","operation":"Keep the joint rigid in operation and separate the launcher for service.","team_rationale":"The team explained that interlocking profiles stiffen the attachment compared with relying on screws alone.","engineering_analysis":"The service gain depends on actual extraction order and whether the locating faces wear. Measure return to aim datum after multiple swaps.","interfaces":"Shaft removal, belt release, wiring and tool access all affect the real service time.","service_and_failure_modes":"Practice removal and calibrate after reassembly. Inspect locator faces for trapped debris or impact wear.","unknowns":"Fit specification, assembly time and repeatability data.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838?page=5"]}],"revisions":["Team describes top-first ground compression as a tested alternative and the lower kicker as the adopted approach. Detailed competition revision boundaries remain in the older dossier."],"transferable_principles":["For a sliding ring, test the initial contact direction before specifying more ground compression. Verify power loss and restart for any compact mechanism that uses relative position sensing."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A bottom-first roller can fail if it throws pieces forward or if the next contact cannot take them in before the chassis overtakes them. Extreme low packaging loses value if clearance or recovery degrades primary cycles."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-specific full-path release drawings, measured pickup current and accuracy, full captions and installed arm recovery behavior."],"recommended_images":["CAD reply figures for leading intake geometry and clamshell joint","Side section through the shooter in travel pose"]}

title: 2024-2056 LOW-KEY complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-2056","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf","title":"OP Robotics 2024 Crescendo Technical Binder","locator":"Drivetrain, Swerve Module, Intake, Frame and Tower, Shoulder Gearbox, Shooter and Climber","review_basis":"Read team binder text","facts":["Front MK4i modules are modified to clear the note and carry kicker mounts. One motor drives opposed intake rows through a gearbox and belts.","The note passes under a solid front steel bar. The tower carries a dead-axle shooter pivot and low-backlash shoulder drive.","Post-Newmarket changes include braced aluminum intake plates, a rear reinforcement and revised flywheels and hooks."],"limitations":"Published values and intentions belong to the binder configuration. Full tolerance, maintenance and installation records are absent."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2024-technical-binder-release/465867","title":"LOW-KEY binder and drawing release","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read primary release announcement","facts":["Team identifies the 2024 robot as LOW-KEY and publishes binder and drawing package."],"limitations":"No drawing dimensions derived in this pass."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"LOW-KEY is built around a low protected note path and a variable-angle scorer. The front end is one mechanism in practice even though its parts belong to the chassis, swerve and collector. A front bar leaves the ring a passage beneath it. Modified drive modules clear that passage and carry nearby intake hardware. A fixed tower supports a compact launcher that both receives and aims the note. The team's choice to pursue low pivot backlash made the structure and gearbox part of the shot-angle measurement system.","piece_flow":["The front roller pinches a floor note against carpet. Opposed linked rollers move it upward and toward the center.","Belts carry motion between conveyor shafts and help guide the note between roller pairs. An intake photoeye supports automation.","The scorer receives the note on small feed rollers, applies side pre-compression and accelerates it through independent left/right flywheel pairs. Shoulder pitch also enables amp geometry."],"packaging_and_motion":"Keep the note corridor drawn alongside the wheel and gear envelopes. The inverted front module motor and modified bottom plate are local accommodations for that corridor. A cover keeps notes out of the electronics bay. The pivot support is a fixed tower axle, which gives a defined load path from shooter to frame. In a copy, the shoulder transmission and tower together determine whether a motor encoder reflects true exit angle during acceleration.","subsystems":[{"name":"Integrated front intake","construction":"Steel front member, aluminum frame, modified swerve mounts and multi-roller pickup driven by a Kraken through belts and a reversing gearbox.","operation":"Pinch the note, center it and move it up the conveyor under the front of the chassis.","team_rationale":"The team wanted a protected intake with forgiving perimeter and open-field pickup, plus centered shooter delivery.","engineering_analysis":"The front module is a note-path part. A nominally equivalent swerve replacement can put a motor or fastener in the capture corridor. Wide contact only buys useful acquisition if both edges hand off reliably.","interfaces":"Carpet, bumper opening, steel crossmember, corner module and kicker mounts.","service_and_failure_modes":"After an impact, measure the mouth and conveyor nip at both sides. Confirm a replacement module preserves the passage before re-enabling automated pickup.","unknowns":"Measured capture distribution and post-impact datums.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Shoulder, shooter and feed","construction":"Bronze bushings around a dead axle, bonded gears and custom broached sprockets. Feed and passive pre-compression rollers lead to independent side flywheels.","operation":"Set the pitch and feed the note into a repeatable compressed state before launch.","team_rationale":"The team sought small backlash during motion and shots so it could use motor encoder feedback. Side speed differences apply spin.","engineering_analysis":"The reported radial pre-compression and flywheel nip act in different directions. A damaged ring can retain asymmetry into the shot. Under load, elastic deflection can remain even when free backlash is small.","interfaces":"Frame stiffness, shoulder mesh and launch readiness interact with note centering.","service_and_failure_modes":"Measure physical exit angle under acceleration and torque reversal. Track angle after chain adjustment and after a representative hit.","unknowns":"Shot dispersion, long-term gear fit and actual angular compliance.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Climber","construction":"Binder documents a double hook actuated by two pneumatic cylinders, with extension flow management and integrated camera mounting.","operation":"Reach the chain and retract to load it. The revised hook accommodates a chain already pulled down by a partner.","team_rationale":"Fast reliable engagement and partner clearance were requirements.","engineering_analysis":"The chain geometry can inform an electric design. Retraction force and holding behavior must be sized for that new actuator and evaluated across full stroke.","interfaces":"Hooks, cylinders, frame brackets and note-camera mount share space.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect one-sided loading and retention. Verify electrical actuation separately if transferring the reach geometry.","unknowns":"Measured impact loads and actual match-by-match climb outcome.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Binder explicitly marks post-Newmarket reinforcements, flywheel change and double-hook update."],"transferable_principles":["Make the note corridor an explicit chassis interface. Qualify true loaded pivot angle before relying on motor feedback alone."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The integrated front package is a poor copy if module swaps alter the throat or field-contact deflection consumes the floor gap. The published pneumatic drive is outside the workspace's electric-actuation scope."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact event revisions, logged shot and climb data, dimensional inspection of front intake interfaces."],"recommended_images":["Binder front module and intake views","Binder shoulder final-drive and flywheel/pre-compression figures"]}

title: 2024-254 Vortex complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-254","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf","title":"Team 254 VORTEX technical binder","locator":"Drivebase through Climber and Teleop Automation","review_basis":"Read team binder mechanism text","facts":["Mecanum and lateral funnel wheels feed an annular path. Feeder motors can reverse the direction of circulation to shorten the path or recover.","The turret uses bidirectional cable management across a stated 720-degree range. The second shooter revision has feed rollers, four flywheels and an adjustable sector-gear hood.","A separate Amplifier elevator receives from the feeder, can accept a human-player note and reacts against the stage with passive wheels."],"limitations":"Binder gives architecture and selected specifications. No independent shot or climb timing distribution."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2024-vortex-technical-binder-code-q-a/472576","title":"VORTEX binder and code release","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read team publication announcement","facts":["Team publishes binder and code for VORTEX."],"limitations":"Code execution and event revision validation were outside this entry."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"VORTEX uses a continuous note route around a moving launcher so the shooter can keep aiming while the chassis picks up a note. A floor collector and circular feeder are therefore as central to the architecture as the turret itself. The feeder can send the piece around either direction and can also supply a separate elevator carriage for amp and trap. The payoff is concurrent aim and acquisition. It requires a circular volume, wire travel and a reliable way to hand a deformable ring across a moving boundary.","piece_flow":["Under-bumper rollers and lateral funneling guide the note into the feeder.","High-grip rollers carry it around the turret in the chosen direction and into the launcher, or redirect it toward the Amplifier.","For speaker, feeder rollers supply a quad-flywheel shooter with adjustable hood. For amp/trap the carriage receives, rises as required and feeds the note downward. It also offers a separate human-player loading route."],"packaging_and_motion":"The annular feeder occupies the same plan-view region in which a conventional drivetrain might put electronics or bracing. The rotating throat and bidirectional energy chain add a sweep above it. The Amplifier and intake share sideplates and use a distinct endgame envelope. The binder places the battery opposite those mechanisms for balance. An endgame package drawing must add stage reaction forces to the normal lift load case.","subsystems":[{"name":"Intake and annular feeder","construction":"Under-bumper intake with mecanum and lateral contacts. The feeder uses high-grip wheels and independent drives for bidirectional routing.","operation":"Center and carry the note toward the shooter at its present angle, with the other route available when useful.","team_rationale":"The team sought uninterrupted target tracking and shorter feeder travel.","engineering_analysis":"Any-heading access needs continuous capture through the turns. The short route could still be slower if its entrance pinches or the turret is moving away from it.","interfaces":"Intake exit, annular guide and rotating feed throat must stay aligned with a note deforming under roller load.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test skewed notes near each routing transition and deliberate reversal after loss of contact.","unknowns":"Measured route latency, jam frequency and clearances at each yaw.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Turret, cable system and shooter","construction":"Rotating shooter with bidirectional energy chain, second-revision quad-flywheel launcher and sector-gear hood.","operation":"Track speaker heading while the drivetrain moves. Set pitch and feed after the shot is ready.","team_rationale":"Binder explains the turret as a means to align faster and shoot on the move.","engineering_analysis":"The main transfer lesson is to decouple motions when concurrent work saves actual time. The same reasoning can apply to staging and chassis aim in a fixed-heading design. Cable drag and wide yaw travel must be evaluated under continuous cycling.","interfaces":"Cable travel, angle reference and moving feed entrance. Camera measurements also depend on orientation.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test loss of reference, cable extremes and readiness when the feeder reverses.","unknowns":"Logged angle accuracy, cable life and event-specific software.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Amplifier and climb","construction":"Roller carriage on elevator, passive stage-contact wheels and a Dyneema winch drive.","operation":"Supply amp, trap or an alternate player intake. Load the chain and react against the structure before trap release.","team_rationale":"The team assigned multiple functions to the carriage, including aiding a passing strategy.","engineering_analysis":"Stage contact should constrain the suspended chassis while leaving note placement loads to the carriage. Different chain and trap geometry can move that reaction into the guides.","interfaces":"Climber line, passive rollers and carriage position establish final trap geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect rope wear, one-sided reaction and clearance if a note stops during climb.","unknowns":"Loaded fixture measurements and repeatability by chain approach.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Binder explicitly identifies the shooter as second revision. Exact cutover and earlier feed variants need event records."],"transferable_principles":["Compare gain from concurrent aim and acquisition against the longest realistic feed time. Separate climbing load reaction from placement precision."],"disconfirming_conditions":["The circular feed is unlikely to pay for its space when a fixed exit or short chassis turn meets timing. Stage reaction hardware is specific to the supported geometry and load direction."],"remaining_gaps":["Event-pinned code, physical revision map, feeder timing versus yaw and moving shot distributions."],"recommended_images":["Binder labeled full robot","Annular feeder and bidirectional cable routing","Loaded Amplifier/stage interface"]}

text: {"robot_id":"2024-3467","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf","title":"Windham Windup GSD technical binder for Nocturne","locator":"PDF pp. 6–10 and 13, arm, shooter, intake and autonomous intake stopping","review_basis":"Read team binder text","facts":["The arm uses four chain runs with turnbuckles and a direct through-bore encoder. The intake uses passive wedges and a protected fast leading roller.","Powered feeder rollers accelerate the note before wheel contact. HDPE panels guide it, and structural tubing stiffens the shooter.","Autonomous logic stops the fixed intake after detection to reduce accidental additional note possession."],"limitations":"GSD publication describes a specific configuration and does not certify later trap or arm changes."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-3467-2025-build-blog/473888/1","title":"Windham Windup 2025 kickoff retrospective","locator":"First post, offseason discussion","review_basis":"Read team retrospective","facts":["Team reports late-season Nocturne availability problems and less use of its alpha robot due to changes and wiring issues."],"limitations":"Availability observations do not identify a common root cause."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Nocturne uses a fast protected intake and a moving arm carrying a variable-angle shooter. The team connects capture speed to contested autonomous notes, where the drivetrain can otherwise overtake the capture mechanism. The shot itself depends on more than flywheel speed. Small feed rollers give the ring initial motion and fixed guides keep it moving into the wheel contacts. The arm borrows from prior team experience and uses direct output sensing and tensioned chain to preserve aim.","piece_flow":["The front roller catches the rim while passive wedges bring the note into the capture corridor.","Staging rollers accelerate the note along the supported path and into the shooter wheels. Early stop logic limits multiple-note possession during autonomous pickup.","The arm establishes exit angle for speaker shots. The inherited dossier also describes shared arm geometry for amp and climb, and later blower trap work."],"packaging_and_motion":"The low intake opening and shooter pivot define separate tolerances. If chassis braking changes the gap or a worn note catches at a wedge, higher roller speed alone will not restore capture. On the arm, a compact hard stop and direct encoder establish reference, but the arms, chains and guides still carry the forces from moving and shooting. The team relocated its encoder for access after earlier problems, which is a concrete service choice independent of shot modeling.","subsystems":[{"name":"Fast protected collector","construction":"Polycarbonate rollers, compliant leading contacts and passive centering wedges. Team binder describes one Falcon drive and a fixed under-bumper position.","operation":"Take notes at drivetrain speed and stop when detection establishes possession.","team_rationale":"The team wanted immediate capture when contesting midline notes and used stopping logic to reduce the chance of taking a second note.","engineering_analysis":"Compare effective roller grip and piece speed with the maximum realistic approach. Extra speed can increase note deformation or drive a second piece into a stopped path.","interfaces":"Bumper opening, wedges, feed roller and detection logic share responsibility for serialization.","service_and_failure_modes":"Proposed tests are a rapid second arrival and a first note wedged off-center. Verify reversal can free either without drawing the second note farther in.","unknowns":"Installed sensor geometry, field pickup rate and timing margins.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf"]},{"name":"Scoring arm and angle control","construction":"Four tensioned chain runs, turnbuckles, direct arm angle encoder and physical hard stop.","operation":"Set pitch and retain angle through the launch event.","team_rationale":"Team attributes chain tension to reducing backlash and encoder relocation to improved access.","engineering_analysis":"Encoder location matters because it measures the driven arm directly. The shooter structure can still flex downstream of that measurement and alter the actual exit angle.","interfaces":"Chain runs, arm shaft, guide stiffness and stowed clearance under stage.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check angle error under torque reversal and settle after a chain service. Verify the hard-stop reference with the unloaded and loaded mechanism.","unknowns":"Measured exit-angle change under acceleration and shot repeatability.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf"]},{"name":"Shooter and secondary functions","construction":"Team documents grip-taped feed rollers, HDPE guides and a stiffened flywheel structure. Later endgame functions come from the older dossier.","operation":"Give the note initial velocity before final acceleration. Move the arm for different releases.","team_rationale":"The team wanted a light moving assembly that would remain stiff and feed consistently.","engineering_analysis":"Pre-acceleration can improve consistency if it keeps the ring in control up to the flywheel nip. It can also introduce skew if the top and bottom guides grip unevenly.","interfaces":"Feeder exit, panel spacing and flywheel entry. Shared arm functions add load cases.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect wear of the grip surface and guide alignment after impact. Test damaged notes and recovery before copying the nominal speed.","unknowns":"Later trap construction, loaded climb geometry and exact revision boundaries.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Binder contrasts its capture with a beta wedge arrangement and records direct encoder relocation. Later blower development is inherited and needs a versioned primary read."],"transferable_principles":["Match capture velocity to actual drivetrain approaches. Use output-side sensing and accessible adjustments when a transmission is expected to wear."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Faster capture may give worse net throughput if it doubles or folds notes. A shared arm loses value if its climb or placement features reduce primary scorer uptime."],"remaining_gaps":["Review later trap publication and event installation, actual arm calibration and measured capture distribution."],"recommended_images":["Binder arm chain and encoder diagrams","Intake wedge and feeder side views"]}

title: 2024-3847 Ultraviolet complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2024-3847","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.spectrum3847.org/seasons/2024/","title":"Spectrum 2024 season build log","locator":"Belton and Houston event recaps, days 62–64 and Houston Upgrades","review_basis":"Read team event and development text","facts":["At Belton, a deformed top roller trapped a note against a blocker. Misfeeds also turned notes upright. The team replaced the roller and used eject/re-intake during matches.","Amp/trap gearbox tilted and jammed. A fastener at the bearing location stopped the cantilever in the reported fix.","Houston changes include new rollers, metal intake gearbox, steel launcher sector, vision launch and a revised climber."],"limitations":"Some sections discuss practice robot and 8515 Photon. Only 3847 competition robot observations are used as installed facts. Electrical root cause was unresolved."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Ultraviolet combines floor capture, a variable-angle launcher and a separate route for amp/trap. The team's event notes are especially informative because they show different failures of a piece that rotates inside a constrained path. One note wedged beside a deformed roller, and others flipped upright during feeding. The alternate scorer also failed when its gearbox moved out of line. Those incidents make the key interface clear. A roller or gear can still rotate freely in isolation while the assembled robot can no longer pass a note through the intended route.","piece_flow":["Capture feeds the note past an intake roller and front blocker into the internal path. Belton reports show the path depends on keeping the ring horizontal.","The older dossier describes the primary launcher and a transfer up to amp/trap. The team reports changing the operator climb sequence to automate the secondary feed.","Houston changes included vision-based launch, a refined amp/trap system and a redesigned climber to improve reach over the lower trap lip."],"packaging_and_motion":"The upper intake roller, blocker and front chassis should be drawn with clearance for a bent roller and a skewed ring, as both can occur together. Keep the alternate gearbox supported against reaction torque. The release path changes as the chassis hangs, so the Houston trap work should be evaluated with the lip and chain present. A successful unloaded move is weak evidence for the combined loaded pose.","subsystems":[{"name":"Intake and blocker","construction":"Build log describes intake rollers and a polycarbonate front-rail blocker. Houston added rollers and a metal gearbox.","operation":"Pass a floor note toward the launcher while keeping it horizontal.","team_rationale":"Team wanted to remove known jams and intake failures between events.","engineering_analysis":"A blocker can prevent one wrong path while creating a pinch point next to a deflected roller. Observe the piece and the mechanism together under failure, including the note's tendency to spring upright.","interfaces":"Roller straightness, blocker height and entry guide position determine the allowed shape of the path.","service_and_failure_modes":"Replacement solved one observed jam. Eject/re-intake was an in-match recovery for vertical notes. Verify it after a bent roller as well.","unknowns":"As-built gap, added flap installation and quantitative jam rate.","source_urls":["https://www.spectrum3847.org/seasons/2024/"]},{"name":"Launcher and aiming","construction":"Team reports a launcher sector change to steel and a move to vision-based launching for Houston.","operation":"Set launch angle and use target localization for the shot.","team_rationale":"Steel change follows reported tooth damage. Vision was logged at Belton while still under evaluation.","engineering_analysis":"Moving to vision after data collection lets the team isolate pose changes from mechanical shot behavior. A steel sector can resist tooth damage while moving shock into another drive component.","interfaces":"Sector support, launcher structure and localization share responsibility for the actual shot angle and heading.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect tooth contact and angle calibration after impacts. Replay poor camera conditions before assuming vision improved every shot.","unknowns":"Pitch tolerance, exact active cameras, current data and hit distributions.","source_urls":["https://www.spectrum3847.org/seasons/2024/"]},{"name":"Secondary scorer and chain","construction":"Team reports a separate amp/trap gearbox with bearing support and redesigned climber for higher trap clearance.","operation":"Transfer to the placement path, engage chain and position the note above the lip.","team_rationale":"The team identified a tilted gearbox and need for higher access.","engineering_analysis":"A fastener added at the bearing can control torque reaction that previously cantilevered the transmission. Extra height is only useful if the chassis hangs at the expected angle and the piece stays under control.","interfaces":"Gearbox support, stage lip and chain load all affect the release.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the bearing support and test under side load. Attempt piece recovery with the robot in the loaded fixture.","unknowns":"Exact loaded geometry, field success and final revision details.","source_urls":["https://www.spectrum3847.org/seasons/2024/"]}],"revisions":["Belton exposed intake and placement failures. Houston list identifies distinct mechanical, camera, launch and climb changes. Practice-machine and Photon failures remain separate."],"transferable_principles":["Use event fault reports to trace each jam to contact and support geometry. Validate repairs with a live piece path and representative loaded pose."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A guide change is ineffective if roller deflection still closes the exit. text: {"robot_id":"2024-5940","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.team5940.org/2024","title":"BREAD 2024 season page, Roti","locator":"Robot description and mechanism summary","review_basis":"Read team write-up","facts":["The two-stage elevator carries a differential-speed shooter, can raise it over defense and supports amp/trap. Roti tilts during trap scoring and reverses the note out the rear of the shooter.","Team describes under-bumper acquisition and live/dead axle contacts that hold a note until the scoring pose."],"limitations":"Qualitative team architecture. It gives no measured defense clearances or trap success distribution."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/5940-bread-2024-cad-and-code-release-uncensored-6-piece/466729","title":"Roti CAD, code and binder release Q&A","locator":"Posts 1, 12–14, 17 and 20","review_basis":"Read team technical replies","facts":["The mecanum and tapered feed contacts act to reopen a distorted ring, distinct from inward acquisition centering. Tapered PLA rollers with grip tape retain driving compression near the middle.","Gas springs bias the shooter pivot's backlash to one side. The team also used shims and inline chain tensioners.","Team selected thicker first-stage tube where it saw denting and needed countersunk fasteners."],"limitations":"The tech and electrical binder links were identified. Their full bodies were not re-read here. Team measurements and impressions are condition-specific."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Roti places the shooter and note retention on a two-stage elevator. The robot can travel low, raise its release point and set pitch for different targets. BREAD's note-path explanation distinguishes two tasks that can be easy to conflate. The intake gathers and centers. Farther along the path, specially shaped contacts let the deformed ring spread before the wheels see it. Raising the shooter only helps if the same controlled note survives the lift and exits in a repeatable shape.","piece_flow":["The protected floor intake catches and centers the ring under a raised bumper section.","The handoff retains the note using live/dead axle contacts. Tapered rollers and mecanum contacts act to restore note shape following the intake.","The elevator and pivot position the note. Speaker uses differential flywheel speeds. Amp uses a downward aim, and the team's trap account describes a tilted chassis with the note reversing out of the shooter."],"packaging_and_motion":"The elevator carries a substantial moving assembly, so travel height changes both shot origin and chassis load. The pivot counterbalance can bias drive clearance to one side under nominal gravity. It still needs enough preload at each pitch and while the lift accelerates. The hanging pose should be modeled with the lift extended and the note loaded. The older binder synopsis adds a passive lower hook load transfer that needs direct confirmation before copying.","subsystems":[{"name":"Acquisition and shape recovery","construction":"Under-bumper intake with centering contacts. Team describes outward mecanum action and tapered PLA feed rollers wrapped with grip tape.","operation":"Gather, center and reshape the ring so it reaches the shooter in a more repeatable state.","team_rationale":"The team observed rings arrive distorted from ground pickup and reported better shot consistency after restoring their shape.","engineering_analysis":"Test the guide profile with note stiffness and damage distributions. Inward centering after deformation could increase distortion, while outward force too early could lose orientation entirely.","interfaces":"Intake exit, middle compression, side clearance and launcher nip need coordinated geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect the grip tape and roller surface after repeated reversals. Compare ring shape entering and leaving the taper.","unknowns":"Deformation measurements, speed and pressure settings and wear rates.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/5940-bread-2024-cad-and-code-release-uncensored-6-piece/466729","https://www.team5940.org/2024"]},{"name":"Pivot and elevator","construction":"Two-stage elevator with pivoted shooter. Team specifies two gas springs, shims and chain tensioners and thicker first-stage tubing.","operation":"Translate and aim the scorer while retaining the note. Bias the pivot to one side of its drivetrain clearance.","team_rationale":"Springs address functional backlash. Thicker tubing was selected in response to denting and countersink depth.","engineering_analysis":"A preload can keep the mechanism on one side of its lash under normal load. text: {"robot_id":"2025-604","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-cad-code-release-for-our-2025-robot-the-flush/502824","title":"The Flush CAD and code release","locator":"Post 1 Mechanical Design and Software, posts 14–15 and 20","review_basis":"Read team write-up and detailed replies.","facts":["Single-stage dual-chain elevator, detuned arm, three-sided station funnel, independently driven gripper sides, shared ramp/climb volume and distinct reef-relative and field localization are described.","The team explains cantilever gripper evolution, tube crush block and through-axle stiffness."],"limitations":"Team performance figures are self-reported. This review did not audit linked CAD or implementation files."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"The Flush prioritizes automation from station intake through final placement. A broad loading funnel creates a forgiving upstream interface, while a rigid elevator, arm and wrist keep downstream pose predictable. Mechanical precision supports automation, but arm acceleration still had to be reduced because moving the superstructure affected the whole chassis. The offseason Quixshot is a distinct robot and supplies no evidence about this build.","piece_flow":["Station coral enters a full-width funnel. Upper and lower driven contacts cooperate with the gripper’s two independent sides to seat the pipe.","Elevator sets height and arm and wrist set reach and release orientation.
