For algae the gripper uses separate roller contacts, and the arm can throw toward the net."],"packaging_and_motion":"The 29-inch-square chassis supports a long reach. Cross-braced 2-inch uprights carry elevator guides and cameras, so stiffness benefits both localization and placement. The climb stows beneath the funnel and relies on the rear ramp unfolding to admit the cage. Check both the moving ramp and wiring clearances with the mechanism in intermediate states.","subsystems":[{"name":"Funnel and open-top gripper","construction":"Corrugated plastic funnel, two funnel rollers, four coral rollers and two algae rollers. Left and right gripper sides are independent.","operation":"Receive from three sides, center with opposing contacts, then rotate or eject the piece for the target.","team_rationale":"Team cites weight, stiffness, L1 packing and room for L4 release. An earlier two-plate gripper was bulkier and difficult to stiffen for one-sided wrist actuation.","engineering_analysis":"A shallower release depends on the piece being able to roll out while the chassis retreats. Compare nominal clearance with a bowed pipe, a full trough and hard contact at the reef.","interfaces":"The funnel exits into the wrist at a specific pose and the open gripper must clear branch hardware through retreat.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect cantilever roller support after side loads. Test a skewed or doubled input and confirm the sensor state can recover.","unknowns":"Wear and controlled insertion-angle data.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-cad-code-release-for-our-2025-robot-the-flush/502824"]},{"name":"Elevator and arm","construction":"Chain drive on both sides of a single-stage elevator. Shimmed arm gearbox and through-axle reinforced by gusset and internal crush block.","operation":"Raise the carriage, rotate the arm and maintain reef clearance during approach and retreat.","team_rationale":"The team wanted low backlash and later reduced arm drive to address tipping. The axle ties the carriage together and the block prevents tube collapse under clamp load.","engineering_analysis":"Synchronous side drive reduces racking only when chain lengths and initial tension match. The long arm still imposes a pitching moment and its speed profile matters.","interfaces":"Camera reference is attached to the rigid structure, so impact distortion can move the camera and effector in different ways.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sprocket clamp preload, chain alignment and camera calibration following impact. Evaluate stall current and brownout under combined drive and lift.","unknowns":"Original and final current values must be tied to configuration.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-cad-code-release-for-our-2025-robot-the-flush/502824"]},{"name":"Scoring control and cage access","construction":"Team describes state machine, velocity lookahead, nearest-tag reef localization and separate field localization. text: {"robot_id":"2025-1690","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2025-robot-cad-release/501057","title":"Orbit Whisper CAD release","locator":"Post 1 and team reply on build timeline","review_basis":"Read release text and team development account.","facts":["Ground intake feasibility shaped the robot concept. Retained dossier describes suction, powered transfer and cage-retention changes."],"limitations":"Exact cycle performance and full interview captions not verified."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Whisper separates the high moving structure from much of its drive mass. A continuous-belt differential couples elevator and arm movement, and a lightweight vacuum end effector serves both pieces. The payoff depends on more than suction force. The ground collector and centering conveyor must present a reliable sealing surface, and the lift and arm must coordinate motion without disturbing that seal.","piece_flow":["A four-bar floor collector and floating upper roller acquire coral in the retained design. Powered V geometry centers it before handoff.","The vacuum cup takes the piece from the conveyor, and the differential moves it to the placement pose. The retained account reports a common cup for coral and algae.","Separate cage capture and winch handle endgame."],"packaging_and_motion":"Retained construction places major motors and the vacuum source low. The team's CAD account shows why intake mounting interfaces had to be settled early even though roller geometry was still being tested.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and conveyor","construction":"Retained collapsing polycarbonate linkage, slotted upper roller and powered V conveyor. Team release confirms extended intake development.","operation":"Acquire across pipe orientations, center under driven contact and present a stable sealing pose.","team_rationale":"Team says floor pickup feasibility affected concept selection.","engineering_analysis":"A passive slot adds compliance only in its travel direction. Test upright pipes and edge impacts, since a yawed pipe may load both sides before the roller can float.","interfaces":"Conveyor exit must constrain the pipe for the cup, with room for the loading motion.","service_and_failure_modes":"Retained four-screw removal is worth timing with belt/shaft reconnection and recalibration.","unknowns":"Detailed intake dimensions and acceptance map.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2025-robot-cad-release/501057"]},{"name":"Differential and vacuum","construction":"Closed-belt differential confirmed by reveal. Confirm a lost seal is visible to controls.","unknowns":"Pressure, sensor logic and motion allocation.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2025-robot-cad-release/501057","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064"]},{"name":"Cage capture","construction":"Retained magnetic capture, ratcheted winch and wider wedges.","operation":"Guide a tube into capture and restrain it as the winch loads.","team_rationale":"Retained dossier reports cage slip drove wedge changes.","engineering_analysis":"Use magnet force for acquisition only if a structural load path reliably takes over under tension. Einstein station allocation was tactical."],"transferable_principles":["Define intake interfaces early enough to continue parallel CAD.","Treat seal formation, carry and release as separate validation tasks."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A shared cup is poor fit for porous or inconsistent surfaces.","Independent axes can simplify fallback if coupled actuator limits dominate."],"remaining_gaps":["Dimensioned CAD audit, vacuum pressure and a full match/installation timeline."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2025-robot-cad-release/501057","locator":"CAD release views for conveyor removal, differential routing and vacuum hardware"}]}

title: 2025-341 Miss Daisy XXIII complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-341","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-341-miss-daisy-2025-cad-code-and-documentation-release/500739","title":"Miss Daisy XXIII design release","locator":"Post 1 and response on shoulder gear and pulleys","review_basis":"Read team-authored release and technical responses.","facts":["Floor intake, continuous elevator, lantern shoulder, 180-degree wrist and compact deep climb. Team shortened lantern tooth tips about 0.020 in for smooth transitions and described printed CF-nylon lift pulleys. Software superstructure restricts collision states. Alpha, Beta and Comp were separate builds."],"limitations":"Team cautions that pit renders may differ from CAD after iterations."},{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iKZZWQoEGuDlWmwzl61e7Nzo4c3IQF_k/view?usp=sharing","title":"Miss Daisy design binder","locator":"Corpus dossier and release link","review_basis":"Read retained construction synopsis. Linked viewer did not expose binder body here.","facts":["Retained account describes mock-game selection, direct wrist station fallback, L1 flip and sprung cage latch."],"limitations":"Details are inherited."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Miss Daisy XXIII uses a floor intake to supply a continuous elevator with a shoulder and wrist. The combination can present coral through a wide range of orientations, but that freedom increases the number of dangerous intermediate configurations. The team's software superstructure is part of the mechanical solution, along with a lantern shoulder designed to move smoothly through tooth transitions.","piece_flow":["Floor coral is centered and handed to the wrist. Prior notes identify a direct station alternative.","Elevator, lantern shoulder and wrist move coral to the target. The retained L1 flip places coral above existing trough pieces.","A separate deep-cage subsystem loads through sprung one-way retention in the retained account."],"packaging_and_motion":"The wrist's available rotation can support both a loading pose and release into a crowded L1 trough. Check clearance against the intake, uprights, bumper and reef for the entire path. Keep Alpha, Beta and Comp figures version-labeled because nominally similar mechanisms could be built with different details.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and wrist handoff","construction":"Floor intake and rotating wrist confirmed. Passive centering geometry and direct loading are retained.","operation":"Present the pipe consistently to the wrist before moving the elevator or shoulder out of the load pose.","team_rationale":"Retained binder ties floor pickup selection to mock-game testing.","engineering_analysis":"A direct station mode is a real fallback only if an impact that breaks floor pickup cannot also block the wrist's access or stow.","interfaces":"Collector exit, wrist axis and carriage height share a tolerance stack.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test off-axis arrivals and station feed with collector physically immobilized.","unknowns":"Exact sensors and tolerances.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-341-miss-daisy-2025-cad-code-and-documentation-release/500739","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iKZZWQoEGuDlWmwzl61e7Nzo4c3IQF_k/view?usp=sharing"]},{"name":"Continuous elevator and lantern shoulder","construction":"Continuous lift with printed pulleys, a lantern gear shoulder and a wide wrist rotation.","operation":"Coordinate height, shoulder rotation and wrist angle for placement. Team software constrains allowed states.","team_rationale":"Team adjusted tooth tips to ease tooth transitions.","engineering_analysis":"Gear tooth engagement is sensitive to center distance, plate flex and pin wear. Smooth unloaded travel can mask backlash or lost contact at a long arm reach.","interfaces":"The software envelope needs to reflect actual loaded joint and frame motion.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check first reversal at max reach and inspect pin/tooth marks. Test an interrupted trajectory at every transition.","unknowns":"Cable reeving and full source-state graph.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-341-miss-daisy-2025-cad-code-and-documentation-release/500739"]},{"name":"Compact climb and operating modes","construction":"Deep climber confirmed. Spring latches and motor/chain pivot are retained construction.","operation":"Engage the cage and bring the suspension point toward a usable hang geometry.","team_rationale":"Retained binder connects attachment geometry to CG.","engineering_analysis":"A nominally centered hang can still have poor capture if side loads bind one latch. Validate both capture and retention.","interfaces":"Check the arm's park state and cage clearance throughout the load transition.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test one-sided engagement and repeat a cage load after impact.","unknowns":"Disable retention, installed stops and chronology.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-341-miss-daisy-2025-cad-code-and-documentation-release/500739","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iKZZWQoEGuDlWmwzl61e7Nzo4c3IQF_k/view?usp=sharing"]}],"revisions":["Three development robots and ongoing iteration are directly reported. Exact event transition dates remain open."],"transferable_principles":["Build collision-aware transition states with real swept volumes.","Verify lantern mesh with actual arm load and stiffness."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A simpler station scorer can outperform when ground supply and packed L1 are rare.","A broad wrist envelope pays only if its use justifies tuning and service burden."],"remaining_gaps":["Primary binder text, event revisions and measured collision/placement tolerances."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-341-miss-daisy-2025-cad-code-and-documentation-release/500739","locator":"Release pit-poster and CAD links. Use version-labeled shoulder and floor transfer views."}]}

title: 2025-2910 Spectre complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-2910","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2025/500310","title":"Spectre CAD and tech binder release","locator":"Post 13 and team release discussion","review_basis":"Read team reply on manufacturing.","facts":["Nested arm tubes are face-machined to provide internal chain room without increasing section size. Team highlights tube faces, bearing blocks and pivot parts as difficult fabrication."],"limitations":"Direct measurements of as-built flatness and strength were not made."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-reveal-2025-spectre/494648?page=4","title":"Spectre reveal discussion","locator":"Post 63","review_basis":"Read team's transmission explanation.","facts":["Prior extension belt overload drove chain choice. Extension motors moved to base with coaxial drive through shoulder. Third run drives climb carriage."],"limitations":"Earlier belt failures concern Phantom, not a Spectre event."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2025/500310?page=14","title":"Spectre CAD discussion","locator":"Post 280","review_basis":"Read team rationale for powered carriage.","facts":["Forward carriage position helps acquisition, aft travel helps loaded hang. Sensitivity to CG in early layouts justified powered travel."],"limitations":"A possible fixed point was described as uncertain, not disproven."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Spectre uses a low shoulder and telescoping arm to move an intake/scorer and to lift the robot. The chassis carries the extension motors while power crosses the shoulder coaxially. That makes the arm a shared structural path with different load cases. Scoring needs low tip error with the arm extended. Climbing needs capture reach first and a useful suspended attitude after the cage takes the weight.","piece_flow":["Shared intake grips coral or algae. Retained dossier describes perpendicular and lengthwise coral indexing with range sensors.","Pivot, extension and wrist carry the piece to the branch or algae destination.","A separate carriage on the arm moves the cage capture point as the arm raises the robot. Retained binder account describes a lock into the bumper frame."],"packaging_and_motion":"Nested chain runs fit inside deliberately machined tubing. Moving the extension motors to the base reduces moving mass, but the coaxial transmission and tensioners need clearance through shoulder rotation. Keep the stage overlap and arm bending under reach distinct from the cage loading case.","subsystems":[{"name":"Telescoping arm","construction":"Face-machined nested tubes, internal chain, base-mounted extension motors and coaxial shoulder input.","operation":"Extend and pivot to position the wrist, then use the shoulder for the lifting portion of climb.","team_rationale":"Team cites prior belt overload and greater arm/intake load as reasons to adopt chain.","engineering_analysis":"Chain can increase load margin while bringing pitch wear, tension and sprocket alignment concerns. Machining thinner walls for routing makes local buckling and fastener bearing relevant.","interfaces":"Transmission passes through the pivot and shares the arm with the climbing carriage.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect guides and chain engagement under bending and after a hard stop. A full spare arm reduces repair time only when reinstallation preserves calibration.","unknowns":"Duty-cycle load, tolerance stack and event as-built dimensions.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2025/500310"]},{"name":"Intake and scoring","construction":"Retained dual-roller directions, reversible wrist and range-based indexing.","operation":"Orient coral for the required release direction or retain algae in the shared effector.","team_rationale":"Team season summary identifies both reef and ground acquisition. Exact mechanism rationale is inherited.","engineering_analysis":"A shared collector removes a separate transfer but puts acquisition impact on the long arm structure. Test settling after intake contact at useful extension.","interfaces":"Piece detection, wrist sweep and arm deflection jointly affect placement.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test obscured range sensing and a partially indexed pipe. Confirm recovery at a safe arm pose.","unknowns":"Exact source code and acceptance envelope.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-reveal-2025-spectre/494648?page=4"]},{"name":"Moving cage carriage","construction":"Independent chain-driven carriage on main arm confirmed by team.","operation":"Capture high with the carriage forward, then move it aft for balance as the arm changes orientation.","team_rationale":"Team explicitly links travel to two different desired hook locations and uncertain CG margin.","engineering_analysis":"Compare hook reaction and bumper clearance across intermediate poses. A carriage stalled between endpoints could load the system differently from either intended endpoint.","interfaces":"Arm pivot, translation, cage retention and retained bumper lock must agree.","service_and_failure_modes":"Validate partial engagement, power loss and wrong carriage position with controlled load support.","unknowns":"Climb force trace and fixed-position margin.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-reveal-2025-spectre/494648?page=4","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2025/500310?page=14"]}],"revisions":["Arm changed from the earlier Phantom belt lineage to Spectre chain. Retained dossier reports Worlds module conversion and ballast changes."],"transferable_principles":["Size a shared axis for all load cases.","Separate capture geometry from the stable hanging geometry."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A fixed hook can be simpler when CG and approach tolerances leave adequate margin.","An elevator can reduce wrist pose variation if direct floor acquisition on the arm has little value."],"remaining_gaps":["Full CAD and binder review, current traces and event-level validation."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-cad-and-tech-binder-release-2025/500310","locator":"Post 1 assembly and machining discussion; add carriage at both ends of travel from reveal"}]}

title: 2025-2056 OP Robotics 2025 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-2056","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf","title":"OP Robotics LIGHTNING technical binder","locator":"Intake, Straightenator, Coral Cradle, Gripper Arm, Elevator and Climber sections","review_basis":"Read primary PDF text and figure descriptions.","facts":["Independently driven Straightenator halves feed a printed cradle beneath the elevator. Current-triggered opposing motion clears jams. Two beam breaks have distinct staging and handoff functions. Two-stage internal belt elevator. Gripper rollers are commanded to match chassis motion on release. Ratcheted winch and cage guides protect the hang."],"limitations":"Binder requirements and team claims do not supply a distribution of cycle times or reliability."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"LIGHTNING divides floor coral handling into acquisition, orientation, storage and final scoring. Its cradle creates a known handoff pose and lets the main gripper do algae work while a pipe waits. This makes the architecture a logistics system as much as a fast elevator. An improvement to any one stage only matters when it reduces total travel, waiting or fault recovery.","piece_flow":["Floating front collector gathers floor coral. The Straightenator brings it into line with independent roller sides.","Coral travels under the elevator into a cradle. The first sensor stages the piece. The second supports handoff to the gripper.","The elevator/arm places coral or handles algae. Retained accounts describe hybrid cycles and specific high-output auto runs."],"packaging_and_motion":"The coral travels below the elevator and next to a hinged ramp that opens for the battery. This puts battery service and transfer repeatability on the same hardware. The cage guide ties to the upright and prevents the cage from swinging into it. Inspect the load paths with the robot assembled and the cable carrier in motion.","subsystems":[{"name":"Straightenator and cradle","construction":"Independently powered compliant and star wheels, belt drives, a hinged ramp and printed PA-CF cradle with lip and step.","operation":"Move the coral lengthwise into the cradle. On a current-detected jam, command a brief opposing motion.","team_rationale":"Team explicitly links uncoupled sides to independent slip and lower jam likelihood.","engineering_analysis":"Current is an indirect jam signal. Compare a pinned pipe against normal high current from first contact, a full cradle or a worn drive. Test how many retries remain useful.","interfaces":"Cradle end stop and sensor ordering must agree with gripper arrival. Ramp must return to the same alignment after a battery change.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test parallel pipe jams, sensor blockage and repeated ramp access. Check cradle joints and dowels after impact.","unknowns":"Thresholds and retry policy in deployed code.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Elevator and shared gripper","construction":"Two-stage internally belted mast with tube-plug mounting and bracing. Light arm/gripper uses powered contacts.","operation":"Lift to place coral or move algae while retaining coral separately. Outtake speed is matched to chassis motion in the binder.","team_rationale":"Binder links the release behavior to smooth placement.","engineering_analysis":"The useful quantity is pipe motion relative to the branch, so drive and roller speeds must be synchronized through slip and transient error. A light arm still needs adequate stiffness at high reach.","interfaces":"Cradle cutouts clear the gripper, and cameras on the uprights maintain the reef reference.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect belt clamps, guide play and loaded release after a hit. Test failure to confirm the handoff before driving away.","unknowns":"Event-level path timing and joint pose tolerances.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]},{"name":"Deep cage","construction":"Surgical tubing deployment, Dyneema winch, ratchet, magnet, collars and guides.","operation":"Guide in the cage, keep it from bouncing or rotating out and winch into a supported position.","team_rationale":"Team describes guide and collar features to control entry and retention.","engineering_analysis":"A magnet is an aid during capture. The geometry and ratchet should carry load through a swing or disable.","interfaces":"The cage must clear the mast and chain through approach and load pickup.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test lateral offset, a worn spool or line and power loss immediately after load pickup.","unknowns":"Capture time distribution and event hardware changes.","source_urls":["https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Retained account notes starting-piece orientation and path changes. Binder supports the released configuration."],"transferable_principles":["Break the piece path into recoverable stages with defined sensing.","Reserve battery access without changing the final transfer geometry."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A protected station can make the ground serializer's added motors and controls unnecessary.","Hybrid work loses value if algae targets lie off route or disrupt upper coral throughput."],"remaining_gaps":["Full competition code trace, jam statistics, autonomous split times and configuration chronology."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf","locator":"Straightenator rendering, Coral Cradle section and Climber close-up"}]}

title: 2025-254 UNDERTOW complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2025-254","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://media.team254.com/2025/09/985607eb-2025-Tech-Binder-254.pdf","title":"UNDERTOW technical binder","locator":"Robot Design pp. 12–18, AlphaBot p. 22 and Programming section","review_basis":"Read primary PDF passages and figure descriptions.","facts":["Floor intake and station funnel share the indexer. Rubber bands act as transport contacts across intake dead spots. Continuous internally belted lift, A-frame, opposite-side cable carrier and roller claw with winch are described."],"limitations":"Binder distinguishes design requirements from hardware. Targets such as sub-second climb are not measured distributions."},{"url":"https://www.team254.com/robots/2025/","title":"Team 254 season robot page","locator":"2025 robot overview","review_basis":"Read team season summary surfaced by search.","facts":["Undertow competed at Sacramento, East Bay and Houston."],"limitations":"Event use of individual mechanisms follows the retained dossier."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"UNDERTOW keeps two acquisition options and one shared indexing/scoring route. The floor intake is the exposed high-throughput option. The steep station funnel can bypass it after damage or support different autonomous routes. The protection has a boundary: both routes still need the indexer, loading pose and upper scorer to work.","piece_flow":["Floor collector and wedge guides move coral across the bumper; belt-like rubber-band contacts assist dead spots.","Station feed enters a steep funnel. Both routes feed an eight-wheel indexer that orients coral for handoff.","The internally belted elevator carries the wrist, which places coral or manipulates algae. Cage capture has a separate claw and winch."],"packaging_and_motion":"Battery sits between intake and lift to balance mass. The welded A-frame stiffens the elevator and mounts the climber. The cable carrier sits opposite the climber to protect it from the cage. Keep the fallback station throat clear even after the exposed collector is damaged or removed.","subsystems":[{"name":"Dual infeed and indexer","construction":"Floating floor collector with wedges and belt-like contacts, steep station funnel and shared powered indexer.","operation":"Acquire a pipe through either opening, then orient it consistently for the wrist.","team_rationale":"Team explicitly cites autonomous and redundancy for the funnel.","engineering_analysis":"Evaluate the failure boundary by blocking the floor intake. A piece or broken panel left in the common indexer can defeat both sources.","interfaces":"Different incoming angles must converge to the same handoff. Mounting the station funnel to the mast links its alignment to that structure.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test station use with a bent or isolated collector, and check access to rubber-band and printed contact replacements.","unknowns":"Failure frequency and quantitative station cycle penalty.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2025/09/985607eb-2025-Tech-Binder-254.pdf"]},{"name":"Elevator and wrist","construction":"Two-stage continuous internal belts, A-frame, wrist with pipe guides and distinct algae contacts.","operation":"Raise and orient the shared effector. The L1 pass-through geometry uses a compliant feature in the retained dossier.","team_rationale":"Team chose short-cycle acceleration gearing and a compact scoring architecture.","engineering_analysis":"A fast lift has limited effect when reorientation or approach dominates. Examine tip deflection and cable motion when the wrist makes reef contact.","interfaces":"Indexer load pose depends on stage reference. Cage exclusion depends on the cable carrier's mounting side.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check stage guide wear, belt retention and interference with an out-of-square cage.","unknowns":"Live scoring pose errors and load tests.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2025/09/985607eb-2025-Tech-Binder-254.pdf"]},{"name":"Powered cage grab","construction":"Roller claw and latch with a remote winch. Guide plates deflect the cage away from neighboring mechanisms.","operation":"Roll into cage capture, retain it with the latch and pivot under load.","team_rationale":"Binder explains the claw-to-winch sequence. Stated cycle targets are requirements.","engineering_analysis":"A well-powered grab cannot recover a blocked approach. Check cage articulation and whether guide contact twists the support before latch engagement.","interfaces":"Climber shares the A-frame with the elevator and sits adjacent to funnel structure.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test failed first contact, latch obstruction and disable during winching.","unknowns":"Successful capture envelope and individual event revisions.","source_urls":["https://media.team254.com/2025/09/985607eb-2025-Tech-Binder-254.pdf"]}],"revisions":["AlphaBot and final build are documented separately. Retained dossier identifies regional station use and Worlds fallback value."],"transferable_principles":["A fallback acquisition route should be evaluated against common downstream failures.","Use parts that guide a cage away from the wiring and scoring load path."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Redundancy may add little when both sources depend on a jam-prone shared indexer.","An open station route offers limited benefit when match traffic strongly favors floor feeding."],"remaining_gaps":["Source-code audit, event failure logs, measured funnel and climb performance."],"recommended_images":[{"url":"https://media.team254.com/2025/09/985607eb-2025-Tech-Binder-254.pdf","locator":"Binder pp. 13–18 for intake, indexer, funnel, lift, climb and wrist views"}]}

title: 2025-254 Dual infeed and indexer

text: {"robot_id":"2026-9470","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://9470techbinder.vercel.app/","title":"9470 Technical Binder","locator":"Acts 1–3 and Software","review_basis":"Read downloaded team-authored HTML","facts":"Deadline preceded each competition by 1.5 weeks. Documents divider jams, floor service, shot maps and chassis control.","limitations":"The narrative is retrospective. Linked figures and specifications cannot establish deployment of each controls revision."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Ctrl-Alt-Defeat used a forgiving collector and a chassis-aimed launcher as the core of both competition builds. The first shooter had three channels. It earned the team two district wins while leaving time for driver practice, although the hopper details record divider jams that needed attention. The DCMP build substituted a full-width drum and open feed geometry. The Worlds changes focused on impact tolerance of the collector. These are three different decisions: finish a known design early, raise output after enough practice and testing, and protect the mechanism that actually failed.","piece_flow":["The deployed roller collects into the hopper. A deflector in an early intake revision suppressed fuel ejection during agitation.","In the first competition version the floor supplied three channels. The DCMP powered floor feeds an open entrance through three feeder rollers.","The full-width drum accelerates fuel into the pivoting hood assembly. The chassis establishes shot yaw while the controls choose range-dependent settings."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team retained its prior chassis basis and packages the electronics beneath a floor that pivots open after two screws are removed. The reinforced collector combines compliant side mounts and a hard stop. Its bending path needs clearance with the intake powered and the chassis against the field. Underfloor access can improve electronics work while creating a different pit workflow for batteries.","Log measured speed droop and recharge before copying the lower-inertia arrangement described in the prior study."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Low feed compression can produce slip with worn or undersized pieces or on a steep transfer path.","An open wide path can lose to a turret if chassis yaw or blocked shooting poses consume the saved feed time.","An underside battery can be unsuitable if pit turnaround or safe robot handling makes inversion slow."],"remaining_gaps":["Later drum inertia and loaded release traces remain unresolved. Match software, current traces, loaded clearance and event-specific climb use remain unverified."],"recommended_images":["Early binder annotated whole robot, serpentine and turret cable path. text: {"robot_id":"2026-5687","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515683","title":"Team 5687 Presents Glenn","locator":"Posts 12, 14, 16, 38, 40 and 42","review_basis":"Read original team-authored Discourse text","facts":"Details collector geometry and the lower current, improved presentation and rope tension findings.","limitations":"The team does not supply exact comparative BPS or current data."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc5687/2026-robot/blob/main/src/main/cpp/subsystem/shooter/ShotCalculator.cpp","title":"Glenn public ShotCalculator","locator":"Constructor and Calculate","review_basis":"Read original C++ source","facts":"Uses distance tables, predicted pose, release-point rotational velocity, iterative flight-time compensation and a combined readiness gate.","limitations":"Static release review. Does not establish which settings or commands ran in competition."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Glenn’s collector and floor changes both addressed problems that show up under load. The Outliers limited pickup compression to avoid motor bogging, switched deployment after impacts sheared rack teeth, and later preferred a belt floor to the original rolling floor. The belt change affected both current and the arrangement of fuel presented to the drum. The public C++ shot calculator shows that the team also modeled how the launcher moves relative to the chassis center while turning, a separate problem from making the mechanical stream consistent.","piece_flow":["Two upper intake rollers pull fuel toward a lower kicker. The early kicker shares a motor with the roller floor.","The early rolling floor could spin fuel in place. Later separated belts created informal lanes and improved formation of wide volleys according to the team.","Fuel is presented across the drum. The code computes hood, flywheel and drive-angle targets against a motion-compensated aim point."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team identifies a 30-inch-wide by 24-inch-long base. The later collector deploy uses a bidirectional rope arrangement with the midpoint attached to the hub, rather than a tooth engagement at the vulnerable rack. Later floor belts use spacing to guide fuel without requiring a rigid divider. Service questions are rope tension and attachment access, loaded belt tracking, and reaching drive or electronics hardware beneath the scoring path.","subsystems":[{"name":"Pickup and deployment","construction":"Two two-inch upper rollers and a 1.25-inch kicker in the early description. Later rope deploy winds one side while paying out the other.","operation":"Maintain a light nip to send fuel over the intake entry and use the drive to extend or retract.","team_rationale":"Team chose low compression that still captured fuel and replaced the impact-sensitive rack.","engineering_analysis":"Compliance and low compression must be tested against capture at an oblique approach as well as direct pickup.","interfaces":"Sharing a motor with the kicker ties lower contact availability to floor commands in the early build.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check rope tension, terminal attachments and damage near the frame side guides.","unknowns":"Later kicker drive details and quantified shock loads.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515683"]},{"name":"Belt floor and shot control","construction":"Spaced floor belts in the later build and a chassis-aimed launcher with distance maps in C++.","operation":"Present broad volleys and require agreement of predicted range and measured heading, hood and flywheel state before reporting readiness.","team_rationale":"Belt tests reportedly reduced power draw and stationary fuel spin.","engineering_analysis":"An offset launcher acquires lateral velocity during yaw, even with the chassis center nearly stationary.","interfaces":"A reliable feed delay and pose timestamp are needed for the predicted release pose.","service_and_failure_modes":"Recheck belt tracking after a frame hit, and time a loaded volley after a power dip.","unknowns":"Mechanical drum specs were not established by these sources.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515683","https://github.com/frc5687/2026-robot/blob/main/src/main/cpp/subsystem/shooter/ShotCalculator.cpp"]}],"revisions":["Early release: two upper rollers, floor-driven kicker and low compression.","Post-first-event work compared several roller and belt floors. The team shortened autonomous shot timers by more than half a second after the change, without publishing directly measured BPS.","Rack teeth sheared under impacts. Later capstan deploy traded tooth engagement for a rope tension requirement."],"transferable_principles":["Use fuel travel, power and lane balance as separate outcomes in floor tests.","Aim compensation should use the velocity of the release point when yaw rate and launcher offset matter.","Keep maintenance time and post-impact function in the deployment comparison."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Belts can lose their floor advantage if lateral loads cause tracking problems or belt deflection opens a dead zone.","Rope deployment needs enough retained tension and a clear path after impacts or debris ingress.","A motion model loses accuracy when launch delay or shooter recovery changes materially during a full burst."],"remaining_gaps":["Independent lane-by-lane throughput, exact event variants, capstan tension settings, and authenticated deployed software are unresolved."],"recommended_images":["Reveal thread post 40 capstan CAD. Add paired floor views and an overhead frame showing 3–4-wide presentation."]}

title: 2026-3467 Windham Windup 2026 complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-3467","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/tCSdRLZUkGbcmTd11fFiZwq5TuN.pdf","title":"Perry the Platypus Technical Binder","locator":"Architecture evolution and printed pages 12–16","review_basis":"Read original team PDF text","facts":"Defines doubled racks, the five-roller indexer, progressive feeder arc, low-mounted powertrain and adjustable hood.","limitations":"Designed or binder-reported features do not establish event installation by themselves."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/508474","title":"Windham Windup 2026 Build Blog","locator":"Posts 97, 106, 108, 115, 156, 178 and 202","review_basis":"Read team text and prototype table via Discourse JSON","facts":"Differentiates prototype jams, fielded robot versions and the unbuilt expansion option.","limitations":"Prototype BPS runs vary in fuel count and test conditions."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Windham Windup’s early Platypus divided fuel into two streams, a deliberate choice for an early-season build. Perry retained the drivetrain and much of the collector layout but changed the flow after the pickup to a wide drum and continuous acceleration path. The team had already compared indexers and observed both wedging and fuel spinning in place. The rebuild used a more controlled progression of contacts rather than treating a wide hopper opening as sufficient. The binder’s theoretical package and the CAD release’s unbuilt option need separate scopes.","piece_flow":["Two intake rollers lift fuel over the bumper, with a passive kick-up shaft occupying part of the dead zone.","Five floor rollers move fuel toward the shooter. The last three use compliant wheels to tolerate clustered arrivals.","A nine-roller feeder uses a rising arc and opposing tower contacts. Surface speed rises along the lower arc before fuel reaches the drum, backing rollers and adjustable hood."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team kept the Thrifty Narrow drivetrain and bellypan across both robots. The later intake runs on doubled compliant polycarbonate racks. An idle gear supports the rack alongside the powered gear. Shooter motors and the auxiliary flywheel sit low to leave storage volume above. The PDF describes moving hopper walls and net capacity, while the release specifically calls its extra CAD expansion add-on unbuilt and untested on carpet. Those statements should not be merged into an as-run capacity.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and storage","construction":"Linear rack, paired powered rollers and passive kick-up shaft.","operation":"Capture over the bumper while maintaining alignment during impacts and retraction.","team_rationale":"Team designed compliance into the rack supports and retained the known layout during the rebuild.","engineering_analysis":"A compliant rack and thin wall can collide at a standoff as the assembly deflects.","interfaces":"Include both loaded wall deflection and bolt or standoff sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team found a wall that caught and held the intake extended.","unknowns":"Clearance margin and installed expansion configuration by event.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/tCSdRLZUkGbcmTd11fFiZwq5TuN.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/508474"]},{"name":"Floor and launch","construction":"Compliant floor exit, progressive arc, four-motor aluminum drum and auxiliary flywheel.","operation":"Stage and accelerate fuel with overlapping contacts through the curve into the drum.","team_rationale":"The rebuild avoided splitting and recentering.","engineering_analysis":"A fuel can remain trapped if it reaches a fast lower roller without an effective opposing contact.","interfaces":"Floor, arc and tower share mechanical drive and compression requirements.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pulley end support, belt tracking and the first contacts after a blockage.","unknowns":"Loaded roller-speed data and lane output.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/tCSdRLZUkGbcmTd11fFiZwq5TuN.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/508474"]}],"revisions":["Week 1–2 Platypus used a dual-stream divided shooter.","Early test jams concentrated after the star roller, at a contact with higher compression. Removing that roller helped.","Week 5, district championship and Worlds used Perry with the full-width drum and updated floor. A late report documents a wall catching on a slide standoff."],"transferable_principles":["Test where pieces spin without translating. Adjust roller spacing and opposing support before relying on a higher-friction surface.","Hold the known drivetrain and collector architecture steady when the scoring path is the source of the performance limit.","Measure each stage’s loaded surface speed, since an upstream speed advantage can create a queue at the next nip."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A divided stream can be the better early solution if the wider path needs more development or distributes fuel poorly across the drum.","Higher surface speed can worsen bounce or draw more current if the arc loses positive support or the adjacent contact stalls."],"remaining_gaps":["No controlled full-match output comparison, exact event hopper configurations, or authenticated deployed software. The prototype table compares runs with different sample counts and drives."],"recommended_images":["Perry binder pages 12–16 intake, floor and feeder arc. Build blog post 178 for the slide interference and post 202 for the two CAD variants."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2026-27","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515699","title":"Team RUSH Robot Reveal","locator":"Post 1","review_basis":"Read team-authored Discourse post text","facts":"Team identifies its 2026 reveal and early event schedule.","limitations":"Announcement text does not provide technical specifications."},{"url":"https://www.teamrush27.net/history/2026-rebuilt","title":"Team RUSH 2026 season page","locator":"Game, schedule and judging material sections","review_basis":"Read original team website HTML","facts":"Links team materials and gives season schedule.","limitations":"Reviewed page contains no construction specification."},{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8","title":"Team RUSH Behind the Bumpers","locator":"Watch description and retained interview study","review_basis":"Read publisher description and older dossier. The retained mechanism study describes a three-wide drum fitted into the existing robot. Its engineering lesson is the interaction between the footprint already allocated to scoring and the degree of positive control needed to keep fuel moving. The old account attributes jams to a powered upper roller, which was subsequently made passive. That is a testable explanation for why removing an actuator could improve net output.","piece_flow":["The older account places a powered collector below a passive upper guide, with additional tubes to retain control across the entry.","A powered floor with successive roller contacts feeds a compact preacceleration path.","The retained report describes a drum and powered hood contacts, with a beam break used to signal that discharge has finished."],"packaging_and_motion":"A retrofit retains existing interfaces. The older technical account describes variable compression to fit within the available space and passive hopper motion linked to deployment. Analyze the changing contact gap rather than treating the retained frame as empty space. Fuel volume, wiring access and collector motion should be checked through the full travel before evaluating launcher output.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and transfer","construction":"Retained account describes a main roller, passive carbon upper contact and active roller floor.","operation":"Pull across the entry, guide fuel clear of the intake and present it at the next contact.","team_rationale":"The old account associates a powered-to-passive change with reducing jams.","engineering_analysis":"Compare queue growth, slip and wedging as each contact is powered or free. Test after a full bin compresses fuel backward.","interfaces":"Hopper linkage, upper contact and intake stow all share the collector sweep.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for damage to the exposed roller and test removal without disturbing the floor.","unknowns":"Original configuration and exact guide location.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8"]},{"name":"Shooter and feedback","construction":"Prior dossier describes a three-wide drum path, adjustable hood and beam break.","operation":"Accelerate fuel progressively, then use flow feedback to decide when to leave the shot.","team_rationale":"Retained rationale emphasizes compact retrofit geometry and detecting emptying.","engineering_analysis":"A clear beam can mean no fuel reaches the sensor. Validate timing with other signals or an independent inventory count.","interfaces":"Exit readiness couples drive heading, hood, drum speed and feeder state.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test partial obstruction and vibration-induced sensor misalignment.","unknowns":"Measured recovery, sustained shot rate and exact compression profile.","source_urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8"]}],"revisions":["Team reveal gives the early event schedule but does not describe an exact as-revealed mechanism set.","Retained study describes a drum retrofit and a change from a powered upper roller to a passive guide. Exact dates remain open."],"transferable_principles":["Test a passive guide against powered contact where the main job is preventing escape or bridging.","Instrument full-hopper emptying and measure how often an empty signal arrives while fuel remains upstream.","Keep an impacted collector easy to replace without resetting the shooter path."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A passive upper guide can lose when a steep rise or worn fuel needs active opposing traction.","Beam-break silence can mean a blocked or starved transfer rather than an empty hopper.","A compact variable-compression path can become more sensitive to fuel wear and dimensional spread."],"remaining_gaps":["No complete fresh captions or published 2026 source code found in the reviewed public team repository listing. text: {"robot_id":"2026-254","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.team254.com/frc/2026/","title":"Team 254 Overload","locator":"Specifications","review_basis":"Read complete team season page","facts":"Lists SDS MK5n swerve, linear intake, pivoting belt floor, full-width adjustable drum and four-camera Jetson vision.","limitations":"The 70-plus capacity claim is published specification and not a controlled loaded route test."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/516252","title":"Overload release and engineering discussion","locator":"Posts 85, 90, 91 and 105","review_basis":"Read original team posts via Discourse JSON","facts":"Describes Alphabot, cam motion and failure history, V1–V4 floors and power limits.","limitations":"Team reports its own tests and failures. The quoted observations do not establish matched test conditions."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Overload uses a full-width drum and adjustable hood to turn a large batch into a wide volley. Its most instructive engineering history is the floor under that batch. Team 254 describes four floor versions and reports failures where a short, lightly supported axle bowed, a split tension shaft failed, and fuel reached beneath a floor that was free to lift. The final answer was a stiffer assembly and a captured cam integrated with intake motion. The progression connects the theoretical advantages of a full-width path to the stiffness and service that make it available during a match.","piece_flow":["A full-width linear intake gathers fuel into the net hopper.","A pivoting belt floor takes the bottom layer toward the feeder. Intake retraction raises the floor enough to clear the collector while compacting the load.","The full-width drum and adjustable hood launch for scoring or passing. Heading and motion determine the achievable aim."],"packaging_and_motion":"The front swerve modules were reoriented for a continuous active floor instead of a T-shaped area. The floor’s cam is designed to lift it only enough to clear the retracting roller, preserving feeder compression. The team describes a separate position in the track where the floor can swing higher to reach the battery and electrical equipment. The constraint at that position matters because a service degree of freedom was a failure mode during play.","subsystems":[{"name":"Linear collector and cam","construction":"A rack-mounted Delrin follower engages a floor plate, with a large washer capturing the follower in the later configuration.","operation":"Lift the floor with retraction, constrain it down over the operational path and preserve a service motion at the end.","team_rationale":"Avoid collector collision and fuel entering beneath the floor.","engineering_analysis":"The stiffer floor and captured cam address separate effects: loss of alignment and escape from the guide.","interfaces":"Floor lift changes the feed opening and compression at the first feeder roller.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify free movement after a side impact and inspect flange, fasteners and track for wear.","unknowns":"Exact clearances under field loading.","source_urls":["https://www.team254.com/frc/2026/","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/516252"]},{"name":"Belt floor and launch","construction":"Full-width belt-driven floor and adjustable-hood drum. V4 replaced fine adjustment with fixed centers and increased support rigidity.","operation":"Maintain useful belt tension and present the load evenly.","team_rationale":"Team reports eight evenly spaced belts performed slightly better than the lane arrangement it tested.","engineering_analysis":"Check whether the floor moves fuel across the whole width at peak load rather than only keeping unloaded belts tracking.","interfaces":"Current demand overlaps drive and launcher spin-up. Team reports dynamic limits after brownouts.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect pulley drift and tracking after lateral load. Check whether field repairs restore geometry quickly.","unknowns":"Loaded bus-voltage and discharge traces, and final setup dimensions.","source_urls":["https://www.team254.com/frc/2026/","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/516252"]}],"revisions":["Alphabot V1 used a fixed deployed intake and a metal-pulley floor that bound and lost belt tension under loading.","Silicon Valley V2 introduced clamp-on pulleys and a cam, but its split shaft tension system came apart in finals.","Central Valley V3 removed the split shaft. The floor could still deflect enough for the follower to escape.","Worlds V4 used fixed centers, welded supports, a captured follower and secured pulleys."],"transferable_principles":["Design the floor stiffness and its side-load path before adding adjustable tension devices.","Test any cam with full fuel load and a deliberately displaced side plate. A nominal CAD motion is only one operating case.","Use electrical logs to distinguish spin-up draw from full-hopper feed or driving load."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A lighter roller floor can reverse the trade when the belt supports and cam structure erase the weight savings.","Discrete lanes can help when the actual entrance starves unevenly, even though the team preferred evenly spaced belts in its geometry.","A moving floor and collector linkage only helps when there is enough tolerance for field distortion and fast service access."],"remaining_gaps":["No controlled scoring-rate comparison across all floors, full measured current traces, or verified event-specific code snapshot."],"recommended_images":["Team post 105 images for the four floor generations. Post 91 isolated follower and cam plate. Official robot photo for assembled packaging."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2026-2056","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OPR26-B-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf","title":"OP Robotics 2026 Technical Binder","locator":"Printed pp. 8–15, 18, 20 and Desperate Times section","review_basis":"Read extracted original team PDF text","facts":"Describes both architectures, revised fuel path, hood and turret travel, current-triggered jam response and hopper-level passing controls.","limitations":"Specifications and design goals are team statements. Deployment and control tuning by event remain unresolved."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"OP Robotics’ first robot, Desperate Times, used a hopperless path that progressively accelerated and narrowed incoming fuel toward the turret. The team could not get enough throughput to justify dispensing with storage. Desperate Measures added a buffered supply and a different singulation path while carrying forward a functionally identical turret. This preserved a tested scoring interface and gave software work continuity during the mechanical transition. The change matters for defense as well as laboratory throughput because the turret can now discharge inventory without requiring a live fuel stream from the floor.","piece_flow":["The revised robot’s two-roller linear intake fills a net-covered hopper with a powered roller floor.","Two rubber-coated conveyors guide the bulk stream into the quarter-pipe feed. A powered vertical kicker resolves conflicts where pieces enter the narrowing path.","Two compliant feed wheels raise fuel into the turret, where the flywheel and driven backspin contact establish release. Passing mode waits for a minimum hopper level and resumes collection if it falls below that threshold."],"packaging_and_motion":"The low turret places a bearing and wiring chain around the feed interface. Its approximately ±185-degree documented travel gives wide coverage but requires wiring clearance and angle management near the stops. The adjustable hood’s clearance is coupled to field position, so the binder describes zone-based logic for trench collision reduction. text: {"robot_id":"2026-1690","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515277","title":"Orbit 1690 KEPLER reveal and technical replies","locator":"Posts 32, 42, 80, 93, 108–109 and 115–117","review_basis":"Read team-authored replies via Discourse JSON","facts":"Covers capacity and fuel loss, L1 decision, shot calibration, moving aim under defense, electrical behavior and PTFE lining.","limitations":"Published recovery and capacity estimates are team accounts. The thread passages do not establish every competition revision."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Orbit’s KEPLER combines a low trench-capable turret with a bulk-to-single fuel path. The team’s public discussion supplies specific reasons for some choices: low added inertia and lower feedback gain reduced electrical demand at the moving shooter, friction-reducing surfaces helped the singulator, and a defensive operating mode addressed the mismatch between commanded and actual motion during contact. This architecture buys freedom to aim without turning the chassis for every release. It spends that benefit on narrow-path feed development, cable travel and pose quality.","piece_flow":["The prior dossier describes pickup into a live-bottom hopper. The team’s thread reports open-bin fuel loss and an approximate capacity estimate rather than an always-retained load.","Fuel converges through low-friction lined walls into a single corridor. The reduced side friction helps fuel translate as powered elements drive the stream.","The turret aims the shot. The team describes an empirical speed scale and a compression term to adapt the modeled release, with a live trim available."],"packaging_and_motion":"The moving turret and its wiring must clear the trench configuration across hood and yaw settings. Orbit describes changing conductor size along the circuit and limiting demand at the shooter. This is a packaging and power interaction, because the harness section that must move differs from a fixed run. Under defense, the commands and actual chassis motion can diverge. The driver can disable moving-shot compensation and command an X-wheel stance.","subsystems":[{"name":"Hopper and single-stream transfer","construction":"Live bottom in the older dossier. Team confirms polycarbonate supporting thin PTFE and PTFE on corridor side walls.","operation":"Advance fuel from the bulk store into a single launcher stream.","team_rationale":"Team identified low friction as the purpose of the lining and described losses from the open tank.","engineering_analysis":"A smooth wall reduces drag but a single exit can still bridge when several balls arrive together.","interfaces":"Collector delivery, floor motion and convergence geometry must remain compatible as fill changes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect liner attachment and edge wear after impact or repeated jam reversals.","unknowns":"Roller geometry, measured rate and loaded retention.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515277"]},{"name":"Turret and shot controls","construction":"Chassis-independent aim with a moving harness. Team describes low added inertia, empirical release compensation and controller rumble for lower voltage.","operation":"Aim while moving in normal operation, and allow a driver-selected defense stance when contact invalidates prediction.","team_rationale":"Desired velocity was less noisy than measured motion, but impact disturbances motivated a separate mode.","engineering_analysis":"Identify misses by voltage, contact state and fuel wear to separate control error from release error.","interfaces":"Shot calculation, chassis motion and drive current share the same operating budget.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check repeatability after a low-voltage burst and after motion near a wiring travel limit.","unknowns":"No recorded event-ready thresholds or transfer gating.","source_urls":["https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515277"]}],"revisions":["Team says it tested L3 and stayed with L1 because L3 did not work as desired.","Open hopper behavior, proposed net testing and trench clearance were discussed together. Net installation is not established by that post.","Team described a calibration mismatch with worn shop fuel and later changes to shot parameters."],"transferable_principles":["Validate moving-shot inputs during contact and across voltage, since chassis command can differ substantially from actual release-point motion.","Measure friction and singulation under packing pressure, not only with isolated balls.","Calibrate with worn and event fuel at multiple distances to separate release-scale and compression effects."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A narrower serial path can lose to a drum if loaded throughput is too low to capitalize on heading independence.","A command-velocity feedforward can be useful in clear space but becomes inaccurate under collisions or wheel slip.","Low added inertia only holds up if speed recovers between actual arrivals under simultaneous drive demand."],"remaining_gaps":["Complete turret sweep and live-bottom construction dimensions, deployed control snapshot, and independent discharge and scoring traces. Base dossier’s drivetrain revision was not independently confirmed by the reviewed posts."],"recommended_images":["Reveal thread post 115 for the corridor liner context. Request an overhead loaded singulation view and a side view showing hood and harness clearance."]}

title: 2026-2910 Blitz → rebuild complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2026-2910","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jPf-aOGhz0dntoAgahFBgRhJiJv9rGpj/view","title":"Team 2910 Blitz Tech Brief","locator":"No Hopper, Double Intake, Intakes and Feeder/Shooter","review_basis":"Downloaded original PDF and read extracted text","facts":"Early architecture used mirrored four-bars and minimal storage to keep passing while sweeping.","limitations":"Requirements in the brief do not establish measured match execution."},{"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r-6zR4afbr_BpeZfWwcM5XL1N74FjScI/view","title":"Team 2910 Re•Blitz Tech Brief","locator":"Strategical and Mechanical Reanalysis, Intake, Feeder and Shooter, Hopper, Software","review_basis":"Downloaded original PDF and read extracted text","facts":"Describes role pivot, single impact-resistant collector, floor and wide drum, as well as control fallback and reported rate.","limitations":"Team measurements lack a complete independent protocol. Design goals and demonstrated outputs have separate scope."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Jack in the Bot initially built Blitz to move fuel continuously for its alliance, using the field as its inventory. Mirrored intakes made side-sweeping possible, and the low-storage path kept the focus on collecting and releasing during travel. The team’s own reanalysis says that intake and shoot-on-the-move limitations prevented this strategy from offsetting the loss of independent scoring, especially in autonomous and under defense. Re•Blitz changed the role and shortened the fuel path. The new robot combined a robust single collector, a buffer and a wide scoring burst while retaining a passing option.","piece_flow":["Blitz’s independent four-bar intakes fed through side transition rollers into a serpentine path for immediate release.","Re•Blitz uses a slapdown collector with a powered lower contact to fill the hopper. Intake deployment pushes the hopper into position and retraction helps compact fuel.","A ten-roller inclined floor and compliant indexing roller present fuel four wide to the drum. The published software account describes sensor-based preload of the tower and a ready-to-score state before discharge."],"packaging_and_motion":"The 27.5 by 27-inch rebuild rotates modules to free space and packages major electronics around a central brainpan. The new hopper slides on bearings when the intake deploys and catches in the extended position, protecting the adjacent shooter from unintended return. It uses clear-enough tinted panels so inventory remains observable. The intake uses thicker side plates, a bash bar and split construction for service. Those are different solutions to impact tolerance and repair time.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and expanding hopper","construction":"Slapdown with bash bar, split side plates and powered lower rollers. Sliding one-piece polycarbonate hopper with retainers.","operation":"Intake deployment opens the hopper. Retraction compacts its contents toward the feed path.","team_rationale":"The team removed redundant intakes for storage volume and serviceability and emphasized impact resistance.","engineering_analysis":"A one-time expansion with catches makes initial deploy and reset decisive. Validate capture after asymmetric impacts and with a fully packed bin.","interfaces":"Collector travel and walls must clear the shooter and maintain feed alignment.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check catch engagement and the time to swap the exposed side plate or a bent lower roller.","unknowns":"No measured impact envelope or fielded variant chronology.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jPf-aOGhz0dntoAgahFBgRhJiJv9rGpj/view","https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r-6zR4afbr_BpeZfWwcM5XL1N74FjScI/view"]},{"name":"Feeder and drum","construction":"Ten-roller floor at a reported 15-degree incline, compliant indexing roller, four-inch aluminum drum and overdriven flywheel.","operation":"Apply broad positive control and use sensor-based preload before the shot.","team_rationale":"Team preferred chains for lower rolling resistance in its arrangement and added guides to improve flow.","engineering_analysis":"Benchmark an equally supported belt or chain design with loaded tension and wear. Overall drive loss depends on more than transmission type.","interfaces":"Feed readiness, tower occupancy and heading gate work together.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check chain tension and empty-sensor behavior during partial blockage.","unknowns":"Loaded current and scoring conversion by range.","source_urls":["https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r-6zR4afbr_BpeZfWwcM5XL1N74FjScI/view"]}],"revisions":["Original Blitz used two mirrored four-bar intakes, minimal storage and a serpentine transfer.","The team allocated three weeks for redesign, assembly and bring-up across the midseason rebuild.","Re•Blitz added a hopper, powered floor, four-wide launcher and low-friction guide boards. Team reports up to 34 BPS over a full hopper under its test conditions."],"transferable_principles":["Evaluate whether a partner-dependent role delivers enough fuel during autonomous and remains useful when the primary scorer is defended.","Reduce redundant acquisition when its service, packaging and tuning cost exceeds the additional usable fuel.","Record clear performance acceptance criteria before selecting a buffer size and feed width."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A high-speed passer can be superior when partner scoring is dependable and the playing area offers continuous fuel access.","A large loaded hopper can lose on a difficult route if fuel escapes, the collector catches or autonomous relocalization fails.","A high launch rate loses its value if pose gating leaves too little time to empty inventory."],"remaining_gaps":["No independent BPS or conversion logs, no authenticated event code and no complete comparison of rate versus fill level or battery state."],"recommended_images":["Original brief double-intake and serpentine pages. Re•Blitz brief intake, feeder and hopper pages for bash bar, four-wide path and passive deployment catches."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2026-1678","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://www.citruscircuits.org/2026-robot","title":"Citrus Circuits Limestone 2026","locator":"Intake, ball tunnel/shooter, drivetrain, hopper and controls","review_basis":"Read original team season page HTML","facts":"Documents guide contacts, floor roller geometry, service pivot, staged acceleration, aluminum drum, linked hood rollers and extension motions.","limitations":"Page presents a team specification without complete event history. Some terminology around the extension directions is internally loose."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515709","title":"Limestone reveal discussion","locator":"Team posts 33, 37 and 63","review_basis":"Read original team replies via Discourse JSON","facts":"Team identifies WCP silicone and high-speed expansion as a problem and gives base and telescoping geometry.","limitations":"Context concerns an unspecified revision. A commenter’s nominal drum size is not a team specification."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Limestone packages a full-width intake, a floor with changing roller geometry and a staged launch tunnel on a compact swerve base. Citrus Circuits’ season page is unusually useful for distinguishing what each contact is intended to do. The intake guides newly acquired fuel away from the main roller, the floor addresses bridging near the feeder, and the tunnel supplies a substantial share of the launch speed before final acceleration. Hopper expansion and Level 1 climbing share structure, so usable volume, clearance and endgame geometry cannot be analyzed independently.","piece_flow":["The slapdown intake uses a silicone-covered main roller, a kicker and smaller guide contacts to keep fuel from returning to the first roller.","Five dead-axle rollers and three flex-wheel rollers form the floor. A steeper compliant section is intended to reduce wedging as fuel approaches the feeder.","Powered backing contacts constrain fuel through the rising tunnel. The team page describes approximately 70 percent of shot speed before final acceleration by the drum and mechanically linked hood rollers."],"packaging_and_motion":"The team lists a 27-inch-square MK5n chassis. The floor pivots for access to battery and electronics, rests on hard stops in operation and is retained by a pin. Horizontal hopper extension is linked to the collector through a slotted connection. The team also describes vertical extension associated with the climb assembly. Check both motions with a packed hopper and a deflected wall, particularly where a shared mechanism must return to a clearance-critical pose.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and expanding storage","construction":"Full-width pivoting collector, silicone-covered carbon main roller, crash bar and replaceable SRPP plates. Slotted horizontal connection and vertical climb-linked extension.","operation":"Sweep in fuel and retain it while linked structures move.","team_rationale":"Official description links guide contacts to preventing recontact and impact parts to rapid replacement.","engineering_analysis":"Keep crash structure above the effective fuel approach while protecting the roller under angled impacts.","interfaces":"The intake sweep drives hopper geometry and must clear the floor stops.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check replaceable plate and slot wear as well as the effort to restore alignment after a strike.","unknowns":"Impact load and loaded route retention.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2026-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515709"]},{"name":"Floor, tunnel and launch","construction":"Sloped roller floor, active backing and separate powered feed roller. Official page lists aluminum drum and linked driven hood rollers.","operation":"Present and accelerate fuel in successive contacts. Pivot the floor for service after releasing its retaining pin.","team_rationale":"The team intended the sloped compliant contacts to reduce keystoning and the tunnel to deliver a controlled entry speed.","engineering_analysis":"The roller path should maintain capture at the last low-speed to high-speed boundary. Verify release uniformity across the width.","interfaces":"Floor latch, first tunnel contact and backing rollers must agree under deflection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check sleeve migration at speed where used and service-floor return alignment.","unknowns":"Actual drum revision and controlled lane-by-lane data.","source_urls":["https://www.citruscircuits.org/2026-robot","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/515709"]}],"revisions":["Reveal discussion describes silicone expansion at high shooter speed, while the later team page describes a grip-tape-covered 3.5-inch aluminum drum.","The older interview synopsis described steel. Exact association among the interview, reveal thread and final team specifications remains unverified.","The team page documents a hot-swappable impact protection approach and integrated horizontal and vertical hopper expansion."],"transferable_principles":["Design the collector exit so captured fuel cannot reenter the first powered nip.","Use floor geometry and compliant contacts to change how pieces load one another at a narrow transition.","Verify service-floor retention as a performance requirement, since its operating position defines the feed boundary."],"disconfirming_conditions":["More preacceleration can create bounce or slug feeding if the drum cannot accept the presented stream.","A shared climb and hopper structure can lose value if wear or impact couples a storage problem into both operating modes.","A change in drum material or surface can invalidate release calibration and loaded recovery comparisons."],"remaining_gaps":["Exact event mapping for drum construction, launch-rate and energy recovery traces, and complete validation of loaded motion and clearance."],"recommended_images":["Official Limestone side and isolated drivetrain views for the floor pivot and latch. Request a cutaway of the rising tunnel and deployed hopper linkage."]}
