text: {"robot_id":"2026-4414","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://2026.team4414.com/","title":"HighTide 2026 Technical Binder","locator":"Dye Rotor, Intake, Shooter, Software and prototype gallery","review_basis":"Read team-authored content in the published site JavaScript bundle","facts":"Documents powered and passive contacts, packing relief, coupled hopper design, compact shooter packaging and trajectory computation.","limitations":"Feature descriptions are published configuration summaries and should not be projected onto all gallery versions."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/519602","title":"RIPCURRENT engineering release discussion","locator":"Team replies 99, 113, 116 and 154","review_basis":"Read original team-authored text via Discourse JSON","facts":"Supplies explicit event version mapping, bumper removal support path, shot tuning and shared block CAD workflow.","limitations":"The event account does not prove every intermediate test outcome or binary deployment."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"RIPCURRENT uses a wide linear collector and a large hopper to gather fuel, then feeds a low rotating shooter through the Dye Rotor. The design concentrates the hard problem at the rotor: bulk inventory needs to reach a narrow vertical path without wedging and without obstructing the turret. The team’s published packaging preserves both a high-volume bin and a limited shooter sweep. Its event history shows the rotor and shooter evolved at different rates. The newer team reply establishes their event pairings, while the older gallery review remains useful for visible comparisons of the intermediate versions.","piece_flow":["The linear collector uses an upper powered roller and a smaller lower powered roller that deploys between bumper gaps and stays down on latches.","Fuel settles around the rotor. A slowly counter-moving feature agitates the bed, contour prints guide fuel, and passive contacts lead into powered feeder wheels.","The compact turret accelerates a single stream. A driven hood contact, backing geometry and flywheel speed govern release while the turret supplies yaw."],"packaging_and_motion":"A chamfered base and bumper-integrated walls leave room for a large rotor. The team arranged shooter motors centrally and vertically, staggered plates to cut swept volume, and placed slim hood belts against the side plates. The turret bearing maintains support when the large bumper/hopper section is removed. The interference case includes the rotating hood, the deformable fuel bed and a trench crossing with stored fuel.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector and hopper","construction":"Paired polycarbonate racks, powered upper and lower contacts, extending hopper and bumper-integrated walls.","operation":"Gather a wide swath and preserve containment when traveling.","team_rationale":"Team uses compliant rack layers and shaped impact guards for collection along field edges.","engineering_analysis":"Verify deployed geometry with side load and packed fuel. Two sides can deflect asymmetrically while the roller couples them.","interfaces":"Lower roller latches, intake extension and bumper geometry define the entry and service envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect axle shear pins, latch engagement and rack travel after a corner hit.","unknowns":"Loaded wall shape and exact capacity by configuration.","source_urls":["https://2026.team4414.com/","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/519602"]},{"name":"Dye Rotor and turret","construction":"Driven rotor and feed wheels, shaped contours and passive roller contacts. Four X44s on the published three-inch launcher flywheel with additional mass and a low-profile driven hood.","operation":"Agitate the bulk bed gently, then impose positive control through feed and release.","team_rationale":"Team sought reduced packing pressure, a smaller sweep and repeatable shots over a region of valid trajectories.","engineering_analysis":"A passive contact can let balls push one another through while reducing torque demand. Test whether it still turns freely under contamination.","interfaces":"Feeder alignment, turret bearing, hood belts and shot model depend on repeatable contact geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking, liner wear and rotor recovery with several pieces pushing against the exit.","unknowns":"Per-version compression maps and performance under current limits.","source_urls":["https://2026.team4414.com/","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/519602"]}],"revisions":["Team reports rotor V9 at Ventura, Orange County and district championship, then V10 at Worlds.","Team reports shooter V6 at Ventura, V8 at Orange County, V9 at district championship, and V11 at Worlds.","Earlier gallery documented ten rotor and eleven shooter renders. Team event mapping now resolves selected pairings without assigning an installation or outcome to every intermediate version."],"transferable_principles":["Set the packaging envelope before final detail. The team used shared block geometry to control collisions across independently developed subsystems.","Differentiate low-energy bulk agitation from controlled acceleration at the final nip.","Preserve a structural support path when removable hopper and bumper assemblies come off for inspection."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Rotating agitation can increase pressure at a narrowing exit if its direction, speed or geometry is mismatched to the packed bed.","A compact single stream can underperform a wide path when delivery rate or sensitivity to irregular fuel prevents sustained output.","Thin hood drives and tight stow gaps need a stiffness and impact margin. Nominal CAD clearance does not show the effect of bent parts."],"remaining_gaps":["No measured per-version jam rate, transfer current, shot conversion or complete prototype test history. Four X44s on the published three-inch launcher flywheel with additional mass and a low-profile driven hood.","operation":"Agitate the bulk bed gently, then impose positive control through feed and release.","team_rationale":"Team sought reduced packing pressure, a smaller sweep and repeatable shots over a region of valid trajectories.","engineering_analysis":"A passive contact can let balls push one another through while reducing torque demand. Test whether it still turns freely under contamination.","interfaces":"Feeder alignment, turret bearing, hood belts and shot model depend on repeatable contact geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt tracking, liner wear and rotor recovery with several pieces pushing against the exit.","unknowns":"Per-version compression maps and performance under current limits.","source_urls":["https://2026.team4414.com/","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/519602"]}

ClimbMotion is commented out.","limitations":"Snapshot differs in scope from team interview and does not establish match deployment."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"WildStang fit a full two-cargo path, fixed-azimuth high-hub shooter and traversal climber on a compact swerve chassis. The intake and feeder could collect from one heading while swerve translated in another direction. Before release, the chassis itself became the yaw axis. On the hangar, compact packaging depended on sequentially transferring the chassis weight between two sets of hooks.","piece_flow":"Compliant pickup wheels bring cargo onto paired belt surfaces over the bumper. A polycarbonate guide leads into the upward feed. Low and high sensors indicate queue occupancy. A pneumatic gate restrains cargo before a powered kicker meters it into the shooter, where a Colson flywheel and backing wheels accelerate it through an adjustable hood.","packaging_and_motion":"The roughly right-angle feed packs the queue near the launcher but creates a junction where incoming cargo can be lifted prematurely. The team replaced a bare crossbar interface with a long spacer to constrain that motion. The climb keeps its envelope small in part by repeating one load transfer rather than deploying a dedicated arm for every rung.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector","construction":"Compliant wheels and paired belt surfaces feeding over the bumper.","operation":"Capture from the floor and guide cargo through the bumper crossing.","team_rationale":"Remove dead zones and pinch points uncovered in prototyping.","engineering_analysis":"Removing contact elements can eliminate a wedge rather than simply reduce grip. Test the outer approach with the chassis translating sideways.","interfaces":"Roller speeds, belt tracking, bumper height and guide edge.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check dropped or scuffed balls and debris at the approach to the guide.","unknowns":"Installed wheel diameters and belt transmission.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/dQxUV3jSOuQ"]},{"name":"Queue and kicker","construction":"Polycarbonate guide, two occupancy sensors, pneumatic gate and independently powered kicker.","operation":"Team describes stopping feed when full and releasing cargo to the kicker on demand.","team_rationale":"Avoid driving through the gate and reduce variation entering the flywheel.","engineering_analysis":"Separate queue pressure from shot feed velocity. Validate the loaded gate under a stalled sensor and the second ball against first-shot recovery.","interfaces":"Intake belt, gate timing, kicker and flywheel.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check false occupancy, gate bounce and reverse-clear access.","unknowns":"Match-specific logic and kicker speeds.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/dQxUV3jSOuQ","https://github.com/wildstang/2022_111_robot_software/tree/main/src/main/java/org/wildstang/year2022/subsystems"]},{"name":"Fixed-azimuth shooter and drive","construction":"Swerve, Limelight, adjustable hood, Colson flywheel and backing wheels.","operation":"Vision informs hood and chassis alignment. Release code includes camera-angle ranging and translation-dependent adjustments.","team_rationale":"Team chose chassis aiming because it already had swerve, and lighter flywheels for faster recharge.","engineering_analysis":"Check time from collecting to shooting while defended. Lower wheel inertia can shorten spin-up while increasing speed droop unless recovery and feed spacing are coordinated.","interfaces":"Heading controller, target detection, hood, kicker and flywheel.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check target dropout, false range, and driver override when automatic yaw conflicts with escape.","unknowns":"Measured dispersion and whether motion corrections were deployed at the filmed regional.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/dQxUV3jSOuQ","https://github.com/wildstang/2022_111_robot_software/tree/main/src/main/java/org/wildstang/year2022/subsystems","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wildstang-robotics-program-team-111-and-112-build-blog-2023/420243/12"]},{"name":"Traversal hooks","construction":"Extending hooks plus a second set of retaining hooks.","operation":"Reach and retract onto a rung, transfer the load to retaining hooks, then extend toward the next rung and repeat.","team_rationale":"Preserve a small chassis footprint for navigating traffic.","engineering_analysis":"A transfer has to be verified with the robot hanging and swinging, since static bar clearance alone misses the approach angle.","interfaces":"Hangar rungs, chassis approach and hook reset.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test partial engagement, missed reset and asymmetric catch.","unknowns":"Hook actuation and confirmed match logic.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/dQxUV3jSOuQ"]}],"revisions":["Team removed two compliant wheels and a rear support bar after observing jams and added a spacer to constrain the upward transition."],"transferable_principles":["Treat each guide, roller and crossmember as part of the piece envelope. Separate retention from launch feed so each can be tuned independently."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A compact 90-degree path can fail if a different ball rebounds or bridges. Chassis aiming loses value when scoring heading prevents evasive translation."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. Public Ballpath.java has low and high inputs but does not corroborate the filmed two-full stop in the inspected update routine. The published climb files are commented out."],"recommended_images":["Select a dated side frame at 2:32–4:29 showing the bumper-to-kicker path and a loaded climb frame showing which hooks support the robot."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2022-148","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/qvxmqMO1hv8","title":"Robowranglers team interview at Texas Championship","locator":"1:30–2:38 drive; 2:40–4:29 pickup; 4:30–6:55 index and turret; 6:56–9:00 climb","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":"Team describes inverted swerve, intake wheel protection, a limit-switch index position, color handling and servo-release hook locks.","limitations":"Interview gives conflicting estimates of turret travel. No numeric angle or motor count inferred."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/404469","title":"Robowranglers Quickdraw reveal","locator":"Post 1 and post 13","review_basis":"Read team announcement and later question","facts":"Post 1 identifies Quickdraw and early schedule. Post 13 asks about shooter power and wheels.","limitations":"The reader question cannot establish installed hardware details."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Quickdraw was a swerve-driven cargo cycler with a low reaching collector, color-aware transfer, yawing launcher and rotating traversal climber. The inverted drive module orientation made better use of volume above the chassis in a season with limited obstacle crossings. The climb occupied a sector that the launcher could face but that the team identified as unusable for shots.","piece_flow":"The collector gets low over bouncing cargo, maintains contact across several rollers and guides the ball inward. A printed transfer part with a Velcro contact surface moves cargo into the index position, where a limit switch stops movement and a color sensor classifies it. Correct cargo proceeds to the launcher. The team describes mostly ejecting opposing cargo upward through the shooter.","packaging_and_motion":"Inverted Swerve X places the Falcons lower. The collector has mechanically controlled deployment so it can retract for hangar clearance. The turret and climber share a region in the upper package, so useful aim is a function of mechanical position and safe shot geometry.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and operator","construction":"Inverted Swerve X modules with low motor packaging.","operation":"Swerve supports lateral escape and translation while the turret aims.","team_rationale":"Save vertical space when repeated obstacle crossings were limited and preserve maneuverability under defense.","engineering_analysis":"Measure bottom clearance and protection at the worst obstacle approach. The driver still needs practice to turn independent translation into usable scoring time.","interfaces":"Bumper height, motor protection, floor obstacles and heading control.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect underbody impact marks and connections after crossings.","unknowns":"Drive reduction, clearance and loaded acceleration.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/qvxmqMO1hv8"]},{"name":"Intake and transfer","construction":"Low multi-roller intake with foam outer wheels, added side guards and a printed transfer element carrying Velcro.","operation":"Multiple contacts keep cargo moving toward the switch-defined queue location.","team_rationale":"Low pickup controls rebound. The team chose mechanical deployment for more control and to retract for hanging.","engineering_analysis":"The surface needs enough traction to advance cargo and enough compliance to release it. A guard that protects a side wheel can become the first obstacle an oblique cargo sees.","interfaces":"Roller-to-transfer gap, bumper, limit switch and color sensor.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check side-wheel damage, Velcro wear, switch hysteresis and accumulation at the inside corner.","unknowns":"Drive details, queue capacity and jam-clear sequence.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/qvxmqMO1hv8"]},{"name":"Scoring and rejection","construction":"A shooter mounted on a routed turret gear and a color sensor at the index point.","operation":"The drive team reports using the launcher to eject opponent cargo in a different direction.","team_rationale":"Team emphasizes time spent tuning the indexer and shot together.","engineering_analysis":"Treat the forbidden firing sector as a state constraint. In a fixed-azimuth transfer, chassis heading and reject trajectory need independent validation.","interfaces":"Indexed cargo position, turret envelope and climber interference.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test false classifications and shot commands across the blocked sector.","unknowns":"Precise turret travel, shooter layout and firing interlocks.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/qvxmqMO1hv8"]},{"name":"Traversal climber","construction":"Spring-assisted deployment from a stowed position and bar-triggered hooks released with linear servos.","operation":"Begin at the second rung, rotate to capture the next rung and repeat through traversal. Bar contact triggers the clamp, and the servo moves a release panel.","team_rationale":"Team describes positively retaining the bar during rotation and releasing once transfer is intended.","engineering_analysis":"Test latch closure under bar misalignment and swing. The release actuator should be tested both unloaded and with residual load at transfer.","interfaces":"Stow restraint, deployment springs, rung contact, clamp, servo and chassis CG.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test one-sided engagement, incomplete opening and spring rebound at full deployment.","unknowns":"Quantified load path and safe release criteria.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/qvxmqMO1hv8"]}],"revisions":["Team added side guards called finger guns after repeated wall contact damaged side foam wheels. The March reveal post identifies Quickdraw and initial events, while the captioned interview describes its later Texas configuration."],"transferable_principles":["Protect the wear part without creating a new capture obstruction. Keep the bar latch and its release as distinct functions."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A low motor package loses value if the next field demands high obstacle clearance. A rotating climber becomes unreliable if the next bar is outside its loaded capture envelope."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. No verified Quickdraw source code, dimensioned model, or measured cycle dataset. The reveal thread shooter reply is a reader question."],"recommended_images":["Use the reveal post 1 full-robot images for overview and a dated Texas interview frame near 8:27 for the latch and release linkage."]}

title: 2022-118 Horizon complete robot study
text: {"robot_id":"2022-118","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/cxhs6sPw3Ys","title":"Robonauts team interview at Indiana Robotics Invitational","locator":"1:24–2:47 drive; 2:47–6:06 intake; 6:06–9:16 feeder and shooter; 9:28–11:58 climb","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":"Team explains the fast gear change, serviceable impact parts, separate powered launch surfaces and center-of-gravity shift during climb.","limitations":"Later offseason interview. Ratios stated from memory are treated as approximate."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-frc-118-robonauts-robot-breakdown/413580","title":"Horizon post-interview technical discussion","locator":"Team replies 2 and 4","review_basis":"Read full replies in saved Discourse JSON","facts":"Explains intake packaging and durability, gearing changes, low-voltage shot issue and climb design.","limitations":"Several dimensions and ratios are recalled rather than verified against CAD."},{"url":"https://www.118robonauts.org/_files/archives/209e0c_3a2eb56c5e1e4b529090cc92b3325f5c.zip?dn=FRC118-Robonauts-2022-Horizon-SourceCode.zip","title":"Official Horizon code archive","locator":"SW-release/2022-Horizon/Shooter/src/Kicker.cpp 73–166 and Climb/src/Climb.cpp 374–448","review_basis":"Read team C++ implementation inside release ZIP","facts":"Debounced cargo counting and separate kick states. Climb operator interface exposes deploy, claws and closed-loop setpoints.","limitations":"Read 2022 directory separately from later work in the archive."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Horizon’s fast swerve cycles, turret and adjustable launcher were paired with a narrow rotary traversal climber. The intake’s size came from putting a large roller on an arm that could clear the shooter in its initial stowed position. The narrow upper package left room for partners on the traversal rung, while the wide lower intake was designed for contact during cargo cycles.","piece_flow":"Large compliant foam wheels gather and center cargo. Guides and an interior omni-wheel feeder carry it toward the turret. A separate kicker holds cargo away from the spinning launcher until commanded, then pushes it into the main flywheel and independently driven upper wheel. The released kicker code counts two debounced beam inputs and supports firing, reversing and idle drive.","packaging_and_motion":"The long intake arms stow over the shooter and deploy through a large sweep. A replaceable polycarbonate strike surface, fence rollers, surgical tubing and landing saddles handle different contact loads. The narrow turret and climber package depends on coordinating the hood and yaw before the climber rotates. The team reports using less than 14 inches of traversal rung.","subsystems":[{"name":"Swerve drive","construction":"SDS Mk4 modules with preconfigured replacement assemblies.","operation":"The team started with L3, tried L1 and L2 after district championship and chose L1.","team_rationale":"Improve acceleration under defense on a full-weight robot. Mk4s were lighter and simpler to replace for the team.","engineering_analysis":"Compare acceleration, braking and recovery after contact over the actual cycle. Do not choose ratio on unloaded top speed alone.","interfaces":"Module plates, bumper, connectors and drivetrain tuning.","service_and_failure_modes":"Team observed plates bending upward. Inspect mount flatness and confirm spare module offsets after swaps.","unknowns":"Quantified acceleration gain.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cxhs6sPw3Ys","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-frc-118-robonauts-robot-breakdown/413580"]},{"name":"Collector and feed","construction":"Large foam contact wheels on a dead-axle assembly, long box-tube arms and staged pneumatic deployment.","operation":"Guide cargo over the entrance to a powered omni feeder and then into a separately controlled kicker.","team_rationale":"Capture quickly, withstand wall contact and swap damaged surfaces or complete rollers.","engineering_analysis":"Arm length amplifies impact moment. A replaceable contact surface limits service cost only if the remaining load bypasses weak bearings and actuator rods.","interfaces":"Pivot clearance, bumper, kicker, foam roller wear and climb envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check distorted arms, loose belts and pieces held at the feeder junction.","unknowns":"Capture data by approach speed and wear state.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cxhs6sPw3Ys","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-frc-118-robonauts-robot-breakdown/413580","https://www.118robonauts.org/_files/archives/209e0c_3a2eb56c5e1e4b529090cc92b3325f5c.zip?dn=FRC118-Robonauts-2022-Horizon-SourceCode.zip"]},{"name":"Launcher and turret","construction":"Two-Falcon main wheel, independently driven upper wheel, geared hood and hollow turret gear.","operation":"Feeder delivers through the yaw axis. Fast turret and hood motion set aim and trajectory.","team_rationale":"Keep up with turning chassis and manage ball spin.","engineering_analysis":"Size the upper wheel for torque and speed margin at low voltage. A faster idle mechanism is irrelevant if it cannot reach its commanded speed during a shot.","interfaces":"Power bus, range estimate, shot table and feeder.","service_and_failure_modes":"Look for hood gear skipping and top-wheel saturation during current peaks.","unknowns":"Shot dispersion and published configuration per event.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cxhs6sPw3Ys","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-frc-118-robonauts-robot-breakdown/413580"]},{"name":"Rotary traversal","construction":"Motorized deployment, mechanical latches and three-Falcon chain-driven rotation.","operation":"Prepare hood and turret, capture successive rungs and use a small rotation to shift CG for the last transfer.","team_rationale":"Use narrow rung width, improve smoothness and finish quickly.","engineering_analysis":"Separate deployment from load-bearing rotation. Assess changing torque and swing about each rung, plus voltage under concurrent loads.","interfaces":"Claw commands, rung geometry, shooter stow and partner envelopes.","service_and_failure_modes":"Verify both supports before transfer and recovery from missed capture.","unknowns":"Loaded timing distribution and full match configuration.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cxhs6sPw3Ys","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/behind-the-bumpers-frc-118-robonauts-robot-breakdown/413580","https://www.118robonauts.org/_files/archives/209e0c_3a2eb56c5e1e4b529090cc92b3325f5c.zip?dn=FRC118-Robonauts-2022-Horizon-SourceCode.zip"]}],"revisions":["L3 to L1 after defense testing. Electric climb deployment replaced the earlier pneumatic actuator. A larger motor and revised upper-wheel gearing addressed low-voltage saturation before Championship. Team also describes changing hood rack tooth size after skipping."],"transferable_principles":["Plan service access and spares at major impact interfaces. Validate cycle-critical actuators at match voltage with realistic concurrent demand."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Longer protected sprints may change the gearing result. Different bar spacing, CG or partner envelopes can defeat the same rotary transfer. A fixed-azimuth electric-only adaptation needs revised packaging and deployment."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. No CAD measurement, independent timing, or complete mapping of released XML configurations to events."],"recommended_images":["Team robots page https://www.118robonauts.org/robots, Horizon in 118 workspace with banners photo. Pair with a loaded transfer image showing the narrow rung occupancy."]}

It saved space by driving the cargo over the battery from above and by making the adjustable shooter hood carry climbing loads as well. The team’s release described a 26-inch square frame. Its Championship interview describes an operator checking the first capture before the automatic sequence, a meaningful division between human confirmation and motion automation.","piece_flow":"Four-inch mecanum intake wheels center cargo toward a path driven from the top. The ball crosses over the battery, then rises along standoffs to the shooter. A feed motor in the rear drives through long belts because that was where it fit. The launcher uses a large wrap and enough flywheel inertia for close-spaced shots, based on the team’s comparison with lighter wheels.","packaging_and_motion":"Low, frame-integrated module motors make more room above the drivetrain. The reveal calls the drive MK4i, while the later interview describes gearing like MK4i with a flipped motor arrangement. The hood’s climb travel extends far beyond its shot range. Its rigid structure and motion are part of the load-bearing system during transfers.","subsystems":[{"name":"Swerve and pickup","construction":"Frame-integrated swerve motors, four-inch mecanum contact wheels, printed pulleys and pneumatic intake deployment.","operation":"Drive and steering are separate. Mirrored intake contact moves cargo inward while the chassis translates.","team_rationale":"Low CG, compact packaging and better pickup than the team’s smaller prior rollers.","engineering_analysis":"Check low-mounted motor clearance and validate edge capture at oblique speeds. Compliant wheels versus mecanums is a test result for this cargo and geometry.","interfaces":"Bumper, module structure, intake entry and printed pulleys.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect roller damage and pulley retention after field impacts.","unknowns":"Module revision dates and measured capture envelope.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/hP9RhZaW5fA","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-2022/404659"]},{"name":"Transfer and shooter","construction":"Top-driven path over the battery, remotely mounted feed motor and long belts, high-inertia flywheel and adjustable printed hood.","operation":"Cargo rises into a long wrap. The team reports roughly an inch of compression from its testing.","team_rationale":"Save space and preserve enough wheel speed to fire twice rapidly.","engineering_analysis":"Stored inertia can reduce droop but increases spin-up energy. Quantify both shots under realistic voltage and spacing. Long remote drives trade packaging for belt tracking and service access.","interfaces":"Battery clearance, belt guides, feeder, hood and aim.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check belt retention under impact. The team reported a shooter belt came off after robot contact.","unknowns":"Loaded droop, shot timing and abrasion near the battery.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/hP9RhZaW5fA","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-2022/404659/46"]},{"name":"Hood and telescope climb","construction":"Telescopes with gearboxes outside the tubes and a two-piece printed Onyx hood assembly.","operation":"Code disables the flywheel, transfers weight from hooks to hood, changes body angle with the hood and extends hooks for the next rung. Different endpoints are selectable.","team_rationale":"Compact traversal, partner clearance and easier gearbox service.","engineering_analysis":"Treat the hood as a primary structural member. Check load transfer, fastener reactions and wear at the hood pivot independently of shot accuracy. The operator’s two-hook check is part of the sequence.","interfaces":"Rungs, gearbox support, hood pivot and stored climb selection.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test one-hook capture, tube dents and backdrive at disable.","unknowns":"Proof load, actual load-bearing inserts and per-event climb success.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/hP9RhZaW5fA","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/2910-robot-2022/404659","https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2022CompetitionRobot/blob/master/src/main/java/org/frcteam2910/c2022/commands/AutoClimbCommand.java"]}],"revisions":["Team reports thickening aluminum after SunDome dents and changing parts that limit backdrive when disabled. The early release identifies extended hood range as climb-only and says the final hood transfer can improve room for partners."],"transferable_principles":["A dual-purpose structure can buy volume if both load cases are designed and verified. Prefer explicit operator confirmation where initial contact is ambiguous."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Different rung geometry or poor first-capture visibility defeats the same automation. The remote feed loses its benefit if service access or belt retention is poor."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. Code establishes intended sequences and selectable end poses, with event-specific settings and structural qualification still unknown."],"recommended_images":["Chief Delphi reveal post 1 full-robot photos for overview. Pair with a loaded transfer frame so the telescopes and hood contact are both identifiable."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2022-1678","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/ijiDMVvGc_E","title":"Citrus Circuits team interview at FIRST Championship","locator":"1:25–4:07 intake; 4:08–7:28 ejector and launcher; 7:29–13:00 control; 13:00–17:29 climb","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":"Team describes electric deployment, a reversible reject roller, lower motor placement, slot-based indexing and passive climb articulation.","limitations":"Automatic captions contain transcription errors. Measurements and reliability claims are attributed to speakers."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/404113","title":"Margie team reveal and intake follow-up","locator":"Posts 1, 2, 62, 66, 70","review_basis":"Read original Discourse post text and replies","facts":"No major Championship rebuild. Team explains bolted bearings, bushing clamps, chain slack and backdrive on impact.","limitations":"Replies describe the team’s own build and experience."},{"url":"https://github.com/frc1678/C2022-Public","title":"Margie public code","locator":"src/main/java/com/team1678/frc2022/subsystems/Indexer.java 98–166, Hood.java 47–86 and Climber.java 268–280","review_basis":"Read Java implementation","facts":"Slot occupancy, slow/fast eject, current-based hood homing and climber current checks.","limitations":"Public snapshot does not establish the exact match build."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Margie paired an electrically deployed front intake with a slot-based cargo path, a separate rear reject route, and a low-mounted launcher drive. Instead of assigning a powered joint to every climb motion, it used telescopes for extension and used chassis weight, gas shocks and stops to achieve the needed angle. The two choices are related: the robot’s mass distribution matters both on the floor and while rotating beneath the first bar.","piece_flow":"Three intake rollers and a singulator feed one cargo at a time past color and beam sensing. Two coupled rollers drive cargo into the junction. An independently driven roller either sends it rearward or advances it toward the kicker and launcher. Code tracks top and bottom occupancy, ignores a bottom pass-through when the top is empty and continues ejection briefly after the relevant beam clears.","packaging_and_motion":"The unequal four-bar stows near vertical and extends the roller outside the bumper. The deployment gearbox drives both sides through a cross-shaft and sprockets. Long transmission runs put most motors near the chassis, including the flywheel drive. The hood uses a printed geared arc. Packaging for the later climb concept avoided compromising scoring around an alternate geometry the team had tried.","subsystems":[{"name":"Collector","construction":"Thick polycarbonate four-bar, three rollers, edge belts and deploy-on-first-use winglets.","operation":"A single gearbox drives both arms. Holding voltage and chain slack allow some backdrive on wall contact.","team_rationale":"Robustness, fewer side jams and easier service.","engineering_analysis":"Separate impact travel from ordinary positional control. Symmetric drive does not guarantee symmetric loading when only one side strikes the field.","interfaces":"Bumper opening, singulator, hard stops and cross-shaft.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect winglet adhesion, chain slack, polycarbonate holes and bearing fasteners.","unknowns":"Impact limits and captured rate by approach.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ijiDMVvGc_E","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/404113","https://github.com/frc1678/C2022-Public"]},{"name":"Cargo routing","construction":"Coupled entry rollers and a separately powered reversible rear roller, beam breaks and color sensing.","operation":"Run forward to stage or reverse to eject. Code includes two ejection magnitudes and uses beam state for clearance.","team_rationale":"Quicker directional choice than the prototyped flap and slower auto ejects to limit rebound.","engineering_analysis":"Keep color sensing upstream of the irreversible decision and validate the timing at minimum spacing. Test bounce paths using actual field materials.","interfaces":"Singulator, slot state, kicker and rear exit.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check dust, missed transitions and recovery from stale queue state.","unknowns":"Classification error and actual reject distance.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ijiDMVvGc_E","https://github.com/frc1678/C2022-Public"]},{"name":"Scoring","construction":"Adjustable hood, driven main and upper rollers, and remote motor drive.","operation":"Vision-based range updates the shot. Code homes the hood by detecting elevated current while driving toward its stop.","team_rationale":"Maintain low CG and reduce reliance on an external home switch.","engineering_analysis":"A jam can imitate a reference stop. Validate homing under wear and voltage variation. Check long-belt compliance during closely spaced shots.","interfaces":"Hard stop, integrated encoder, camera and kicker.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect belt tracking and repeated home-position error.","unknowns":"Shot recovery and range accuracy.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ijiDMVvGc_E","https://github.com/frc1678/C2022-Public"]},{"name":"Passive-angle climb","construction":"Motorized string-driven telescopes, gas shocks, hard-stop slots and shaped hooks.","operation":"Lifting off rotates the chassis until stops establish approach angle. Partial extensions clear each bar before full extension.","team_rationale":"Preserve scoring packaging while improving speed and repeatability.","engineering_analysis":"The pivoting behavior depends on loaded CG and gas-spring force. A shifted battery or different rung spacing changes whether the next hook clears.","interfaces":"String, telescopes, stops, gyro reference and bar geometry.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect string and end stops. Test asymmetry, sensor drift and missed contact.","unknowns":"Loaded contact forces and failure distribution.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/ijiDMVvGc_E","https://github.com/frc1678/C2022-Public"]}],"revisions":["Team moved to all-electric actuation early, added side guides to reduce intake jams and changed bearing retention from rivets to bolts for service. It reports basic maintenance and rewiring before Championship in place of a major rebuild."],"transferable_principles":["Use the roller junction to separate piece routing from launcher aiming. Preserve intentional impact compliance while keeping service fast."],"disconfirming_conditions":["A different payload can bridge the singulator or rebound unpredictably on ejection. Passive climb geometry loses margin when CG, damping or bar spacing changes."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. No dimensioned CAD inspection or event-level electrical and controls mapping."],"recommended_images":["Use team post 66 closeups for bearing and pivot construction. Add a loaded climb view showing hard-stop engagement before using the geometry as a reference."]}

text: {"robot_id":"2022-254","review_date":"2026-11-09","source_reviews":[{"url":"https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","title":"Team 254 Sideways interview at FIRST Championship","locator":"1:27–3:20 drive and intake; 3:20–6:25 serializer and shooter; 6:25–9:15 climb; 9:15–14:28 color, rejection and vision","review_basis":"Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.","facts":"Team describes a fifth intake version, larger flywheel, flexing feed support, direct-to-traversal climb and vision-based rejection.","limitations":"Three physical staging locations described in the interview are distinct from the binder’s two-cargo storage requirement."},{"url":"https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf","title":"Sideways technical binder","locator":"Physical PDF pp. 9–11, 13–19, 21–23","review_basis":"Read binder prose and figure labels","facts":"Design goals, dual intake, serialized feed, launch surfaces, and truss reaction climb.","limitations":"Goals and free speeds are not independent measurements."},{"url":"https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2022-Public","title":"Sideways public code","locator":"Serializer.java 112–127, 214–256, 337–363; Superstructure.java 504–554","review_basis":"Read Java implementation","facts":"Explicit ejection coordination and moving-shot validity checks.","limitations":"Snapshot is distinct from match deployment."},{"url":"https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2022-recap-technical-binder-and-strategy-presentation/415951","title":"Team 254 technical Q&A","locator":"Posts 11, 14–16","review_basis":"Read team replies","facts":"Serializer shuffle and tubing, battery access and bellypan tradeoffs.","limitations":"Team retrospective."}],"whole_robot_explanation":"Sideways combined Team 254’s first competition swerve with opposed full-width intakes and a turreted launcher. The front of the cargo path could change with the driver’s approach, while the serializer protected already-collected friendly cargo. The climb used a truss reaction arm to set chassis angle and reach directly from mid to traversal, reducing the number of rung transfers.","piece_flow":"The active intake pulls cargo over the bumper. Large wheels funnel it inward, and top rollers and compliant surgical tubing feed it upward. A friendly first cargo can be shifted away from the active side so a newly acquired opponent piece can pass to the shooter without dislodging it. Rejection uses its own aim and wheel-speed commands. The released serializer waits for the launcher to be ready during automatic ejection.","packaging_and_motion":"Low module mounting and a solid bellypan lower the mass package. The battery is central because the serializer, climber and stinger constrain other locations. A pivoting feeder ramp gives battery access. The passive stinger stows clear of the shooter, and the turret’s bidirectional energy chain manages wiring over the yaw range.","subsystems":[{"name":"Drive and intake","construction":"MK4i swerve with L3 reduction, two pneumatic four-bars and lightweight tape-covered rollers.","operation":"Either side can become the collection side. Polycarbonate plates flex under impacts.","team_rationale":"Reduce approach turns and survive contact. Team selected swerve for an open field and evasive movement.","engineering_analysis":"Compare dual intake cycle savings against mass and duplicated service burden. Check floor clearance with the lower frame.","interfaces":"Bumpers, serializer, linkage and module plates.","service_and_failure_modes":"Check tape wear, lateral impacts and intake retraction.","unknowns":"Capture rates and module-bearing benefit.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2022-recap-technical-binder-and-strategy-presentation/415951"]},{"name":"Serializer","construction":"Mirrored powered sides, three beam breaks, color sensing, and flexible tubing for feed pressure.","operation":"Shuffle an occupied slot away from the inlet. Code coordinates color and ejection readiness with the superstructure.","team_rationale":"Keep intake available while rejecting through the shooter.","engineering_analysis":"Mixed-color traffic depends on separation and downstream readiness. Test changing intake sides with a friendly cargo already staged.","interfaces":"Ramp, battery access, sensor timing and turret.","service_and_failure_modes":"Inspect sensor contamination, tubing wear and fasteners that can spin in printed pockets.","unknowns":"False classifications and clearance margins.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2022-Public","https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-254-presents-2022-recap-technical-binder-and-strategy-presentation/415951"]},{"name":"Moving shot","construction":"Large billet flywheel, five driven backing rollers, adjustable hood and yaw turret.","operation":"Vision and measured motion inform aim. Released code invalidates shots when compensation exceeds limits or the target observation is stale.","team_rationale":"Long acceleration contact, matched surfaces for low spin and a wider useful scoring area.","engineering_analysis":"Measure velocity and spin separately. A fixed-azimuth adaptation has to resolve yaw through chassis heading and should requalify moving-shot limits.","interfaces":"Pose estimation, hood, flywheel, turret carrier and feed interlock.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test aim dropout, yaw saturation, ball wear and closely spaced shots.","unknowns":"Measured accuracy by speed and approach.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf","https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2022-Public"]},{"name":"Direct traversal","construction":"Chain lift, strapped reaction arm and spring-extending telescopic stinger with latch.","operation":"Pull on mid until the reaction arm presses under the truss and levels the robot. Deploy the stinger to reach traversal.","team_rationale":"Skip the high rung and preserve space for partners.","engineering_analysis":"Reaction load can be much larger than robot weight because of leverage. Check truss contact and strap forces, including capture offset and power loss.","interfaces":"Hooks, truss underside, strap anchor and extension envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test marginal reach, early release and partial latching.","unknowns":"Load distribution and tolerance stack.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf"]}],"revisions":["Interview identifies an early flex-wheel intake changed to taped tubing, smaller shooter wheels replaced by a larger billet wheel, and industrial color sensors replaced by REV sensors via a Teensy. An earlier high-bar reaction concept had a larger packaging sweep."],"transferable_principles":["Design capture, serialization and rejection as one traffic problem. Treat field reaction geometry as part of the climb linkage."],"disconfirming_conditions":["Without the same truss contact or hook reach the direct traversal fails. Electric-only or fixed-azimuth designs must rework actuation and reject routing."],"remaining_gaps":["Older dossier used for navigation. Published design goals and team-reported successes are distinct from measured match distributions."],"recommended_images":["https://media.team254.com/2022/03/8e68079e-sideways-full.jpg — official overview linked from https://www.team254.com/frc/2022/. Binder pp. 15, 18–19 for feed and climb."]}

title: 2022-254 Direct traversal
text: {"name":"Direct traversal","construction":"Chain lift, strapped reaction arm and spring-extending telescopic stinger with latch.","operation":"Pull on mid until the reaction arm presses under the truss and levels the robot. Deploy the stinger to reach traversal.","team_rationale":"Skip the high rung and preserve space for partners.","engineering_analysis":"Reaction load can be much larger than robot weight because of leverage. Check truss contact and strap forces, including capture offset and power loss.","interfaces":"Hooks, truss underside, strap anchor and extension envelope.","service_and_failure_modes":"Test marginal reach, early release and partial latching.","unknowns":"Load distribution and tolerance stack.","source_urls":["https://youtu.be/cKDmHCTDQW8","https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf"]}

title: When a dedicated collector earns the handoff
text: {"id":"possession-handoff","title":"When a dedicated collector earns the handoff","decision":"Choose between acquiring directly with the final tool and adding a separate floor collector.","robots":["2023-1746","2023-1325","2023-6328"],"analysis":"1746’s inclined lift and shared wristed hand keep the piece in the same tool from acquisition to placement. 1325 shows a separate way to simplify a shared tool. Its dossier describes fixing the grip spacing while retaining the articulated arm. 6328’s released code exposes both a direct floor sweep and a dedicated cube handoff, so its added collector can be evaluated as an optional path rather than a universal requirement.","check":"Time approach, acquisition, transfer, scoring and recovery together. Test off-angle pieces and interruptions at the collector-to-hand boundary. A dedicated collector earns its space when its wider capture envelope more than offsets the added transfer and service burden."}

title: Where to put the work of turning
text: {"id":"orientation-in-the-layout","title":"Where to put the work of turning","decision":"Decide whether to rotate the whole chassis, route the piece through the robot, or rotate the scoring assembly.","robots":["2018-254","2018-1678","2019-254"],"analysis":"Lockdown and Lemon Zest illustrate front-and-back delivery with a wristed tool on an elevator during POWER UP. Backlash solved a different access problem with a rotating scoring assembly in DEEP SPACE. Compare which turn the mechanism avoids, where it moves the occupied envelope and what it does to wiring and alignment. The ability to rotate or release on two sides only saves a cycle if the field route lets the robot use it.","check":"Draw pickup and target headings on the field first. Trace the loaded mechanism and bumper envelope through each transition. Compare the travel time saved with the added deployment, repeatability and repair costs under the same driving assumptions."}

title: A wide shooter needs a route that can keep it fed
text: {"id":"fuel-throughput-at-field-scale","title":"A wide shooter needs a route that can keep it fed","decision":"Choose a fuel path and scoring route as one system.","robots":["2026-125","2026-2481","2026-7769","2026-2910"],"analysis":"125 packages a circular serializer around a center-fed turret to gain aiming freedom. 2481 uses a wide fixed discharge path and accepts a loaded bump crossing. 7769 removed a divider that constrained real feed and linked its mechanism layout to service and defense problems. 2910’s original and rebuilt versions illustrate why a robot’s acquisition and release paths must be read together before borrowing a named mechanism.","check":"Measure acquired, retained and scored fuel over an entire active window. Run with a full hopper and near-empty hopper, partial battery, route interference and a feed jam. Compare the complete rate and recovery time instead of comparing bench burst speeds."}

title: When the climber sets the layout
text: {"id":"secondary-task-envelope","title":"When the climber sets the layout","decision":"Test whether an endgame mechanism justifies the space and load path it requires.","robots":["2022-1619","2022-604","2026-7769"],"analysis":"1619’s central climbing layout shaped where its cargo elevator and shooter could fit. 604’s released climb logic shows how reaches, partial lifts and handoffs must be distinct recoverable states. In 2026, 7769’s prototype notes show the opposite pressure when a proposed endgame device competes with scoring hardware for space. Compare endgame value under each game’s actual scoring rules and time window.","check":"Lay out the worst-case loaded climb and normal scoring states before selecting actuator locations. Track route time and service conflicts, then compare the expected match contribution with the cost of keeping the secondary mechanism."}
